text:
Once upon a time, there was a charming little girl named Lily. She loved to skip and play with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends were playing in a big room with many doors. They were having so much fun!
But then, they heard a loud noise. They all stopped and looked around. They saw a big dog barking at them. The dog was not happy. Lily and her friends were scared. They wanted to find the exit to get away from the dog.
Lily said, "Let's skip to the exit!" Her friends nodded and they all started skipping together. They found the exit and went outside. The dog couldn't follow them. They were safe!
Lily and her friends were so happy they could skip away from the dog. They played outside and had even more fun. The charming little girl and her friends learned that when they work together, they can solve any problem.

Torres is a Spanish international and made his debut against Portugal in 2003 . He has been capped over 100 times and is his country 's third-highest goalscorer of all time . With Spain he has participated in six major tournaments ; UEFA Euro 2004 , the 2006 FIFA World Cup , UEFA Euro 2008 , the 2010 FIFA World Cup , UEFA Euro 2012 and the 2014 FIFA World Cup . Spain won the three tournaments from 2008 to 2012 , with Torres scoring in the finals of both Euro 2008 and Euro 2012 .

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to measure things. One day, she found a big book with many pages. The pages were not organized. They were all mixed up.
Lily asked her mom, "Mom, can I measure the pages in this book?" Her mom said, "Yes, but first, we need to organize the pages."
So, Lily and her mom worked together to organize the pages. They put them in the right order. Then, Lily started to measure the pages. She was very happy.
But, something unexpected happened! As she measured the last page, a small door opened in the book. Lily and her mom looked inside and found a hidden treasure! They were so surprised and happy.
The moral of the story is that when you work together and stay organized, you can find amazing things.

Once upon a time, there was a white cat named Snowy. Snowy was very smart and loved to learn. One day, Snowy had a big exam at her school. She was a little scared, but she knew that she could do well if she tried her best.
Snowy's friend, a kind dog named Buddy, saw that she was worried. Buddy wanted to help Snowy feel better. So, he decided to lend her his favorite toy, a soft, red ball. "This will make you feel happy," Buddy said. Snowy smiled and thanked Buddy for being such a good friend.
The day of the exam came, and Snowy took the red ball with her. Every time she felt scared, she looked at the ball and thought of Buddy. The red ball helped her feel brave and strong. Snowy did very well on her exam, and she knew it was because of her friend Buddy. They played with the red ball together and were very happy.

Mommy and Daddy went to the store. They wanted to buy a toy. Daddy said they should look for something that was cheap.
Mommy and Daddy found a toy. It was a circle. Daddy weighed the toy in his hands. He thought it was not too heavy.
Mommy and Daddy bought the toy. They were happy that it was so cheap.
When they got home, Mommy and Daddy gave the toy to their son, Sammy. He was very happy. He couldn't wait to play with it. Sammy smiled and gave Mommy and Daddy a big hug.

Once there was a boy named Tim. He had a toy cooler. He loved to play with it. One day, he saw a girl named Sue. Sue was sad because she lost her toy. Tim thought it was stupid to cry over a toy.
Tim wanted to help Sue, so he shared his cooler. They played together and had fun. Sue stopped crying and smiled. Tim felt happy too.
In the end, Tim learned that being kind and sharing was better than being mean. He was glad that he helped Sue. Now, they were both happy and became good friends. The moral of the story is to always be kind and share with others.

Once upon a time, there was a little cat named Tom. Tom was going on a journey to find his friend, the big dog named Max. Tom walked and walked, feeling happy and peaceful.
On his way, Tom met a bird. The bird said, "Hello, Tom! Where are you going?" Tom replied, "I am going to find my friend Max. Do you know where he is?" The bird thought for a moment and said, "I think Max is by the big tree near the pond. Be careful on your journey, Tom. The big tree is very far away."
Tom thanked the bird and continued on his journey. He walked and walked, and soon, he could see the big tree near the pond. Tom felt excited as he knew he would soon arrive to see Max.
When Tom arrived at the big tree, he saw Max waiting for him. Max was happy to see Tom too. They played and played until the sun went down. The journey was long, but it was worth it to see his friend Max. In the end, Tom and Max walked back home together, feeling peaceful and happy.

One day, a young boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. At the park, Tim saw a big tree. In the tree, there was a small bird. The bird was not happy. The bird started to complain.
"Chirp, chirp! I can't find my food," said the bird. "I am so hungry."
Tim wanted to help the bird. He looked around the park and saw an olive on the ground. He picked up the olive and gave it to the bird. The bird was so happy.
"Thank you, Tim!" said the bird. "Now I am not hungry anymore."
Tim felt good. He helped the bird, and now the bird was happy. Tim and his mom went home, and they told dad about their day at the park.

Lily and Ben were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big house with a fence. They wanted to see what was inside.
They found a hole in the fence and crawled through. They saw a door with a lock. Ben had a key in his pocket. He said, "I can unlock the door. Maybe there is something fun inside."
Lily said, "OK, let's go." They opened the door and went in. They saw a big kitchen with many jars and boxes. They saw a jar with a label that said "sugar". They liked sugar. They opened the jar and took some.
They did not know that the jar was not sugar. It was poison. It was very bad for them. They felt sick and fell down. They could not get up.
The owner of the house came back. He was not kind. He was angry. He saw Lily and Ben on the floor. He called the police. He said, "These kids broke into my house and stole my poison. They are very naughty. They have to go to jail."
Lily and Ben were very scared. They wished they had not unlocked the door. They wished they had stayed in the park. They learned a hard lesson.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk. He saw a big blue gate. The gate was closed. Tim wanted to go through the gate to see what was on the other side.
Tim said, "Hello, gate. Can you please open for me?" The gate opened, and Tim said, "Thank you, gate!" He walked through the gate and saw a big green tree and a small red ball.
Tim played with the ball under the tree. He had lots of fun. When it was time to go home, Tim said to the gate, "Please open again." The gate opened, and Tim said, "Thank you, gate!" Tim went home and told his mom about the blue gate and the fun he had.

Once there lived a happy puppy and a little girl. Every day the puppy and the girl played together on the beach by the ocean. The pup loved to chew on sticks and bones.
One day they were playing on the beach, but the ocean was much bigger than usual. The little girl threw her stick in the water, but the puppy couldn't reach it! He barked and whimpered trying to get it, but it was too far away. The little girl was sad and worried for her pup.
Suddenly, a big friendly whale came to help. He opened his huge mouth and gently grabbed the stick with his teeth. He brought it back to shore and the pup started to chew it. The little girl clapped, happy that her pup got his toy back.
The puppy and the girl were so thankful to the big whale. From then on, the pup was always happy to play near the ocean and chew his stick.

One Sunday, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. He wore his tight blue shoes that he liked very much. Tim saw a big slide and wanted to play on it. He climbed up and slid down fast. It was so much fun!
Tim saw a small girl named Lily standing near the slide. She looked sad and scared. Tim wanted to help her feel better. He walked over to her and said, "Hi, I'm Tim. Why are you sad?"
Lily said, "I'm scared to go down the slide. It looks too big."
Tim wanted to comfort Lily. He told her, "Don't be scared. I will go down the slide with you. It's fun!" Lily smiled and they both climbed up. Tim held Lily's hand as they slid down together.
Lily was not scared anymore. She said, "Thank you, Tim! That was fun!" They played on the slide all day, and Tim and Lily became good friends. They went to the park every Sunday to play together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy car. It was his original toy, the first one he ever got. He loved to play with it all day long.
One day, Tim met a girl named Sue. Sue also had a toy car. They decided to play together. They made their cars go fast and slow, and then they made them reverse. They laughed and had fun.
"Let's have a race!" said Tim. Sue agreed, and they lined up their toy cars. The race began, and their cars zoomed forward. Tim's car went very fast, but Sue's car was faster. Sue's car won the race.
Tim was sad, but Sue said, "Don't worry, we can race again. Maybe your car will win next time." They played together all day, racing their cars and making them reverse. Tim and Sue became best friends, and they always played with their original toy cars together.

Once upon a time, there was a big bucket. It was the first bucket, the original bucket. This bucket had a lock that no one could open. Everyone in the town wanted to see what was inside the bucket.
One day, a little girl named Amy found a key. She thought, "Maybe this key can unlock the bucket!" She ran to the bucket and put the key in the lock. She turned the key and the lock clicked open.
When the bucket was unlocked, everyone gathered around to see what was inside. They all thought there would be something amazing. But they were surprised! Inside the bucket, there were just more keys. The people didn't know that these keys could unlock other things in their town. The keys made everyone happy because they could open new doors and find new adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky lived near a pond. One day, Ducky met a new friend, Froggy. Froggy was green and liked to jump. Ducky was yellow and liked to swim.
"Let me show you my pond," said Ducky to Froggy. Froggy was happy and said, "Yes, please show me!" So, Ducky and Froggy went to the pond together. They played in the water and had lots of fun.
But then, they saw something terrible. A big, mean fish came to the pond. The fish wanted to eat Ducky and Froggy. Ducky and Froggy were scared. They swam and jumped away from the fish. They hid in the tall grass until the fish went away. After that, Ducky and Froggy were safe and happy again. They played at the pond every day, but they always looked out for the big, mean fish.

One day, a little bird named Tim wanted to fly high. He tried and tried, but he could not fly high. Tim was sad. His friend, the big bear named Ben, saw him and wanted to help.
Ben had an idea to help Tim fly high. He told Tim to freeze like a statue. Tim did it. Ben then picked up Tim and threw him high into the sky. Tim was flying high now! He was so happy.
Tim and Ben were a success. They played all day and had so much fun. Tim could now fly high, and Ben was happy to help his friend. They were the best of friends and had many more fun days together.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is brown and fluffy. He has a red collar.
"Can we pet the dog?" Lily asks Tom.
"Let's ask the owner first," Tom says. They see a man sitting on a bench. He is reading a book. He has a leash in his hand.
"Excuse me, sir," Tom says. "Can we pet your dog?"
The man looks up and smiles. "Sure, you can," he says. "His name is Rex. He is very friendly."
Tom and Lily go to Rex. They say hello to him. Rex wags his tail. He licks their faces. Tom and Lily giggle. They pet his fur. They give him a rub on his belly. Rex rolls over and makes a happy sound.
"Rex likes you," the man says. "Do you want to give him a treat?"
"Yes, please," Tom and Lily say.
The man takes out a small bag from his pocket. He opens it and gives them each a biscuit. They hold the biscuits in their hands.
"Say 'sit', Rex," the man says.
"Sit, Rex," Tom and Lily say.
Rex sits down. He looks at them with his big eyes.
"Give him the biscuit," the man says.
Tom and Lily give Rex the biscuit. Rex takes it gently. He crunches it in his mouth. He licks his lips. He looks at them again.
"Say 'good boy', Rex," the man says.
"Good boy, Rex," Tom and Lily say.
Rex barks. He jumps up and down. He wags his tail.
"Thank you, Rex," Tom and Lily say.
"Thank you, sir," they say to the man.
"You're welcome," the man says. "Rex likes to make new friends. He thinks you are very nice."
Tom and Lily smile. They hug Rex. They say goodbye to him and the man. They go back to play in the park. They are happy. They think Rex is a wonderful dog. They think his biscuit is delicious.

Once there was a little otter who lived near a river. She loved to play in the water and have fun. One day, when the sun was shining, she decided to go for a swim. But the little otter started to go too far. Before she knew it, she was out of sight from the riverbank.
The little otter did not know it, but she had gone far away from her home. She swam for miles and miles until she was too tired to keep going. When she looked around, she noticed that she was surrounded by a beautiful meadow of flowers.
The little otter looked at the beauty all around her and wished that she could stay. But, she soon realized that she had strayed too far. She started to regret her decision to go so far and be so adventurous.
She turned around and made her way back to the river. Even though she wanted to stay, she knew it was best to go home. After a long journey, she eventually made it back. The little otter never regretted being adventurous again.

Lily liked to polish her books. She had many books in her room. She liked to make them shiny and clean. She used a soft cloth and some water. She rubbed the cloth on the books gently.
One day, Lily went to the library with her mom. The library had many more books than her room. Lily wanted to polish them all. She took a cloth from her bag and started to polish a book on a shelf. But the librarian saw her and said, "No, no, no! You can't polish the books here. They are not yours. You have to be careful with them. Put the cloth away and use your eyes, not your hands."
Lily felt frustrated. She did not understand why she could not polish the books. She liked to polish books. She thought she was helping. She did not want to use her eyes. She wanted to use her hands. She started to cry.
Her mom heard her cry and came to her. She hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I know you love books. But the library books are for everyone to share. You can't polish them because you might damage them or make them wet. You can look at them and read them, but you have to be gentle and respectful. Do you understand?"
Lily nodded. She wiped her tears and said, "I'm sorry, librarian. I won't polish the books anymore. Can I still read them?"
The librarian smiled and said, "Of course you can, Lily. You are a good reader. And you can polish your own books at home as much as you like. Just don't bring the cloth to the library again, okay?"
Lily agreed. She put the cloth back in her bag and picked a book to read. She was still a little frustrated, but she also felt curious and happy. She liked the library. She liked books. And she liked to polish them.

Grace was very envious of her sister, Josie. Every day, her sister would dance to the jazz music in their house. She was so graceful and light on her feet. Every time her sister danced, Grace would watch with admiration.
One day, she decided to join in. She moved her feet to the beat of the music and felt so free. Josie smiled and said, "Grace, you look amazing! Don't forget to keep dancing and keep on practising".
This reminded Grace of the importance of hard work and dedication. She practised hard every day and soon she was dancing just as well as her sister. Josie cheered her and said, "You've done really well, Grace".
Grace was so proud of herself and she never let the feeling of envy enter her mind ever again.

Mathews returned to the African mainland territories once more in 1884 when he landed with a force which intended to establish further garrisons there to dissuade German territorial claims . This attempt ultimately failed when five German warships steamed into Zanzibar Town harbour and threatened the Sultan into signing away the territories which would later form German East Africa . Further territories were ceded to the German East Africa Company in 1888 but unrest amongst the locals against them prevented them from taking control and Mathews was dispatched with 100 men to restore order . Finding around 8, 000 people gathered against the German administrators Mathews was forced to return with his men to Zanzibar . He landed once again with more troops but found himself subject to death threats and that his troops would not obey his orders and so returned again to Zanzibar .

John and his mom were walking in the park. "Mommy, can I count the trees?" asked John. His mom smiled and said, "Sure, go ahead!" 
John began counting the trees out loud. "One, two, three..." he counted. Soon he had counted all the way to twelve. 
But then something strange happened. A white veil suddenly appeared and blocked his view of the trees. John couldn't count anymore. He looked up at his mom and asked, "What's that veil doing there?" 
His mom frowned and said, "That's a selfish veil. It's keeping us from counting the trees. We have to find a way to get it away." Just then, they heard a loud noise in the sky and looked up. It was a giant number 20! "That number will get rid of the veil," said John's mom. Sure enough, the number flew straight down and knocked the veil away. 
John and his mom cheered. John was able to finish counting all the way to twenty. His mom smiled and said, "See, John, numbers can be very helpful!"

A graduate of the Stevens Institute of Technology and New York University , Reines joined the Manhattan Project 's Los Alamos Laboratory in 1944 , working in the Theoretical Division in Richard Feynman 's group . He became a group leader there in 1946 . He participated in a number of nuclear tests , culminating in his becoming the director of the Operation Greenhouse test series in the Pacific in 1951 .

John was very restless. He wanted to play hockey, like his brother. But he was too small. His brother was big and strong, and could tie up his own hockey stick with thick strings. John tried to do it too, but he couldn't tie the strings tight enough.
John was frustrated and threw the string to the ground. He looked around, desperately looking for a way to play. Suddenly, he saw a rope lying on the ground. He took it and hurried to his brother. He asked if he could tie the rope around his stick. His brother smiled and agreed.
John felt happy. He tried to tie the rope around the stick, but it was too difficult for him. No matter how hard he tried, he just couldn't do it. His brother helped him, and eventually the stick was tied.
John was so excited. He and his brother both had hockey sticks now. Finally, he could play hockey with his brother. The two of them ran to the playground and started playing. John was so happy!

Waymon then applied for a scholarship to study at the prestigious Curtis Institute of Music in Philadelphia , where she was denied despite a well-received audition . Simone became fully convinced this rejection had been entirely due to her race , a statement that has been a matter of controversy . Years later , two days before her death , the Curtis Institute of Music bestowed an honorary degree on Simone .

Once upon a time there was a blue bird named Sunny. She lived in the forest with her family. One day Sunny was playing in the trees when she heard a strange noise. She decided to investigate.
When she looked around a tall bush, she saw two animals. They were arguing loudly. Sunny was surprised and asked, "What's wrong?"
The animals explained that they both wanted the same spot to rest. One of them wanted the spot to get warm from the sun, the other wanted the spot because it was shaded.
Sunny thought for a moment and said, "Maybe you both can share the spot. That way, you will both be happy!"
The animals agreed and settled in the spot together. They were very happy and thanked Sunny for her suggestion.
This is the moral of the story: when everyone works together, everyone wins.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Kelsie. She was playing and running around at the beach with her mum. Kelsie loved to feel the soft sand in her toes.
Kelsie saw something in the sand. She picked it up and realised it was an anchor.
"Mummy! What is this?" Kelsie asked as she squeezed the anchor.
"Thatâs an anchor, Kelsie. Itâs used by lazy boats to stay in the same spot," her mum explained.
Kelsie laughed, and kept squeezing the anchor.
"Letâs put the anchor back in the sand now, Kelsie," Mum said.
Kelsie put the anchor back, and continued running around the beach with her mum. She had enjoyed her first encounter with an anchor.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a big bag of oats. He wanted to know how heavy it was. So, he asked his mom to help him weigh the bag. His mom said, "The bag is very heavy! It must have a lot of oats inside."
Tim had a great idea. He wanted to share the oats with his friends. So, he went to his friend Sally's house. He said, "Sally, I have a big bag of oats. Let's make oat cookies and share them with our friends!"
Sally was very happy. She said, "That's a great idea, Tim! Let's make the cookies together." They made the cookies and shared them with all their friends. Everyone loved the oat cookies and had a fun time. Tim was happy that he could share his big bag of oats with everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a rhinoceros. He was wrapping a present for his friend. It was difficult for him because he had never done it before. He didn't know how to wrap the present well. He tried for a long time but it never looked right.
Then, one day, a friendly man saw the rhinoceros struggling. He came over to help the rhinoceros wrap his present. The man showed the rhinoceros how to do it step by step. With the man's help, the rhinoceros was able to wrap his present until it looked perfect.
The rhinoceros was so happy and thanked the friendly man for helping him wrap the present. The rhinoceros was so proud of his beautiful wrapped present. With the man's help, he had made it!

Once upon a time, there was a big bird named Bob. Bob liked to play in the rain. One day, the rain came and Bob went to play. Bob saw a little bug named Ben. Ben was envious of Bob because he could not play in the rain. Ben was too small to play in the rain and would get sick.
Bob wanted to help Ben. He thought of a plan. He found a tool, a big leaf. Bob put the leaf over Ben so he could play too. The leaf kept Ben dry from the rain. Now, Ben could play with Bob.
Bob and Ben played in the rain. They were very happy. Bob would soak in the rain, and Ben would stay dry under the leaf. They played and played until the rain stopped. Now, Ben was not envious anymore. They became best friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. He lived in the sea. He was an enthusiastic fish who loved to play with his friends. One day, a big fish came to their sea. The big fish wanted to be the boss of all the little fish.
Fin did not like this. He did not want the big fish to be the boss. He wanted all the fish to be friends and play together. Fin talked to the big fish. He asked the big fish to be nice and play with them. The big fish said no. He wanted to be the boss.
Fin did not accept this. He talked to his friends. They all worked together to show the big fish how fun it is to play and be friends. The big fish saw how happy they were. He changed his mind and became their friend. They all played happily in the sea.

Once upon a time, there was a man named Tim. Tim liked to drive his big car. One day, he put on his nice suit and went for a drive.
As Tim drove, he saw a small, fragile bird on the side of the road. The bird looked sad. Tim stopped his car and got out. He walked over to the bird and said, "Hello, little bird. Why are you sad?"
The bird looked up at Tim and said, "I am lost. Can you help me find my way home?" Tim smiled and said, "Of course, little bird. Hop in my car and we will find your home together."
So, the bird got into Tim's car and they drove around, looking for the bird's home. After a while, they found it. The bird was so happy and thanked Tim for his help. Tim waved goodbye to the bird and drove back home, feeling happy that he could help a friend in need.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived an elderly man. He was very kind and always wore a nice suit. He liked to help people and offer them things they needed.
One day, while walking in the park, he saw a little girl crying. She had lost her toy. The elderly man offered to help her find it. They looked and looked, but could not find the toy. The little girl was very sad.
Then, something unexpected happened. A big dog came running with the toy in his mouth. The dog gave the toy back to the little girl. She was so happy! The elderly man smiled and the girl thanked him. The moral of the story is that when we help others, good things can happen.

Once upon a time, there was a big fish. This fish was very selfish. He did not like to share with his friends. One day, the fish saw a tunnel in the water. He thought there might be food inside.
The selfish fish decided to dive into the tunnel. He swam and swam, but he did not find any food. The tunnel was very dark and scary. The fish started to feel alone and sad.
After a while, the fish wanted to leave the tunnel. But he could not find the way out. He was stuck in the dark tunnel. The selfish fish wished he had shared with his friends before. Now, he was all alone in the dark tunnel and could not get out.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the store with his mom. He saw a toy on a high shelf. He wanted the toy very much. But his mom said, "We have to delay buying the toy until your birthday."
Tim was sad, but he waited for his birthday. On his birthday, he was glad to see a big box. He thought it was the toy from the shelf. He opened the box, but it was not the toy. It was a big, soft bear.
His mom said, "I know you wanted the toy, but I saw this bear and thought you would like it more." Tim hugged the bear and smiled. He was happy his mom got him the bear instead of the toy from the shelf.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a wealthy man named Tom. He had a big house and many toys. One sunny day, Tom went for a walk by the river. He saw a little boy named Tim playing with a ball near the water.
Suddenly, Tim's ball rolled into the river. Tim was sad and started to cry. Tom saw this and said, "Don't cry, I will help you get your ball back." Tom hurried to find a long stick to reach the ball in the river.
Tom used the stick and got the ball out of the river. Tim was very happy and said, "Thank you, Tom! You are very kind." Tom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tim. Be careful when you play near the river." From that day on, Tom and Tim became good friends and played together by the river every day.

Once there was this fisherman who went fishing in a pond. He was a bit nervous but he had to go as he wanted to feed his family. He packed his gear, put on his waders and made his way to the pond.
The fisherman had no luck that day. He didn't catch anything. He was feeling a bit sad but he still decided to stay a little longer. The fisherman watied by the pond until he heard a noise. He saw some little fish jumping up into the sky!
The fisherman was so excited! He was so happy that he was able to provide food for his family. He learned a valuable lesson that day - there is always something to value. The fisherman's nervousness had been worth it. The day had been a success after all!

Once upon a time, there was a little fairy. This fairy had a big heart, but she was not pretty. She was ugly. All the other fairies had pretty wings, but her wings were not nice.
One day, a little girl saw the ugly fairy. The girl asked the fairy for help. The ugly fairy wanted to help the girl, but the girl was scared. She said, "No, I want a pretty fairy." The ugly fairy was sad, but she did not refuse.
The ugly fairy went to find a pretty fairy. She asked her friend, the pretty fairy, to help the girl. The pretty fairy said yes. They both went back to the girl. The girl was happy to see the pretty fairy.
The pretty fairy helped the girl, and the ugly fairy watched. The girl said thank you to the pretty fairy. Then, she looked at the ugly fairy. She said, "I am sorry I was scared. You are nice too." The ugly fairy smiled, and they all became friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog. This dog had a tiny flea. The flea was unknown to the dog, but it liked to jump and play in the dog's fur.
One day, the dog felt a tickle in its nose. It was the flea! The dog tried to sniff, but it could not stop the tickle. Then, the dog let out a big sneeze!
The sneeze was so big that the flea went flying! It landed far away, in a big tree. The flea was sad and missed the dog. But soon, it found a new friend, a small bird. The bird and the flea played together and were happy. And the dog never had to sneeze again.

Once upon a time, there was a smart bird named Bobo. Bobo lived in a big tree near a cactus. The cactus had sharp points on it.
One day, Bobo saw a yummy bug on the cactus. He wanted to eat the bug. But the cactus was too sharp. Bobo felt sad because he could not eat the bug.
Bobo had an idea. He used a stick to get the bug from the cactus. He was very happy. Bobo learned not to touch the sharp cactus. He did not regret it.

Timmy was very excite. Today was his birthday and he knew his mother had a big surprise for him. He jumped out of bed and ran to the living room, where he saw a big box with a bow on it.
"Happy birthday, Timmy!" his mother said, hugging him. "Do you want to open your present?"
"Yes, yes, yes!" Timmy said, tearing off the paper. Inside the box, he found a soft and fluffy teddy bear. He loved it and hugged it tight. "Thank you, mommy! He is so cute!"
"You're welcome, sweetie. He is your new friend. You can name him whatever you want," his mother said, smiling.
Timmy thought for a moment. He looked at the teddy bear's brown fur and black nose. He had an idea. "I will name him Lazy," he said.
"Lazy? Why Lazy?" his mother asked, curious.
"Because he looks like he likes to sleep a lot, like me," Timmy said, giggling. "And because he is not a busy bear, like daddy."
His mother laughed. "That's a funny name, Timmy. I like it. Lazy is a lucky bear to have you as his owner. Now, do you want some cake and ice cream?"
"Yes, please!" Timmy said, holding Lazy in his arms. He followed his mother to the kitchen, where a yummy chocolate cake was waiting for him. He was very happy. It was the best birthday ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a magic mirror in her room. The mirror could change things when Lily looked at it. She liked to play with the mirror and change her toys into other toys. One day, Lily felt confused because her favorite toy was gone.
Lily went to the magic mirror to find her toy. She thought the mirror could change and bring her toy back. But the mirror did not change her toy. Lily was sad and confused. She did not know what to do.
Lily tried to change the mirror, but it did not work. She was very sad and cried. The mirror broke and her favorite toy was never found. Lily learned that sometimes, things do not go the way we want them to.

One day, a girl named Sue went to the park. It was a cold day, so she wore her warm coat. She played with her ball near a deep hole. Sue was very careful not to fall in the hole.
Sue saw her friend Tom wake from a nap under a tree. Tom was sleepy and did not see the deep hole. He walked towards Sue, but then he fell in the hole! Sue was scared and did not know what to do.
Then, something unexpected happened. A big bird flew down and picked up Tom with its strong feet. The bird lifted Tom out of the hole and put him back on the ground. Sue and Tom were so happy and thanked the bird. They played together for the rest of the day, staying far away from the deep hole.

One day, a boy named Tim found a watch. The watch was very creative. It could talk and make jokes. Tim liked the watch very much.
"Hi, Tim!" said the watch. "Do you want to hear a joke?" Tim smiled and said, "Yes, please!" The watch told a funny joke and Tim laughed. They became good friends.
Every day, Tim and the watch played together. They had a lot of fun. The watch made Tim laugh with its jokes. Tim was very happy to have a creative watch as his friend.

Once upon a time, there was a pig named Pinky. Pinky lived on a farm with many other animals. Pinky was a little jealous of the other animals because they could do things that Pinky could not do. The horse could run fast, the cow could give milk, and the chicken could lay eggs.
One day, Pinky saw a big tree with yummy fruit. Pinky wanted to get the fruit, but the tree was too tall. Pinky asked the horse, "Can you help me get the fruit?" The horse said, "No, I can't climb trees."
Pinky went to the cow and asked, "Can you help me get the fruit?" The cow said, "No, I can't reach that high." Pinky was sad, but then he had an idea.
Pinky went to the tree and started to push it with all his might. The tree began to yield, and the fruit fell to the ground. Pinky was so happy that he could get the fruit all by himself. The other animals saw what Pinky did and were proud of him. Pinky was no longer jealous, because he learned that he could do something special too.

John and Suzanne were two children who were best friends. They had a lot of fun doing things together. One day, John got an idea.
He said to Suzanne: "Let's get a prize!"
Suzanne was excited. "Yes, let's do it!" she said.
John and Suzanne were very busy. They looked for the best prize. Finally, they found a nice one. It was a toy boat with lots of fun colors.
John said, "Let's get this prize!"
Suzanne was so happy. "Yes, let's do it!"
The two friends got the prize and went back home. They had lots of fun playing with the toy boat.
They were the happiest best friends in the world.

One day, a strong cat named Tom went to the fridge. He wanted a snack. He saw a big bowl of water inside the fridge. Tom thought, "I can soak my toy in this water!"
Tom took the bowl out and put his toy in the water. The toy got all wet. He was very happy. Then, Tom's friend, a dog named Max, came over. Max saw the wet toy and said, "Why is your toy wet?"
Tom said, "I soaked it in the water from the fridge." Max looked at Tom and said, "That's not water, that's milk!" Tom was surprised. He didn't know it was milk. They both laughed and played with the wet toy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big bookcase in her room. It was full of books with many colors. Lily loved to read these books every day. She would sit on her bed and look at the pictures.
One day, Lily saw a book on the top shelf of the bookcase. She wanted to read it, but it was too high for her to reach. She tried to jump, but she could not get it. Lily felt sad. She wanted to read the book so much.
Lily's friend, Tom, came over to play. He saw Lily looking at the bookcase. Tom was taller than Lily, so he tried to help her. He reached up and got the book for her. Lily was so happy. She thanked Tom and they read the book together. Now, Lily was not envious of the book on the top shelf anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a tall man. The tall man had a big sack. In the sack, there were many onions. He liked onions very much. He carried the sack with him everywhere he went.
One day, the tall man went for a walk. He saw a big tree. He put his sack of onions under the tree and sat down. He was very tired. He closed his eyes and went to sleep.
While the tall man was sleeping, a small dog came by. The dog smelled the onions in the sack. The dog liked onions too. So, the dog took the sack and ran away. When the tall man woke up, his sack was gone. He was very sad. But then, he saw the dog with his sack of onions. The dog came back and gave the sack to the tall man. They both smiled and became friends. From that day on, they shared the onions and had fun together.

Between 1764 and 1809 , Sweden built six hemmemas . The hemmema became the largest and most heavily armed vessel in the archipelago fleet and served in the Russo-Swedish War of 1788 – 90 . Oden , the first hemmema , was relatively small and very similar to a turuma , a different type of " archipelago frigate " . Russia built six hemmemas based on the Swedish design between 1808 and 1823 after capturing three of the Swedish vessels at the surrender of Sveaborg in 1808 . The later versions , both Swedish and Russian , were much larger and much more heavily armed than Oden .

Lily and Sam were playing in the park. They liked to make things with sticks, stones and leaves. They were very creative. They made a house, a car and a cake.
"Look at our cake!" Lily said. "It has berries and nuts on top. Do you want some?"
"Yes, please!" Sam said. "It looks yummy. Thank you for sharing."
They pretended to eat the cake. They made funny noises with their mouths. They laughed and smiled.
Suddenly, they saw a big dog. It was brown and furry. It had a long tail and a wet nose. It appeared from behind a tree. It ran towards them. It wanted to play.
"Wow, a dog!" Lily said. "Hello, dog. What is your name?"
The dog barked. It wagged its tail. It licked Lily's face. She giggled.
"Hi, dog. You are friendly. Do you want to play with us?" Sam said.
The dog nodded. It sniffed their cake. It looked tasty. It took a bite.
"Hey, that's our cake!" Lily said. "You can't eat that. It's not real. It's made of leaves."
The dog spit out the leaves. It made a funny face. It did not like the taste. It looked sorry.
"It's okay, dog. We forgive you. You didn't know." Sam said. "But you can't have our cake. You can have this stick instead. Do you like sticks?"
The dog barked. It liked sticks. It took the stick from Sam. It ran away. It came back. It dropped the stick. It wanted Sam to throw it.
"Okay, dog. Let's play fetch. Ready?" Sam said.
He threw the stick. The dog ran after it. It caught it. It brought it back. They played fetch for a long time.
Lily and Sam had fun with the dog. They were happy. They made a new friend. They forgot about their cake. They did not mind. They had something better. They had a dog.

Once upon a time, there was a normal cat named Tom. Tom was black and loved to play. One day, Tom went outside to find a new friend.
Tom saw a bird and offered to play. The bird said yes, and they played a fun game. They ran, jumped, and laughed. Tom was very happy to have a new friend.
But then, something unexpected happened. The bird changed into a big, black dog! Tom was surprised but still wanted to play. The dog smiled and said, "I was just playing a trick on you. I wanted to see if you would still be my friend." Tom laughed and said, "Of course, I will be your friend!" And they played happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named True. True was a very glad dog. He liked to play all day long. One day, True saw a big ball. He wanted to play with it.
True went to his friend, Cat. "Cat, will you play with me?" True asked. Cat said, "Yes, I will play with you. Let's finish our game with the big ball." They played and played until they were tired.
At the end of the day, True and Cat were very glad. They had so much fun playing with the big ball. They said, "We will play again tomorrow!" And they did. True and Cat became the best of friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient chair. It was very old and lived in a big room. The chair had many friends, like the table, the bed, and the lamp. They all liked to play together.
One day, the chair decided to play a game with its friends. The game was called "Who can stand the longest?" The chair, the table, and the bed all stood still. But then, something unexpected happened. The chair started to wobble and fall!
The chair was scared, but its friends were there to help. The table and the bed caught the chair before it hit the floor. The chair was safe! They all laughed and decided that the game was too hard for the ancient chair.
But then, the chair had an idea. "Let's play another game," it said. "A game where we all sit down and tell stories." So, the chair, the table, the bed, and the lamp all sat down and shared their favorite stories. They all had a great time and the chair didn't fall again.

One day, a kind and compassionate queen lived in a big castle. She had a magic shield that could provide help to anyone who needed it. She loved to share her shield with her people, so they could feel safe and happy.
One sunny day, a little girl named Lily came to the castle. She asked the queen, "Can I see the magic shield, please?" The queen smiled and said, "Of course, dear. Here it is." Lily looked at the shield and was amazed by its magic.
Suddenly, a loud noise came from outside the castle. A big dragon came and tried to take the shield away. But the shield did something unexpected. It started to glow and turned the dragon into a cute, little kitten. The queen, Lily, and the people were surprised and happy. They all played with the kitten and lived happily ever after.

Sam and Mia like to play in the park. They like to swing on the swings, slide on the slide, and run on the grass. One day, they see a new thing in the park. It is a pitch. It has a big net and a small ball.
"Look, Mia, a pitch!" Sam says. "Let's play with the ball!"
"OK, Sam, but how do we play?" Mia asks.
Sam picks up the ball and throws it to Mia. Mia catches it and throws it back. They do this for a while, and then Sam has an idea.
"Let's swing the ball!" he says. "I will swing it to you, and you will swing it to me!"
"OK, Sam, but how do we swing the ball?" Mia asks.
Sam shows Mia how to swing the ball. He holds the ball in one hand, and swings his arm back and forth. Then he lets go of the ball, and it flies to Mia.
"Wow, Sam, you swing the ball so well!" Mia says. She tries to swing the ball back to Sam, but she swings too hard, and the ball goes over the net.
"Oh no, Mia, the ball is gone!" Sam says. "How will we get it back?"
They run to the net, and see that the ball is on the other side. There is a gate, but it is closed.
"Maybe we can open the gate," Mia says. She pushes the gate, but it does not move.
"Maybe we can climb the net," Sam says. He tries to climb the net, but it is too high.
They are sad, and do not know what to do. Then they hear a voice.
"Hello, kids, do you need some help?" the voice says.
They look up, and see a man. He is wearing a hat and a shirt with a logo. He is holding a big bag.
"Who are you?" Sam asks.
"I am the coach," the man says. "I work here at the pitch. I teach people how to play with the ball."
"Can you help us get our ball back?" Mia asks.
"Sure, I can," the coach says. "The gate is locked, but I have the key. Follow me."
The coach opens the gate, and walks to the other side. He picks up the ball, and gives it to Sam and Mia.
"Here you go, kids, your ball," he says. "Do you like to play with the ball?"
"Yes, we do," Sam and Mia say. "We like to swing the ball."
"That's great," the coach says. "Do you want to learn more about how to swing the ball?"
"Yes, we do," Sam and Mia say.
"OK, then, come with me," the coach says. "I will show you some tips and tricks. And maybe you can join my team someday."
Sam and Mia are happy, and follow the coach. They learn how to swing the ball better, and have fun. They make a new friend, and find a new game. They like the pitch.

The influx of settlers in the 1850s transformed Minnesota from a sparsely populated territory of less than 10, 000 " white " settlers and a significantly larger native population , to a substantial population center of over 150, 000 predominantly European settlers . The city of Saint Paul expanded from less than 400 people in 1848 to over 2500 in 1852 and over 10, 000 in 1860 .

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She really liked getting a meal every day. But one day, when she sat down to her meal, she tasted something sour! 
Sarah wrinkled her nose. "Yuck," she said. "Meal is sour!" 
Mommy came over. She tasted the meal and said, "Oh no! How did this happen?" 
She looked around and saw a small bottle on the counter. "Sarah, did you put something in the meal?"
Sarah shook her head. "No, Mommy," she said. "I didn't do it." 
Mommy looked very concerned. She told Sarah to wait, and then she went outside. 
After a few minutes, Mommy came back, carrying something. She said, "I found out what happened. A bird flew in our window and it dropped this bottle in the meal. That's why it tasted sour!" 
Sarah looked at the bottle and smiled. She was very happy the mystery was solved. 
The End.

The Principe Amedeo class was a pair of ironclad warships built for the Italian Regia Marina ( Royal Navy ) in the 1870s and 1880s . They were the culmination of a major naval construction program designed to give Italy a powerful fleet of ironclads . The two ships , Principe Amedeo and Palestro , were the last Italian ironclads to feature sailing rigs and wooden hulls . They were armed with a battery of six 10-inch ( 254 mm ) guns and were capable of a speed in excess of 12 knots ( 22 km / h ; 14 mph ) . The ships had uneventful careers , spending much of it in Italy 's colonial empire . By the late 1880s , they were withdrawn from service and employed in secondary roles , first as headquarters ships for harbor defenses . Principe Amedeo was converted into a depot ship in 1895 and was discarded in 1910 , while Palestro was used as a training ship from 1894 to 1900 before being scrapped in 1902 – 04 .

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to solve a problem. The problem was that the rain was falling outside, and Tim wanted to play. He thought very hard about how to have fun even with the rain.
Tim had a great idea! He put on his boots and raincoat. He went outside and jumped in the puddles. The rain felt good on his face. He laughed and splashed in the water.
After a while, the rain stopped. Tim saw a big rainbow in the sky. He was happy that he found a way to play in the rain. Tim learned that even when there is a problem, he can solve it and still have fun.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. They saw a swing set, and Lily wanted to play on it. Her mom said, "Be gentle on the swing, Lily."
Lily got on the swing and started to swing back and forth. She saw a boy named Tom who was trying to complete a puzzle. The puzzle had big pieces, and Tom looked like he needed help. Lily wanted to help Tom, but she was on the swing.
Tom looked up and saw Lily on the swing. He asked, "Can you help me with my puzzle?" Lily stopped swinging and went to help Tom. They worked together and soon the puzzle was complete.
Lily and Tom were happy that they finished the puzzle. They both went back to the swing and played together. Lily remembered to be gentle on the swing, just like her mom said.

Once upon a time, there was a smooth rock. It lived in a group with other rocks. They all liked to play in the sun.
One day, a little boy came. He saw the smooth rock and said, "Hi, rock! Can you read?" The smooth rock did not say anything, but the little boy took it home.
At home, the little boy read a book to the smooth rock. The smooth rock liked the story. It felt happy to listen to the little boy.
The next day, the little boy took the smooth rock back to its group. The smooth rock told the other rocks about the story. They all wanted to hear it too. So, the little boy read the story to the group of rocks. They all had fun together.

One day, a little girl named Sally went outside to play. She liked to skip and say words out loud. She was a very happy girl, but today she felt a little serious. Sally saw her friend Timmy sitting under a tree. Timmy looked sad, so she skipped over to him.
"Hi Timmy, why are you sad?" asked Sally. Timmy looked up and said, "I lost my ball. I can't find it anywhere." Sally wanted to help Timmy find his ball, so they both started to look for it. They looked behind the tree, under the bushes, and even in the sandbox.
As they were looking, a big, mean dog came into the park. The dog saw Sally and Timmy and started to run towards them. Sally and Timmy were scared and tried to run away. They ran as fast as they could, but the big, mean dog caught up to them. The dog took Timmy's ball and ran away.
Sally and Timmy were very sad. They didn't find the ball and the big, mean dog took it away. They walked back to the tree and sat down, feeling sad about their bad day.

Throughout the 19th and 20th centuries , horses were harvested from the feral herds and used as riding and stock horses , as well as being used for their meat , hair and hides . Originally there were many herds that roamed land owned by the British Crown and the native Māori , but many were eradicated with the intensification of large scale farming and forestry operations combined with increased mechanization that decreased the need for stock horses . Kaimanawa horses today have the highest amount of genetic similarity with the Thoroughbred and other Thoroughbred cross breeds .

Once upon a time, there was a wise cat named Tom. Tom lived in a big house with his best friend, a little girl named Lily. They liked to play together every day at noon. One day, they were playing in the garden when a new cat named Max came to visit.
Tom said to Max, "Do you want to play with us?" Max nodded and said, "Yes, I would like that." So, Tom, Lily, and Max played together until they were all very tired. They had so much fun!
Then, something unexpected happened. Max offered Tom and Lily a big, shiny toy. But when they tried to play with it, the toy broke into many pieces! Max felt very sad and said, "I'm sorry, I didn't know it would break." Tom and Lily smiled and said, "That's okay, Max. We can still play together without the toy." And they all played happily ever after.

Lily liked to watch cartoons on TV. She liked the funny animals and the songs. She did not like to share the TV with her brother Ben. Ben liked to watch other shows. He liked the cars and the robots.
One day, Lily and Ben were home with their mom. Mom said they could watch TV for a little while, but they had to take turns. Lily went first. She chose her favorite cartoon. She laughed and clapped. Ben waited patiently. He played with his toys.
When Lily's cartoon was over, Ben said, "My turn now, Lily. Please give me the remote." Lily did not want to give him the remote. She wanted to watch another cartoon. She said, "No, Ben. I want to watch more cartoons. Go away!" She held the remote tightly.
Ben felt sad and angry. He said, "That's not fair, Lily. You had your turn. You have to share. Mom said so." Lily did not listen. She said, "Shut up, Ben. I don't care what mom said. I don't care what you want. I only care about me and my cartoons." She turned up the volume.
Mom heard the noise. She came to the living room. She saw Lily and Ben fighting over the remote. She saw Lily being rude and selfish. She saw Ben being humble and polite. She was very upset. She said, "Lily, how could you be so mean to your brother? You should be ashamed of yourself. You have to learn to share and be kind. You are not the only one who likes to watch TV. You have to respect others. Give me the remote right now. You are in big trouble, young lady. You are not watching any more cartoons today. You are going to your room. And you are going to apologize to Ben."
Lily realized she had made a big mistake. She felt sorry and scared. She cried and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, Ben. I was wrong. I was selfish. Please forgive me. Please let me watch cartoons." But it was too late. Mom took the remote and turned off the TV. She took Lily by the hand and led her to her room. She said, "No, Lily. You have to face the consequences of your actions. You have to learn your lesson. Maybe next time you will be more humble and generous. Maybe next time you will think of others before yourself."
The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Being humble is better than being selfish. Respect others and they will respect you.

Following the storm , the Mexican government sent food , water , and housing supplies to affected families in Oaxaca . Less than a week after Olaf moved through southern Mexico , Hurricane Pauline struck the same region with much stronger winds . Pauline caused heavier rainfall and more damage , killing at least 250 people . Some regions received 10 days of heavy rainfall .

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is brown and fluffy. It has a long tail and a wet nose.
"Can we touch the dog?" Lily asks Tom.
"I don't know. Maybe we should ask the owner first," Tom says.
They look around and see a man sitting on a bench. He is reading a book. He has a leash in his hand. The leash is attached to the dog.
"Excuse me, sir. Can we touch your dog?" Lily says.
The man looks up and smiles. He sees Lily and Tom. They are cute and polite.
"Sure, you can touch my dog. His name is Rover. He is very friendly and loves children," the man says.
Lily and Tom walk towards the dog. They reach out their hands and touch his fur. It is soft and warm. The dog wags his tail and licks their faces. Lily and Tom giggle.
"Hello, Rover. You are a nice dog," Lily says.
"You are a good boy," Tom says.
They pet the dog and play with him. They throw a ball and he fetches it. They rub his belly and he rolls over. They have fun.
But then, they smell something smelly. It is coming from the dog. They pinch their noses and make a face.
"Yuck! What is that smell?" Lily says.
"I think he rolled in something bad," Tom says.
They look at the dog and see some dirt and grass on his fur. They also see some poop.
"Ew! He rolled in poop!" Lily says.
"That's gross!" Tom says.
They run away from the dog and back to the man. They tell him what happened.
"Oh, no! Rover, you naughty dog! You need a bath!" the man says.
He apologizes to Lily and Tom. He says he will take the dog home and clean him. He thanks them for playing with him.
Lily and Tom say goodbye to the man and the dog. They are still friends. They are not mad at the dog. They know he did not mean to be smelly. They hope to see him again. But next time, they hope he will be clean.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion. The lion was rude to other animals. He would growl and scare them away. The animals did not like the lion.
One day, a little bird came to the lion. The bird was lost and scared. The lion wanted to protect the bird. This was unexpected, because the lion was always rude.
The other animals saw the lion being nice. They were surprised. The lion learned that being kind was better than being rude. From that day on, the lion changed and was nice to everyone. The animals became friends with the lion, and they all lived happily together.

Once upon a time, there was a mysterious big book called a dictionary. It lived in a small house with a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play games with his friends.
One day, Tim and his friends decided to play a game. The winner would get the dictionary. They all played very hard. Tim tried his best to win the game.
In the end, Tim won the game! His friends said, "Wow, Tim! You won! You get the dictionary!" Tim was very happy. He took the mysterious dictionary home and shared it with his friends. They all learned new words together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a broken toy. She wanted to fix it but she did not know how. Sue was sad.
One day, Sue found a map in her room. The map showed her where to find a magic man who could fix her broken toy. Sue was happy and wanted to go find the magic man. She put on her shoes and went outside.
Sue followed the map until she found the magic man. The magic man fixed her broken toy with a wave of his hand. Sue was very happy. She thanked the magic man and went back home. Now, Sue could own her new fixed toy and play with it all day.

One hot day, a cat and a dog were playing outside. They liked to jump and run. This was their exercise. They were very happy.
A bird saw them and wanted to play too. The bird flew down and said, "I want to do exercise with you!" The cat and the dog were surprised but happy. They all played together, running and jumping.
Then, the bird had an idea. "I can offer you something fun!" The bird took the cat and dog to a big tree. The bird showed them how to climb the tree. The cat and the dog did not know they could do this. They were so excited! Now, they had a new way to play and exercise together.

Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there lived a fast rabbit. The rabbit liked to run and play all day with his friends. They would jump, hop, and race each other under the tall trees.
One hot day, the fast rabbit was very tired from playing. He found a nice, cool spot under a big tree. He decided to rest there for a while. As he lay down, he looked up at the sky and saw the pretty birds flying above him.
After a short rest, the fast rabbit felt much better. He jumped up and ran to find his friends. They all played together again, happy and full of energy. And when they were tired, they knew they could always find a nice spot in the jungle to rest.

Once upon a time, there was a noisy bell that loved to ring. It lived in a big room with a pretty curtain. The bell was very happy when it rang, and everyone could hear it.
One day, the bell was ringing, and the pretty curtain started to move. The noisy bell was surprised. It had never seen the curtain move before. Behind the curtain, there was a little mouse. The mouse was afraid of the noisy bell.
The bell did not want to scare the little mouse. So, it stopped ringing. The mouse came out from behind the curtain and became friends with the bell. They played together every day. The noisy bell learned to ring softly, so it would not scare its new friend. And they all lived happily ever after.

The band first became involved with Sarajevo in 1993 on their Zoo TV Tour ; approached by aid worker Bill Carter about bringing attention to the Siege of Sarajevo , the band conducted nightly satellite transmissions with Bosnians during their shows . These link-ups were the subject of criticism from journalists for mixing entertainment with human tragedy . Although the war made it impractical for U2 to visit Sarajevo at the time , they vowed to eventually play a concert in the city . After the conflict ended in November 1995 , they made arrangements to visit Sarajevo , and with help from United Nations ambassadors and peacekeeping troops , they scheduled and played the concert in 1997 .

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful rose that lived in a big garden. The rose was very happy because it was surrounded by many friends like the sun, the grass, and the birds that came to visit.
One day, a little girl named Lily came to the garden. She saw the beautiful rose and said, "Hello, pretty rose! I am going on a trip and I want to take you with me. Will you come?" The rose nodded its head, and Lily carefully picked it up.
Lily took the rose home and started to pack her bag. She put her clothes, her toys, and her snacks inside. Then, she made a special spot for the rose so it would be safe on the trip. They were both very excited to go on their adventure together.

One day, a little girl named Sue found a glove on the ground. She thought it was an incredible glove. It was red and shiny. Sue put the glove on her hand and went to show her mom.
On her way, she saw a cat in a tree. The cat was stuck and could not get down. Sue sighed, feeling sad for the cat. She wanted to help it. Sue lifted her hand with the glove and, suddenly, the cat floated down from the tree. It was safe!
Sue knew the incredible glove had magic. She was so happy she could help the cat. She ran to her mom to tell her the story. But when she showed her mom the glove, it was just a normal glove. Sue was confused, but she knew she had done something amazing.

Anna and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park, draw pictures and read books. One day, they found a big letter on the ground. It was red and shiny and had a star on it.
"Wow, what an amazing letter!" Anna said. "I wonder what it says."
"Let's open it and see," Ben said. He tore the letter and looked inside. There was a piece of paper with some words on it.
"What does it say?" Anna asked.
Ben tried to read the words, but they were too hard. He only knew some of them. He read: "This is a magic letter. If you say the word 'disappear', you will go to a wonderful place. But be careful, you can only come back if you say the word 'appear'."
"Wow, that sounds fun!" Anna said. "Let's try it. Maybe we will go to a place with candy and toys and animals."
"OK, but we have to remember the word 'appear'," Ben said. "Or we will be stuck there forever."
They held hands and said together: "Disappear!"
Suddenly, everything went dark. They felt a strange wind and heard a loud noise. They opened their eyes and saw a new place. It was not wonderful at all. It was scary and ugly and cold. There were no candy and toys and animals. There were only rocks and thorns and monsters.
"Help!" Anna cried. "This is a bad place. I want to go home."
"Me too," Ben said. "Let's say the word 'appear' and go back."
They held hands and said together: "Appear!"
But nothing happened. They said it again and again, but nothing changed. They were still in the bad place. They looked at the piece of paper, but it was gone. They had lost it when they tore the letter.
They realized they had made a big mistake. They had opened a bad letter that lied to them. They had said a bad word that trapped them. They had forgotten a good word that could save them.
They started to cry. They wished they had never found the letter. They wished they had never said 'disappear'. They wished they could see their home and their parents and their friends again.
But they couldn't. They were stuck in the bad place forever. The end.

The wind comes in from the window. It blows the glitter all over the kitchen. It makes a big mess. Lila and Ben are scared. They say, "Uh-oh, Mommy will be mad!"
Mommy comes in and sees the glitter. She is not mad. She smiles and says, "Wow, what a beautiful soup you made! It looks like magic!" She hugs Lila and Ben and says, "But next time, please be careful with the fragile jar. It was a gift from Grandma."
Lila and Ben say, "Sorry, Mommy. We love you and Grandma." They help Mommy clean up the glitter. They still like to play in the kitchen. But they do not touch the fragile jar anymore. They stir and stir and stir their water and toys. They say, "Mmm, yummy soup!"

Anna and Ben like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is a big crystal. The crystal is shiny and pretty. It has many colors inside. Anna and Ben like to hold it and look at it.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and look for bugs. They found a big hole under a tree. They wondered what lived inside.
"Maybe it is a rabbit," said Lily.
"Or a mouse," said Tom.
They decided to peek inside the hole. They saw a small, furry animal with a long nose and tiny eyes. It was a mole.
"Hello, mole," said Lily. "Do you want to play with us?"
The mole was scared. He did not like loud noises or bright light. He wanted to hide in his hole.
"Go away, go away," he said. "You are too noisy and too bright. Leave me alone."
Lily and Tom felt sad. They did not want to hurt the mole. They wanted to be friends.
"Sorry, mole," said Tom. "We did not know you were shy. We will be quiet and gentle."
They backed away from the hole. They saw some flowers and leaves nearby. They picked some and made a wreath. They put it near the hole as a gift for the mole.
"Look, mole," said Lily. "We made this for you. It is pretty and smells nice. We hope you like it."
The mole was curious. He sniffed the wreath. He felt the soft petals and the green stems. He liked it. He felt a warm feeling in his heart.
"Thank you, thank you," he said. "You are kind and sweet. I like your gift. I want to be your friend."
He came out of his hole. He smiled at Lily and Tom. They smiled back. They clapped their hands. They were happy.
They played together in the garden. They learned about each other. They had fun.
The moral of the story is: Be respectful and gentle to others who are different from you. You might make a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a big whale. The whale was very big and strong, but it had a fragile heart. It lived in the deep blue sea and liked to play with its friends, the fish.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They run, jump, slide and swing. They have fun.

The inclusive use of the term Wicca — referring to the entirety of Pagan Witchcraft religion — has been traced to Britain in the early 1960s , when it was used by various groups and publicised through use in adverts , magazines , and other literary sources . It was later adopted by figures like Alex Sanders and Gavin and Yvonne Frost , who took it to the United States . There , practitioners of British Traditional Wicca adopted it exclusively for themselves as a means to differentiate their practices from those of other Pagan Witches . This exclusive meaning was countered by its popularisation as a generic term by prolific authors such as Raymond Buckland , Scott Cunningham and Silver RavenWolf . As it entered popular culture , it gained an increasingly eclectic character in its usage . During the 1990s , some attempted to distance themselves from it by utilising the term Traditional Witchcraft .

Once upon a time, there was a red ball. It was a very pretty ball. The red ball had a friend who was a black cat. They liked to play together every day. They played in the sun and had lots of fun.

Sam and Ben are brothers. They like to play on the farm with the animals. One day, they see a big cow in the field. The cow is black and white and has a bell around her neck.
"Look, a cow!" Sam says. "Can we pet her?"
Ben nods. "Yes, let's go. Maybe she will give us some milk."
They run to the cow and try to touch her. But the cow does not like it. She moos loudly and shakes her head. She kicks her legs and runs away.
"Hey, come back!" Ben shouts. "We just want to be your friends."
But the cow does not listen. She runs to the fence and jumps over it. She runs to the road, where there are many cars and trucks.
"Oh no!" Sam says. "The cow is in danger. She might get hit by a car. We need to help her."
They run after the cow, but they are too slow. The cow is faster and runs across the road. The cars and trucks honk and brake. The drivers are angry and scared.
"Stop, cow, stop!" Sam and Ben yell. "You are not safe there. Come back to the farm."
But the cow does not stop. She runs to the woods, where there are many trees and animals. She thinks she is free and happy.
Sam and Ben are sad and worried. They do not know what to do. They need to find the cow and bring her back. They need to tell their dad what happened. They hope the cow is okay.
They look around and see a man on a bike. He is wearing a helmet and a bright vest. He is alert and smart. He sees the cow and the boys.
"Hey, kids, what are you doing here?" he asks. "Do you know that cow?"
Sam and Ben nod. "Yes, she is from our farm. She ran away and we followed her. But we can't catch her. She is too fast and wild."
The man smiles. "Don't worry, I can help you. I have a rope and a whistle. I can call the cow and tie her to my bike. Then we can take her back to your farm. Do you want to come with me?"
Sam and Ben smile. "Yes, please. Thank you, mister. You are very kind and brave."
They get on the bike with the man. He blows his whistle and waves his rope. The cow hears him and stops. She is curious and tired. She comes closer and lets him tie her to the bike.
"Good girl, cow," the man says. "You are safe now. Let's go home."
They ride back to the farm. The cow moos softly and follows the bike. Sam and Ben are happy and relieved. They hug the cow and the man.
"Thank you, thank you, thank you," they say. "You saved the cow and us. You are our hero."
The man laughs. "You're welcome, kids. You are very brave and caring. You love the cow and the farm. You are good friends."
They reach the farm and see their dad. He is surprised and glad. He sees the cow and the man and the boys.
"What happened?" he asks. "Where did you go? How did you find the cow?"
Sam and Ben tell him everything. They tell him how the cow ran away and how the man helped them. They tell him how they learned a lesson.
"We are sorry, dad," they say. "We did not mean to scare the cow. We just wanted to pet her. But we learned that we need to be gentle and respectful with the animals. We need to listen to them and watch them. We need to keep them safe and happy."
Dad smiles and hugs them. "I'm proud of you, boys. You did the right thing. You helped the cow and the man. You are good sons."
He thanks the man and gives him some milk and cheese. He invites him to stay for dinner. He is grateful and friendly.
They all go inside the house. They eat and talk and laugh. They are a big family. The cow is in the barn. She is calm and warm. She has a new friend. She is a happy cow.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a happy boy who liked to play with his toys. One day, Tim saw a pretty mirror on the wall. He wanted to look at himself, but he was too small to see. He tried to jump, but he could not manage to see his face.
Tim was sad that he could not see himself in the mirror. He thought of a plan to fix the problem. Tim went to his room and found his big toy box. He pushed the box across the floor to the mirror. It was hard work, but Tim did not give up.
Finally, Tim managed to get the toy box close to the mirror. He climbed on top of the box and looked into the mirror. Tim saw his happy face and smiled. He was proud of himself for solving the problem. From that day on, Tim knew that he could do anything if he tried his best.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big, unusual hat that she wore every day. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a boy named Tim and his dog, Spot. Tim loved to eat sausages for breakfast. One day, Tim's mom made a big plate of sausages for him. Tim was very happy.
"Mom, can I have a sausage, please?" Tim requested. His mom gave him a sausage, and he ate it quickly. Spot, the dog, saw Tim eating the sausage and wanted one too. Spot looked at Tim with big, sad eyes.
"Okay, Spot. You can have one too," said Tim. He gave Spot a sausage, but Spot was a little bit stupid. Instead of eating the sausage, Spot took it outside and buried it in the ground. Tim laughed and said, "Silly Spot, that's not what you do with a sausage!"
The next day, Tim and Spot went outside to play. They saw that the sausage Spot buried had started to grow into a sausage tree! Tim and Spot couldn't believe their eyes. From that day on, they had all the sausages they could ever want.
And so, Tim and Spot lived happily ever after, eating sausages from their very own sausage tree.

Otra Nota ( English : Another Note ) is the debut album by American singer Marc Anthony that was released on January 26 , 1993 , by RMM Records . Produced by Sergio George , it was the first album by Anthony to record in salsa after starting his career as a freestyle musician . Recording of the album began after Anthony asked RMM president Ralph Mercado to record Juan Gabriel 's " Hasta Que Te Conocí " in salsa after hearing it on the radio during a taxi ride . Recorded on a low budget , the album peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Tropical Albums chart and reached No. 30 on the Billboard Top Latin Albums chart .
