East Carolina started their series on their 41 – yard line . A substitution infraction on ECU and an incomplete pass forced ECU to punt the ball away . On the Broncos ' fourth drive of the second quarter , the team began with three complete passes for 18 yards . On the fourth play , however , BSU 's Titus Young fumbled the ball away . Pirates ' defender Jay Ross recovered the fumble , and ECU had another chance on offense before the end of the first half . East Carolina ran five plays for 38 yards . With the clock running down , ECU elected to kick a field goal . The kick was good , and made the score 31 – 14 ECU . Boise State had one final chance on offense , and Boise Quarterback Taylor Tharp went two-for-four , but ran out of time before coming into field goal range .

One day, a boy named Tim went to a tidy nation. In this nation, everyone liked to do fun things. Tim saw a girl named Sue. Sue was playing with her toys. Tim wanted to play with Sue.
"Hi Sue, can I play with you?" Tim asked. Sue said, "Yes, you can play with me. Let's do something fun!" They played together and had a great time.
Suddenly, a big wind came and made everything messy. Tim and Sue were surprised. They did not like the messy nation. So, they decided to do something about it. They worked together to make the nation tidy again. Everyone was happy and thanked Tim and Sue for their help.

Not included in the official fatalities number were deaths that were recorded as pneumonia . Workers alleged that this diagnosis was a cover for death from carbon monoxide poisoning , brought on by the use of gasoline-fueled vehicles in the diversion tunnels , and a classification used by Six Companies to avoid paying compensation claims . The site 's diversion tunnels frequently reached 140 ° F ( 60 ° C ) , enveloped in thick plumes of vehicle exhaust gases . A total of 42 workers were recorded as having died from pneumonia ; none were listed as having died from carbon monoxide poisoning . No deaths of non-workers from pneumonia were recorded in Boulder City during the construction period .

Once there was a white home with a big problem. At night, lots of animals would attach to the house and make noise. This made the family inside the home very sad.
One day, the family decided to do something. They built a fence around the house to keep all the animals away. But the family was still not sure if that was enough.
The next night, the family watched through the window, worried. As the animals tried to attach to the fence, the family saw something exciting. A big white cat appeared and scared away all the animals.
The family and the cat became friends, and the animals never came back. The white cat became part of the family and made their home safe. The family was happy to have their white home back.

Once upon a time, there was a young dog named Hope. Hope liked to play outside in the sun. She loved to roll in the grass and run fast.
One day, Hope saw a little bird on the grass. The bird was sad because it could not fly. Hope wanted to help the bird. She had a big heart.
Hope and the bird became friends. They played in the grass every day. Soon, the bird learned to fly. Hope was very happy for her friend. They played together in the sun and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was an adventurous musician. He played a big drum. He liked to go to new places. One day, he went to a town far away. The people in the town loved his drum. They danced and sang.
But, the musician had a big sack. He put things in the sack. He took the things from the town. The people did not like this. They said, "Stop! You cannot take our things!"
The musician felt bad. He put the things back. He played his drum again. The people danced and sang. They were happy. The musician learned that it is not nice to take things from others.

Once upon a time, there was a young man who wanted to go on an adventure. He took his coat, his shoes and his hat, and he marched off down the street. He took the long path, going around corners and down roads until he came upon a big field.
He looked around and saw that there were many other people, all of them marching in a line. He asked one of them, "What are you doing?"
The person replied, "We are in an order. We are all going the same way, marching together in the same steps."
The young man thought it looked fun and he wanted to join in. He got into line and started marching with the others. They all marched in the same direction and it was a pleasant journey.
Soon, the young man noticed that the others were a lot older than him. He felt a little out of place, but he kept marching with them anyway. As he got near the end of the field, he felt proud that he had walked the same path as them.
He made it to the side of the field and saw that everyone else had stopped. He had reached the end of their order. He waved goodbye to the others and smiled. In that moment, he was glad that he had joined the march.

Tom and Lily like to play ball in the park. They throw the ball to each other and catch it. Sometimes they miss and the ball rolls away. They run after it and laugh.
One day, a big boy comes to the park. He sees Tom and Lily playing ball. He wants to play too. He walks over to them and says, "Give me the ball. I can throw it better than you."

The big boy does not listen. He grabs the ball from Lily's hand. He says, "Watch this. I can throw the ball very high and far." He throws the ball with all his might. He makes a loud noise. He thinks he is very good.
But the ball does not go high and far. It goes low and near. It hits a tree and bounces back. It hits the big boy on the head. He falls down and cries.
Tom and Lily look at the ball and the big boy. They think he is very silly. They say, "That was a bad pitch. You are not good at throwing. You are good at falling." They pick up the ball and run away. They play ball in another part of the park. They are happy and have fun.

Tom and Lily liked to play in the park. They liked to run, jump, and swing. One day, they saw a big hill with rocks and dirt. They wanted to climb it and see what was on the other side.
They held hands and started to go up the hill. It was hard and steep. They had to be careful not to slip or fall. They felt anxious, but also excited. They wanted to reach the top.
When they got to the top, they saw a big drop. It was a cliff. They could not see the bottom. They could only see the sky and the birds. They were scared. They did not want to go near the edge.
They heard a loud noise. It was thunder. A storm was coming. They saw dark clouds and lightning. They heard the wind and the rain. They wanted to go back down the hill. They wanted to go home.
They turned around and ran. They did not look where they were going. They did not see the rock. Tom tripped and fell. He hit his head on the rock. He cried out in pain. He had a big bump. Lily saw blood. She was scared. She wanted to help Tom.
She ran to Tom and hugged him. She tried to make him feel better. She said, "It's okay, Tom. I'm here. We'll go home soon." She looked for help. She saw a man. He was a park ranger. He had a hat and a badge. He had a radio and a first aid kit. He heard Tom and Lily. He came to them.
He saw Tom's wound. He said, "Don't worry, kids. I'm here to help. I'll strike a bandage on your head, Tom. It will stop the bleeding and the pain. Then I'll take you both to your parents. They're waiting for you at the gate. They're anxious to see you."
He did what he said. He struck a bandage on Tom's head. He picked up Tom and Lily. He took them to his truck. He drove them to the gate. He found their parents. They were happy and relieved to see them. They thanked the park ranger. They hugged Tom and Lily. They said, "We're so glad you're safe. We love you."
Tom and Lily said, "We love you too. We're sorry we climbed the hill. We won't do it again. It was scary and dangerous. We learned our lesson."
They went home. They had hot chocolate and cookies. They told their parents what happened. They said, "We're lucky the park ranger was there. He was nice and helpful. He struck a bandage on Tom's head. He saved us."
Their parents said, "Yes, he did. He was a hero. You should thank him again. And you should be careful next time. Don't go near the cliff. It's not a place for kids. It's a place for birds."
Tom and Lily nodded. They agreed. They said, "We will. We promise." They smiled. They felt better. They cuddled with their parents. They watched a movie. They fell asleep. They dreamed of the park, the hill, the cliff, and the birds. But they did not dream of the storm, the rock, or the blood. They dreamed of the sun, the grass, and the flowers. They dreamed of happy things.

Frame Analysis : An Essay on the Organization of Experience ( 1974 ) is Goffman 's attempt to explain how conceptual frames – ways to organize experience – structure an individual 's perception of society . This book is thus about the organization of experience rather than the organization of society . A frame is a set of concepts and theoretical perspectives that organize experiences and guide the actions of individuals , groups and societies . Frame analysis , then , is the study of the organization of social experience . To illustrate the concept of the frame , Goffman gives the example of a picture frame : a person uses the frame ( which represents structure ) to hold together his picture ( which represents the content ) of what he is experiencing in his life .

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a man sitting on a bench. He had a wallet in his pocket. Tom had an idea.
"Let's steal his wallet!" he whispered to Lily. "We can buy candy and toys with his money."
Lily was scared. "No, Tom, that is bad. We can't take what is not ours. He will be sad and angry."
Tom did not listen. He was creative. He picked up a stick and threw it at a bird. The bird flew away, making a loud noise. The man looked up. Tom ran to the bench and grabbed the wallet. He ran back to Lily.
"Come on, let's go!" he said.
But Lily did not go. She stayed where she was. She saw the man looking for his wallet. He looked worried and sad. She felt sorry for him.
"Tom, give it back!" she said. "It is not yours. It is his. He needs it."
Tom did not want to give it back. He wanted to keep it. He opened the wallet and saw many papers and cards. He did not see any money.
"This is no good!" he said. "There is no money here. Only papers and cards. What can we do with them?"
Lily had an idea. She was creative too. She took the wallet from Tom and ran to the man. She gave him the wallet and said, "Sorry, mister. We found this on the ground. We thought it was yours."
The man was happy and surprised. He thanked Lily and smiled. He gave her a candy and a toy. He did not see Tom hiding behind a tree.
Lily ran back to Tom. She gave him the candy and the toy. She said, "See, Tom, it is better to be good than bad. You can't steal what is not yours. You can make people happy with your creativity."
Tom felt ashamed and sorry. He learned his lesson. He said, "You are right, Lily. I was wrong. I am sorry. Thank you for being my friend. Can we share the candy and the toy?"
Lily nodded and smiled. They hugged and played. They were happy. They were creative. They were good.

The entrance road was constructed from Military Road to the fort 's rear gates . Its path is largely followed by the modern Queen Elizabeth II walk , though the former road was slightly to the south . This walk links the conservation park 's visitor centre to the fort gates ; some of the old road can still be seen close to the gates . What was the muster ground is partly taken up by the caravan and camping park and a car park . It was levelled and filled in the 1950s for this use . What remains of this ground , north of the caravan park , was returned to its 1880s profile in 1993 funded by a Federal Government grant . In the 19th century , the muster ground was used for training of the Volunteer Military Force including artillery , who camped on the site . As designed the fort 's rear was protected with a wooden palisade or stockade . In 1881 a masonry wall was added , greatly strengthening defence . Most of the stockade was reconstructed in the 1970s ; some of the original wooden structure is visible in the fort 's north .

Anna was a big sister to a little infant named Ben. Ben liked to make noises and repeat what Anna said. Sometimes Anna thought this was funny, but sometimes she got annoyed.
One day, Anna was playing with her dolls and Ben was in his crib. Ben saw Anna and wanted to play too. He said, "Anna, Anna, play with me!"
Anna ignored him and kept playing. Ben said again, "Anna, Anna, play with me!" He was persistent and did not give up.
Anna got angry and said, "Ben, stop it! You are too little to play with dolls. Go to sleep!"
Ben felt sad and cried. He did not understand why Anna did not want to play with him. He only wanted to be with her.
Mom heard Ben crying and came to see what was wrong. She saw Anna playing with her dolls and Ben in his crib. She said, "Anna, why are you not playing with your brother? He loves you and wants to learn from you."
Anna said, "But Mom, he is annoying. He always repeats what I say and he is too little to play with dolls."
Mom said, "Anna, repeating is how infants learn to talk. He is trying to copy you because you are his big sister and he admires you. He is not too little to play with dolls. He can play with you in his own way. You should be kind and patient with him. He is your family and he needs your love."
Anna felt sorry and realized she was wrong. She said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry, Ben. I love you and I want to play with you. Come, let me show you my dolls."
Ben smiled and stopped crying. He said, "Anna, Anna, play with me!"
Anna hugged him and said, "Yes, Ben, let's play together."
Mom smiled and said, "That's better. I'm proud of you, Anna. You are a good big sister."
The moral of the story is: Be kind and patient with your younger siblings. They look up to you and want to learn from you. You can have fun and teach them at the same time.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly king. He lived in a big castle. The king had a shiny crown. He liked to wear it every day. The king was very kind to all the people in his land.
One day, the king wanted to cook for everyone. He put on an apron and went to the kitchen. He cooked a big pot of soup. The soup was very yummy. The king was happy to make food for his people.
The people came to the castle to eat the soup. They saw the elderly king with his shiny crown. They said, "Thank you, King, for the yummy soup!" The king smiled and said, "You are welcome!" Everyone was happy and full.

One day, a little cat named Fluffy felt a bit nervous. She had a small rip in her favorite toy, Mr. Mouse. Fluffy didn't know what to do. She was scared that her toy would break more.
Fluffy went to her friend, a wise old dog named Buddy. "Buddy," she said, "my toy has a rip. What should I do?" Buddy thought for a moment and then said, "I recommend you ask your human to fix it with a stitch."
Fluffy went to her human and showed her the rip in Mr. Mouse. Her human smiled and said, "Don't worry, Fluffy. I can fix this with a stitch." Fluffy felt happy and less nervous.
Her human fixed Mr. Mouse with a stitch, and Fluffy was very thankful. She played with Mr. Mouse all day long, and they had lots of fun together. From that day on, Fluffy knew that if she ever had a problem, her friends would help her.

Once upon a time, there was a green bee. The bee lived in a big tree. The bee loved to fly around the tree and make sweet honey.
One sunny day, the green bee saw a big stick. The bee wanted to play with the stick. The bee pushed the stick with its tiny legs. The stick began to break.
The green bee was happy. It danced and buzzed around the broken stick. Then, the bee went back to its tree to make more honey. The green bee lived happily ever after.

One day, a smelly potato lived in a garden. The potato was sad. It did not like being smelly. Other potatoes did not want to play with it. The smelly potato would often suffer alone.
One day, a little girl came to the garden. She saw the smelly potato and said, "Why are you sad, potato?" The potato told the girl, "I am smelly, and no one wants to play with me." The little girl smiled and said, "I will play with you!"
The little girl took the smelly potato home. She washed the potato and made it clean. The smelly potato was not smelly anymore! It was a happy potato now. The other potatoes in the garden saw this and wanted to be friends too. The potato had many friends and did not suffer anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a clever clown. He had a big red nose and funny clothes. He liked to make people laugh and smile.
One day, the clever clown went to a party. There were many kids at the party. They played games, ate cake, and had lots of fun. The clever clown made them laugh by making funny faces and doing silly dances.
Suddenly, a little girl lost her toy. She was very sad. The clever clown saw her and wanted to help. He shouted, "I will find your toy!" He looked everywhere and found the toy under a table. The little girl was so happy. Everyone clapped for the clever clown, and they all had a great time at the party.

One day, a clever cat named Zip went to play outside. Zip liked to jump and run in the sun. Zip saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. So, Zip climbed the tree very fast.
When Zip was high in the tree, he saw a bird. The bird said, "Hi, I am Bill. Do you want to play with me?" Zip said, "Yes, I want to play with you. But I am a cat, and I cannot fly." Bill the bird had an idea. "I will call my friend, the bug. The bug can help you fly."
Bill called the bug, and the bug came to help. The bug was strong and could carry Zip. Zip held on to the bug, and they flew in the sky. Zip, Bill, and the bug had a fun day playing together. The clever cat, Zip, was happy he made new friends.

Lily and Ben are playing in the pool. They like to splash and swim and have fun. Lily sees a white cloth at the bottom of the pool. She wants to get it.
"Look, Ben, a white cloth!" she says. "I want to dive and get it. Can you dive too?"
Ben nods. He likes to dive. He can hold his breath for a long time. He follows Lily as she dives into the water. They swim to the white cloth.
Lily reaches the cloth first. She grabs it and swims up. Ben swims up too. They both come out of the water and smile.
"Wow, you did it, Lily!" Ben says. "You are a good diver. What is the white cloth?"
Lily looks at the cloth. It is soft and fluffy. It has a picture of a duck on it. She remembers. It is her towel. She left it on the edge of the pool.
"It is my towel, Ben," she says. "I forgot it here. It is wet now. But it is still my towel. I like it. Do you want to share it?"
Ben nods. He likes Lily. He likes to share. They wrap the towel around them and hug. They are happy. They are friends.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. He took a big red apple with him. Tim wanted to eat his apple under a tree. He felt safe there.
Tim saw a girl named Sue. She was crying. "Why are you sad?" Tim asked. "My apple is bad. It is spoiled," Sue said. Tim wanted to help her. He gave her his big red apple.
Sue was happy now. She said, "Thank you, Tim!" They played together in the park. They had a lot of fun.
Then, something strange happened. A big wind came and blew a lot of apples from the tree. Now, Tim and Sue had many apples to eat. They laughed and shared the apples with their friends. The spoiled apple was not so bad after all.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy had a long garden with many flowers. She loved to play with her friends in the garden. One day, she saw a new flower in her garden. It was very pretty. Amy wanted to show her friends the new flower.
Amy asked the flower, "Can I please show you to my friends?" The flower said, "Yes, please take me to your friends." Amy was so happy. She picked up the flower and went to find her friends.
Amy showed the flower to her friends. They all thought it was very pretty. But then, something unexpected happened. The flower started to talk! It said, "Thank you for bringing me to your friends, Amy. Now, I can play with you all too!" Amy and her friends were very surprised. They did not know flowers could talk. But they were happy to have a new friend. So, they all played together in the long garden with the talking flower.

One day, a little boy named Tim had a big box of toys. He wanted to sort his toys into two groups. He had his expensive toys and his cheap toys. Tim loved his expensive toys more because they were special.
Tim found a hammer in the box. He thought it was an expensive toy because it looked very nice. He put the hammer with the expensive toys. But he didn't know that the hammer was not a toy. It was a real hammer that his dad had left in the box by mistake.
One day, Tim wanted to play with his expensive toys. He picked up the hammer and hit his other toys with it. The toys broke! Tim was very sad. He didn't know that the hammer was not a toy. His dad came and saw the broken toys. He told Tim that the hammer was not a toy and should not be in the toy box. Tim learned to be more careful when sorting his toys.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park. She saw a clean, blue pond with ducks swimming in it. Lily wanted to play with the ducks, so she went closer to the water.
Lily saw a big, yellow duck stuck in some mud. The duck said, "Help me, please!" Lily wanted to help the duck, so she tried to pull it out. She pulled and pulled, but the duck was still stuck.
Then, Lily had an idea. She found a long stick and used it to push the mud away from the duck. With one big push, Lily was able to release the duck from the mud. The duck was so happy and said, "Thank you, Lily!"
Lily and the duck played together in the clean pond all day. The duck was very thankful to have a new friend like Lily. And Lily was happy she could help the duck and make a new friend.

Anna and Ben wanted to decorate the big tree in the garden. They had many shiny things to hang on the branches. They also had a star for the top.
"Look, Anna, I found a tap!" Ben said. He pointed to a metal thing on the wall. "We can use it to make water for the tree."
Anna nodded. She liked water. She ran to the tap and turned it. But nothing came out. She turned it harder. Still nothing.
"Maybe the tap is broken," Ben said. He tried to turn it too. But he only made a loud noise.
"Shh, Ben, you will wake up Grandpa!" Anna said. She looked at the house. Grandpa was sleeping on the sofa. He was very old and wise. He knew many things.
They tiptoed to the house and opened the door. They saw Grandpa snoring softly. They also saw a big jug of water on the table.
"Let's take the water for the tree," Anna whispered. She picked up the jug and carried it outside. Ben followed her with the shiny things.
They poured the water on the tree and hung the shiny things on the branches. They also put the star on the top. The tree looked very pretty.
Grandpa woke up and saw them. He smiled and came outside.
"What a lovely tree!" he said. "You did a good job, Anna and Ben. You are very clever and kind."
Anna and Ben hugged Grandpa. They were happy. They liked to decorate the tree. They also liked to make Grandpa proud.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful kitten named Kitty. Kitty liked to play outside in the sun. One day, it started to rain. Kitty did not like the rain.

Soon, the rain stopped, and the sun came out again. Kitty and the tree were very happy. They played together all day long, and Kitty stayed cheerful and dry.

Once upon a time, there was a little rat. The rat lived in a big house with a nice family. The rat was happy but sometimes he would complain. He wanted to play with the family, but they did not like rats.

The rat found a ball and rolled it to the family. The little girl saw the ball and laughed. She said, "Look, the rat wants to play!" The family was surprised, but they started to play with the rat. They were not ashamed anymore, and the rat never complained again. They all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly comet. The comet liked to fly through the sky at night. It would make big loops and shine bright for everyone to see.
One day, the comet decided to step down from the sky to visit the Earth. It wanted to make friends and play with the kids. So, it waited until nighttime and then gently stepped down to the ground.
When the kids saw the jolly comet, they were so happy. They played games and danced with it all night long. The comet was very glad it stepped down to Earth. After the fun night, it stepped back into the sky, and the kids waved goodbye. They knew the jolly comet would always be there, shining bright in the night sky.

Once upon a time, there was a unique little cat. The cat loved to play with a big, round melon. Every day, the cat would push the melon around the yard.

When the cat woke up, it saw a little bird. The bird also liked the melon. The cat and the bird became friends. Together, they played with the melon and had lots of fun.

One day, a boy named Tim and his mom went to the store. They wanted to buy a film to watch at home. Tim saw a film with a big red dog on it. He liked dogs, so he took the film to his mom.
"Mom, can we get this film?" Tim asked. His mom looked at the film and said, "Yes, we can watch it tonight."
At home, Tim and his mom put the film in the TV. But, when they watched it, the big red dog was not there. Instead, there was a pink cat. They were surprised and embarrassed. They did not know what to do.

One day, a girl named Lucy wanted to print a big picture of her dog. She wanted to give it to her mom as a gift. She went to her dad and said, "Dad, can you help me print the picture?"
Her dad said, "Of course, Lucy! Let's go to the computer and print it." They printed the picture, but it was hidden behind some papers on the desk. Lucy looked and looked, but she could not find it. She felt sad and asked her dad, "Where is the picture? I can't see it."
Her dad looked around and saw the picture hidden behind the papers. He said, "Here it is, Lucy! It was hiding!" Lucy felt happy and said, "Thank you, Dad!" Then, they found some wrap to put around the picture. They wrapped it up and put a pretty bow on it.
Now, Lucy was ready to give the gift to her mom. She went to her mom and said, "Mom, I have a surprise for you!" Her mom opened the wrap and saw the big picture of their dog. She smiled and said, "I love it, Lucy! Thank you so much!" Lucy felt proud and happy that her mom liked her gift.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to dress up like a superhero. He had a big, heavy cape that he wore when he played. It made him feel strong and brave.

Once upon a time, there was a small mouse named Mimi. Mimi lived in a tiny house in a big field. She had many friends, like birds, bugs, and other mice. One day, Mimi decided to invite all her friends to a fun party at her house.

Large flocks typical of this species can be beneficial to agriculture by controlling invertebrate pests ; however , starlings can also be pests themselves when they feed on fruit and sprouting crops . Common starlings may also be a nuisance through the noise and mess caused by their large urban roosts . Introduced populations in particular have been subjected to a range of controls , including culling , but these have had limited success except in preventing the colonisation of Western Australia . The species has declined in numbers in parts of northern and western Europe since the 1980s due to fewer grassland invertebrates being available as food for growing chicks . Despite this , its huge global population is not thought to be declining significantly , so the common starling is classified as being of least concern by the International Union for Conservation of Nature .

The quick collapse of the Liao led to more negotiations between the Song and the Jin . Jurchen military success and their effective control over the Sixteen Prefectures gave them more leverage . Aguda grew increasingly frustrated as he realized that despite their military failures the Song still intended to seize most of the prefectures . In the spring of 1123 the two sides finally set the terms of the first Song – Jin treaty . Only seven prefectures ( including Yanjing ) would be returned to the Song , and the Song would pay an annual indemnity of 300, 000 packs of silk and 200, 000 taels of silver to the Jin , as well as a one-time payment of one million strings of copper coins to compensate the Jurchens for the tax revenue they would have earned had they not returned the prefectures . In May 1123 Tong Guan and the Song armies entered the looted Yanjing .

A collected edition of Wilde 's works , published in 1908 and edited by Robert Ross , helped to restore his reputation as an author . Alexander presented another revival of The Importance at the St James 's in 1909 , when he and Aynesworth reprised their original roles ; the revival ran for 316 performances . Max Beerbohm said that the play was sure to become a classic of the English repertory , and that its humour was as fresh then as when it had been written , adding that the actors had " worn as well as the play " .

Hurricane Diana struck eastern Mexico and managed to hold together , remaining a tropical depression as it entered the eastern Pacific Ocean late on August 8 . Although Tropical Depression Diana entered the eastern Pacific , the National Hurricane Center did not re-classify the system . No re-intensification occurred after the system entered the eastern Pacific , and it had dissipated as a tropical cyclone by the following day . The remnant tropical disturbance recurved through the Gulf of California while developing significant convection before it moved into northwest Mexico , which brought rainfall amounts of over 10 in ( 250 mm ) to local areas within the state of Sonora . The remnant disturbance moved into the American Southwest on August 11 .

When Bob arrived at the park, he saw some other children playing on the swings. He quickly joined them, skipping around the playground. As he skipped, his rope got caught in the desk he had seen earlier. He stopped to untangle it and noticed something shiny glinting in the sun. It was a big, shiny coin!
Bob was so excited. He picked up the coin and quickly ran to a nearby shop to find out how much it was worth. The shopkeeper said it was a silver dollar and it was worth a lot of money.
Bob was so happy, and he skipped all the way home. He couldn't wait to show his parents what he had found. He was sure that they would be so excited, and they'd be able to buy all the things they needed with the money from the coin.

Once upon a time, a gifted rhinoceros named Remy lived in a big forest. Remy was very good at making friends. One day, he met a small bird named Betty. Betty was sad because she could not raise her voice. Remy wanted to help her.
Remy said, "I can help you raise your voice, Betty!" He put Betty on his back and ran very fast. The wind blew hard and made Betty's voice loud. Betty was very happy and said, "Thank you, Remy!"
But then, something unexpected happened. Remy and Betty found a big bell in the forest. They rang the bell to help other animals raise their voices too. All the animals were so happy. The moral of the story is that when we help each other, we can make good things happen.

One day, a cat named Jazz went for a walk. Jazz was an independent cat who liked to go on adventures by herself. She walked and blinked her eyes at the bright sun.
On her walk, Jazz met a big dog. The dog said, "Hi, I'm Max. Who are you?" Jazz said, "I'm Jazz. I like to walk alone." Max said, "Can I walk with you?" Jazz thought for a moment and said, "Okay, but only for a little bit."
As they walked, Jazz saw a big tree. She wanted to climb it, but she was scared. Max said, "I can help you." He gave her a push and Jazz climbed the tree. When she got to the top, she saw a big surprise. There was a big party with lots of cats and dogs playing together. Jazz was happy she had Max to help her and they both had fun at the party.

Once upon a time, in a big wood, there lived an old bear. The old bear had a big heart and loved to help his friends. One day, a small bird came to the old bear and asked for help. The bird had lost her way and could not find her family. The old bear decided to help the small bird find her family.
Together, they looked all around the wood for the bird's family. They met other animals who tried to help, but no one knew where the bird's family was. The old bear and the small bird were getting tired and sad. Just when they were about to give up, they heard a sound in the trees.
To their surprise, the bird's family was hiding in the trees all along! They were playing a big game of hide and seek with their friend, the old bear. The bird's family knew the old bear loved to help others, so they wanted to give him a fun game to play. The old bear laughed and forgave them for hiding. They all became good friends and played together in the wood every day.

Once upon a time, there was a weak little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy called Laser. Laser was a toy robot. Tim loved to play with Laser every day.
One day, Tim and Laser were playing in the park. Laser could blink with its eyes. Tim said, "Laser, let's play hide and seek!" Laser blinked and said, "Okay, Tim!" So they played hide and seek together.
While playing, Tim saw a girl who was sad. Tim and Laser went to her. Tim asked, "Why are you sad?" The girl said, "I lost my toy." Tim and Laser helped her find her toy. The girl was happy and said, "Thank you, Tim and Laser!" They all played together and had fun.
Moral: Always help others when they need it.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a poor lion named Leo. Leo was very sad because he could not roar like other lions. He tried and tried, but only a tiny sound came out. All his lion friends laughed at him. One day, Leo met a wise old owl who said, "I can help you roar, but first, you must find a special spear."
So, Leo went on a long walk to find the special spear. He looked under rocks, in trees, and even in the river. Finally, he found the spear near a big tree. Leo was very happy and ran back to the wise old owl.
The wise old owl said, "Now that you have the spear, I will teach you the secret to roar." Leo listened carefully and practiced with the spear. Then, one day, Leo let out a big roar! All the other lions were amazed and stopped laughing at him. From that day on, Leo was no longer a poor lion, and he roared with pride.

Once upon a time, there was a man who lived in a town. He was very ignorant and never paid attention to what was happening around him. 
One day, the man was walking through town, when he saw a big sign with a big mark on it. He was curious to see what the sign said, so he stopped to read it, but he couldn't understand the words. 
He asked the person next to him, "What does the sign say?"
The person replied, "It says that it's illegal to do something wrong in this town."
The man was very surprised. He hadn't paid attention to the rules and he had broken the law. Luckily, he was not punished for his ignorance. 
The man learned his lesson and was careful to mark the signs so he would never be ignorant again.

Released on July 10 , 2012 , the album debuted at number 23 on the American Billboard Classic Albums chart . It has received mixed reviews from critics , most of whom highlighted its challenging and free-form composition .

One day, a little girl named Lily went outside to play in the snow. She was so happy to see the white snow on the ground. She put on her warm coat, hat, and gloves. Lily started to make a big snowman.
While she was making the snowman, a big dog came running up to her. Lily was worried. The big dog knocked over her snowman. Lily started to cry. She was sad that her snowman was gone.
Lily's mom saw her crying and came outside. She saw the big dog and the broken snowman. Lily's mom hugged her and they both started to make a new snowman together. The big dog sat and watched them. Soon, Lily was not worried anymore and she was happy again.

Wales played in the inaugural Rugby World Cup in 1987 where they achieved their best ever result of third . Following the sport allowing professionalism in 1995 , Wales hosted the 1999 World Cup and , in 2005 , won their first-ever Six Nations Grand Slam . That was the first Grand Slam won by a team playing most of the matches away from home . Wales won two more Grand Slams in 2008 and in 2012 , and in 2011 came fourth in the Rugby World Cup .

Once upon a time there was a beautiful princess. She loved playing outside and looking up at the stars in the sky. One night while she was playing, she stumbled across something magical. It was a tiny mint that was glowing bright.
The princess was so surprised to see a glowing mint that she wanted to pick it up and keep it for herself. She carefully bent over and picked it up. But then she heard a loud snap and the glowing mint suddenly broke into two pieces.
The princess was so sad that her mint was broken, but just then a tiny light began to glow from the broken mint itself. She was surprised to see that a tiny fairy had been living inside the mint. The fairy thanked the princess for setting him free, and as a thank you, he cast a spell.
The spell made it so that every time the princess looked up at the night sky, she would see a glowing mint in the stars. The princess smiled and thanked the fairy, happy that her broken mint still made the sky glow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a fancy dress that she loved to wear. One day, she saw a pretty stamp on the table. It was a picture of a beautiful flower. Lily wanted to put the stamp on a letter for her friend, Sam.
Lily said, "Mom, can I use this stamp for Sam's letter?" Her mom said, "Yes, you can. But don't miss the mailbox when you put the letter inside." Lily smiled and put the stamp on the letter. She was so excited to send it to her friend.
Lily walked to the mailbox with her mom. She held the letter tightly in her hand. When they got to the mailbox, Lily opened the door and put the letter inside. She made sure she didn't miss the mailbox. Lily was happy that her friend would get the pretty flower stamp and her letter soon.

It was a wild day. Zoey and her dad decided to go outside to paint the creek. Zoey was so excited she ran around looking for the perfect spot to start painting. Her dad watched with a smile.
At last, Zoey found the best spot in the creek. She told her dad she was ready to start painting. He helped her set up, and then said goodbye for a moment as he went to get the paints.
Zoey waited and waited and then, finally, her dad returned with the paints! Zoey yelled, "Let's paint!" and they began. With each brush, the creek came alive in color.
The creek glowed with all the hues of color. Zoey and her dad beamed with pride at their amazing work. The wild creek was beautiful and Zoey knew she'd never forget it's beauty.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a kind man named Tom. Tom loved to catch fish in the river near his home. One sunny day, he went to the river with his fishing net to catch some fish for dinner.
As he was fishing, he found a big bottle in the water. The bottle had a label that said "wine." Tom thought it was strange to find wine in the river, but he decided to take it home with him. He thought maybe he could share it with his friends.
When Tom got home, he opened the bottle of wine. But, instead of wine, out came a mean and angry fish. The fish was not happy that Tom had taken him out of the river. Tom was scared, but he wanted to be kind to the fish. So, he quickly caught the fish with his net and took it back to the river. The fish swam away, and Tom went back to catching fish for dinner. From that day on, Tom learned to be careful with things he found in the river.

Sara and Ben were playing with their blocks. They wanted to build a big castle with towers and walls and a gate. They worked hard and helped each other. They put the blocks on top of each other and made shapes and patterns.
"Look, our castle is almost done!" Sara said. "We just need a flag for the top."
"I have a red cloth we can use," Ben said. He ran to his room and came back with the cloth. He tied it to a stick and put it on the highest tower. "There, now it looks like a real castle!"
Sara and Ben were very proud of their castle. They clapped their hands and cheered. "Yay, we did it!" they said.
Mom and Dad heard the noise and came to see what they were doing. They saw the castle and smiled. They were happy that Sara and Ben played nicely and shared their blocks. They also clapped their hands and praised them.
"Wow, what a beautiful castle you made!" Mom said. "You are very creative and clever."
"And you are very obedient and kind," Dad said. "You followed the rules and cleaned up your mess."
Sara and Ben hugged Mom and Dad. They felt good and loved. They learned that building a castle was fun, but building a family was even better.

One day, a little boy named Tim felt sick. His tummy hurt and he was sleepy. His mom gave him medicine to help him feel better. Tim did not like the taste of the medicine, but he knew it would make him feel better.
Later, Tim's friend, Sam, came to play. Tim told Sam, "I had to take medicine today because I was sick and sleepy." Sam said, "I don't like medicine. It tastes bad. Let's play and forget about it."
As they played, they found a big box. They opened it and saw a lot of candy inside. They were so happy! They started to eat the candy, but then Tim remembered the medicine. He thought, "If I eat too much candy, it will spoil the medicine and I will feel sick again." So, Tim told Sam, "We can eat some candy, but not too much. We don't want to spoil the medicine."
Sam agreed, and they ate a little candy. They played all day and had lots of fun. Tim was glad he did not spoil the medicine, and he felt better the next day.

Once upon a time, in a lively little town, there was a big clock. This clock was very important to the town. Every day, the people looked at the clock to know when to wake up, eat, and go to bed.
One day, the clock stopped working. The people in the town did not know what to do. They needed the clock to tell time. So, a kind man named Tom decided to fix the clock. He worked very hard to set the clock right.
When Tom fixed the clock, everybody was happy. The lively town was back to normal. The people woke up, ate, and went to bed at the right time. They thanked Tom for setting the clock and making their town lively again. And they all lived happily ever after.

Unlike their adversaries , the South Vietnamese military suffered heavily in their attempts to recapture the village of Bình Giã and secure the surrounding areas . The South Vietnamese and their American allies lost the total of about 201 personnel killed in action , 192 wounded and 68 missing . In just four days of fighting , two of South Vietnam 's elite Ranger companies were destroyed and several others suffered heavy losses , while the 4th Marine Battalion was rendered ineffective as a fighting force . At that stage of the war , Bình Giã was the worst defeat experienced by any South Vietnamese army . Despite the humiliating defeat inflicted on them , the South Vietnamese army stubbornly considered the battle as their victory and erected a monument at the site of the battle to acknowledge the sacrifices of the soldiers who had fallen to retake Bình Giã .

Once upon a time, there were twin cats named Tom and Tim. They liked to play outside in the sun. One day, it rained a lot and they got all wet. They did not like being wet.
When the rain stopped, the sun came out. It was big and clear in the sky. Tom and Tim went outside to dry their fur. They sat in the sun and felt warm again.
After they were dry, the twin cats played with their ball. They were happy in the clear sun. They knew they could always dry off and play when the rain went away.

Jill and Jack were best friends who loved playing together. One day Jack asked Jill to come to his house. He told her he had a surprise for her and she was so excited!
When Jill arrived, she saw that Jack had a pile of dresses scattered around the room. She was confused. 
âWhatâs all this?â she asked.
âThese are for us to wear! We will gather them and make them even prettier. Then we can show our friends,â said Jack.
Jill helped Jack gather all the dresses. They spent the day making them even more beautiful. Finally, Jill put on a dress with spicy orange flowers on it. She looked like a doll. 
But when Jack's parents saw the dresses, they were angry. Jill and Jack had taken the dresses without permission. 
The moral of the story is that it's important to always ask for permission. Even if it's something small.

The High Five Interchange , north of downtown in Dallas , Texas , is a massive five-level freeway interchange . It is the junction of two major highways carrying heavy rush hour traffic , the Lyndon B. Johnson Freeway ( Interstate 635 ) and the Central Expressway ( US 75 ) , and is the first five-level stack interchange to be built in the city .

Once upon a time there was a girl who wanted to see the world. She had a special ticket.
One day, the girl was ready to start her travels. She were very excited. She went to the train station, but when she got there, she saw that all the trains were empty. She was very sad.
Suddenly, something happened. She saw a bright light in the sky. Then a magical train appeared in front of her. She couldn't believe it! The train wasn't empty. There were lots of people inside.
The girl was so happy. She got on the magical train with her ticket. As she travelled through the sky, she saw amazing sights - magical forests, glittering seas and magical castles.
The girl had the most amazing journey and when she got back home, she couldn't wait to tell her family and friends all about it!

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl called Emma. One day, Emma wanted to show her mother something special. She started counting the number of steps from the door of their house to the gate. But try as she might, Emma just couldn't remember how many steps there were. 
Frustration started to arise in her little heart, so her mother went to her and asked, "Emma, why are you upset?" Emma told her mother, "I can't remember how many steps I have to take. I want to do something good". Her mother knew that Emma was trying to be patient and replied, "It's alright, my dear. Remember, patience is the key". 
Tears started to roll down Emma's cheeks, so her mother hugged her and said, "Let's start counting together". So they began counting the steps together until they got to the gate. And when they finally reached the gate, Emma was beyond happy that she was able to remember the number of steps without any help.
The moral of this story is to never give up, and patience is key in achieving success.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to collect pretty things. Her favorite thing to collect was bracelets. She had many bracelets in all colors.
One sunny day, Lily saw a very pretty bracelet on the ground. She wanted to add it to her collection. But when she tried to pick it up, a little boy named Timmy saw her. Timmy was angry because he thought the bracelet was his.
Lily and Timmy both wanted the bracelet. They did not want to share. They both pulled on the bracelet, but it did not break. Then, Lily had an idea. She said they could take turns wearing the bracelet. Timmy liked the idea, and they both were happy. They learned to share and became good friends.

" Caught Up " is a song by American R & B singer Usher . It was written by Ryan Toby , Andre Harris , Vidal Davis and Jason Boyd , and produced by Dre & Vidal for Usher 's 2004 album Confessions . The song was released as the fifth and final single from the album on November 30 , 2004 . The single peaked at number eight in the United States , the only single released from Confessions without topping the Billboard Hot 100 , and generally below top ten on most charts worldwide . It received positive reviews from contemporary critics .

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his blocks. One day, he found some hidden blocks under his bed. "Wow!" he said, "I didn't know these were here!"
Tim played with the hidden blocks all day. Then, his friend Sam came over. "Look at my new blocks!" Tim said. Sam looked at the blocks and said, "Hey, those blocks belong to me! I lost them when I came over to play last week."
Tim was sad. He didn't want to give the blocks back. But he knew it was the right thing to do. So, he gave the blocks to Sam. Sam smiled and said, "Thank you! Let's play together with my blocks." Tim smiled too, and they played together all day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was an ordinary clock. It lived in a little house with a girl named Sue. Sue was a happy girl who liked to learn new things. The ordinary clock wanted to learn too.
One day, Sue's mom showed her how to tell time. The ordinary clock listened and learned too. Now, the ordinary clock knew when it was time to eat, play, and sleep. It was very happy to learn.
Every day, Sue and the ordinary clock would learn together. They learned about colors, shapes, and numbers. They had lots of fun, and the ordinary clock was not just an ordinary clock anymore. It was a very smart clock, and Sue was a very smart girl. They were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Sue lived in a small house. She had a dog named Spot. One day, Sue and Spot went for a walk in the park. They saw a big tree with sweet red apples. Sue said, "Spot, let's pick some apples!"
As they picked apples, a little boy walked up to them. He had a frown on his face. Sue asked, "What's your name?" The boy said, "My name is Tim." Sue asked, "Why do you frown, Tim?" Tim said, "I lost my toy car."
Sue and Spot wanted to help Tim. They looked all around the park for the toy car. Then, Spot started to bark at the big tree. Sue looked up and saw Tim's toy car in the tree! They all laughed. Sue said, "How did it get there?" Tim said, "I don't know." They picked the car from the tree and Tim's frown turned into a big smile. From that day, Sue, Spot, and Tim became best friends.

" New Year 's Eve " received mostly positive reviews from critics . According to the Nielsen Media Research , " New Year 's Eve " drew 4. 28 million viewers and received a 2. 0 rating / 5 % share in the 18 – 49 demographic , marking a 5 % rise in the ratings from the previous episode , " First Christmas " . It ranked third in its timeslot and was the second highest-rated NBC program of the night after The Office .

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a unique little dog named Spot. Spot was not like other dogs. He had a special job to protect the town. Every day, he would take his turn walking around and keeping everyone safe.
One day, while Spot was on his turn, he saw a little girl named Lily. Lily was lost and scared. Spot knew he had to protect her. He walked up to her and wagged his tail. Lily smiled and knew she was safe with Spot.
Together, they walked through the town until they found Lily's mom. Lily's mom was so happy to see her and thanked Spot for protecting her. From that day on, Lily and Spot were best friends, and the town knew how special and unique Spot was.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big pond with ducks and fish. They wanted to feed them, so they asked their mom for some bread.
"Here you go, but be careful not to fall in the water," mom said, giving them each a slice.
Tom and Lily ran to the pond and threw some bread to the ducks and fish. They were happy to see them eat and swim. But Tom wanted to have more fun. He saw a big stick and had an idea.
"Hey, Lily, watch this!" he said, and swung the stick at the water. He made a big splash that wet his clothes and shoes.
"Tom, stop that! You are making a mess!" Lily said, feeling angry. She did not like to get wet.
But Tom did not listen. He swung the stick again and again, making more splashes. He laughed and said, "This is fun!"
Then he saw something in the water. It was an old turtle with a hard shell and a long neck. It looked at Tom with its small eyes.
"Hello, turtle," Tom said, and tried to touch it with his stick. But the turtle did not like that. It snapped at the stick and broke it in half.
"Ow!" Tom said, dropping the stick. He felt scared and sorry. He had hurt the turtle and its home.
"Tom, you are naughty! You should not bother the turtle. It is old and honest. It does not hurt anyone," Lily said, feeling sorry for the turtle.
She picked up some bread and threw it to the turtle. The turtle ate it and swam away. Lily smiled and said, "Bye, turtle. I hope you are okay."
Tom felt bad. He knew he had done wrong. He looked at his wet clothes and shoes. He looked at his mom, who was coming to get them.
"Mom, I am sorry. I was silly. I splashed the water and broke the stick and hurt the turtle. I will not do it again," he said, feeling sad.
Mom hugged him and said, "I am glad you are honest, Tom. But you have to be careful and kind. The pond is not a toy. It is a home for the ducks and fish and the turtle. They have feelings too. You have to respect them and their space."
Tom nodded and said, "I understand, mom. I will respect them and their space. And I will say sorry to the turtle."
Mom smiled and said, "That is good, Tom. Come on, let's go home and change your clothes. And maybe next time, you can play with Lily and the turtle nicely."
Tom and Lily held mom's hand and walked home. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be careful and kind and honest. And they hoped the turtle would forgive them.

Once upon a time, there was a little cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to eat meat. One day, Kitty's friend, Doggy, gave her some meat to eat. Kitty was very happy.
While Kitty was eating the meat, she made a big mess. She felt embarrass because all her friends were watching. Kitty looked at the mess and felt sorry.
Kitty said to her friends, "I am sorry for the mess." Her friends smiled and said, "It's okay, Kitty. We all make messes sometimes." They all helped Kitty clean up the mess, and then they played together. Kitty was happy to have such good friends.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to visit their grandma and grandpa. Grandma and grandpa live in a big house with a garden. They have a dog named Spot. Spot is black and white. He has a long strip on his back.
One day, Sara and Ben go to visit their grandma and grandpa. They bring a ball and a book. They say hello to Spot. Spot is happy to see them. He wags his tail and licks their faces. He wants to play with the ball.
"Can we play with Spot, grandma?" Sara asks.
"Of course, dear. But be careful. He is very loud. He barks a lot. He might scare the birds," grandma says.
Sara and Ben nod. They take the ball and go to the garden. They throw the ball and Spot runs after it. He catches it and brings it back. He barks and jumps. He is loud. Sara and Ben laugh. They have fun.
But then, Spot sees a cat. The cat is on the fence. It is gray and fluffy. It has green eyes. Spot does not like the cat. He drops the ball and runs to the fence. He barks and growls. He is very loud. He tries to catch the cat.
"Spot, no!" Sara and Ben shout. They run after him. They want to stop him.
But the cat is fast. It jumps from the fence to the roof. It looks down at Spot. It hisses and spits. It is not afraid.
Spot is angry. He jumps and scratches the fence. He is very loud. He makes a hole in the fence. He goes through the hole. He chases the cat.
"Spot, come back!" Sara and Ben shout. They go through the hole. They follow him.
Grandma and grandpa hear the noise. They come out of the house. They see the hole in the fence. They see Sara and Ben running. They see Spot and the cat on the roof.
"Oh, no!" grandma and grandpa say. They are worried. They call Sara and Ben. They call Spot. They want them to come back.
But Sara and Ben do not hear them. They are too far. They are on the street. They see Spot and the cat on the roof of another house. They see a ladder. They climb the ladder. They want to get Spot and the cat.
But the ladder is old. It is weak. It breaks. Sara and Ben fall. They land on a pile of leaves. They are not hurt. But they are scared. They cry.
Spot and the cat hear them. They stop fighting. They look at them. They feel sorry. They come down from the roof. They go to them. They lick them. They are not loud. They are quiet.
Sara and Ben hug them. They are happy. They are not scared. They stop crying.
Grandma and grandpa find them. They are relieved. They hug them. They are glad. They are not angry. They smile.
They take them back to the house. They fix the fence. They give them cookies and milk. They read them the book. They are not loud. They are calm.
Sara and Ben say thank you. They say sorry. They say goodbye. They love their grandma and grandpa. They love Spot and the cat. They had a good visit. They will come back soon.

Once upon a time, there was a big, yellow ball. The ball was very hot. It lived up in the sky. It was friends with a little cloud. They liked to play together.
One day, the yellow ball said to the cloud, "I want to play push with you." The cloud said, "Okay, let's play!" So the yellow ball pushed the cloud. The cloud moved and laughed.
When the yellow ball pushed the cloud, they both felt happy. The heat from the yellow ball made the cloud warm. They played push all day until it was time for the yellow ball to go to sleep. The cloud said, "Good night, yellow ball!" The yellow ball said, "Good night, cloud!" And they both slept, waiting for another fun day to play push again.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a girl named Lily. She had a toy sword that she loved to play with. One day, she went to the park with her friend, Tom.
At the park, they saw a big tree. Lily said, "Let's climb the tree!" Tom agreed, and they both started to climb. Lily used her toy sword to help her reach the high branches. She stretched her arm to grab the branches, and her toy sword was flexible, so it bent a little bit.
As they climbed higher, they heard a voice from above. "Hello, little ones!" it said. They looked up and saw a big bird sitting on a branch. The bird had a shiny key in its beak. "I found this key," said the bird, "but I don't know what it opens. Can you help me?" Lily and Tom agreed to help the bird. They took the key and climbed back down the tree.
They searched the park and found a small door hidden in the bushes. They used the key to open the door, and inside, they found a room full of toys! The bird had led them to a secret playroom. Lily and Tom were so happy, and they played there all day with their new friend, the bird.

Once upon a time, there was a giant. The giant lived in a big, bright house. The house was on a tall hill. The giant was very kind and liked to help people.
One day, the giant saw a little boy. The little boy was sad. He lost his toy. The giant wanted to help the little boy. The giant said, "I will send my bird to find your toy."
The giant sent his big bird to look for the toy. The bird flew high in the sky. It saw the bright, shiny toy on the ground. The bird picked up the toy and brought it back to the giant.
The giant gave the toy to the little boy. The boy was very happy. He said, "Thank you, giant!" The giant smiled. The boy and the giant became good friends. They played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a long snake named Spike. Spike liked to play with his friends in the big forest. They loved to play hide and seek.
One day, Spike was hiding from his friends. He found a big bush and thought, "I can cover myself with leaves!" So he went under the bush and covered himself with the green leaves. He was very good at hiding.
Soon, his friend, a little bird, found him. The bird said, "Spike, I found you!" Spike laughed and said, "You are good at this game!" They played all day and had lots of fun in the big forest.

Once there was a poor dog named Max. Max was very sad because he lived in a small, cold bathroom. He wanted to find a new home where he could be happy and warm.
One day, a nice lady named Sue came to visit Max. She saw how sad he was and wanted to help him. Sue said, "Max, let's choose a new home for you!" Max wagged his tail and barked, "Yes, please!"
Sue took Max to a big, warm house with a soft bed and yummy food. Max was so happy to leave the cold bathroom behind. He cuddled with Sue, and they played all day. Max finally had the loving home he always wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max loved to dig in the yard. One day, Max found a big bone. He was so happy! He played with the bone all day long.
Max saw a little bird who looked helpless. The bird said, "Help, I can't fly!" Max wanted to help the bird. He thought, "Maybe the bone can help the bird fly." Max gave the bone to the bird. The bird held the bone tight in its beak.
Suddenly, the bird began to fly! Max had rescued the bird with the bone. Max and the bird were now friends. They played together every day. Max was happy that he could help his new friend.
Apollo Justice : Ace Attorney is the fourth entry in the series . It was released for the Nintendo DS in 2007 in Japan and in 2008 in the West .

One day, a goose went to the park. The goose liked to enjoy the sun and play with the kids. The goose had a hard time making friends, but he was happy.
In the park, the goose met a boy. The boy said, "Hi, goose! Do you want to play?" The goose was very happy and said, "Yes, I want to play!" They played all day and had lots of fun.
But then, something unexpected happened. The boy took off his hat and showed the goose that he was a goose too! The first goose was so surprised, but now they were both happy. They played together every day and became best friends.

One day, a little bee was flying in the sky. The bee was looking for flowers to make sweet honey. The bee saw a big, pretty flower and went to it.
As the bee got close to the flower, it saw a dead bug on the ground. The bee felt sad for the bug. The bee knew it was important to be careful and stay away from danger.
Just then, a girl saw the bee and started to clap her hands. She liked the bee and wanted to be friends. The bee flew to her hand, and they became friends. The girl and the bee played together all day, and they were both very happy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the yard. They liked to pretend they were explorers in the jungle. They had a tent, a map, and a flashlight. They also had a big stick that they used as a fire.
"Look, Ben, I made a fire!" Lily said, holding the stick in the air. She smiled and waved it around.
"Be careful, Lily, don't burn yourself!" Ben said. He was a helpful brother. He always looked after Lily.
Lily nodded, but she did not listen. She wanted to make the fire bigger and brighter. She ran to the pile of leaves and threw the stick on it. The leaves caught fire and made a lot of smoke.
"Oh no, Lily, what did you do?" Ben shouted. He ran to the tent and grabbed the flashlight. He turned it on and pointed it at the fire. He hoped it would scare the fire away.
But the fire did not go away. It grew and grew. It reached the tent and burned it. It reached the map and burned it. It reached the flashlight and burned it.
Lily and Ben were scared. They cried and hugged each other. They did not know what to do.
Then they heard a siren. It was a fire truck. It came to the yard and sprayed water on the fire. The fire went away. The firemen came out and checked on Lily and Ben.
"Are you okay, kids?" one of them asked.
"Yes, we are okay, thank you," Ben said.
"Why did you start a fire?" another one asked.
"It was an accident, we were playing," Lily said.
"Playing with fire is very dangerous, you know. You could have hurt yourself or others. You should never do that again," the fireman said.
"We are sorry, we won't do that again," Lily and Ben said.
The firemen were nice. They gave Lily and Ben a hug and a sticker. They told them to be careful and to listen to their parents. They also told them to smile and be happy.
Lily and Ben smiled and thanked the firemen. They learned their lesson. They decided to play something else next time. Maybe they would pretend to be astronauts or pirates. But they would never play with fire again.

Lily and Ben were playing in the pool. They liked to splash each other with water. They had a lot of fun.
But then, Ben saw a big bowl of celery on the table. He loved celery. He wanted to eat some. He got out of the pool and ran to the table.
"Hey, where are you going?" Lily asked. She followed him.
Ben grabbed a piece of celery and bit it. But it did not taste good. It tasted like plastic. He spat it out.
"Yuck! This is not celery. This is fake celery!" he said.
Lily laughed. She knew it was fake celery. She had put it there as a joke. She wanted to trick Ben.
"Ha ha, I got you! That is not real celery. That is fake celery. I made it with paper and paint. You are so silly!" she said.
Ben was not happy. He felt angry and fooled. He threw the fake celery at Lily. It hit her in the face.
"Ow! That hurt!" she said.
She threw some water at Ben. He threw some water back at her. They started to splash each other again. But this time, they were not having fun. They were having a fight.

Once there was a little girl named Amy. She was always looking for new adventures. One day, she opened the door to her house and found a brand new hockey stick leaning against the wall. She couldn't believe her luck! 
Amy took the hockey stick and ran outside. She called her best friend, Adam, and said "Come over, I have something unique for us to play with."
Adam arrived quickly and was amazed when he saw the hockey stick. Amy explained that she found it by the door. Together they entered the backyard, and started to play a game of hockey with the unique hockey stick. 
It was so much fun! Amy and Adam played the game until it was time to go in the house. As they left the hockey match, they both had smiles on their faces. They surely had a unique day, playing hockey with a special hockey stick!

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Tim. Tim loved to dance on the floor in his room. He would spin, jump, and clap his hands with joy.
One day, Tim's mom and dad came to watch him dance. They sat on the floor and smiled. Tim danced and danced, his feet tapping on the floor. He was so happy to show his mom and dad his moves.
When Tim finished dancing, his mom and dad clapped their hands. They were so proud of their young boy. Tim felt so happy and proud too. They all laughed and hugged, and Tim knew he would dance again and again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, her mom asked her to provide her with a pot. Sue was very happy to help.
Sue looked and looked for the pot. She found it under the sink. But, oh no! The pot was disgusting! It had dirt and yucky stuff all over it. Sue knew she had to clean the pot for her mom.
Sue washed and scrubbed the pot until it was shiny and clean. She gave the pot to her mom with a big smile. Her mom was so proud of Sue for helping and making the pot clean. They cooked a yummy meal together and had a great day.

Once upon a time, there was a little train. Its engine was old and loud, but the little train was very happy with it. Every day it would meet all the other trains on the railway, and they would talk and share stories. But one train was very envious. It was brand new and had a much better engine than the little train. It wished that its engine could be just like the little train's engine.

But the little train answered, "No thank you. Even though my engine is old, it is still my best friend. We can't switch."
The envious train was so surprised. It had never had a friend like that before. It quickly made a new friend with the little train and they have been friends ever since. The little train taught the envious train that there is more to friendship than having the best engine.

One day, a farmer was walking through the quiet farm. The sun was out and everything was peaceful. The farmer heard something strange. He looked around and saw a puddle of water. It was soaking the grass. The farmer knew that it had rained the night before, so he thought the puddle was from the rain. He smiled, knowing that rain is always a good thing on the farm.
He walked closer to the puddle and saw a bright, yellow duck. The duck must have been thirsty because it was drinking all the water in the puddle. The farmer laughed and said hello. The duck quacked in response and the farmer watched as it waddled away into the quiet fields.
The farmer was happy that the rain had made a puddle for the thirsty duck and that the farm was quiet enough for the duck to find it and get a drink. He knew that nature was doing its job. So he went on his way, making sure to be quiet too.

Lily was sick. She had a red nose and a sore throat. She did not want to play or eat. She only wanted to sleep. Mommy was worried. She gave Lily some medicine to make her feel better. She said, "Drink this, Lily. It will help you."
Lily did not like the medicine. It was bitter and yucky. She made a face and spit it out. She said, "No, Mommy. I don't want it. It is bad." Mommy was sad. She said, "But Lily, you need the medicine. It will make you strong and healthy. Please, try again."
Lily shook her head. She did not want to try again. She hid under the blanket. She said, "No, no, no. Go away, Mommy. Leave me alone." Mommy sighed. She did not know what to do. She said, "Okay, Lily. I will go away. But I will come back soon. I love you."
Mommy left the room. Lily felt lonely and scared. She missed Mommy. She wished Mommy would come back. She heard a noise outside. She peeked from the blanket. She saw a big dog. It was barking and jumping. It looked angry and mean. Lily was afraid. She said, "Mommy, Mommy, help me!"
Mommy heard Lily's cry. She ran back to the room. She saw the dog. She was angry and brave. She said, "Go away, dog. You are not welcome here. You are scaring my Lily." She opened the door and stepped outside. She shooed the dog away. She said, "Go, go, go. Don't come back."
The dog ran away. Mommy came back inside. She hugged Lily. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. I am here. The dog is gone. You are safe." Lily hugged Mommy. She said, "Thank you, Mommy. I love you. You are my hero." Mommy smiled. She said, "I love you too, Lily. You are my sweetie. Now, will you drink the medicine?" Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, Mommy. I will drink the medicine. I want to feel better." Mommy gave Lily the medicine. Lily drank it. She made a face, but she did not spit it out. She said, "It is still yucky, but I can do it." Mommy said, "Good girl, Lily. I am proud of you. Now, let's cuddle and read a story." Lily said, "Okay, Mommy. That sounds nice." They cuddled and read a story. Lily felt warm and cozy. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. Mommy kissed her forehead and whispered, "Good night, Lily. Sweet dreams."

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He had a big, old ashtray. He liked to keep it in his room.
One day, a little bird flew into the old man's room. The bird saw the old ashtray and thought it was a nest. The bird sat in the ashtray and made it her home.
The old man came into the room and saw the bird. He was not happy. He told the bird, "Go away! That is my ashtray!" The bird did not want to go. She said, "No, this is my nest!" The old man and the bird both wanted the ashtray.
Then, something unexpected happened. The old ashtray began to shake and wiggle. It turned into a magic flying ashtray! The old man and the bird were very surprised. They decided to share the magic flying ashtray and go on adventures together. And they became the best of friends.

Once, there was a young zebra who wanted to explore the world. He had never been anywhere, but he wanted to change that. He left the herd and set off on an adventure. Everywhere he went, he shrugged his shoulders and smiled.
The zebra explored many places and saw many wonders, but he wanted more. One day, he came upon an open field. He ran straight into the open space and felt the warm sun on his fur. But something strange happened. He heard a loud noise and he could feel the ground shaking. He looked up and his heart sunk; a large lion was going to attack him!
The zebra tried to run away, but he was too late. The lion pounced on him and the zebra knew there was nothing he could do. He shrugged and accepted his fate. The lion ended the life of the young zebra much too early.

All six ships operated in the Atlantic or Caribbean until the U.S. entrance into World War I in April 1917 , when all six were sent overseas to Queenstown , Ireland , for convoy escort duties . Several of the ships rescued passengers and crew from ships sunk by U-boats , and several had encounters with U-boats themselves ; Nicholson helped sink U-58 in November 1917 , the first U-boat sunk by the U.S. Navy . All six members of the class had returned to the United States in January 1919 and were decommissioned by June 1922 . In 1924 , two of the six — Ericsson and McDougal — were commissioned into the United States Coast Guard to help enforce Prohibition as a part of the " Rum Patrol " . They were returned to U.S. Navy custody in 1932 and 1933 , respectively . All six ships had been sold for scrapping by June 1936 .

Once upon a time, in a small, humble house, there lived a girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her pastel colors. One day, she was drawing a big, pretty flower when her friend, Tim, came to play.
"Hi, Lily! What are you doing?" Tim asked. Lily said, "I am drawing a flower. I want to finish it soon." Tim wanted to help, so they drew together.
As they drew, something unexpected happened. The flower came to life! It jumped off the paper and danced around the room. Lily and Tim were very surprised but happy to have a new friend. They played together all day long, and the flower made their day extra special.

One sunny day, a humble dog named Max went for a walk in the park. Max loved to play with his ball and chase butterflies. While playing, he saw a girl with a big box. The girl was taking pictures of the pretty flowers.
Max went to the girl and said, "Hi! What are you doing?" The girl smiled and said, "I am taking pictures of the flowers. They are so pretty!" Max looked at the flowers and saw how pretty they were. He wanted to be in a picture too.
The girl said, "Would you like to be in a picture, Max?" Max wagged his tail and said, "Yes, please!" The girl took a picture of Max with the flowers. She showed Max the picture and they both laughed. Then they played together and became good friends.

Once, there was a boy named Tim. He loved to rush and play all day. Tim had a big cat named Max. Max liked to sleep and eat.
One day, Tim wanted to make a sandwich. He needed butter for his sandwich. Tim looked in the kitchen, but there was no butter. He asked his mom where the butter was. She said they needed to go to the store to buy more.
Tim and his mom went to the store. There were many things in the store. They found the butter, but it was expensive. Tim's mom said they could still buy it. They went home and Tim made his sandwich. Tim and Max were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play catch with his friends. One sunny day, they were playing catch with a fragile ball near a big hole. The hole led to an underground world.
While playing, Tim threw the ball too hard, and it went into the hole. He was very sad. Tim and his friends looked into the hole and saw a tiny light. They wanted to get the ball back, so they decided to go into the underground world.
When they got underground, they found a magic land with talking animals. The animals had caught Tim's ball and were playing with it. The animals saw the kids and decided to give the ball back. Once upon a time, there was a long cat named Nod. Nod loved sugar. He would eat it all day if he could. One day, Nod found a big bag of sugar in the kitchen. He was very happy.
But there was a problem. Nod's friend, a little dog named Momo, also liked sugar. Momo saw the big bag of sugar and wanted some too. Nod and Momo looked at each other. They both wanted the sugar, but there was only one bag.
Nod had an idea. He thought they could share the sugar. Nod and Momo agreed to share the sugar and be happy friends. They each took some sugar and ate it together. From that day on, Nod and Momo always shared their treats and stayed the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful mule named Mimi. Mimi lived on a farm with many friends. She loved to play all day with her friends, the cows, the pigs, and the chickens.
One day, Mimi and her friends were playing a game of hide and seek. Mimi was very good at hiding. She found a big tree to hide behind. While she was hiding, Mimi heard a strange sound. She paused and listened. "What could that be?" she thought.

Once upon a time, there was a wild human. Everyone was very scared of him. One day, he decided to show his friends how he could be nice. He smiled and waved his arms. When he did this, all the kids around were so excited. They ran up to him and smiled. He laughed and said "Hi!". He started to play with them, showing them lots of fun games.
