Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a flashlight that he loved very much. Every night, he would turn it on and play with it in his room. He liked to make shadows on the wall with his flashlight.
One day, Tim's flashlight stopped working. He tried to turn it on, but it would not light up. Tim felt sad and began to frown. He wanted his flashlight to work again. He asked his mom for help. His mom looked at the flashlight and saw that it needed new batteries.
Tim was a persistent little boy. He did not give up. He asked his mom to put new batteries in the flashlight. His mom did, and the flashlight started working again. Tim was very happy. He played with his flashlight all night long and made shadows on the wall. His frown turned into a big smile.

One day, a cat named Sam saw a red laser. Sam wanted to catch it. He started to follow the laser. It moved fast, but Sam moved fast too.
Sam saw the laser go into a big room. In the room, there was a huge dog named Max. Max was playing with the laser too. Sam was scared, but Max said, "Don't worry, we can play together."
They played with the laser all day. Suddenly, the laser stopped moving. Sam and Max looked around and saw a little girl holding the laser. She was laughing. They didn't know it was her all along. Sam and Max became friends with the little girl, and they all played together every day.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in their bedroom. They have a big slide that goes from their bed to the floor. They take turns to slide down and laugh.
One day, Anna slides down too fast and bumps her head on the wall. She cries and holds her head. Ben hears her and runs to her. He hugs her and says, "Are you okay, Anna? I'm sorry you hurt your head."
Anna stops crying and smiles at Ben. She says, "Thank you, Ben. You are very compassionate. You always help me when I'm sad or hurt."
Ben smiles back and says, "You're welcome, Anna. You are my sister and I love you. Do you want to slide again?"
Anna nods and says, "Yes, I do. But let's slide slower and be careful."
They hold hands and slide down together. They giggle and have fun. They are happy and compassionate twins.

On the day of the party, Tim and his dad set up the fireworks. When it was time to start, they lit the first firework. But instead of going up, it went down! It made a big hole in the ground. Tim and his dad laughed. They did not know the fireworks were magic! The hole led to a secret room full of more fun fireworks. The party was even better than they thought it would be.

One day when Milly was playing in the garden, she spotted something strange. She ran towards it and saw it was a root sticking out of the ground that was almost as tall as her. It looked very old, like it had been there a long time.
Milly started to pull at it and soon it was out of the ground. She was so excited! She couldn't figure out why no one had noticed it before. 
But then suddenly there was a loud creaking noise. Milly looked up to see a dead tree standing in front of her. She was scared and started to sob.
Suddenly, a voice came from behind her. "What have you done," it said.
Milly turned around to see her mother's angry face. "I'm sorry, Mama," she said, "I didn't know the root was connected to the tree." 
But it was too late. The tree had been weakened by the root being pulled out and now it was standing but ready to collapse at any moment.
Milly and her mother ran away quickly, but moments later the tree fell to the ground with a loud crashing sound. It had been dead for a long time and was now gone forever.

Once upon a time, there was a furry dog named Spot. Spot loved to play in the surf at the beach. One sunny day, he went to the beach with his family to have fun and splash in the water.

Billy loved to go to his grandma's house. He knew she always had something yummy to eat. On this particular day, Grandma put some soup on the kitchen table. Billy knew it must be special soup. It smelled so good! Grandma said it was dependable!

Once upon a time there was a big, silly bear. He lived in the forest, and every day he would roar and stomp his feet.
One day he found a big boot in the forest. He put the boot on his foot and started to walk around. But the boot was too big, and it made him wobble and fall over.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lucy went for a walk. She wanted to choose a pretty landscape to draw. The sun was light and warm on her face. Lucy liked to draw pictures of trees, flowers, and animals.
As Lucy walked, she saw a big tree. The tree had many leaves and was very tall. Lucy thought it was perfect for her drawing. So, she sat down and started to draw. She drew the tree, the grass, and the sky. Lucy was very happy with her picture.

Once there was a little girl named Maria. She was very shy and every day she went to her friend's house to play.

The next day, Maria brought something else to mail to the wall. Her mom had made her a card with a message on it. It said, "We are all connected, even if we are shy".

One day, a little boy named Tim was eager to go outside and play. He put on his shoes and ran out the door. In the yard, he saw a big pile of junk. Tim was curious and wanted to see what he could find.
Tim's friend, Sam, came over and said, "Let's get some toys and play!" Tim looked at the junk and said, "I want to play with the junk. It looks fun!" Sam didn't like the junk and said, "No, junk is dirty. Let's play with our toys instead."

Once upon a time, a funny frog named Freddy lived near a pond. He liked to jump and play all day. One day, he found a long pole near the water. He thought it would be fun to play with the pole.

Freddy was very happy. He started to play with the pole near the pond. Suddenly, the pole moved! It was not a pole, but a long snake! Freddy and Ducky were surprised, but the snake was nice. They all played together and had a great day.

Once upon a time, there was a small figure named Tim. Tim wanted to become strong. Every day, he would try to lift big things to get strong.

On a bright Wednesday, two friends, Alex and Sarah, decided to go on an adventure. The sun was shining, the sky was blue, and the birds were singing. Alex thought the day was brilliant.

When they were finished, they stayed in the park to have lunch. The sun was still shining and it was a wonderful afternoon. As they ate, the friends talked and laughed.
Finally, it was time to end the adventure. Both Alex and Sarah said goodbye and agreed that their Wednesday had been brilliant fun.

Anna and Ben were playing with blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and bridges and castles with the blocks. They had many colors and shapes of blocks to choose from.
Anna wanted to make the tallest tower ever. She stacked the blocks as high as she could, but she needed more. She saw a big box of blocks on the shelf. She asked Ben to help her lift the box.

Ben nodded and went to the shelf. He tried to lift the box, but it was too heavy for him. He pulled and pushed, but the box did not move. He felt frustrated and angry.
He decided to use a chair to reach the box. He dragged the chair to the shelf and climbed on it. He grabbed the box and tried to lift it again. But he lost his balance and fell off the chair. The box fell with him and hit the floor. The blocks spilled out of the box and made a loud noise.

The other animals saw how Tom helped the bird. They said, "Tom, you are not so grumpy after all!" Tom smiled and played with the other animals. From that day on, Tom was not grumpy anymore, and he had many friends. The pan had changed Tom's life.

SR 67 existed as a route to reach the north rim of the Grand Canyon National Park as early as 1927 as a dirt road . By 1935 , the road had been improved to a gravel road , and by 1938 it had been paved . In 1941 , the road was designated as a state highway and signed as SR 67 . In 1985 , the highway received the designation of Kaibab Plateau – North Rim Parkway as an Arizona State Scenic Byway . The designation included SR 67 in its entirety as well as extending south into Grand Canyon National Park . Two years later , ADOT obtained the right-of-way for improvement of the highway from its northern terminus approximately 10 miles ( 16 km ) south . In 1989 , an additional right-of-way was acquired by ADOT from its southern terminus approximately 5 miles ( 8. 0 km ) north . By June of that year , the parkway received the designation of a National Forest Scenic Byway , and in June 1998 , the Kaibab Plateau – North Rim Parkway received another designation , this time as a National Scenic Byway . Since establishment , the route has not been realigned and retains its original routing .

The plan of attack was for the British raiding force to sink two obsolete cruisers in the canal mouth at Ostend and three at Zeebrugge , thus preventing raiding ships leaving Bruges . The Ostend canal was the smaller and narrower of the two channels giving access to Bruges and so was considered a secondary target behind the Zeebrugge Raid . Consequently , fewer resources were provided to the force assaulting Ostend . While the attack at Zeebrugge garnered some limited success , the assault on Ostend was a complete failure . Once upon a time, there was a friendly cat named Tom. Tom liked to play with his ball. One day, Tom went to a fun event with his mom. At the event, there were many games and other animals to play with.
Tom saw a big dog named Max. Max liked to tease Tom by taking his ball away. Tom was sad, but he didn't give up. He thought of a plan to get his ball back from Max. Tom found a bigger ball and rolled it towards Max.
Max saw the big ball and let go of Tom's ball to chase the big one. Tom got his ball back and was very happy. But then, something unexpected happened. Max came back with the big ball and wanted to play with Tom. They both played with the big ball and had a great time. In the end, Max and Tom became good friends and didn't tease each other anymore.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big lock on the gate. They want to go inside, but they cannot.
"Who put the lock there?" Sara asks.
"I don't know. Maybe the park is closed," Ben says.
They are sad. They look around. They see a big tree near the fence. The tree has a branch that goes over the fence.
"Look, Sara! We can hop on the branch and go inside the park!" Ben says.
He runs to the tree and climbs up. He hops on the branch and swings over the fence. He lands on the grass.
"Come on, Sara! It is fun!" he shouts.
Sara is scared. She does not like to hop high. She stays on the ground.
"Ben, I don't want to hop. It is too high. I might fall," she says.
Ben sees that Sara is scared. He feels sorry. He hops back on the branch and climbs down the tree.
"It is okay, Sara. We don't have to hop. We can play here," he says.
He gives Sara a hug. He sees a candy shop across the street. He has some money in his pocket.
"Hey, Sara! Do you want some candy? They have sweet candy there. We can share," he says.
Sara smiles. She likes candy. She likes Ben.
"Yes, Ben! I want some candy. You are a good friend," she says.
They hold hands and cross the street. They buy some candy and eat it. They are happy. They forget about the lock.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He had a favorite costume that his mommy made for him. He wore it everywhere.
One day, the little boy was playing in the yard when he accidentally broke his favorite costume. He felt really sad and sad. He was so upset that he ran to his mommy and told her what had happened. 
His mommy told him it was ok and not to worry. She went to the store and bought him a new costume, even prettier than the old one. He was so happy.
But the little boy remembered his old costume with sadness. He remembered how alive it made him feel. He wished he hadn't broken it. He knew he couldn't get it back and the feeling in his heart was dead.

Following the storm in South Africa , workers restored the original course of the Umfolozi River after it had moved . Officials later purchased a new dredge to remove sediment from Lake St. Lucia , and the canal connecting the lake to the Umfolozi River was later finished . Local governments coordinated relief efforts in the country , including delivering food and providing shelter for those who lost their homes . The South African Red Cross provided food to storm victims , many of whom were beneficiaries of the food program during the extended drought . The South African government declared KwaZulu Natal as a disaster areas . The country 's military provided 25 helicopters to rescue flood victims and donated 3, 000 tents . The government later authorized $ 85 million to fund repairing damaged rails and roads . The American government donated $ 100, 000 to the country , mostly to purchase supplies . West Germany also donated about $ 231, 000 , mostly for the feeding program .

On Daydream , Carey collaborated with Jermaine Dupri for the first time , and co-wrote and produced a song with Kenneth " Babyface " Edmonds , with whom she had collaborated on Music Box . It was also the first time she had worked with Boyz II Men , an R & B group consisting of four male vocalists . Together , they wrote the concept and lyrics for " One Sweet Day , " a song that Carey co-produced with Afanasieff . With his assistance and the addition of a few contemporary producers , she was able to make a subtle transition into the R & B market . Daydream was nominated for six Grammy Awards at the 38th annual ceremony , during which Carey performed live . Due to the album 's critical and commercial success , critics believed Carey would be one of the night 's big winners . However , to her dismay , she was completely shut out , causing the subject to become very public and controversial . She left the annual ceremony empty-handed .

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play together. One day, they were playing with their blocks and cars in the living room. Sara wanted to build a big tower with the blocks, but Ben wanted to drive his cars around the tower and make noises.
"Ben, stop!" Sara said. "You are making my tower fall down!"
"But I want to play with my cars!" Ben said. "They are fun and fast!"
Sara and Ben started to argue and shout. They did not hear their mom calling them for lunch.
Mom came into the living room and saw the mess and the noise. She was not happy.
"Sara and Ben, what are you doing?" she asked. "It is time for lunch. Why are you fighting?"
Sara and Ben stopped and looked at their mom. They felt bad.
"We are sorry, mom," they said. "We wanted to play different things and we did not agree."
Mom nodded and said, "I understand. Sometimes it is hard to share and cooperate. But you are twins and you love each other, right?"
Sara and Ben nodded and hugged each other.
"Right, mom," they said. "We love each other."
Mom smiled and said, "That's good. Now, let's go to the kitchen and have some lunch. I made your favorite sandwiches and fruit salad."
Sara and Ben followed their mom to the kitchen. They were hungry and happy.
"Mom, you are so thoughtful," Sara said. "Thank you for making us lunch."
"Yes, mom, you are the best," Ben said. "Can we request something?"
Mom looked at them and said, "Sure, what is it?"
Sara and Ben said, "Can we help you clean up the living room after lunch? We want to show you that we are sorry and that we can work together."
Mom hugged them and said, "Of course, you can. That is very kind and responsible of you. I am proud of you, Sara and Ben."
Sara and Ben smiled and ate their lunch. They learned that it is better to share and cooperate than to fight and argue. They also learned to appreciate their mom and her thoughtful gestures. They had a good day.

Once upon a time, a little girl called Joy was playing in the park. Suddenly, she heard a loud siren. She peeked out of the bushes and saw an ambulance. All of the grown-ups were running away, so Joy felt scared. 
Suddenly, a hairy dog came running up to Joy. The dog barked loudly! Joy said, "What is it, doggy? Is something wrong?" 
The doggy kept running and barking, and led Joy to where the ambulance was. Joy found out that a little boy had fallen down, and he was hurt. Joy called out to the ambulance, and the driver stopped to help the boy. 
The driver smiled at Joy and said, "Thanks for peeking around, little girl. You saved the day!" Everyone was very happy, and the little boy was okay. The hairy dog even licked Joy's face, to say a big thank you. 
Joy and the doggy happily walked back to the park, and Joy was proud of her brave act. She knew she had made the world a better place. 
The End.

Once upon a time, there was a unique cat. This cat liked to hide under the big tree. One day, a dog came to the tree. The dog wanted to play with the cat.
The cat did not want to play. The cat said, "No, let me be." The dog was sad, but he went away to find another friend. The cat stayed under the tree, happy to be alone.
Later, the cat saw the dog playing with a bird. The cat felt lonely and wanted to join them. The cat learned that it is good to let others play with you. Sharing and playing together makes everyone happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to read her big book called a novel. One day, Sue was very troubled. Her novel was lost! She looked everywhere for it, but she could not find it.
Sue went to her friend Tom and said, "Tom, I can't find my novel. Can you help me?" Tom was a kind boy and wanted to help Sue. They looked everywhere for the novel, but they still could not find it. Sue was very sad.
Then, Tom had an idea. He said, "Sue, let's ask the dog to help us." They went to the dog, and the dog sniffed around. The dog found the novel under a big tree. Sue was so happy! Tom and the dog rescued her novel. Sue thanked them and they all sat down to read the novel together.

Once upon a time, in a far away land, there was a thin tree. The tree was very wise and could answer any question. Many people came to the tree to ask for wisdom.
One day, a little boy named Tim came to the tree. He was sad because he did not know how to tie his shoe. He asked the tree, "Can you help me tie my shoe?" The tree answered, "Yes, I can help you. First, make a loop. Then, make another loop. Finally, put one loop through the other loop and pull tight."
Tim did what the tree said and tied his shoe. He was very happy and thanked the tree for its wisdom. From that day on, Tim and the thin tree became good friends. They would talk and play together every day. And the tree always had an answer for Tim's questions, helping him learn new things.

The sun shined in the big sky. Tommy was playing outside in the garden and he felt warm. As he walked around, he noticed something different in the ground. It was a step. He touched the step and it felt warm too. Suddenly, the step started to melt!
Tommy got scared and he ran to get his mom. "Mom! Mom! The step is melting!"
Tommy's mom laughed. "It's just the sun, Tommy," she said. "It's making the step a bit different."
Tommy felt relieved. He knew now that the step wasn't melting, it was just feeling a bit different. Tommy ran around and played in the garden happily for the rest of the day.

Teams that toured other countries often became frustrated by lbws given against them ; there was often an assumption of national bias by home umpires against visiting teams . Several studies investigating this perception have suggested that home batsmen are sometimes less likely than visiting batsmen to be lbw . However , the data is based on lbw decisions awarded , not on the success-rate of appeals to the umpire . Fraser points out that it is impossible to determine from these studies if any of the decisions were wrong , particularly as the lbw law can have different interpretations , or if other factors such as pitch conditions and technique were involved . A 2006 study examined the effect that neutral umpires had on the rate of lbws . Although the reasons were again ambiguous , it found that lbws increased slightly under neutral umpires regardless of team or location .

The first dent to morale came after about a week when the volunteers were first issued ranks in the Rhodesian Army . In the eyes of some of the French-speaking soldiers , the ranks assigned appeared to have been chosen almost at random by their superiors , and did not reflect their actual respective levels of training , ability and experience . Some men who considered themselves to have been overlooked began to have problems with discipline . The brazen attitude of most of the company 's soldiers jarred strongly with that of their Rhodesian commanders , who had high standards regarding presentation and dress which many of the Frenchmen had little inclination to meet .

One sunny day, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mommy. Lily loved to swing high in the sky. She would laugh and shout, "Swing me higher, Mommy!" Her mommy would push her higher and higher.
In the park, Lily saw a big box. "What is that?" she asked her mommy. "It's a mystery, sweetie," her mommy said. They opened the box and found lots of yummy treats inside. Lily was so happy and excited.
Just then, a little boy named Tommy came running up to them. "That's my box!" he cried. Lily felt sad, but she knew she had to do the right thing. "I'm sorry, Tommy," she said, giving the box back to him. But Tommy had a big smile on his face. "That's okay, Lily! We can share the yummy treats and be friends!" And so they did, and they all had a fun day at the park together.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly girl named Sue. Sue loved to share her toys with her friends. She had a favorite toy, a mixer, that she would use to mix pretend food for her friends.
One sunny day, Sue and her friends were playing in the park. They were all taking turns using the mixer to mix pretend cake. Sue was happy to share her mixer with her friends because it made everyone happy.
Then, something unexpected happened. A big dog came running into the park and took the mixer in his mouth. Sue and her friends were scared, but the dog was just playing. The dog ran back to them, dropped the mixer, and wagged his tail. Sue and her friends laughed and played with the dog. They even let the dog join their game and pretended to mix food for him. They all had a fun day sharing and playing together.
In the reserve race , Cambridge 's Goldie defeated Oxford 's Isis in the fastest time ever , while Cambridge won the Women 's Boat Race .

Emily was a chubby three-year-old girl. She liked to play in the garden and explore the world around her. 
One day, when Emily was in the garden, she found a puddle. She was so excited that she kneeled down and put her hands in the puddle. She cupped the water in her hands and made little splashes on the ground.
The water felt very nice and Emily was so happy. She stayed in the garden for hours and played with the puddle. She splashed around and laughed until she was very tired. 
Finally, Emily kneeled down and said goodbye to the puddle. She waved goodbye and looked forward to coming back and playing in the puddle again.

Once there was a princess who wanted to be happy. She decided to pray to a special magic magnet. But when the princess got the magnet it was fake! She was very sad. 
But the princess didn't give up. She prayed more and more and more until the magnet became real. She was so happy and smiled all day. 
But then one day the magnetic forces were too strong and the magnet stuck the princess to the wall! She was stuck there for days and no one could help her. The princess was so sad. 
Finally, the princess was rescued and she vowed never to pray for another fake magnet again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, round moon. The moon liked to sit high up in the sky at night. It would watch over the animals and people as they slept.
One day, a little bird saw the moon and thought it looked like a fun place to sit too. So, the bird flew up, up, up, to try to sit on the moon. But, the sky was very high and it was dangerous for the little bird to fly so high.
A kind wind saw the little bird and knew it was dangerous for the bird to fly so high. The wind gently blew the bird back down to its nest. The little bird was safe and could still see the moon from its nest. From then on, the bird knew it was better to watch the moon from the ground. And every night, the bird and the moon would sit and watch each other from far away.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a gloomy day. The sky was very gray, and the rain was falling. A little girl named Lily wanted to go outside and play but she couldn't because of the rain. She felt sad and looked out the window, hoping the rain would stop soon.
Later that day, the rain stopped and the sky became clear. Lily went outside to play. She saw something shiny on the ground. It was a little star! The star was lost and wanted to go back to the sky. Lily wanted to help the star, so she picked it up and held it in her hand.
Lily had an idea. She climbed up a big hill with the star. When they got to the top, Lily threw the star up into the sky as hard as she could. The star flew up into the air and twinkled brightly. The star was so happy to be back in the sky, and Lily was happy to have helped her new friend. They waved goodbye and promised to meet again someday.

Once upon a time, there was a big race in the park. Many animals joined the race. There was a fast rabbit, a slow turtle, and a foolish dog.
The foolish dog had very big ears. He liked to show off and make others laugh. He thought he could win the race just by being funny. So, the dog did not run fast like the rabbit or slow like the turtle. Instead, he jumped around, making his big ears flap in the wind.
In the end, the rabbit won the race because he was very fast. The turtle came in second place because he never stopped trying. The foolish dog did not win, but he made everyone laugh with his big ears. And that day, all the animals had fun in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby dancer named Lily. She loved to dance and play with her friends. Every day, she would take her pink shoes and dance in the park.
One sunny day, Lily went to the park to dance. She saw a big, round thing on the ground. She did not know what it was. She thought it was a ball. So, she kicked it and started to dance around it.
But, the big round thing was not a ball! It was a big, sleepy cat! The cat woke up and saw Lily dancing. The cat liked her dance and started to dance too. Lily and the cat became best friends and danced together every day.

Innis maintained that scholars had no place in active politics and that instead , they should devote themselves , first to research on public problems , and then to the production of knowledge based on critical thought . He saw the university , with its emphasis on dialogue , open-mindedness and skepticism , as an institution that could foster such thinking and research . " The university could provide an environment " , he wrote , " as free as possible from the biases of the various institutions that form the state , so that its intellectuals could continue to seek out and explore other perspectives . "

One day, a cat and a dog went on a walk. They saw a big mill. The mill was very old. The cat said, "Let's go inside." The dog said, "Okay, let's include our friend, the bird." They all went into the mill together.
Inside the mill, they saw a silly man. The man was dancing and laughing. The cat, dog, and bird laughed too. They thought the man was funny. They wanted to dance and laugh with him.
But then, something unexpected happened. The silly man was not a man at all! He was a big puppet! The cat, dog, and bird were very surprised. They looked around and saw a little girl. The little girl was holding the puppet strings. She laughed and said, "I made you all laugh!" The cat, dog, and bird laughed again. They had fun with the little girl and her puppet.

Jim looked out the front window of his house and noticed something was strange. He saw a green box by the door. He ran out and opened the box excitedly. Inside, he found a jar of jam. Jim was so excited he could hardly contain himself. He shouted out "Welcome!"
He took the jam back inside and ran to his mom. He said to her, "Mom, look what I found outsideâjam!" His mom smiled and thanked him for being so excited. She suggested that they invite the jam over for a visit.
The next day, the family welcomed the jam inside. They showed it around the house and made sure it was comfortable. Later on, they all ate together happily.
As they were enjoying the jam, Jim noticed something strange was happening. The jam was turning green. His mom smiled and said, "That jam was a special green jam from a secret store. I thought it would be a great surprise for you today." Jim smiled excitedly and thanked his mom. He loved his surprise and was happy to share it with his family.

Once upon a time, there was a huge tree in the forest. The tree was so big that all the animals liked to play around it. One day, a little squirrel named Squeaky wanted to measure how big the tree was. So, he asked his friend, a wise old owl named Oliver, to help him.
Oliver said, "I can help you, Squeaky. Let's start at the bottom and go all the way to the tip of the tree." They began to measure the tree together, but when they reached the middle, they heard a loud noise. It was a big surprise!
A family of birds was living inside the tree. The mommy bird said, "Why are you making noise? My babies are trying to sleep." Squeaky and Oliver said sorry and told the bird family that they were just measuring the tree. The mommy bird laughed and said, "You don't need to measure it. It's the biggest tree in the forest!" So, Squeaky and Oliver stopped measuring and played with the bird family instead.

Jessica was so excited to go on her first nature walk. She ran through the meadow, admiring all the beautiful trees and plants. Suddenly, she heard a sound. It sounded like a pipe. Jessica stopped and followed the sound. She wondered what it could be. 
Finally, she saw it. It was a beautiful, shining silver pipe. She smiled, and ran to it. She picked up the pipe and shook it. She listened carefully to the music it made. Jessica was amazed. She ran back to her mom and showed her the pipe.
Her mom smiled and said, "That's a penny whistle. It's a special type of pipe that you blow into and make music. I have one too. We can play together". Jessica was so excited to learn about the pipe. She knew she'd use it for lots of fun. 
Jessica will never forget the day she found the beautiful silver penny whistle. From that day on, she couldn't wait to go on nature walks and listen to the music of the pipe.

A 2007 report commissioned by the Haifa Municipality calls for the construction of more hotels , a ferry line between Haifa , Acre and Caesarea , development of the western anchorage of the port as a recreation and entertainment area , and an expansion of the local airport and port to accommodate international travel and cruise ships .

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a lucky jacket with a zipper. He loved to wear it all the time. The jacket made Tim feel happy.
One day, Tim saw a small dog. The dog was lost and sad. Tim wanted to help the dog find its home. He thought, "I can act like a hero with my lucky jacket." So, he put on his jacket and zipped the zipper up.
Tim and the dog walked and walked. They found the dog's home. The dog's family was so happy. They said, "Thank you, Tim!" Tim felt very lucky to have his jacket with the zipper. He knew he could be a hero when he wore it.

Anna and Ben like to play with boats. They have many boats of different colors and sizes. They go to the pond and sail their boats on the water. They have fun watching their boats go fast or slow, turn or stop.
One day, they find a new boat in the toy store. It is big and red and shiny. It has a sail and a flag and a wheel. Anna and Ben want to buy it, but it is too expensive. They ask their mom if they can have it, but she says no. She says they have enough boats already.
Anna and Ben are sad. They go back to the pond and sail their old boats. But they still think about the new boat. They wish they could have it.
Then they see a boy with the new boat. He is sailing it on the pond. He looks happy. Anna and Ben go to him and say hello. They ask him if they can play with his boat. The boy says yes. He says his name is Sam and he got the boat for his birthday. He says he likes to share his toys.
Anna and Ben are happy. They take turns sailing the new boat with Sam. They have fun together. They make a new friend. They learn that the new boat is not too big for the pond. It fits just right. They also learn that their old boats are still good. They can play with them and with the new boat. They have more boats and more fun.

Once upon a time, in a small house, lived a boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat pears. One day, he found an unknown pear tree in his yard. He was very happy to see it. The tree had many big, sweet pears. Tim wanted to eat them all.
Before Tim could eat the pears, he had to wash them. Tim took a big pear from the tree and went inside. He turned on the water and washed the pear. The water was cold and made the pear shiny and clean. Tim was excited to eat the clean pear.
Tim took a big bite of the pear. It was the best pear he had ever eaten. He shared the pear with his mom and dad. They all loved the unknown pear tree in their yard. And from that day on, they washed and ate pears every day, always happy and full.

Tom and Lily are playing with blocks. They have many blocks of different shapes and colors. They like to build towers and houses with them.
"Look, I made a big tower!" Tom says. He shows Lily his tower of red and blue blocks. It is very tall and has a circle on top.
"Wow, that is nice!" Lily says. She likes Tom's tower, but she wants to make something different. She has a yellow and green block in her hand. It is not a circle, it is a square.
"I want to put this on your tower," Lily says. She tries to put the square on the circle, but it does not fit. It falls down and makes a loud noise.
"Hey, don't do that!" Tom says. He is angry. He does not want Lily to ruin his tower. He pushes Lily away and grabs the square.
"No, this is mine!" Lily says. She is sad. She wants to play with Tom, but he does not share. She pulls the square and tries to take it back.
They both pull and tug on the block. They do not see that their tower is shaking. It is about to fall.
"Stop, stop!" a voice says. It is Mom. She sees the children fighting and the tower wobbling. She runs to them and catches the tower before it crashes.
"Tom, Lily, what are you doing?" Mom says. She is not happy. She does not like to see them fight. She puts the tower on the floor and looks at them.
"Sorry, Mom," Tom and Lily say. They feel bad. They know they were wrong.
"Can you say sorry to each other?" Mom says. She wants them to be nice and make up.
"Sorry, Tom," Lily says. She gives him the square. She does not need it. She can find another block.
"Sorry, Lily," Tom says. He gives her the circle. He does not mind. He can use another block.
They hug and smile. They are friends again.
"Good, now can you play nicely?" Mom says. She is glad. She likes to see them happy.
"Yes, Mom," Tom and Lily say. They nod and look at their blocks.
They have an idea. They can make something together. They can use the circle and the square and the other blocks. They can make an open house. They can put the circle on the door and the square on the window. They can invite Mom to see their house.
They start to build. They are having fun. They are playing with blocks.

Once upon a time, there was a wealthy man named Tom. Tom had many things, but he was not happy. He wanted to receive a special gift to make him happy.
One day, Tom went for a walk. He saw a big puddle on the ground. He jumped in the puddle and got all wet. Tom laughed and felt happy.
From that day on, Tom knew that the best gifts were not things he could buy. The best gifts were the simple things, like jumping in a puddle. Tom was happy and shared his story with others.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside with his ball. One day, he kicked his ball very hard and it flew far away. Tim felt sorry because he did not want to lose his ball.
Tim went to look for his ball. He saw a big tree and thought his ball might be there. He walked to the tree and saw a girl named Sara. Sara was kneeling by the tree, looking at something. Tim asked Sara if she saw his ball.
Sara said, "Yes, I found your ball. But first, let's look at this cool thing I found!" Tim and Sara looked at a big rock. On the rock, there was a word: "oxygen." They did not know what it meant, but they liked how it sounded. Tim and Sara laughed and played with the ball and the rock. They became good friends and always remembered the word "oxygen" as their special secret word.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the beach with his mom. They saw a big rock near the water. Tim wanted to climb the rock, but his mom was troubled. She said, "Tim, be careful when you climb. It can be dangerous."
Tim started to climb the rock. He was very careful. He put one foot up, then the other. He held on tight with his hands. When he got to the top, he saw a little bird with a hurt wing. The bird was sad and couldn't fly.
Tim called his mom to help the bird. They took the bird home and took care of it until its wing was better. The bird was happy and flew away. Tim learned that if you are careful and kind, you can help others.

At 17 : 20 McCay signalled Bridges that large numbers of unwounded men were leaving the battlefield and heading for the beaches . This was followed by Maclagan asking for urgent artillery fire support , onto Gun Ridge , as his left was under a heavy attack and at 18 : 16 Owen reported the left flank was " rapidly " being forced to retire . At dusk Maclagan made his way to Bridges headquarters and when asked for his opinion replied " It 's touch and go . If the Turks come on in mass formation ... I don 't think anything can stop them . " As it got dark the Turkish artillery ceased firing , and although small arms fire continued on both sides , the effects were limited when firing blind . Darkness also provided the opportunity to start digging more substantial trenches and to resupply the troops with water and ammunition .

Lily and Ben wanted to build a snowman in the yard. They put on their hats, coats, gloves and boots and went outside. The snow was soft and white and cold.
They rolled a big ball of snow for the body and a smaller one for the head. They found a carrot for the nose, two rocks for the eyes and a stick for the mouth. They looked for something to make the arms, but they could not find any more sticks.
"Let's go inside and ask Mom for help," Lily said.
They ran back to the house and opened the door. Mom was in the living room, decorating the Christmas tree. She had a box of shiny ornaments that sparkled in the light.
"Mom, can we have some ornaments for our snowman?" Ben asked.
"Sure, you can have some of these old ones that I don't use anymore," Mom said. She gave them a red scarf, a blue hat, a green button and a silver star.
"Thank you, Mom!" Lily and Ben said. They hugged Mom and went back outside.
They wrapped the scarf around the snowman's neck, put the hat on his head, the button on his chest and the star on his hand. They stepped back and admired their work.
"Our snowman looks so pretty!" Lily said.
"And so calm!" Ben said.
They smiled and played with their snowman until it was time for dinner. They had a lot of fun building their snowman with the ornaments.

Once upon a time there was a small, gray shield. It was very special. Every day the shield would sit in the corner and do nothing.
One day, a monster came along and wanted to take the shield away. The shield was scared and tried to run away, but it was too late. The monster grabbed the shield and took it away.
The shield was very sad, so it sat down and started to cry. But no matter how much it cried, it was still stuck with the monster.
The monster kept the shield away from its home forever. The shield was so sad and it never got to see its corner again.

Once upon a time, in a peaceful town, there was a big building. Inside the building, there were many bikes. A little boy named Tim loved to ride his bike every day. He would ride around the town, waving to his friends and having fun.
One day, Tim saw a girl who was sad. She didn't have a bike to ride. Tim thought for a moment and had an idea. He went back to the building and found a bike for the girl. Tim gave the bike to her and her face lit up with a big smile.
They both rode their bikes together, laughing and playing. All the kids in the town joined them, and they had a great time. The peaceful town was full of happy children riding bikes. The moral of the story is that sharing with others can make everyone happy.

One day, a little insect was in the garden. He liked to listen to the birds sing. The insect had a friend, a bossy ant. The bossy ant always told the insect what to do.
One sunny day, the bossy ant told the insect, "You must help me carry food." The insect did not want to help, but he did it anyway. They walked and walked, carrying food together. They were very tired.
Then, something unexpected happened. A big wind came and took the food away. The bossy ant was sad, but the insect was happy. He said, "Now we can listen to the birds again!" The bossy ant smiled and they both listened to the birds sing. The bossy ant learned to have fun and not be so bossy anymore.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One was an elephant, the other a gorilla. They were the best of friends and did everything together.
One day, they heard a strange noise outside. When they looked out, they saw a helicopter!
"Let's go and see it!" said the elephant.
But the gorilla was worried. He had never seen a helicopter before. 
"What if it wants to fight?" said the gorilla.
"Don't worry" said the elephant. "I'll protect you."
The two friends walked outside. The helicopter was hovering in the sky. 
"See, it's just a helicopter" said the elephant.
The two friends looked up in awe. Suddenly the helicopter flew away and they laughed. 
"It was nothing to be worried about" said the elephant. 
The two friends hugged and laughed. They were so happy that nothing had happened. 
And they lived happily ever after!

Once there was a friendly brown bear named Bear. He had many friends in the port, including a fish named Fish. Each morning, Bear and Fish would go to the port to play. One day, Fish grabbed a stick and said, "Let's play catch!"
Bear was so excited he could hardly contain himself. He shouted, "Yes!" and they began to play. As they threw the stick back and forth, Bear and Fish laughed and had so much fun.
Soon it was time to go, so Fish threw the stick one last time. However, Bear's paws were so big that he missed it. Fish started to laugh.
"That's okay," Bear said. "Let's just keep playing tomorrow!" Bear and Fish said goodbye and each went their own way, but they were both thinking about how much fun they had in the port that day.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had an ancient toy boat. He loved to play with it in the pond near his house. One day, he saw a big tree branch in the water. Tim thought it would be fun to use the branch to make a bridge for his boat.
Tim tried to move the branch, but it was too heavy. He asked his friend, Sam, for help. Sam said, "Let's try together. I think we can do it." They pushed and pulled, and finally, they moved the branch to make a bridge.
Tim and Sam put the boat in the water. They watched as it floated under the bridge. They were so happy that they succeeded. They played with the boat all day, and they knew that they could do anything if they worked together.

One day, a little girl named Lily was playing in her room. She had a big bowl and she liked to imagine it was a magic bowl. Lily was very brave and loved to go on adventures with her magic bowl.
One day, Lily was playing with her bowl and said, "Magic bowl, take me to a fun place!" Suddenly, the bowl started to shake and it took Lily to a land full of toys and candy. Lily was so happy and started to play with all the toys.
While Lily was playing, a big toy bear came to life and said, "Hi Lily! I am the toy bear king. You are very brave to come to our land. Will you help us find our lost toy friends?" Lily said, "Yes! I will help you!" They looked all over the land and found all the lost toys. The toy bear king was very happy and thanked Lily for her help. Then, Lily went back home with her magic bowl and told her mom and dad about her amazing adventure.

One day, a girl named Mia and her mom went to the store. They wanted to buy cocoa to make a great hot drink. Mia was very happy because she loved cocoa.
In the store, Mia saw a boy named Tim. He was with his dad. They were also buying cocoa. Mia said, "Hi, Tim! Are you making cocoa too?" Tim said, "Yes, Mia! We love cocoa. It is great!"
Mia and Tim passed the cocoa to their mom and dad. They paid for the cocoa and went home. Mia and Tim both made great cocoa with their families. They were very happy and warm.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was three years old and he loved vegetables. He especially loved celery. Every day after school, he would come home and eat a long and crunchy celery stick.
One day, he tried something weird. He put peanut butter on his celery stick. He scooped some peanut butter onto the celery and took a bite. It was strange, but he liked it.
The little boy couldnât wait to show his friends. He ran to the playground and told them all about his weird snack. His friends couldnât understand why anyone would put peanut butter on celery. But the little boy said it was delicious and he kept eating it.
Finally, the little boyâs friends all gave it a try. They all agreed it was strange, but yummy too. Now all the kids love eating celery with peanut butter. The little boy was happy to have shared something he understood with all his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She had a new bedroom in her home. Amy loved her bedroom because it was big and had her favorite toys.
One day, Amy heard a noise in her bedroom. She was scared. She yelled for her mom. Her mom came and looked around, but she did not see anything. She told Amy that it was just her toys making noise. Amy felt better.
The next day, Amy heard the noise again. She yelled for her mom. This time, her mom found a little kitten hiding under the bed. Amy was so happy! She named the kitten Fluffy. Now, Amy and Fluffy play in her new bedroom every day.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She sat in her garden and looked for something to pick. She saw a worm and picked it up. Suddenly, the worm spoke, telling her it wanted to go back to its family, but the girl didn't know where that was.
The girl asked everyone she knew, but no one knew the worm's family so she decided she had to help the worm by herself.
The girl went on a long journey, trying to find the worm's family, but it was unknown to her where they were. She looked under rocks and in grass, everywhere she could think of, but she couldn't find the family.
She felt so sad because it looked like the worm would never find its family. But suddenly she heard a voice and saw many worms coming towards her. The family was so happy to see the worm that the girl had brought back and they thanked her for reuniting them.
The little girl was so happy that the worm found its family and went back to her garden with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to eat peaches. They were her favorite fruit. One day, she found a big, orange peach under a tree. She was so happy and took it home.
Lily wanted to show the peach to her mom, but her mom was busy. So, she left the peach on the table and went to play with her toys. When she came back, the peach was gone. Lily was sad and looked everywhere, but the peach had disappeared.
Lily asked her mom if she saw the peach, but her mom said no. She asked her dad, but he didn't see it either. Lily was very sad and cried. She never found her big, orange peach again.

Once upon a time, in a big garden, there was a pretty flower named Lily. Lily lived with her friends, the bees and the birds. They all played together every day.
One day, Lily heard a little girl say, "I want to eat something delicious." Lily thought, "Maybe I can help." So, she called her friend, Bee. "Bee, can you help the girl find something delicious to eat?"
Bee buzzed and said, "Yes, Lily! I know where to find some sweet honey." So, Bee flew to the girl and said, "Follow me, I will show you something delicious." The girl was happy and followed Bee.
But, surprise! When they reached the honey, it was not honey at all. It was a big, yummy cake! The girl was so happy and said, "Thank you, Bee and Lily!" And they all enjoyed the delicious cake together.

Once there was a cool cop. His uniform was very bright and it shone and glowed in the dark. He loved to go on night patrol and show off his glowing suit. 
One night another cop came to visit. He saw the bright uniform and exclaimed with amazement. He asked the cool cop, "Where did you get that suit? It looks so awesome!"
The cool cop replied, "I'm so glad you asked! It was a special gift from my grandmother. She said that I should always remember to glow, no matter what time of day it is!" 
The second cop nodded and said, "That's very wise advice indeed!"

Once upon a time, there was a wise cat. The cat loved to question things. One day, the cat found a letter on the ground.
The cat looked at the letter and said, "What is this? Who is it for?" The cat did not know what to do with the letter. Then, the cat had an idea. The cat would take the letter to the wise owl.
The wise owl looked at the letter and smiled. The owl said, "This letter is not for a person. It is for you, wise cat!" The cat was very surprised. The cat opened the letter and found a toy inside. The wise cat and the wise owl played with the toy and had lots of fun.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the bus stop. He saw a big, red bus coming. Tim was happy because he liked to ride the bus. It was fun to go up and down the hills.
On the bus, Tim met a new friend. Her name was Sue. Sue had a tasty snack. She shared her snack with Tim. They both liked the snack a lot. Sue mentioned that she got the snack from her mom.
Then, the bus stopped. Tim and Sue were sad because it was time to go home. They said goodbye and got off the bus. Tim walked home, but he felt sad because he missed his new friend Sue. The day was not so fun anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a big powerful dog named Max. Max lived in a small house with his best friend, a little girl named Lily. They loved to play together all day.
One day, Lily and Max were playing near a table. Max seemed very happy as he wagged his tail. He jumped up and down, and then he bumped the table. The table shook, and a glass of water fell on the floor. Splash!
Lily and Max looked at the water on the floor. Lily said, "Oh no! We need to clean this up." So, they got a towel and wiped the water. Then they went back to playing, being more careful near the table. They had a fun and happy day.

Jimmy was a very happy boy. He loved to play with his toys. Today he decided to take his cart and go for a walk. 
As Jimmy was walking, he saw a nice park. He was so excited that he ran to the entrance.
When he got there, he saw his friend Jenny. "Hi Jenny," Jimmy said. "Want to come sit with me in my cart?"
Jenny said, "Yes, let's sit together! This is going to be so nice!"
So Jimmy and Jenny both sat in the cart and had a great time. They rode around the park and laughed. It was the best day ever!

Lisa loved to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna. Anna had a delicate dress and long hair. Lisa always took good care of Anna and brushed her hair every day.
One day, Lisa went to the park with her mom and Anna. She saw a big pond with some ducks and fish. She wanted to play near the water and feed the ducks. She asked her mom if she could go. Her mom said yes, but told her to be careful and not go too close to the water.
Lisa walked to the pond with Anna and some bread. She threw some bread to the ducks and they came to eat. Lisa was happy and smiled. She saw a big log floating in the water. She thought it would be fun to put Anna on the log and pretend she was a pirate. She walked closer to the water and reached out to put Anna on the log.
But the log was not a log. It was an alligator. The alligator opened its mouth and snapped at Anna. Lisa screamed and dropped Anna. The alligator caught Anna in its teeth and dragged her into the water.
Lisa ran back to her mom and cried. She told her what happened. Her mom hugged her and said she was sorry. She said that alligators are dangerous animals and they should never go near them. She said that Lisa should always listen to her and be careful.
Lisa learned a lesson that day. She learned that she should not play with things she does not know. She learned that she should respect nature and its creatures. She learned that she should cherish her toys and not take risks with them. She missed Anna, but she was glad she was safe. She hoped that Anna would find a new friend in the pond. She said a silent goodbye to Anna and thanked her for being her doll. She said she would always remember her.

One day, a girl named Sue got a new pet. It was a cute and attractive cat. Sue was very happy. She loved her cat and took good care of it. They played together and had fun.
One day, while they were playing, the cat said, "Sue, you are nice to me. You make me happy." Sue was surprised. She did not know her pet could talk! She said, "Wow, you can talk! This is fun. We can be best friends and talk all day."
But then, the cat said, "Sue, I need to tell you something important. It is good to be nice to others, not just pets. It makes everyone happy." Sue thought about it and said, "You are right. I will be nice to everyone now."
From that day on, Sue was nice to everyone she met. She learned that being kind to others made her happy too. And her talking cat was always there to remind her of the important lesson she learned.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to pinch things. Her mama called it "junk". She loved to pinch it and pull it apart.
One day, the little girl found a box. Inside the box was a big surprise! It was a big, fluffy puppy. The puppy was so cute, the little girl just had to pinch it.
The puppy was ready to play. It jumped around the room and barked with excitement. The little girl was so happy. She was able to pinch the puppy and it just kept on playing.
The little girl and the puppy played together every day. They ran and jumped and the little girl even pinched the puppy's fur. The little girl and the puppy were the best of friends.

Jack was frustrated. He wanted to get to the bathroom, but his mom said he had to wait. He couldn't wait any longer, so Jack jumped from his chair, and ran to the bathroom.
Jack smiled when he got there. He was happy he was able to get there so fast. But as soon as he opened the door, he found it was already full! His mom was in there taking a bath.
Jack was frustrated again. He didn't know what he should do. He wanted to take a bath too, but he couldn't go in while his mom was in there. Suddenly he had an idea. He decided to wait outside the bathroom until his mom finished.
At last the bathroom door opened, and Jack ran inside. His mom had finished her bath. Quickly, Jack got in and started to play. He was so happy to finally have his turn in the bathroom.

One day, a polite frog named Fred went out to play. He liked to jump high and far. The sun was hot, so he looked for a wet place to cool down. He found a big puddle and jumped in.
Fred saw a small bug named Ben near the puddle. Ben was sad because he could not jump. He wanted to play with Fred, but he was too small. "I wish I could jump like you," said Ben.
Fred wanted to help Ben. He had an idea. He told Ben to climb on his back. Ben did as he was told. Fred jumped high and far with Ben on his back. They both laughed and played all day. Now, Ben was happy because he could jump too.

Once upon a time in a big forest, there was a bear. This bear was very long. One day, the long bear saw a sign. The sign had a picture of a bear and an arrow. The long bear thought, "I am a bear. I should follow the arrow."
The long bear walked and walked. He followed the arrow on the sign. He saw another sign with a bear and an arrow. The long bear was very happy. He thought, "I will find something good at the end."
At last, the long bear found a big box. He was very excited. He thought there would be food inside. But when he opened the box, he found a long, soft bed. The long bear was tired from walking. He lay down on the bed and slept. When he woke up, he was so happy. He had the best sleep ever. The signs had led him to a perfect bed just for him.

One day, a big dog and a little cat had a quarrel. They were not happy with each other. The big dog wanted to play in the rain, but the little cat did not like rain. The big dog said, "Rain is fun! We can jump and splash!" But the little cat said, "No, I do not like getting wet."
The rain started to fall, and the big dog ran outside. He jumped and splashed in the puddles. The little cat stayed inside and watched from the window. She saw the big dog having fun, but she still did not want to get wet.
After a while, the rain stopped, and the sun came out. The big dog came back inside and shook off the water. He looked at the little cat and said, "I had fun in the rain, but I am sorry we had a quarrel. Let's play inside now." The little cat agreed, and they played together happily.

Once there was an old forest. In the forest, there lived a family of rabbits. One day, the rabbit family decided to have a picnic. The rabbits unpacked all their food, and then the baby rabbit started clapping. His parents were so proud and clapped along with him. All around the forest, the birds and animals heard the clapping and started to clap too! Not long after, there were so many different creatures clapping together in the old forest. It was a beautiful moment that nobody would forget. 
The clapping echoed through the forest until the sun began to set. Everyone said goodbye and went to their homes for the night. But the memory of the clapping in the old forest remained with them. 
 
The End.

Lily liked to jog with her dad in the park. She felt happy and strong when she ran. She saw many things: trees, birds, flowers, dogs, and people. Sometimes she waved at them and said hello.
One day, she saw a big, black dog with a red collar. It looked scary and angry. It barked loudly and ran towards Lily and her dad. Lily was afraid and wanted to run away.
But her dad was wise. He told her to stay calm and not to scream. He said, "Lily, don't worry. The dog is just playing. He won't hurt us. We just need to be friendly and gentle. Look, he has a name tag. His name is Max. Can you say hi to Max?"
Lily listened to her dad and tried to be brave. She said, "Hi, Max. You are a big dog. Do you like to jog too?" The dog stopped barking and wagged his tail. He licked Lily's hand and sniffed her dad's leg. He seemed happy and friendly.
Lily smiled and petted the dog. She said, "You are a nice dog, Max. I like you. Do you have a home?" The dog nodded and pointed his nose to a house nearby. There was a man standing at the door. He waved and said, "Sorry, I'm Max's owner. He escaped from the room when I opened the door. He loves to jog and chase things. He didn't mean to scare you. He's a good boy."
Lily's dad said, "It's okay. We're not scared. We like Max. He's a good jogger. Maybe we can jog with him again sometime." The man said, "Sure, that would be great. Come on, Max. Let's go back to the room. Say bye to Lily and her dad." Max barked and wagged his tail. He said bye to Lily and her dad and followed his owner to the house.
Lily and her dad continued to jog in the park. They felt happy and safe. They learned that sometimes scary things are not so scary after all. They just need to be wise and friendly.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a little boy named Tim. Tim was a troubled boy because he always wanted to catch things. He tried to catch butterflies, birds, and even his pet cat! His parent, Mom, always told him to be gentle with the animals.
One day, while playing outside, Tim saw a big, red ball bouncing down the street. He thought, "I want to catch that ball!" So, he ran as fast as he could, trying to grab it. The ball kept bouncing away, but Tim did not give up. He chased the ball all the way to the park.
At the park, Tim finally caught the ball. He was so happy! His parent, Mom, came running after him. She was worried but also proud that Tim caught the ball. Tim learned that it was more fun to catch a ball than to catch animals. From that day on, Tim played with his big, red ball and left the animals alone.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk. He saw an enormous alligator by the river. The alligator was green and had big teeth. Tim was scared, but the alligator said, "Don't be scared. I am a nice alligator."
Tim asked, "What are you doing here?" The alligator said, "I like to count the fish that swim by." Tim thought that was fun. So, he sat down next to the alligator and they started to count the fish together. One, two, three, four, five fish swam by.
After they counted the fish, the alligator said, "Thank you for counting with me." Tim smiled and said, "You're welcome. I had fun." Then, Tim went back home and told his mom about the enormous alligator who liked to count fish.

Once upon a time, there was a rainy day. Little Tommy had wanted to go out and play, but the rain was drenching everything. So he hopped, skipped and jumped around the house, instead. 
Suddenly, there was a knock on the door. It was Grandpa! He had a big, black cane and a large umbrella in his hand. Grandpa said, "Let's go out and have some fun, even though it is wet!"
Tommy giggled, "But how can we do that?"
Grandpa winked and said, "I will provide!" He opened the umbrella and they went outside.
It was wet, but together they began to splash in the puddles. The cold water splashed onto their faces, and it felt so amusing! They laughed with delight, and before long the sun was shining and it was dry again. Grandpa had provided lots of fun for little Tommy, on a very wet and rainy day.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who was very messy. She loved making messes and couldn't help it.
One day, her mom gave her a special gift. It was a beautiful necklace, with a pink and sparkly gem in the middle. The girl was so excited and hugged her mom with a big smile on her face.
But then the girl realized that the necklace was a bit messy, as she had been playing with it. So her mom showed her how to polish it.
She took a cloth and slowly started polishing the necklace. She went round and round and round, until the gem was brighter and shinier than ever!
The girl and her mom hugged again, and the girl loved her special gift even more now it was beautifully polished.

Once upon a time, there was a furry dog named Spot. Spot liked to play near the fireplace. He liked to feel warm and cozy. One day, Spot saw something new near the fireplace. It was a big puzzle. Spot wanted to complete the puzzle.
Spot started to put the puzzle pieces together. He was having so much fun. But then, something unexpected happened. Spot heard a strange noise. It came from behind the fireplace. Spot was scared, but he wanted to find out what it was.
Spot went behind the fireplace and saw a little bird. The bird was scared too. Spot helped the bird find its way back outside. The bird was so happy, it gave Spot a special puzzle piece. Spot went back to the puzzle and put the special piece in. The puzzle was now complete. Spot and the bird became best friends, and they played together every day.

Oldham became the world 's manufacturing centre for cotton spinning in the second half of the 19th century . In 1851 , over 30 % of Oldham 's population was employed within the textile sector , compared to 5 % across Great Britain . It overtook the major urban centres of Manchester and Bolton as the result of a mill building boom in the 1860s and 1870s , a period during which Oldham became the most productive cotton-spinning town in the world . In 1871 , Oldham had more spindles than any country in the world except the United States , and in 1909 , was spinning more cotton than France and Germany combined . By 1911 there were 16. 4 million spindles in Oldham , compared with a total of 58 million in the United Kingdom and 143. 5 million in the world ; in 1928 , with the construction of the UK 's largest textile factory Oldham reached its manufacturing zenith . At its peak , there were more than 360 mills , operating night and day ;

One day, a wise old cat saw a little bird by a pond. The bird was thirsty and wanted to drink water. The cat wanted to have fun and play with the bird.
"Little bird, I will help you drink," said the wise cat. The bird was scared, but the cat looked kind. The bird let the cat help it. The cat put its paw in the water and let the bird drink from it. The bird was happy and they both had fun.
But then, a big dog came and saw them. The dog wanted to catch the bird too. The wise cat quickly jumped on the dog's back and said, "Let's play, dog!" The dog was surprised and forgot about the bird. The bird flew away to safety. The cat and the dog played together and became friends. The moral of the story is to be kind and help others, even when it is unexpected.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a mighty king. The king had a very pretty gem. He loved the gem so much that he would call it his best friend. The gem was shiny and bright, and everyone in the town liked to look at it.
One day, a little boy came to the king. The boy said, "I have a gift for you." The king was happy and asked, "What is it?" The boy showed the king a small stone. It was not shiny like the gem, but the boy said it was special.
The king did not think the stone was special, but he took it anyway. That night, the king put the stone next to his gem. When he woke up the next morning, the gem was gone! The king was very sad and called for help. The little boy came back and showed the king that the stone was now shiny like the gem. The king was happy again and learned that even small things can be special too.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty boy named Tim. He had a sister named Sue. Tim and Sue liked to play outside in the sun. One day, they found a spray bottle.
Tim had a bad idea. He wanted to spray his sister with the bottle. Sue did not like this. She said, "No, Tim! That is naughty. Don't spray me."
But Tim did not listen. He sprayed Sue with the bottle. Sue was very sad. She cried and ran to tell their mom.
Mom was not happy with Tim. She said, "Tim, you are naughty for spraying your sister." Mom took away the spray bottle. Tim was sad because he could not play with the spray bottle anymore. The end.

On September 8 , 1900 , the island was struck by a devastating hurricane . This event holds the record as the United States ' deadliest natural disaster . The city was devastated , and an estimated 6, 000 to 8, 000 people on the island were killed . Following the storm , a 10-mile ( 16 km ) long , 17 foot ( 5. 2 m ) high seawall was constructed to protect the city from floods and hurricane storm surge . A team of engineers including Henry Martyn Robert ( Robert 's Rules of Order ) designed the plan to raise much of the existing city to a sufficient elevation behind a seawall so that confidence in the city could be maintained .

Set in rural Yorkshire during the summer of 1920 , the film follows a destitute World War I veteran employed to carry out restoration work on a Medieval mural discovered in a rural church while coming to terms with the after-effects of the war .

One day, a little boy named Tim saw something strange. A hairy ghost appeared in his room. Tim was scared of the ghost. The ghost was big and had long, hairy arms. Tim wanted the ghost to go away.
Tim thought of a plan. He would ask the ghost to play a game. If Tim won, the ghost would leave. The ghost agreed to play. They played a game of hide and seek. Tim hid behind a chair, and the ghost looked for him.
The ghost found Tim, but Tim was fast. He ran away and hid again. The ghost could not find him this time. Tim won the game. The hairy ghost said goodbye and disappeared. Tim was happy and not scared anymore.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. There is a big slide in the park. Lily and Ben want to go on the slide.
"Me first!" Lily says. She runs to the slide and climbs up the ladder. She sits on the top and smiles. "Whee!" she says as she slides down.
"Me too!" Ben says. He follows Lily and climbs up the ladder. He sits on the top and waves. "Whee!" he says as he slides down.
They do this again and again. They have fun on the slide. They laugh and shout.
After a while, they feel tired. They go to a big oak tree. The oak tree has green leaves and brown bark. It gives shade and cool air.
Lily and Ben sit under the oak tree. They drink some water and eat some cookies. They rest and talk.
"That was fun!" Lily says. "I like the slide."
"Me too!" Ben says. "I like the slide."
They hug each other. They are happy. They love the park. They love the slide. They love the oak tree. They love each other.

Once upon a time, there was a red fish named Fin. Fin had a big hook that he found near his home. He liked to play with it and show it to his friends.
One day, Fin saw a small fish stuck in a net. The small fish cried, "Help me, please!" Fin had an idea. He used his hook to open the net and free the small fish. The small fish was very happy and said, "Thank you, Fin!"
All the other fish saw what Fin did and started to applaud. They all learned that helping others is a good thing to do. From that day on, Fin and his friends always tried to help each other. And they all lived happily together.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little monkey named Momo. Momo loved to play and swing on the flexible vines all day. He had many friends, like the birds, the bugs, and the other animals in the forest.
One sunny day, Momo saw a big bird send a little bird away. The little bird was sad and could not play with the others. Momo felt bad and wanted to help the little bird. He thought of a plan to make the little bird happy again.
Momo climbed up the tree and found a long, flexible vine. He held the vine and swung to the little bird. Momo said, "Come, little bird! Swing with me on this vine, and we will have fun together!" The little bird was so happy and joined Momo. They played and laughed all day long.
The big bird saw Momo and the little bird having fun. The big bird felt sorry for sending the little bird away. The big bird flew down and said, "I am sorry, little bird. I want to play with you too." The little bird forgave the big bird, and they all played together.
The moral of the story is to be kind and include everyone in our play. When we are nice to others, we can have more fun and make more friends.

In Mozambique , workers assisted people in moving to higher grounds following flooding . Members of the Mozambique Red Cross helped distribute food and clothing to the affected residents , and planes helped drop off supplies to residents in isolated areas .

Once upon a time, in a tidy room, there was a big machine. This machine could make toys. Tom, a little boy, loved to play with the toys from the machine. One day, Tom's friend, Sue, came to visit him. They played with the toys together.
"Tom, do you believe this machine can make a toy we have never seen before?" Sue asked. Tom thought for a moment and said, "I don't know, but let's try it!"
Tom and Sue pushed the button on the machine. They waited for a new toy to come out. But instead of a toy, a big, colorful bird came out of the machine! Tom and Sue were very surprised.
The bird looked at them and said, "Thank you for letting me out of the machine. I was stuck in there for a long time!" Tom and Sue couldn't believe the bird could talk. They became friends with the bird and played together all day long. From that day on, the bird lived with Tom and his family, and they all had lots of fun together.

Once upon a time, there was an old closet. The closet was in a small room. The room had a big window. The closet had many toys inside. The toys were happy in the closet.
One day, it rained a lot. The rain came in through the window. The rain started to soak the room. The toys in the closet got wet. The toys were sad and scared.
A nice girl named Lily lived in the house. Lily saw the rain and the wet toys. She wanted to help them. Lily closed the window. She got a big towel. Lily dried the toys and the closet. The toys were happy again.

Different modes of condom failure result in different levels of semen exposure . If a failure occurs during application , the damaged condom may be disposed of and a new condom applied before intercourse begins – such failures generally pose no risk to the user . One study found that semen exposure from a broken condom was about half that of unprotected intercourse ; semen exposure from a slipped condom was about one-fifth that of unprotected intercourse .

Lily likes to play in the garden. She sees many things that make her happy. She sees flowers, birds, and bugs. She likes to watch the bugs and learn about them.
One day, she sees a large ant. The ant is bigger than the other ants. It has a big head and big jaws. Lily thinks the ant is scary. She wants to run away. But she also wants to know more about the ant. She decides to be brave and watch the ant.
She follows the ant as it walks on the ground. She sees the ant find a crumb of bread. The ant picks up the crumb with its jaws. The crumb is almost as big as the ant. Lily is amazed. She wonders how the ant can carry such a big thing.
She sees the ant take the crumb to a hole. The hole is the ant's home. The ant goes inside the hole with the crumb. Lily wants to see what is inside the hole. She decides to peek inside.
She bends down and puts her eye near the hole. She sees many ants inside. They are all busy. They are moving food, making tunnels, and taking care of eggs. Lily thinks the ants are smart and hard-working. She decides she likes the ants. She is not scared of them anymore.
She smiles and says hello to the ants. She hopes they can hear her. She says thank you for letting her see their home. She decides to leave a piece of cookie for them. She thinks they will like it. She says goodbye to the ants and goes back to her mom. She tells her mom what she saw and learned. She says she wants to be friends with the ants. Her mom hugs her and says she is proud of her.

Once there was a small boy called Sam. He was only three years old and he loved to help his Mom.
"Mom, what can I do to help? Can I carry something?" Sam asked.
"Sure Son. Here, carry this tray for 
me," Mom said.
Sam took the tray and held it carefully. He carried it with both hands, not wanting to drop it. He felt so big and important bringing things to his mom.
Mom smiled. "Thanks for helping Sam. Now, here's something else for you to do. It's smaller, so it's easy to carry. Can you carry this inside for me?"
Sam smiled and nodded. He took the small item and carried it carefully inside. He thought it felt special to help his mom in this way.
When he was done, his mom couldn't help but smile at him. "Thanks for helping Sam. I'm so proud of you!" she said, giving him a big hug.
Sam felt proud of himself, too. He loved helping his mom and carrying things for her. It was something special he could do to show her how much he cared.

One day, a little boy named Tim woke up. He was confused because he could not find his toy car. He looked under his bed, in his toy box, and behind the couch. But the toy car was not there. Tim felt sad.
Tim asked his mom for help. They looked everywhere in the house. Then, Tim remembered he played with the toy car outside. So, they went to the yard to look for it. Tim saw something shiny near a tree. He was sure it was his toy car.
But when Tim got closer, he saw it was not his toy car. It was a toy robot with one leg! Tim took the robot inside and showed it to his mom. She smiled and said, "Let's fix the robot's leg." They found a leg from an old toy and fixed the robot. Now, Tim had a new friend to play with, and he was not sad anymore.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a yellow house. In the yellow house, there lived a little girl named Lucy. Lucy loved her yellow house and her nice neighbor, Mr. Brown.
One sunny day, Lucy went outside to play. She saw Mr. Brown and wanted to play with him. They decided to play ball together. Lucy threw the ball and Mr. Brown tried to strike it.
As they played, the ball went very high in the sky. Lucy and Mr. Brown both looked up to see where the ball would come down. They laughed and had fun playing together. Lucy was happy to have a kind neighbor like Mr. Brown. They played until the sun went down, and then Lucy went back to her yellow house.
