Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They wanted to make a cake for Mommy. They found a big bowl, some flour, some eggs, and some butter. They also saw a jar of sugar on the shelf.
"Let's put some sugar in the cake," Lily said. "It will make it sweet and yummy."
"Okay," Ben said. "But how much?"
Lily shrugged. "A lot," she said. She climbed on a chair and reached for the jar. She opened it and poured some sugar into the bowl.
"Is that enough?" Ben asked.
"No, more," Lily said. She poured more sugar into the bowl. The jar was almost empty.
"Stop, Lily, that's too much!" Ben said. "Mommy will be mad."
But Lily did not listen. She poured the rest of the sugar into the bowl. She smiled and said, "Now it will be brilliant!"
She got down from the chair and picked up a big spoon. She started to stir the mixture in the bowl. Ben watched her with a worried look.
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was Mommy. She came into the kitchen and saw the mess. She saw the empty jar, the sugar everywhere, and the sticky bowl.
"What are you doing?" Mommy asked. She was very angry.
"We're making a cake for you, Mommy," Lily said. She held up the spoon and showed her the mixture.
Mommy looked at the mixture. It was not a cake. It was a gooey mess. It was too sweet and too sticky. It was not brilliant. It was awful.
Mommy sighed. She took the bowl and the spoon from Lily. She threw them in the trash. She said, "You can't make a cake like this. You wasted all the sugar. You made a big mess. You have to clean it up. And you have to say sorry."
Lily and Ben felt sad. They did not want to make Mommy angry. They did not want to waste the sugar. They did not want to clean the mess. They wanted to make a cake for Mommy. But they did not know how.
They said sorry to Mommy. They helped her clean the kitchen. They did not play with the sugar anymore. They learned their lesson. But they still wished they could make a cake for Mommy. Maybe next time, they would ask her for help.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. He had a big bag with him. Tim was very glad because he loved to play at the park. In the bag, he had a big red ball to play with his friends. Tim and his friends played catch and had lots of fun.
As they played, the sun started to rise high in the sky. It was getting very hot. Tim and his friends were getting tired, so they sat down to rest. They put the ball back in the bag and sat under a tree. They drank water and talked.
Suddenly, the bag started to move! Tim and his friends were very surprised. They looked inside the bag, and there was a little puppy! The puppy had been hiding in the bag all along. Tim and his friends were so happy to meet the puppy. They played with the puppy all day and had even more fun!

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a boy named Tim. One day, it began to rain. The rain was terrible, and Tim felt sad. He wanted to play outside, but he couldn't because of the rain. Tim's mom saw him and said, "Don't be sad, Tim. We can play inside."
Tim and his mom played with his toys. They had a lot of fun. Tim's mom had an idea. She took a big box and said, "Let's put all your toys in this box." Tim saw that the box was heavy. He thought it would be hard to lift it. But Tim's mom said, "If we work together, we can lift the weight."
So, Tim and his mom put all the toys in the box. They tried to lift the box together. It was still heavy, but they could carry it. They moved the box to the other room. Tim was happy because he learned that working together makes things easier.
The rain stopped, and the sun came out. Tim went outside to play. He remembered the lesson he learned with his mom. He knew that if he ever faced a terrible situation or a big weight, he could always ask for help and work together with others.
The moral of the story is: When things are hard, don't be afraid to ask for help and work together with others.

The Eshmun Temple complex comprises an elaborate hydraulic installation channeling water from " Ydll " spring that is made up of an intricate system of water canals , a series of retaining basins , sacred ablution basins and paved pools . This system demonstrates the importance of ritual ablutions in Phoenician therapeutic cults .

Once upon a time, there was a powerful prize. Many people wanted it and wanted it very badly. But none of them could have it. Every time someone asked for it, the prize would refuse.
One day, a brave young boy came along. He asked the prize if he could have it. Amazingly, the prize did not refuse him. It said yes!
The boy was so excited. He thanked the prize and held it tight in his hands. From that day forward, the boy and the prize were very happy together. The powerful prize made the boy feel special. He kept it for a very long time.

One day, a little girl named Mia went for a walk with her mom. They saw a high cactus. Mia looked at the cactus and said, "Mom, the cactus is very high!" Her mom said, "Yes, Mia, it is. The cactus reminds me of a tall tree."
As they walked, they saw a little bird sitting on the cactus. The bird was singing a pretty song. Mia and her mom stopped to listen. Then, something unexpected happened. The bird started to talk! It said, "Hello, Mia and Mom. I can help you find a big surprise."
Mia and her mom were very surprised. They followed the talking bird. The bird led them to a big, shiny box. Mia opened the box and found lots of yummy candy inside. Mia, her mom, and the talking bird had a fun day eating candy and playing together.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a big red boot. One day, he went to the park to play. He saw a pretty flower and wanted to pick it. He bent down to pick the flower, but his big red boot was uncomfortable.
Tim saw his friend, Sam, at the park. Sam said, "Hi, Tim! Why do you look sad?" Tim said, "My big red boot is uncomfortable. I want to pick the flower, but I can't." Sam tried to help Tim pick the flower, but the big red boot was still uncomfortable.
The sky turned dark and it started to rain. Tim and Sam were sad because they couldn't pick the flower. They went home, wet and unhappy. The big red boot was even more uncomfortable in the rain. Tim wished he didn't wear the big red boot that day.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park. She saw a display of pretty flowers. They were many colors: red, blue, and yellow. Lily liked the flowers a lot. She wanted to pick one, but her mom said no. Lily felt impatient.
Lily and her mom walked around the park. It was a cold day, so they wore warm coats. They saw ducks in the pond. The ducks were swimming and quacking. Lily laughed and clapped her hands. She liked the ducks, too.
After playing in the park, Lily and her mom went home. Lily was still impatient about the flowers. Her mom saw this and had an idea. They went to the store and bought seeds. They planted the seeds in their garden. Soon, Lily had her own display of pretty flowers. She was very happy.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to run. He put on his favorite shirt. It was a messy shirt with many colors.
Tim went outside to run. He ran very fast. He saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. When he got to the top, he saw something unexpected. There was a big, shiny star in the tree.
Tim was very surprised. He took the star and put it in his messy shirt. He climbed down and ran home. When he got home, the star was not in his shirt. It was back in the tree. Tim learned that some things are better left where they are.

While staying true to most adventure game conventions , Voyage has some unique features for its genre . These include two dexterity minigames which take advantage of the reduced gravity in the game 's lunar setting , and an " Intelligence Management System " , in which a score is assigned to the player for every puzzle he solves , and for certain actions . The Adventure Company introduced this feature to motivate players to replay the game to increase their cumulative score .

Once upon a time, in a big gloomy building, there lived a little girl named Lily. She was sad because the building was dark and not fun to play in. One night, Lily had a dream. In her dream, she saw a happy, colorful world with many friends to play with.
The next day, Lily met a little boy named Tom. Tom was new to the gloomy building. Lily said, "Hi, I'm Lily. Do you want to play?" Tom smiled and said, "Yes, I would love to play with you!" They played all day and had lots of fun.
One day, while they were playing, they found a hidden room in the building. Inside the room, there were many colors and toys. The room was just like Lily's dream! Lily and Tom decided to share the room with all the other kids in the building. Soon, the gloomy building became a happy place for everyone.
The moral of the story is that even in dark places, we can find happiness and joy by sharing with others.

On October 16 , 2009 , the Champlain Bridge was closed to traffic due to structural concerns . The bridge was demolished on December 28 , 2009 , as a result of those concerns , temporarily reducing NY 185 in purpose to a spur route linking NY 9N and NY 22 to Crown Point . Its replacement , the Lake Champlain Bridge , opened to traffic on November 7 , 2011 .

One day, a little girl named Sara asked her dad if she could go on a plane. Her dad said it was a brilliant idea, so he booked her a ticket. She was so excited to go. 
Sara arrived at the airport and got on the plane. She looked out of the window and saw a brilliant sky. After a couple of hours, the plane started to shake. Sara was scared and asked the flight attendant what was happening. 
The flight attendant said that they were having engine trouble. The plane was going to crash! 
Sara started to cry and held onto her dad tightly. The plane crashed and Sara was killed. Her dad was very sad. 
The end.

In October 2011 , NME placed it at number 148 on its list " 150 Best Tracks of the Past 15 Years " . The sculpture rests atop a grey granite base that is 6. 33 feet ( 1. 93 m ) tall , 3. 166 feet ( 0. 965 m ) wide and 3. 5 feet ( 1. 1 m ) deep . The corners of the base have small leaf designed and has 2 feet ( 0. 61 m ) by 2. 66 feet ( 0. 81 m ) bronze reliefs with arched tops on each side . The front relief states that it was erected in the memory of the citizens of East Providence who served in World War I from 1917 to 1918 , and lists the names of twenty three soldiers . The left relief depicts a marching infantry column of one man on horseback and four on foot , the right relief depicts four or five men loading a cannon and the rear relief depicts a nurse assisting two wounded soldiers .

Once upon a time, there was a cute little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play and run around the park. One day, Spot found a big box. Inside the box, there was a radio. Spot did not know what it was, but he thought it was fun to play with.
Spot tried to pick up the radio, but he had a struggle. He tried and tried, but it was too heavy for him. Then, a kind girl named Lucy saw Spot and said, "Do you need help, Spot?" Spot wagged his tail and barked, "Yes, please!" Lucy picked up the radio and carried it for Spot.
Lucy and Spot played with the radio together. They danced and laughed to the music. Spot learned that it's okay to ask for help when you struggle. And Lucy learned that helping others can be fun. They both had a great day and became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. Tom had a big black ball. He loved to play catch with his black ball. One day, Tom went on a journey with his mom and dad. They went to a big park. Tom was very happy.
At the park, Tom played catch with his dad. They threw the black ball back and forth. Tom's mom watched and clapped her hands. She was so proud of Tom. The sun was shining, and the birds were singing. It was a perfect day.
As they went home, Tom held his black ball tight. He was tired from the journey and the fun day of catch. Tom's mom and dad smiled at him. They knew they had a great day together. Tom couldn't wait for the next journey and more catch with his black ball.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a mitten on the ground. It was a very cold day, so he put the mitten on his hand to keep warm. As he walked, he met a fierce dog. The dog barked at Tim and showed its big teeth.
Tim said to the dog, "Why are you so fierce? I just want to be friends." The dog stopped barking and looked at Tim's hand with the mitten. The dog wagged its tail and said, "I am not fierce, I am just cold. Can I have the mitten to keep warm?"
Tim thought for a moment and said, "I can lock the mitten on your paw so it won't fall off." The dog let Tim lock the mitten on its paw. The dog was very happy and not fierce anymore. Tim and the dog became best friends and played together all day.

The construction of Canning Dam ended a long period during which Perth 's water supply was generally unsatisfactory in quality ( either due to salinity or bacterial pollution or both ) and in quantity . The project , the biggest public works program of the decade , stimulated significant growth in the local economy and provided desperately needed work for around five hundred men .

Once upon a time, in a humble little house, a ghost lived. This ghost liked to play and have fun with the kids. One day, a new family moved into the house. The ghost wanted to play with them, but they did not know he was there.
The ghost tried to show them he was there, but they only got scared. They began to quarrel with each other because they were scared. The ghost did not like to see them fight. He wanted them to be happy and play with him.
Then, one day, something unexpected happened. The ghost found a way to make the family laugh. He made funny faces and danced around. The family saw the ghost and laughed! They were not scared anymore. They played with the ghost every day and they all became best friends.

A tropical wave move off the coast of Africa on September 5 , and crossed the Atlantic waters , the Caribbean Sea and eventually into the Pacific Ocean as a weak system . An area of convection entered into the northeastern Pacific Ocean a few hundred miles south of Acapulco , Mexico . On September 2 , Tropical Depression Nineteen-E formed from this convection , while 746 mi ( 1, 201 km ) south-southeast from the southern tip of Baja California . The depression moved on a west-northwestward track , rounding the southwest side of a strong high pressure system . The depression continued to strengthen and was upgraded to Tropical Storm Odile on September 24 and into a hurricane on September 25 . Its intensity peaked with maximum sustained winds of 145 mph ( 233 km / h ) on September 26 .

Once upon a time, there was a small village near a big river. The people in the village were very happy. They played and worked together every day.
One day, a wise old man mentioned that a big flood was coming. The people were scared. They did not want their village to be in danger. So, they worked together to build a tall wall to keep the water away.
The big flood came, but the wall was strong. The village was safe. The people were happy again. They had a big party to celebrate. They danced and sang songs about the brave old man who helped them. And they always remembered to listen when someone mentioned something important.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a red rod. He liked to play with his red rod all day. He would run and jump with his red rod in the park.
One day, Tim went to the park with his red rod. He saw a big tree. He did not know what was behind the big tree. Tim was very curious. He went to see what was behind the big tree.
When Tim went behind the big tree, he found a big red ball. The big red ball was just like his red rod. Tim started to play with the big red ball. He had so much fun! From that day on, Tim played with his red rod and the big red ball every day at the park.

One day, a little boy named Tim was very restless. He could not sit still. His mom was a patient lady. She tried to tell him a story to help him calm down. "Tim, do you want to hear a story about a big surprise?" she asked.
"Yes, Mom!" Tim said, sitting down to listen. "Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to find surprises. One day, she saw a big, shiny box. She could not wait to see what was inside. She asked her mom if she could open it."
Tim listened as his mom told the story. The little girl in the story opened the box, and inside was a small, fluffy dog. The dog jumped out and licked her face. The little girl was so happy! She did not know she would find a new friend in the box.
As the story ended, Tim's mom said, "Now, I have a surprise for you too!" She brought out a big, shiny box, just like in the story. Tim's eyes grew wide as he opened the box. Inside was a soft, cuddly teddy bear. Tim was so happy and hugged the bear tight. He had not expected a surprise like the girl in the story. From that day on, Tim was not as restless, and he loved to hear his mom tell stories.

Once upon a time, there was a delicate little bird named Tiny. Tiny loved to fly high in the sky. One day, while flying, Tiny saw a shiny mirror on the ground.
Tiny flew down to see the mirror. The mirror was very big and pretty. Tiny looked at her reflection and saw her beautiful wings. She was so happy to see herself.
But then, something unexpected happened. A big wind came and blew the mirror away. The mirror broke into many pieces. Tiny was sad because she could not see her wings anymore. And that was the bad ending for Tiny and the mirror.

Once upon a time, there was a parrot who was very different. He had many colors on his body. One day, he met a new friend. The friend was a small bird. They both liked to play and spread their wings.
The parrot said, "I can fly high and spread my wings wide. Can you do that too?" The small bird said, "I can't fly as high as you, but I can spread my wings too." They played together and had fun.
One day, the sky became very dark. The parrot knew that a big storm was coming. He told the small bird, "We need to find a safe place to hide. The storm will be here soon." They found a big tree and hid under it. The storm came, and they were safe. After the storm, the parrot and the small bird spread their wings and flew up high together. They were happy to be safe and to have each other as friends.

Tim and Kim liked to play in the farm. They liked to see the cows, the pigs and the chickens. They liked to help Dad and Mom with the work. One day, Dad asked them to load some barrels on the truck. The barrels had apples inside. Tim and Kim were happy to help.
They rolled the barrels to the truck. They pushed and pulled. They lifted and lowered. They worked hard. They loaded all the barrels on the truck. They were proud. Dad smiled and said, "Good job, Tim and Kim! You are very strong and helpful."
Dad drove the truck to the market. Tim and Kim went with him. They saw many people and things. They saw fruits, vegetables, flowers and bread. They saw cheese, honey, jam and nuts. They saw a man with a big hat and a red coat. He had a barrel with a sign. The sign said, "Spicy sauce. Try some."
Tim and Kim were curious. They liked to try new things. They asked Dad if they could try some spicy sauce. Dad said, "OK, but be careful. It might be very hot." He gave them each a small spoon. They dipped the spoon in the sauce. They put the sauce in their mouths.
Tim and Kim made a funny face. The sauce was very spicy. It burned their tongues. It made them cough. It made their eyes water. They did not like the sauce. They ran to the truck. They drank some water. They ate some apples. They felt better.
Dad laughed and said, "I told you it might be very hot. Next time, listen to me." Tim and Kim nodded. They learned their lesson. They did not want to try spicy sauce again. They liked apples better. They were happy. They hugged Dad and said, "We love you, Dad. You are very smart and kind."

Once upon a time, there lived an ostrich who was always very hungry. Everyday, the ostrich would wander around looking for food. One day, he came across a big door, and he decided to go in. He found himself in a room filled with wonderful treats, but the door had shut behind him. 
The ostrich was so happy at being surrounded by delicious food and he quickly ate it all up. He was so full that he soon fell asleep. But when he woke up, he found that the door was still shut. He started to panic as he realised he was trapped.
The ostrich tried and tried to open the door, but no matter how hard he tried, he could not get it open. Suddenly, he saw a little mouse scurrying around the floor. The mouse said to the ostrich, âIf you really want something, you must be willing to work for it. You can't just eat your way out.â 
The ostrich understood what the mouse was saying. He stopped panicking and used all his strength to push open the door. To his relief, it opened and he walked out, feeling relieved. He never forgot the lesson the little mouse had taught him and the moral of the story is that hard work is more important than just having what you want.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little dog named Spot. Spot loved to run, play, and sleep. He had a lot of friends in his neighborhood. They all liked to play together.
One day, while Spot was playing outside, he found a shiny diamond on the ground. It was so pretty! Spot wanted to show his friends the diamond, so he picked it up in his mouth and ran to find them.
Spot showed the diamond to all his friends. They all thought it was very pretty too. After a long day of playing and sharing the diamond, Spot was very tired. He went home and had a good sleep, dreaming about the fun day he had with his friends and the shiny diamond.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the lake with his mom and dad. They had a fine day to play in the water. Tim saw a small kayak near the shore. He asked his mom and dad if he could try it. They said yes, but they would watch him closely.
Tim got in the kayak and began to paddle. He was having so much fun! As he moved, he made a big splash with each stroke. The water felt cool on his face. Suddenly, something unexpected happened. A big fish jumped out of the water and landed in the kayak with Tim!
Tim was scared at first, but then he saw the fish was also scared. He knew he needed to help the fish. Tim carefully picked up the fish and put it back in the water. The fish swam away, happy to be back home. Tim felt proud that he could help a new friend.

One day, a smelly cat and a little dog were playing with a ball. The cat wanted to kick the ball, but the dog wanted to play with it too. They both tried to get the ball at the same time.
"Let me kick the ball!" said the cat. "No, I want to play with it!" said the dog. They were not happy and did not want to share. The cat and the dog started to fight over the ball.
Then, a big fan came and blew the ball away. The cat and the dog stopped fighting and looked at each other. They decided to work together to get the ball back. They ran and jumped to catch the ball.
In the end, the cat and the dog learned to share the ball and play together. They had fun and became good friends. The smelly cat and the little dog were happy, and they played with the ball every day.

One day, a big, intelligent dog named Max went for a walk. He saw a small house and decided to enter. Inside the house, he found a little bird named Timmy. Timmy was sad because he lost his toy.
Max said, "Don't worry, Timmy. I will help you find your toy." They looked everywhere in the house. Suddenly, they heard a noise coming from a box. Max and Timmy opened the box, and there was the toy!
But there was also a note inside the box. The note said, "I took your toy to teach you the truth about sharing." Timmy realized that he had not been sharing his toys with his friends. He promised to be a better friend and share from now on. Max and Timmy became best friends and played with the toy together.

Once upon a time, there was a horse. The horse was big and strong. The horse lived in a place that was very icy. The horse liked the icy place.
One day, the horse went for a walk. The horse saw something. It was a box. The box had a note. The note said, "Include me!" The horse opened the box. Inside the box was a coat. The coat was warm and soft.
The horse put on the coat. The horse felt warm. But something unexpected happened. The horse turned into a person! The person was happy. The person said, "Thank you, horse, for including me!" Now the person and the horse were friends. They lived happily in the icy place.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy dog named Sam. Sam lived in a small house with his friend, a little girl named Amy. They loved to play together. One day, they went for a walk in the park.
In the park, Sam and Amy saw a bell hanging from a tree. "Look, Sam! A bell!" said Amy. They walked up to the bell and Amy gave it a ring. The bell made a loud noise that made Sam frown. He did not like the loud noise.
Just then, a tiny bird flew down from the tree. The bird looked at Sam and Amy, and then it started to talk! "Hello, friends! I am a magic bird, and you have found my bell. I will give you one wish for finding it." Amy and Sam were very surprised, but they were happy too. They wished to be best friends forever, and the magic bird made their wish come true.

Lily was a popular girl in her class. She had many friends who liked to play with her. She was good at sharing, singing and jumping. One day, she saw a new boy in the playground. His name was Ben. He looked shy and lonely. Lily wanted to be his friend.
She went to him and said, "Hi, I am Lily. Do you want to play with me and my friends?"
Ben nodded and smiled. He followed Lily to the slide. Lily climbed up the ladder and slid down. She laughed and said, "This is fun! Come on, Ben, it's your turn!"
Ben climbed up the ladder, but he was scared. He looked down and saw how high the slide was. He felt dizzy and wanted to go back. He said, "No, I can't do it. It's too high. I want to go down."
Lily saw that Ben was afraid. She wanted to help him. She said, "Don't be scared, Ben. I am here with you. You can do it. Just trust me and trust yourself. The slide is safe and the ground is soft. You will have fun, I promise."
Ben looked at Lily. He saw that she was kind and brave. He wanted to be like her. He said, "Okay, Lily. I will try. I trust you and I trust myself."
He slid down the slide with Lily. He felt the wind in his hair and the sun on his face. He landed on the ground and laughed. He said, "You were right, Lily. That was fun! Thank you for being my friend."
Lily hugged him and said, "You're welcome, Ben. You are my friend too. You are brave and smart. I am proud of you."
They played together with the other children. They had a lot of fun. They learned that being friends means helping each other, trusting each other and having fun together. They were happy.

Having been held south of Romani , the German and Ottoman force attempted a further outflanking manoeuvre to the west , concentrating 2, 000 troops around Mount Royston another sand dune , south-west of Romani . At 05 : 15 , the Ottoman 31st Infantry Regiment pushed forward ; then the 32nd and the 39th Infantry Regiments swung around the left and into the British rear . This outflanking movement was steadily progressing along the slopes of Mount Royston and turning the right of the 2nd Light Horse Brigade , whose third regiment , the Wellington Mounted Rifles , was now also committed to the front line .

One day, a little girl named Amy went to the mall with her mom. They walked past many stores and saw many things. Amy felt tired from walking so much, but she was happy to be at the mall.
In one store, Amy saw a big sign with a picture of a toy she liked. She asked her mom, "Can I have that toy, please?" Her mom said, "No, Amy. We are here to buy a gift for your friend's birthday. We can't buy a toy for you today."
Amy was sad, but she knew it was important to think of others. They picked out a nice gift for her friend and went to pay. When they got to the counter, the store worker said, "You are our 100th customer today! You win a prize!" The prize was the toy Amy wanted!
Amy was very happy and learned that when you think of others first, good things can happen to you too.

One day, Susie and her mom were going on an adventure. They decided to go to the village store. As Susie and her mom walked up to the porch, Susie noticed something strange. She could hear a little squeak coming from the porch. 
"Mom, what is that noise?", Susie asked.
"I'm not sure, why don't you go and take a look?", Mom replied.
Susie carefully stepped onto the porch and looked around. There, in the corner, was a tiny mouse recording a song. It was the strangest thing she had ever seen. It made her feel a bit uncomfortable.
"Mom! Look!", Susie exclaimed. 
Her mom gasped. "That is so cute!", she said.
The little mouse kept on recording its song, unaware of its audience. Susie and her mom just watched in amazement. 
Finally, Susie and her mom said goodbye to the singing mouse, and continued on their way to the village store. Susie had never seen something so special before. She knew she would always remember the singing mouse on the porch.

Once upon a time there was an old man who had a tidy house. Every day, he woke up and cleaned it from top to bottom. Then one day, a flea decided to enter the old man's house.
At first, the flea explored everywhere and had so much fun. But soon, it began to cause a mess everywhere it went. The old man was not happy.
The old man thought of a plan. He got a big jar filled with water and caught the flea. Then, he asked it why it decided to enter his tidy house.
The flea explained that she wanted to have some fun and explore. The old man was not angry and decided to let the flea go. He told the flea that it was okay to explore, but it must remember to stay tidy and not to cause a mess.
The moral of the story is that it's okay to explore and have fun, as long as you remember to be responsible and stay tidy.

Once upon a time, there was a baby shark who liked to behave badly. He played too much and didn't listen to his mommy and daddy shark. 
One day, when baby shark was playing in the ocean, he came across an old bottle and started playing with it. "Be careful," warned mommy shark, "it might be dangerous!" 
But baby shark ignored her warning and started to act crazy. He swam around and around with the bottle, not realizing how much trouble he was getting into. 
Suddenly, the bottle bumped into a group of strong whales. Furious, the whales chased after baby shark. 
The mommy and daddy shark saw their little baby getting chased and were very worried. They swam as fast as they could and came to baby shark's rescue. 
Using their strength, mommy and daddy shark pushed the whales away and saved baby shark. 
The mommy and daddy shark hugged their baby and made sure he was okay. "You need to listen to us and behave," said mommy and daddy shark. "You could have gotten hurt if we hadn't been here." 
From that day onwards, baby shark no longer behaved badly and always listened to his mommy and daddy shark. 
The moral of the story is that we should always listen to our parents and behave no matter what.

On September 12 , Norbert absorbed Tropical Depression Eighteen-E which was in close proximity . Norbert strengthened as it moved north-northwestward . The tropical storm was upgraded to a hurricane on September 14 , and formed an eye on September 15 . The storm reached its peak strength of 80 mph ( 130 km / h ) sustained winds that day . Turning north of due west , Norbert then weakened as it moved over cooler waters . It was downgraded to a tropical storm later on September 15 , and then to a tropical depression on September 18 . Norbert dissipated as a tropical cyclone on September 19 after losing all its deep convection .

One day, a big dog named Max was playing on the lawn. He liked to run and jump with his ball. Max saw a cat named Luna sitting near a tree. Max wanted to play with Luna, but Luna did not want to play with Max.
Max ran to Luna with his ball. He shouted, "Luna, play with me!" But Luna was scared of Max and his big voice. She climbed up the tree to get away from Max. Max was sad because he just wanted to play.
Max's mom came outside with a delicious treat for Max. She said, "Max, come here and eat this yummy snack." Max ate the treat and felt better. He knew that he could still have fun even if Luna didn't want to play with him.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max had big ears that could hear very well. One cold day, Max went outside to play with his friend, a little bird named Lily.
Max and Lily were playing when Max started to shiver. "Brrr, I am cold," Max said. "My ear is cold too!" Lily wanted to help Max, so she thought of an idea.
"Wait here," Lily told Max. She flew away and came back with a small, important hat. She put the hat on Max's head to cover his ears. Max stopped shivering and smiled. "Thank you, Lily! Now my ears are warm, and we can keep playing." And they played happily all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a modest little girl named Lily. She had a big dream to fly like a bird. Every day, she would look up at the sky and watch the birds fly.
One day, Lily saw a little bird who couldn't fly. She went to the bird and asked, "Why can't you fly?" The bird said, "I am too small and scared." Lily wanted to help the bird, so she thought of a plan.
Lily found a big leaf and put the bird on it. She held the leaf and started to run. The bird started to yell, "I can fly! I can fly!" Lily smiled as she watched the bird fly away. Now, Lily knew she could make her dream come true by helping others.

One day, a little girl named Lily wanted to play. She went to the attic where she found her old toys. The attic was cold, but Lily did not mind. She put on a warm sweater and began to play with her toys. She found a toy bathtub and a little doll. 
Lily said to the doll, "You are dirty. You need a bath!" She took the toy bathtub and filled it with warm water. She put the doll in the water and began to bathe it. She scrubbed the doll with a little sponge until it was clean. 
When the doll was all clean, Lily took it out of the water and wrapped it in a soft towel. She said, "Now you are clean and warm!" Lily played with her doll in the cold attic all day long. They had a lot of fun together.

Once upon a time there was a truck that could drive fast. Its name was True and it was very powerful.
True loved to drive around and explore the world. Everywhere it went, adults and children were amazed.
One day, True needed to drive to the store to get special tools, but it was too far away. Suddenly, a small three year old boy came up and said, "Let me help!"
True thought to itself, "How can this little boy help me?" But he decided to let him try.
The boy hopped in and said, "I'll help you drive!" True was skeptical, but it allowed him to steer the wheel. The boy was surprisingly powerful, and he lead True all the way to the store. 
When they arrived, they were both happy. True was so impressed with the little boy's help that it take the time to give him a special gift.
The boy who drove True was very happy. He said "Thank you, True! I will never forget your kindness." 
And he never did.

Lily wanted to play with her new doll, but she had to take a bath first. She did not like baths. They made her wet and cold. She tried to run away, but Mom caught her and put her in the tub. Lily was frustrated. She cried and splashed and made a mess.
Mom washed Lily's hair and body with soap and water. She said, "You have to be clean, Lily. It's good for you." Lily did not care. She wanted to get out. She tried to grab the towel, but it was too far. She stretched and reached, but she could not gain it. She was more frustrated. She screamed and kicked and made more mess.
Mom was not happy. She said, "Stop it, Lily. You are being naughty. You have to calm down." She took the towel and wrapped Lily in it. She lifted her out of the tub and dried her off. She said, "There, you are done. Now you can play with your doll." Lily was still frustrated. She did not want the towel. She wanted to be free. She wriggled and squirmed and made the towel fall.
Mom sighed. She said, "Lily, you are making this hard. You have to cooperate. You have to wear clothes." She picked up the towel and Lily and took them to the bedroom. She put Lily on the bed and tried to dress her. Lily did not want clothes. She wanted to play. She pushed and pulled and made the clothes fall.
Mom was tired. She said, "Lily, you are being silly. You have to listen. You have to be nice." She hugged Lily and kissed her. She said, "I love you, Lily. But you have to behave. You have to follow the rules." Lily looked at Mom. She saw that Mom was sad. She felt sorry. She said, "I love you, Mom. I'm sorry. I'll be good." She smiled and hugged Mom back. She said, "Can I play with my doll now?" Mom smiled and nodded. She said, "Yes, you can. But first, let me put on your clothes." Lily agreed. She let Mom put on her clothes. She was not frustrated anymore. She was happy. She said, "Thank you, Mom. You are the best." Mom said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are the best, too." They hugged and kissed again. Then they went to the living room, where Lily played with her doll and Mom watched her with love.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a little girl named Mia. Mia had a big brain. She was very smart. One day, she met a talking bird named Bobo. Bobo could not find his way home. He was sad.
Mia wanted to help Bobo. She said, "Do not be sad, Bobo. I will take you home." Bobo was happy. They walked and walked. Mia used her big brain to find the way.
On the way, they found a bitter fruit. Bobo said, "Mia, do not eat that fruit. It is bitter and not good." Mia listened to Bobo. They walked some more and found Bobo's home. Bobo was so happy. Mia and Bobo became best friends.

Lily and Mom went to the market. Lily saw a big red ball. She wanted the ball very much. She asked Mom to buy the ball for her.
Mom said, "No, Lily. We have no money to pay for the ball. We need to pay for food and milk and eggs. The ball is too much."
Lily was sad. She cried and cried. She did not listen to Mom. She ran away from Mom and took the ball. She hid behind a big box.
Mom looked for Lily. She was scared. She called Lily's name. She did not see Lily. She saw a man with a big bag. The man saw the ball. He liked the ball. He took the ball and put it in his bag. He ran away.
Lily came out from behind the box. She saw the man with the bag. She saw the ball in the bag. She screamed and screamed. She wanted the ball back. She ran after the man. She did not see the car. The car was fast. The car hit Lily. Lily fell down. She did not get up. She was hurt. She was bad.
Mom heard Lily scream. She saw Lily on the road. She saw the car. She saw the blood. She ran to Lily. She cried and cried. She hugged Lily. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I love you, Lily." She was too late. Lily was gone. Lily was bad.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Sam. Everywhere he went, Sam liked to build. He could build blocks and he could build houses.
One day, Sam was in the park. It was very dark outside and he was alone. Suddenly, Sam heard some voices. He looked around and saw they were coming from a big tree.
He went up to the tree and he realized there was a meeting happening! He was very excited and he wanted to join in.
The other people at the meeting were also building things. Everyone was building something different. There were block towers and there was an enormous rope swing. 
Sam was so excited to join them! He grabbed some blocks and started building a castle. Everyone said it was very nice. 
The end.

Sara liked to do yoga with her mom. Yoga was when they moved their bodies in different ways and breathed slowly. Sara felt calm and happy when she did yoga. She also liked to watch her mom's hairy cat, Luna, who sometimes joined them on the mat.
One day, Sara and her mom were doing yoga in the living room. Luna was sleeping on the couch. Sara saw a big book on the coffee table. It had a picture of a scary monster on the cover. Sara was curious and wanted to see what was inside.
"Mom, can I look at this book?" Sara asked.
"No, sweetie, that book is not for you. It has scary stories that might give you bad dreams. Why don't you do the tree pose with me?" Mom said.
Sara nodded and stood on one leg. She lifted her other leg and put her foot on her knee. She raised her arms and pretended to be a tree. She felt strong and balanced.
But she still wanted to see the book. She thought maybe she could peek at it when mom was not looking. She waited for a chance.
Mom closed her eyes and did the savasana pose. She lay on her back and relaxed her whole body. She looked very peaceful.
Sara saw her chance. She tiptoed to the coffee table and grabbed the book. She opened it and saw a big picture of the scary monster. It had sharp teeth, red eyes, and long claws. Sara gasped and dropped the book. She was very scared.
Luna woke up from the noise. She saw the book on the floor and the scary monster on the cover. She thought it was a real monster and it was going to hurt Sara and mom. She jumped off the couch and ran to the book. She used her paws to cover the monster and protect her family.
Sara saw Luna cover the monster. She realized Luna was brave and smart. She felt sorry for being naughty and looking at the book. She ran to Luna and hugged her.
"Thank you, Luna, you are a hero. I'm sorry, mom, I should have listened to you. I don't want to see the scary book anymore. I love you and Luna." Sara said.
Mom opened her eyes and saw what happened. She smiled and hugged Sara and Luna.
"I love you too, Sara. And I'm proud of you, Luna. You are a good cat. Let's put the book away and finish our yoga. How about we do the cat pose?" Mom said.
Sara and Luna agreed. They did the cat pose and purred. They felt happy and safe. They liked to do yoga with mom.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim liked to go to the market with his mom. One day, they went to the market to buy some fruit. While they were there, Tim saw a mysterious door. He had never seen it before.
Tim asked his mom, "Can we go see what's behind the door?" His mom said, "Okay, but we must stay together." They went to the door and opened it. Inside, they found a big room with many people. The people were having a party.
Tim and his mom went to the party and had fun. They danced and ate yummy food. Then, a big cake came out. Tim was surprised because it was his birthday! His mom had planned the party for him. They had a great time and Tim was very happy.

One day, a little girl named Amy went upstairs to play. She found her toys all dry and dusty. She wanted to clean them, so she took a bow and wiped them.
Amy's brother, Tom, came into the room. He saw Amy with his bow. "That's my bow!" he said. "Give it back!" Amy didn't want to give it back. She wanted to keep cleaning her toys.
Tom tried to take the bow from Amy. They both pulled on it. Then, Amy let go. Tom fell down on the floor. He started to cry. Amy felt bad. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. Here's your bow." Tom stopped crying and they played together with the clean toys.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. They have many cars and trucks in a big box. They share the box and take turns.
One day, Tom sees a new car in the box. It is red and shiny. It has a zipper on the back. Tom thinks the zipper is cool. He wants to play with the new car.
"Can I have the new car?" Tom asks Sam.
"No, I want the new car," Sam says. "It is mine. I got it from my mom."
Tom and Sam disagree. They both want the new car. They pull the car from each other. They are angry and sad.
"Stop!" a voice says. It is their teacher, Miss Lee. She sees Tom and Sam fighting. She is not happy.
"Tom, Sam, what are you doing?" Miss Lee asks. "Why are you fighting?"
Tom and Sam tell Miss Lee about the new car. They both say it is theirs.
Miss Lee shakes her head. She says, "You need to share the new car. It is not nice to fight. How about you take turns? Tom can play with the new car for five minutes, then Sam can play with it for five minutes. Is that fair?"
Tom and Sam think about it. They nod. They say, "Okay, Miss Lee. We will share the new car. We are sorry."
Miss Lee smiles. She says, "Good. I am glad you are friends again. Now, go and play nicely."
Tom and Sam hug each other. They say, "We are sorry, too. We are still friends."
They go and play with the new car. They take turns. They have fun. They like the zipper. They zip and unzip it. They make vroom vroom sounds. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous tree. A little boy named Tom lived near the tree. He liked to play under the tree every day. One day, Tom saw a pipe near the tree. He did not know what the pipe was for.
Tom told his friends about the pipe. They all went to look at it. They noticed that the pipe was very long. It went from the tree to a big hill. They were all very curious about the pipe.
They decided to follow the pipe to see where it went. When they got to the hill, they saw a big door. They opened the door and found a room full of toys! The pipe was a secret way to bring toys to the tree. Tom and his friends played with the toys and had a lot of fun. They were very happy that they found the secret toy room.

Once there was a big bear named Billy. He lived at the edge of the forest. One warm and sunny day, he heard a strange noise from the trees. It was a very sweet smell, like perfume. He had never heard anything like it before. 
Billy wanted to find out what the special noise was. He looked around but couldn't find it. He asked his best friend, Rabbit, if he had heard it too. Rabbit said, "Yes, I have heard the noise. It sounds like flowers." 
Billy was very excited. He walked into the forest to find the source of the special noise. He followed the sound until he came to a big and beautiful flower. He smelled the sweet perfume of the flower, and he knew it was the source of the noise. 
Billy was very happy. He waited in the forest until sundown when the perfume scent filled the air and the stars shone in the night sky. 
He enjoyed the special smells and sights of the forest, and he never forgot the perfume.

Already suffering from severe flooding that killed at least 18 people and left 200, 000 homeless , Hurricane Brenda worsened the situation with torrential rainfall and additional flooding . The storm killed at least 10 people in the country . Following the damage wrought by Brenda , a large earthquake struck the region , hampering relief efforts and collapsing numerous structures . Winds on land gusted up to 112 mph ( 180 km / h ) , leading to severe wind damage . Two of the fatalities occurred in Campeche after 80 % of the city was flooded . This was considered the worst flooding in the city in over 25 years . An estimated 2, 000 people were left homeless as a direct result of Brenda throughout Mexico . Offshore , a freighter with 25 crewman became trapped in the storm after its engines failed . They were safely rescued several days later once the storm had dissipated .

One day, a mild jellyfish named Jilly was swimming in the sea. She was a very kind and friendly jellyfish. All her friends loved to play with her. Jilly was always happy to help others.
One sunny day, Jilly saw a little fish who was very tired. The little fish told Jilly that he needed a nap, but he could not find a safe place to sleep. Jilly wanted to help her new friend. She thought for a moment and had a great idea.
Jilly told the little fish to take a nap on her soft, mild body. The little fish was so happy and thankful. He took a nap on Jilly, and when he woke up, he felt much better. The little fish thanked Jilly and they became good friends. From that day on, all the sea animals knew that Jilly was very kind and helpful. The moral of the story is to always help others when they need it.

Once upon a time, in a small, pale house, there lived a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside with her friends. They would run, jump, and laugh all day long. This was their favorite exercise.
One sunny day, Lily's friends came to her house and asked her to play. But Lily did not want to play. She wanted to stay inside and watch TV. Her friends told her that playing outside was more fun. Lily tried to resist, but her friends were very convincing.
Finally, Lily decided to go outside and play with her friends. They played tag, hide and seek, and other fun games. At the end of the day, Lily was very happy that she did not resist. She learned that exercise and playing with her friends was much better than staying inside alone.

Sam and Ben are brothers. They like to play with their toys in the living room. One day, they find a big box in the garage. They have an idea. They want to make a spaceship with the box.
They take the box to the living room and start to cut and tape and draw on it. They make windows and wings and a door. They are very happy with their spaceship. They pretend to fly to the moon and the stars.
But then, Mom comes home. She sees the box and the mess. She is not happy. She says, "What are you doing with that box? That is not a toy. That is for the new TV. You have to return it to the garage. Now!"
Sam and Ben are sad. They do not want to return the box. They love their spaceship. They say, "But Mom, this is our spaceship. We made it. We want to play with it. Please, Mom, can we keep it?"
Mom shakes her head. She says, "No, you cannot keep it. That is a crazy idea. The box is not a spaceship. It is for the TV. You have to be careful with it. It is expensive. You have to return it to the garage. And clean up this mess. Or you will be in trouble."
Sam and Ben are very sad. They have to return the box to the garage. They have to say goodbye to their spaceship. They have to clean up the living room. They have no more fun. They wish they had a real spaceship.

One day, a lazy cat named Tom went to the ocean. He liked to watch the waves and feel the sand on his paws. He saw a big crab walking near the water.
Tom said to the crab, "Hi, I am Tom. I like the ocean. Do you like the ocean too?" The crab said, "Yes, I like the ocean. But sometimes, I want the waves to stop so I can rest."
Tom and the crab sat on the sand, watching the waves. They talked and laughed. They had a lot of fun. Then, the waves stopped for a little while. The crab was happy.
The lazy cat and the crab played in the ocean until the sun went down. They became good friends. From that day on, Tom and the crab met at the ocean to play and have fun together.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to wait for the bus. It was a cold day, and Tim started to shiver. His mom gave him a big, warm hug to help him feel better. She said, "We will get on the bus soon, and you will be warm."
While they waited, Tim saw a man selling toys. He saw a fake dog that looked like his dog at home. Tim asked his mom if he could buy the toy. His mom said, "Let's wait until after we ride the bus. Then, we can come back and get it."
When the bus came, Tim and his mom got on. They sat down, and Tim felt warm again. He stopped shivering and smiled. Tim was happy to be on the bus and remembered the fake dog. He knew that after the bus ride, he would get the toy and play with it all day.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old bird who loved to laugh. One day, while sitting in a big tree, the bird saw a little boy playing with a toy aeroplane. The boy was very happy and laughed as he made the aeroplane fly high in the sky.
The wise bird wanted to join the fun. So, it flew down from the tree and sat on the aeroplane. The boy laughed even more, and the bird laughed too. They played together, making the aeroplane go up and down, round and round.
After a while, the sun started to set. The boy and the wise bird said goodbye and the boy went home. The bird flew back to its tree, feeling happy that it had made a new friend. The bird and the boy would always remember the fun day they had playing with the aeroplane.

To protect the construction site from the Colorado River and to facilitate the river 's diversion , two cofferdams were constructed . Work on the upper cofferdam began in September 1932 , even though the river had not yet been diverted . The cofferdams were designed to protect against the possibility of the river flooding a site at which two thousand men might be at work , and their specifications were covered in the bid documents in nearly as much detail as the dam itself . The upper cofferdam was 96 ft ( 29 m ) high , and 750 feet ( 230 m ) thick at its base , as thicker than the dam itself . It contained 650, 000 cubic yards ( 500, 000 m3 ) of material .

One day, Tim and his dog, Max, went for a walk. They liked to watch cars and people on the street. Max was a reliable dog and always stayed close to Tim. They were best friends.
As they walked, they saw a cat. Max wanted to chase the cat, but Tim said, "No, Max! We must be nice to the cat." Max listened to Tim, but the cat was scared and climbed a tree. The cat was stuck and couldn't get down.
Tim and Max wanted to help the cat. They found a tall man who helped the cat get down from the tree. The cat was happy and said, "Thank you, Tim and Max!" The moral of the story is to always be kind to others, even if they are scared.

Tim liked to play hockey with his friends. He had a stick and a puck and he wore a helmet and gloves. He was good at hitting the puck and scoring goals. He was proud of his hockey skills.
One day, he went to the park with his friends to play hockey. There was a big ice rink where they could skate and play. Tim was excited and he wanted to show off his skills. He skated fast and tried to hit the puck hard. But he was careless and he did not look where he was going.
He bumped into a girl who was also skating on the ice. She fell down and dropped her hat and scarf. She was not happy. She looked at Tim and said, "Hey, watch where you are going! You are so careless! You made me fall and you messed up my hat and scarf!"
Tim felt bad. He did not mean to bump into the girl. He said, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I did not see you. Are you okay? Here, let me help you." He picked up her hat and scarf and gave them to her. He helped her get up and asked if she was hurt.
The girl was not hurt, but she was still angry. She said, "You should be more careful. You could have hurt me or yourself. You should not play hockey here. This is not a hockey rink. This is a skating rink. Go play hockey somewhere else!"
Tim felt embarrassed. He did not know that this was not a hockey rink. He thought he could play hockey anywhere. He looked around and saw that everyone was staring at him. He felt his face turn red. He said, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I did not know. I will go play hockey somewhere else." He took his stick and puck and skated away. He felt sad and ashamed. He wished he had been more careful. He learned a lesson that day. He learned to be more careful and to respect other people's space. He hoped the girl would forgive him. He hoped his friends would not laugh at him. He hoped he could still play hockey and have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to pick soft flowers in her garden. One day, Lily picked many flowers and wanted to put them in water.
Lily went to the kitchen with her flowers. She saw the sink and thought it was a good place for her flowers. She put the flowers in the sink and turned on the water. The flowers floated in the water and looked very pretty.
Lily's mom came into the kitchen and saw the flowers in the sink. She said, "Lily, the sink is for washing, not for flowers." Lily said, "But Mom, the flowers look so pretty in the water!" Her mom smiled and said, "Let's find a vase for your flowers." They found a vase and put the soft flowers in it. The flowers looked even prettier in the vase, and Lily was happy.

One day, a little girl named Lily found a small cat with incredible soft skin. The cat was stuck in a tree and could not get down. Lily wanted to help the cat, so she tried to think of a way to manage getting the cat down from the tree.
Lily asked her friend, Tom, "Can you help me get the cat down?" Tom said, "Yes, let's use a long stick to reach the cat." They found a long stick and managed to get the cat down from the tree.
The cat was very happy and thanked Lily and Tom. They both learned that working together can help solve problems. The moral of the story is that teamwork makes everything easier.

One day, a little girl named Sue went to the park with her mom. Sue loved to play and watch the birds fly in the sky. She saw a big pile of junk near the swings. Sue was sad because the park was dirty.
Sue said to her mom, "Mom, can we clean the junk? I'm sorry the park is dirty." Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, let's clean the park together." They put on gloves and started to pick up the junk. They found old cans, papers, and even a broken toy.
As they cleaned, a little boy named Tim saw them and wanted to help. Tim said, "I want to help too! I'm sorry the park is dirty." Sue, Tim, and Sue's mom all cleaned the park together. When they were done, they watched the birds fly in the clean park. They were happy the park was clean and pretty again.

Once upon a time, there was a big dog named Max. Max loved to lie down under the big tree in his yard. One sunny day, Max was lying under the tree when he saw a little bird. The little bird was sad and ashamed because it lost its treasure.
Max wanted to help the little bird, so they looked for the treasure together. They looked in the yard, they looked in the bushes, but they could not find the treasure. Max and the little bird were very sad.
Then, something unexpected happened! Max found the treasure in his own dog house! It was a shiny, pretty stone. The little bird was very happy and not ashamed anymore. Max and the little bird became best friends and played together every day.

One day, a little dog named Max went for a walk. He saw a big tree and gazed at the pretty leaves. Max was happy to be outside. He wagged his tail and ran around the tree.

The 1986 Peach Bowl was a post-season American college football bowl game at Fulton County Stadium in Atlanta , Georgia between the Virginia Tech Hokies and the North Carolina State Wolfpack from on December 31 , 1986 . The game was the final contest of the 1986 NCAA Division I-A football season for both teams , and ended in a 25 – 24 victory for Virginia Tech , the first bowl victory in school history .

ML 177 , the launch that had successfully taken off some of the crew from Campbeltown , was sunk on her way out of the estuary . ML 269 , another torpedo-armed boat , had the unenviable task of moving up and down the river at high speed to draw German fire away from the landings . Soon after passing Campbeltown it was hit and its steering damaged . It took ten minutes to repair the steering . They turned and started in the other direction , opening fire on an armed trawler in passing . Return fire from the trawler set their engine on fire .

After the Indian Premier League 's second season demonstrated the importance of spin bowling in Twenty20 cricket , and due to Somerset 's lack of a front-line spin bowler , Somerset picked young leg spinner Max Waller to make his Twenty20 debut in their opening match of the campaign . He claimed three wickets in two overs to help Somerset win by one run , and finished the competition as Somerset 's joint second-highest wicket-taker with 10 wickets . Despite a number of good performances by Somerset 's bowlers , a batsman was named man of the match in each of the team 's victories : James Hildreth , Craig Kieswetter and Marcus Trescothick were all awarded the accolade once , while Zander de Bruyn picked up the award on three occasions . Somerset completed the group stage with six wins , three losses and one no result , placing them third in the Midlands / Wales / West Division . They qualified for the knockout-stage as they were the best third-placed team in the three groups .

The moral of the story is to be careful with whom you play and always listen to good advice.

Soon, the kids learned how to play "win". They felt happy and not uncomfortable anymore. They played "win" in the park every day. They made new friends and had more fun together. And they all lived happily ever after.

At the moment what we know about them , they ... seemingly just observe . That 's kind of it , but [ in ] the episode that we have coming up , we 're not sure if all they do is just observe " .

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Bob. Bob was very nervous because he wanted to escape to the west. He had heard that the west was the best place to find yummy food and make new friends.
One day, Bob met a big bird named Sam. Bob asked, "Can you help me escape to the west?" Sam said, "Yes, I can show you the way. But first, we must be brave and not be nervous."
Bob and Sam started their journey to the west. They flew over hills and rivers. Bob felt less nervous because Sam was with him. They talked and laughed as they flew together.
Finally, they reached the west. Bob was so happy to see all the yummy food and new friends waiting for him. He thanked Sam for helping him escape and not be nervous. From that day on, Bob and Sam were best friends, and they lived happily in the west.

Once upon a time, there was a big boat. The boat had a big anchor. One day, a little boy named Tim went on the boat. Tim had a red ball. He loved his red ball. Tim said, "I hope I don't lose my red ball."
As the boat moved, the big anchor went up and down. Tim played with his red ball near the anchor. Suddenly, the red ball fell into the water. Tim was sad. He thought his red ball was spoiled.
Then, a big fish jumped out of the water. The fish had Tim's red ball in its mouth! The fish said, "Here is your red ball, Tim." Tim was very happy. His red ball was not spoiled. The big fish and Tim became friends. They played with the red ball together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emma. Emma liked to help her mom cook. One day, mom asked Emma to get the salt. Emma looked and looked, but she could not find the salt. She was sad. 
Emma asked her mom, "Mom, where is the salt?" Mom said, "The salt is close, look in the cupboard." Emma looked in the cupboard and found the salt. She was happy. The salt was available to use.
Mom and Emma put the salt in the soup. They stirred and stirred. When it was all mixed, they tasted the soup. It was yummy! Emma and her mom were so happy they found the salt. They ate the soup together and had a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Mark. He loved to bake with his mom. They would make yummy cakes and cookies. One day, Mark and his mom were baking a big cake for a party. It was a fun and noisy day in the kitchen.
Mark wanted to help his mom mix the cake batter. He used a big spoon to mix, but it was hard. The spoon slipped from his hand and made a loud noise. Mark's mom said, "It's okay, we can try again." Mark was happy his mom was not mad.
They baked the cake and took it to the party. Everyone said the cake was very good. Mark was proud that he helped his mom. The moral of the story is: it's okay to make mistakes, as long as you learn from them and keep trying.

Once upon a time, there was a reindeer named Rudy. Rudy was a careless reindeer. He loved to run and play with his friends. One day, Rudy and his friends were playing in the forest. They were all having fun and enjoying the sunny day.
Rudy's friend, a squirrel named Sammy, said, "Rudy, be careful! You might trip and fall!" But Rudy didn't listen. He was too busy enjoying the game they were playing.
Suddenly, Rudy tripped on a rock and fell down. His friends gathered around him, worried. Rudy said, "I'm okay, but I should have listened to you, Sammy. I was careless." From that day on, Rudy learned to be more careful while playing, but he still enjoyed having fun with his friends.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a humble cat named Mimi. Mimi had a box of shiny jewelry. She loved to play with her jewelry every day. Mimi's best friend was a dog named Bubu. They liked to play together.
One day, Mimi and Bubu were playing with the jewelry. Mimi said, "Bubu, be careful with my jewelry. It is very special to me." Bubu nodded and said, "I will, Mimi. I promise."
While they were playing, Bubu started to sneeze. "Achoo! Achoo!" he sneezed. The sneeze made the jewelry fly into the air. Mimi and Bubu watched as the shiny jewelry fell all around them.
Mimi and Bubu looked at each other and started to laugh. They knew they had to pick up all the jewelry. They worked together and put the jewelry back in the box.
From that day on, Mimi and Bubu were more careful when they played with the jewelry. They always had fun and remembered to be humble and kind to each other.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear and a small bird. They were good friends. The big bear had strong muscles and the small bird could sing sweet songs.
One day, they found a big box with a heavy lid. The small bird tried to open it, but it was too hard. The big bear urged the small bird, "Let me try to open it with my strong muscles." The small bird said, "Okay, please help me."
The big bear used his strong muscles and opened the heavy lid. Inside the box, there were many nice things. There were toys and food, and they shared them. The small bird sang a happy song to thank the big bear.
The big bear and the small bird learned that if they help each other, they can do many things. They were happy to have each other as friends. The moral of the story is that friends should always help each other when they can.

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They liked to dig in the sand and find rocks. Lily found a big, shiny rock. She was very happy.
"Look, Max, I found a pretty rock!" she said.
Max looked at the rock. He wanted it too. He said, "Give me the rock, Lily. It is mine."
Lily said, "No, Max, it is mine. I found it first."
Max was angry. He said, "Give me the rock now, or I will hit you."
Lily was scared. She said, "No, Max, you are being mean. You can't demand the rock. You have to share."
Max did not listen. He tried to grab the rock from Lily. They both pulled and pushed. The rock fell on the ground. It broke into two pieces.
Lily and Max both cried. They were sad and tired. They had lost their pretty rock.
Mom came and saw them crying. She said, "What happened, Lily and Max?"
Lily and Max told Mom what happened. Mom said, "I'm sorry, Lily and Max. You both made a mistake. You should not fight over a rock. You should be kind and gentle to each other. You are friends, not enemies."
Lily and Max said, "We're sorry, Mom. We're sorry, Lily. We're sorry, Max."
Mom said, "It's okay, Lily and Max. I forgive you. Do you forgive each other?"
Lily and Max nodded. They hugged each other. They said, "We forgive you, Lily. We forgive you, Max."
Mom said, "That's good, Lily and Max. Now, let's go home and have some juice and cookies. You must be thirsty and hungry."
Lily and Max said, "Yes, Mom. We are thirsty and hungry. And we are tired too."
Mom said, "Then let's go home and rest. You can play again tomorrow. Maybe you will find another pretty rock. Or something else."
Lily and Max said, "Okay, Mom. Thank you, Mom."
They held Mom's hand and walked home. They were still sad about the rock, but they were happy to have each other. They learned a lesson. They learned to share and not to demand.

One day, Tom and his dog, Spot, went to the park. They wanted to play with their ball. But when they got there, it started to rain. Tom said, "Oh no, the rain will delay our play time." Spot barked, as if he agreed.
They saw a big tree and ran under it for some space to hide from the rain. Tom said, "Let's wait here until the rain stops." Spot wagged his tail and sat down. While waiting, Tom found a lemon on the ground. He picked it up and took a bite. "Yuck!" he said. "This is sour!"
After a while, the rain stopped. Tom and Spot were very happy. They played with their ball and had lots of fun. Tom threw the ball far away and Spot ran to catch it. They played until the sun went down. Then, they went home, tired but happy.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big bridge over a river. They wanted to cross the bridge and see what was on the other side.
They asked their mom if they could go. Mom said yes, but be careful and hold hands. Lily and Ben were happy and ran to the bridge. They started to walk on the bridge, but it was very high and shaky. Lily felt dizzy and scared. She stopped and held Ben's hand tighter.
Ben saw that Lily was dizzy and scared. He said, "Don't worry, Lily. I'm here with you. Let's pray to God and ask Him to help us cross the bridge. God loves us and He will keep us safe."
Lily nodded and closed her eyes. She prayed to God and asked Him to help them cross the bridge. She felt a warm and calm feeling in her heart. She opened her eyes and smiled at Ben. Ben smiled back and said, "Let's go, Lily. We can do it."
They walked slowly and carefully on the bridge, holding hands and praying to God. They reached the other side and saw a beautiful park with flowers and trees. They thanked God for helping them cross the bridge and for the beautiful park. They played and had fun until mom came to pick them up. They hugged mom and told her about their adventure. Mom was proud of them and said, "You are very brave and faithful, Lily and Ben. God is always with you and He answers your prayers."

One day, a little girl named Amy found a baby bird in her yard. The baby bird could not fly. Amy wanted to help the baby bird, so she picked it up and took it to her mom. "Mom, can we help this baby bird?" Amy asked. Her mom shrugged and said, "We can try, but it might be hard."
Amy and her mom took the baby bird inside and gave it some food and water. They made a warm bed for the baby bird to sleep in. The next day, Amy went to her friend Tom's house. She told Tom about the baby bird. Tom said, "I don't think you should help the baby bird. It's not your job." But Amy knew it was the right thing to do. She said, "I want to be honest and kind, so I will help the baby bird."
Amy and her mom took care of the baby bird for many days. They helped it get strong and learn to fly. One day, the baby bird was ready to go back to the wild. Amy and her mom took the baby bird outside and said goodbye. The baby bird flew away, happy and free. Amy felt good because she had been honest and kind. The moral of the story is to always be honest and kind, even when it's hard.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She lived in a small house with her mom and dad. Lucy had a great big yard to play in. She liked to run, jump, and play with her ball.
One day, Lucy found a well in her yard. She wanted to look inside, but her mom and dad did not permit her. They said it was not safe. Lucy was sad, but she listened to her mom and dad.
After a few days, Lucy saw a cat stuck near the well. She wanted to help the cat, but she remembered her mom and dad's words. So, she called her mom and dad. They came and saved the cat together. Lucy was happy that she listened to her mom and dad, and the cat was safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who really liked to build. She built houses and bridges and boats out of all sorts of things. One day the little girl's mom said, "Today we are going to build something special." She gave the little girl wood and bricks and tools and said, "Let's build a sport court together!" 
The little girl was so excited. She worked hard building walls and measuring the court and setting it up just so. Then she painted lines and put up a net. When the little girl was finished, she was so proud. 
Every day that week the little girl played on her sport court with her friends. Each day they played a new game and had so much fun.
Finally the little girl's mom said, "It's time to take a break. How about we make this a regular thing to do?" The little girl smiled and said, "Yes, let's build again soon!"

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a girl named Sally. Sally had a basket. In the basket, there were pretty flowers. Tim wanted to play with Sally.
"Can I play with you?" Tim asked. Sally was careful with her flowers. She did not want Tim to mess them up. "No, you can't play with me," Sally said. She refused to let Tim play.
Tim was sad. He ran away from Sally. He did not see a big hole in the ground. Tim fell into the hole. No one could help him get out. Sally and her basket of flowers went home.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack wanted to buy a movie so he went to the store with his mom.
Jack's mom said, âWhat movie do you want to buy?â

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to visit her friend Tim. Tim lived near the shore. They both loved to play by the water.
As they played, they saw a brilliant shell. "Look, Lily!" said Tim. "What a pretty shell!" Lily smiled and nodded. They both wanted the shell, but they knew they should share.
Lily and Tim decided to take turns holding the shell. They played and laughed all day by the shore. When the sun went down, they gave the shell back to the sea.
The two friends learned that sharing made them happy. They knew that playing together was better than having the shell all to themselves. And so, Lily and Tim stayed best friends forever.

Thomas had a beautiful team of his own. He loved playing with them every day. They had so much fun together. He owned some toy cars and trains that his team would drive together. They would also fly kites together in the park. It was so much fun to be together in a team. 
Sometimes their friends would join them. They would make forts and races together. Thomasâs team was so special. They got along so well and had lots of fun.
Thomas was very proud of his own beautiful team. He couldnât imagine the days without them. Sometimes they would even play games at night, like hide and seek. Thomas felt like they were family, and that made him so happy. 
He wanted to keep his special team together forever. He wanted to always be with his beautiful team.

Once upon a time, in a small country, there lived an elderly man named Tom. He had a big farm with many animals. Tom loved his animals and took good care of them. One day, a little duck came to live on the farm.
"Hello, little duck," said Tom. "Do you want to live on my farm with the other animals?"
The little duck looked at Tom and said, "Yes, please. I would like that very much."
But the other animals on the farm didn't like the little duck. They would not let him play with them. One day, the little duck decided he had enough. He went to the other animals and said, "I want to play with you. Please let me join you."
The other animals looked at the little duck and said, "No, we will not play with you. We refuse."
The little duck was sad, but he did not give up. He went to the river and started to practice swimming very fast. Day after day, he practiced and got better and better. One day, a big storm came to the country. The river started to flood, and the other animals were scared.
The little duck saw the animals in trouble and swam very fast to save them. One by one, he brought them to safety. After the storm, the animals were very grateful to the little duck.
"Thank you, little duck," they said. "We were wrong to refuse to play with you. From now on, we will be your friends."
And so, the little duck and the other animals lived happily ever after on the farm, and they all became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. He had a big heart and was always cheerful. One day, Jack was feeling a bit sick, so his parents gave him some medicine.
"Take the medicine, Jack!" said his dad. 
Jack frowned. He didn't want to take the medicine.
"It'll make you feel better, Jack," said his mum. She encouraged him with a big smile.
Jack took one sip of the medicine and soon his smile returned. 
"Thanks for encouraging me, Mum," said Jack.
"Anytime, Jack," said his mum, still smiling. 
Jack felt much better after taking the medicine. He was cheerful again and ready to have some more fun. The end.

Lily liked to sign with her hands. She learned sign from her mom, who was deaf. Lily could hear, but she loved to talk with her mom in sign. She also liked to teach sign to her friends at school.
One day, a new boy came to her class. His name was Ben. He was very big and had a lot of weight. He looked mean and scary. He did not talk to anyone. He just sat in his seat and frowned.
Lily wanted to be nice to Ben. She thought maybe he was lonely or sad. She walked up to him and smiled. She said hello with her voice and her hands. She asked him his name in sign.
Ben looked at her and laughed. He said, "What are you doing with your hands? Are you crazy? That's not how you talk. You talk with your mouth, like this." He made a loud and rude noise with his mouth.
Lily felt hurt and angry. She ran away and cried. She did not understand why Ben was so mean. She did not want to be his friend.
The next day, Lily's mom came to her class. She wanted to show the kids how to sign. She said sign was a beautiful and fun way to communicate. She said sign was for everyone, not just for deaf people. She said sign was a gift that Lily shared with her.
Lily was happy to see her mom. She hugged her and signed, "I love you, mom." She also saw Ben. He was sitting in his seat and frowning. He did not look happy.
Lily's mom asked the kids if they wanted to learn some sign. All the kids raised their hands and said yes. Except for Ben. He said no. He said sign was stupid and silly. He said he did not want to learn it.
Lily's mom looked at him and smiled. She said, "That's okay, Ben. You don't have to learn sign. But you should know that sign is not stupid or silly. It is a way to express yourself and connect with others. It is a way to show respect and kindness. It is a way to make friends. Maybe one day, you will change your mind and want to try sign. I hope you do. Because sign is not just for deaf people. It is for people who want to listen with their hearts."
Lily's mom then taught the kids some sign. They learned how to say hello, goodbye, thank you, and sorry. They learned how to say their names and their favorite colors. They learned how to say they were happy, sad, angry, or scared. They had a lot of fun.
Lily looked at Ben. He was still sitting in his seat and frowning. He did not join the fun. He did not learn any sign. He did not make any friends.
Lily felt sorry for Ben. She thought maybe he was lonely or sad. She walked up to him and smiled. She said goodbye with her voice and her hands. She said, "I hope you have a good day, Ben. Maybe tomorrow, you will want to learn sign with us. Maybe tomorrow, you will want to be my friend."
Ben looked at her and did not say anything. He did not laugh or make a rude noise. He just watched her walk away. He saw her sign with her mom and her friends. He saw her happy and ordinary. He felt something in his chest. He did not know what it was. He wondered if it was his heart. He wondered if it wanted to listen.
