Tom was a boy who liked to run. He ran every day with his dog, Spot. He ran in the park, in the street, and in the yard. He ran so fast that he could beat anyone in a race.
One day, Tom saw a poster for a big race. The poster said that the winner would get a prize: a shiny vest. Tom wanted the vest very much. He thought it would make him look cool and strong. He decided to join the race.
The day of the race came. Tom put on his shoes and his hat. He took Spot with him. He went to the park where the race was. He saw many other boys and girls who wanted to run. Some of them looked bigger and faster than him. Tom felt a little scared.
But he did not give up. He said to himself, "I can do it. I can run fast. I can win the vest." He said to Spot, "You can help me. You can run with me. You can cheer me on." Spot barked and wagged his tail.
The race started. Tom ran as fast as he could. He ran past some of the other runners. He ran with Spot by his side. He ran and ran and ran. He saw the finish line. He saw the vest. He ran even faster.
He crossed the line. He looked around. He was the first one. He had won the race. He had won the vest. He was so happy. He hugged Spot. He put on the vest. It fit him well. It was shiny and warm. He felt cool and strong.
He had gained a vest. He had gained a prize. He had gained a smile. He had been successful. He was proud of himself. He was proud of Spot. He was a boy who liked to run.

Once upon a time, in a normal little town, there lived a girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her pebbles. She had a big box full of them. She had pebbles of all colors: red, blue, green, and yellow. Lily would spend hours playing with her pebbles, making pictures and patterns on the ground.
One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, it's time to wash your pebbles. They are very dirty." Lily agreed and took her box of pebbles outside. She filled a big bowl with water and began to wash her pebbles one by one. As she washed them, they became shinier and prettier than before.
As Lily was washing her pebbles, her friend Tom came over. He saw the shiny pebbles and asked, "Lily, can I help you wash the pebbles?" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, Tom! Let's wash them together." So, Lily and Tom washed all the pebbles until they were clean and shiny.
When they were done, Lily and Tom made a big rainbow with the pebbles on the ground. It was the most beautiful rainbow they had ever seen. They were very happy and proud of their work.
From that day on, Lily and Tom would wash their pebbles and make beautiful pictures together. And they lived happily ever after, playing and creating with their shiny, clean pebbles.

Lily wanted to play with the sand in the park. She liked the texture of the sand. It was soft and smooth and she could make shapes with it. She asked her mom if she could play with the sand.
"Mom, can I play with the sand?" Lily said.
"Yes, you can, but only for a little while. We have to go home soon," Mom said.
Lily was happy. She ran to the sand and started to make a castle. She used a bucket and a shovel and some sticks. She was very proud of her castle.
But then, a big boy came and kicked her castle. He broke it and made a mess. Lily was very sad and angry. She cried and shouted at the boy.
"Hey, why did you do that? That was my castle! You are very mean!" Lily said.
The boy laughed and said, "I don't care. It's just sand. You can't tell me what to do. I can do whatever I want."
Lily felt very hurt. She wanted to hit the boy, but she knew that was wrong. She looked for her mom. She saw her mom coming towards her. She ran to her mom and hugged her.
"Mom, that boy broke my castle. He was very rude. He didn't permit me to play with the sand," Lily said.
Mom hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. That was not nice of him. He should have asked you first. He should have respected your work. You did a great job with your castle. I'm proud of you."
Mom took Lily to another spot in the park. She helped her make a new castle. She gave her a cookie and a juice. Lily felt better. She thanked her mom and smiled. She learned that some people are mean, but some people are kind. She learned that she should always ask before she touches someone else's things. She learned that she should always be polite and gentle. She learned that her mom loves her very much.

One day, a little cat named Tim went outside to play. It started to rain. The rain was persistent. Tim did not like getting wet, but he wanted to play.
Tim saw a big tree and ran to it. He used his strong legs to climb the tree. The tree kept him dry from the rain. Tim felt happy and safe in the tree.
While Tim was in the tree, he saw a little bird. The bird had a hurt leg. Tim wanted to help the bird. He picked up the bird with his mouth and climbed down the tree. Tim took the bird inside his warm and dry house. The little bird was thankful for Tim's help. They became good friends and played together even when it stopped raining.

Tim and Sam were brothers. They liked to play in the park with their ball. One day, they saw a big dog in the park. The dog was black and had a wide mouth. It looked angry and loud.
"Look, a dog!" Tim said. He wanted to pet the dog. He ran to the dog with his ball.
"Wait, Tim!" Sam said. He was scared of the dog. He followed Tim with his ball.
The dog saw Tim and Sam. It did not like them. It growled and barked. It stared at them with its big eyes.
"Go away, dog!" Tim said. He threw his ball at the dog. The ball hit the dog's nose.
The dog was more angry. It bit the ball. The ball popped. The dog spit out the ball. It tasted bitter.
"Ow, ow, ow!" the dog said. It ran away from Tim and Sam.
Tim and Sam were sad. They lost their ball. They went back to their mom.
"Mom, a dog popped our ball!" Tim said.
"Mom, the dog was mean and scary!" Sam said.
Mom hugged Tim and Sam. She gave them a new ball. She said, "I'm sorry, boys. Some dogs are not nice. But you are brave and smart. You did well to stay away from the dog. Now, let's go home and have some cookies."

Once upon a time, there was a lovely cat named Lucy. Lucy loved to go to the library. One day, she went to the library to find a fun book to read. In the library, she met a big dog named Max. Max was loud and liked to ring the library bell. Lucy did not like the loud noise.
"Please stop," Lucy said to Max. "I want to read my book in peace." Max did not listen and kept ringing the bell. Lucy was sad and did not know what to do.
Then, something unexpected happened. A tiny mouse named Tim came out from behind the books. Tim said, "I can help you, Lucy!" Tim went to Max and asked him to stop ringing the bell. Max saw the tiny mouse and got scared. He ran away from the library, and Lucy could finally read her book in peace. Lucy and Tim became best friends from that day on.

One day, a parrot named Polly was very tired. Polly wanted to take a nap in her cozy nest. She closed her eyes and tried to sleep, but there was a loud noise outside. Polly was a persistent parrot, so she tried to ignore the noise and sleep.
The loud noise did not stop. Polly opened her eyes and saw a big, friendly dog named Max. Max was playing with a ball and making the noise. Polly asked Max, "Can you please be quiet? I want to take a nap." Max felt bad and said, "I am sorry, Polly. I will go play somewhere else."
Polly went back to her nest and tried to nap again. But guess what? Max came back! He said, "Polly, I found a new place to play, but I am lonely. Will you come with me?" Polly was a persistent parrot and still wanted to nap, but she also wanted to help Max. So, Polly agreed to go with Max.
When they reached the new play area, Polly saw a big tree. The tree had a perfect spot for her to take a nap. Polly told Max, "You can play here, and I will nap in this tree." Max was happy, and Polly finally took her nap. The unexpected thing was that Polly and Max became best friends, even though they were so different.

Once upon a time there were two siblings, Jack and Jill. They had gone to the park to play.
Jack said to Jill, "Let's go play jazz!"
Jill replied, "That sounds like a lot of fun! I have a plan, let's have a jazz party!"
The siblings smiled at each other and ran off to find some friends to join the party. Jack was feeling extra bossy, so he shouted at his friends, "Come on, hurry up!"
Jack and Jill had assembled quite a few friends, and everyone was ready to get the party started.
Jack had his saxophone, Jill had her clarinet, and the rest of the kids had their tambourines and drums, and it sounded like all the angels in heaven were singing.
Everyone was having a great time dancing and playing all the jazz music. The party went on for a few hours, and when it was all over, the friends agreed it was the best jazz party ever. 
Jack was very proud of himself for being so bossy and getting everyone together.

One day, a little girl named Amy went to the park. She saw a cat with a brush in its mouth. The cat looked impatient. Amy wanted to help the cat, so she sat down next to it.
"Hi cat, why do you have a brush?" Amy asked. The cat looked at her and meowed. It was trying to tell her something. Amy thought the cat wanted her to brush its fur. So, she took the brush and started brushing the cat.
As she brushed the cat, something unexpected happened. The cat started to talk! "Thank you, Amy! I am a magic cat. I could not talk until someone brushed me," the cat said. Amy was very surprised, but happy she could help. Now, Amy and the magic cat were good friends and had lots of fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a mysterious box. Inside the box was a journal. The journal was very old and had many stories in it. One day, a little girl named Lucy found the box in her room. She was very curious about what was inside.
Lucy opened the box and saw the journal. She wanted to remove the journal from the box to read the stories. She said, "Mommy, look what I found! Can I read the stories in this journal?" Her mommy said, "Of course, Lucy! Let's read them together."
So, Lucy and her mommy removed the journal from the box and started to read the stories. They found many fun and exciting stories about animals, fairies, and adventures. Lucy and her mommy had a great time reading the mysterious journal together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very hungry. He wanted to eat a big apple. He looked at the apple tree in his yard. There were many apples on the tree.
Tim found a long cloth. He thought, "I can use this cloth to get an apple." He threw the cloth up to the tree. The cloth caught an apple. Tim pulled the cloth down. The apple came down too.
Tim was happy. He said, "I did it! I got an apple!" He took a big bite. His hungry tummy was now complete. Tim shared the apple with his friend. They both smiled and played together.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill, who loved to have fun. They decided to have a race. They looked around and found a big triangle. It was so pretty! 
Jack said, "Let's use it as a start line for our race." Jill said, "Yay!"
So they raced towards the finish line. Jill was pretty fast, but Jack was even faster. He won the race!
Jill was sad that she didn't win, but Jack said, "That was a fun race! Let's do it again another day." Jill said, "Yay!"
The two friends smiled and went off to play with the pretty triangle.

Lily and Ben love to play with their cart. It is red and has four wheels. They can put their toys in the cart and push it around the yard. Sometimes they take turns riding in the cart, too.
One day, they see a chubby cat sitting on the fence. The cat is black and white and has a fluffy tail. Lily and Ben want to pet the cat, but they are afraid it might scratch them.
"Hello, cat," Lily says. "Do you want to play with us?"
The cat looks at them and meows. It jumps down from the fence and walks towards them. Lily and Ben are happy. They think the cat likes them.
They offer the cat some of their toys, but the cat is not interested. It sniffs the cart and climbs inside. It curls up and closes its eyes. It looks very cozy.
"Look, Ben," Lily says. "The cat likes our cart. It wants to sleep in it."
Ben nods. He thinks the cat is cute. He strokes the cat gently. The cat purrs.
Lily and Ben smile. They decide to let the cat sleep in their cart. They sit next to the cart and watch the cat. They love the cat and the cat loves their cart. They are all happy.

Lily and Ben went to the park with Mom. They saw a big pond with many ducks and swans. Lily liked the swans. They were white and pretty. She wanted to feed them some bread.
"Mom, can I give bread to the swans?" Lily asked.
"Sure, but be careful. Swans can bite sometimes," Mom said.
Lily took a piece of bread and walked to the edge of the pond. She saw a swan that looked weird. It had a black spot on its neck and a limp wing. It looked sad and lonely.
"Hello, swan. Do you want some bread?" Lily said.
The swan nodded and swam closer to Lily. Lily threw the bread to the swan. The swan ate it and made a soft noise.
"Thank you, little girl. You are very kind," the swan said.
Lily was surprised. She did not know swans could talk.
"How can you talk?" Lily asked.
"I can talk because I am a magic swan. I used to be a prince, but a witch turned me into a swan. She said I have to suffer until someone breaks the spell," the swan said.
"That's not fair. How can someone break the spell?" Lily asked.
The swan sighed.
"I don't know. The witch said only true love can break the spell. But who would love a weird swan like me?" the swan said.
Lily felt sorry for the swan. She wanted to help him.
"I love you, swan. You are not weird. You are beautiful and brave. Maybe I can break the spell," Lily said.
She hugged the swan gently. The swan felt a warm feeling in his heart. He felt something change in his body. He looked at his reflection in the water. He was not a swan anymore. He was a boy.
"Wow, you did it! You broke the spell! Thank you, Lily. You are my true love," the boy said.
Lily smiled. She liked the boy. He had brown hair and blue eyes. He looked like a prince.
"You're welcome, boy. What is your name?" Lily asked.
"My name is Leo. What is yours?" the boy asked.
"My name is Lily. Do you want to play with me and Ben?" Lily asked.
"Yes, I do. But first, can I kiss you?" Leo asked.
Lily nodded. Leo kissed her on the cheek. Lily giggled.
Mom saw Lily and Leo. She was shocked.
"Lily, who is that boy? Where did he come from?" Mom asked.
Lily and Leo ran to Mom. They told her the story of the magic swan and the witch.
Mom did not believe them at first. She thought they were making it up. But then she saw the black spot on Leo's neck. It was the same as the swan's.
Mom realized it was true. She was amazed and happy.
She hugged Lily and Leo.
"I'm glad you found each other. You are both very special. Now, let's go home and have some cake," Mom said.
Lily and Leo agreed. They held hands and followed Mom. Ben joined them too. He liked Leo. He wanted to be his friend.
They all went home and had cake. They were happy. They did not see the witch. She was watching them from a distance. She was angry and jealous. She wanted to curse them again. But she could not. The spell was broken. She had lost her power. She had to suffer. She flew away on her broom. She never bothered them again.

It was a sunny day when John and his Mom went to the park. John was very excited to go there. He wanted to see the swings and the slides. 
But when they got there, John was not happy. His Mom was looking for a bench to sit on but there were none. John ran around trying to find the perfect spot to rest his tired feet.
Then, John noticed something. It was a very attractive television in the corner of the playground. He rushed over and asked his Mom, "Can we sleep here?".
"No, John," replied his Mom. "We can't sleep here. It's too far away from home and you need your rest."
John was disappointed, and he knew there was nothing he could do. He wanted to stay and watch the television, but he knew his Mom was right. They said goodbye to the television and went home. 
John knew it was time for bed, even though he was reluctant. When he laid his head on his pillow, he thought of the television and smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a little white cat named Fluffy. Fluffy had delicate fur that was soft and smooth. Fluffy liked to play and learn new things every day.
One day, Fluffy wanted to learn how to catch a ball. Fluffy's friend, a big brown dog named Buddy, was very good at catching balls. Buddy showed Fluffy how to jump and catch the ball in the air.
Fluffy tried to jump and catch the ball, but it was hard at first. Fluffy did not give up. Fluffy practiced and practiced. Soon, Fluffy learned how to catch the ball just like Buddy. They played and had fun together all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a big, round pumpkin. It lived in a garden with many other pumpkins. They all liked to play and have fun together. But one day, two pumpkins had a quarrel. They were both mad and did not want to play anymore.
A wise old owl saw the quarrel and decided to help. The owl talked to the two pumpkins and asked them why they were mad. One pumpkin said, "I wanted to play hide and seek, but the other pumpkin wanted to play tag." The other pumpkin nodded, still mad.
The wise owl thought for a moment and then said, "Why don't you both play a game together that you both like?" The two pumpkins looked at each other and thought it was a good idea. They stopped their quarrel and played a fun game together. All the pumpkins in the garden were happy again, and they learned that it is better to play together than to quarrel.

Alice in Chains is an American rock band formed in Seattle , Washington , in 1987 by guitarist and songwriter Jerry Cantrell and original lead vocalist Layne Staley . The initial lineup was rounded out by drummer Sean Kinney and bassist Mike Starr , who was replaced in 1993 by Mike Inez .

Once upon a time, there was a lady named Sue. Sue loved to lead her dog, Spot, on walks. Spot was a good dog who liked to play and run.
One day, Sue and Spot went to the park. They saw a big tree. Sue said, "Spot, let's go sit under the tree." Spot wagged his tail and followed Sue. They sat under the tree and enjoyed the nice day.
Sue had a tasty snack in her bag. She took out a big apple and said, "Yum, this apple is so tasty!" Spot looked at Sue, and she gave him a tasty treat too. They both ate their snacks and played together all day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Ella. She was eager to make something special for her mom. Ella thought and thought about what to make. Then, she had a great idea! She would make a pretty bag for her mom to carry things in.
Ella found some soft cloth and cut it into two big pieces. She put the pieces together and sewed them with a needle and thread. She made a handle for the bag too. Ella was very happy with her work.
Ella put the bag in a box and wrapped it with a big bow. She gave it to her mom with a big smile. Her mom was so happy and gave Ella a big hug. From that day on, Ella's mom used the bag all the time. Ella felt proud that she could make something so special for her mom.

Once upon a time, in a charming little house, there lived a girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her toys and talk on her toy telephone. She would pretend to call her friends and have long chats with them.
One day, Lily's mom told her it was time to clean up her toys. Lily didn't want to quit playing with her telephone. She kept talking and laughing, ignoring her mom. Her mom asked her again, but Lily still didn't listen.
Finally, her mom took the telephone away and said, "Lily, you must learn to listen and do what you are told." Lily was sad, but she understood. She cleaned up her toys and said sorry to her mom. From that day on, Lily always listened to her mom and did what she was told. The moral of the story is that it's important to listen and follow directions.

Once upon a time, there was a playful little boy. He had a friend who lived next door and the two always had fun together.
One day the little boy wanted to show his friend his freshly made sack. He was very proud of it and thought it looked clean and nice.
He said to his friend, "Look! I made this sack by myself. Isn't it nice and clean?"
But his friend shook his head and muttered, "No! It's not clean. I don't like it!" 
The little boy was very sad to hear this and quickly ran away, tears streaming down his face. He never saw his friend again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to play outside with his friends. They would run, jump, and laugh all day long.
One sunny day, Tim saw a fast figure run by. The figure was so quick, it was hard to see. Tim wanted to know what it was, so he decided to follow it. He ran as fast as he could, trying to catch up to the figure.
As Tim followed the fast figure, he found himself in a beautiful park. The figure slowed down and Tim could see it was a cute bunny. The bunny hopped over to Tim and they became friends. Tim and the bunny played together in the park until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a nice nurse. She had a gray dress and a kind smile. She always wanted to lend a helping hand. 
One day, a little boy needed help. He was only three years old and he was hungry. The nurse kindly lent him a snack. She watched him enjoy his snack and smiled. 
Next, the nurse lent the boy a toy. He was so excited to play with it and thanked the nurse. He was so happy as he went off to play with his new toy. 
The nurse was happy too. She was glad that she could lend a helping hand to the little boy. The nurse knew that she made him smile and it made her feel good inside.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was three years old and very alert.
One day, Jane went to the park with her mom. She was so excited that she wanted to explore.
When they got to the park, Jane wanted to jump on the swing. But her mom said, "No, you need to remove your vest before you can swing."
But Jane didn't want to. She did not want to take off her vest.
So, Jane got frustrated. She started to cry and said, "No! I want to keep it on!"
But her mom said, "No, Jane. You need to remove your vest in order to swing. It's not safe otherwise!" 
Finally, after a few minutes of crying, Jane agreed to take off her vest. She removed her vest and went on to have a lot of fun in the park.

The Act effectively removed the right of the Lords to veto money bills completely , and replaced a right of veto over other public bills with a maximum delay of two years . It also reduced the maximum term of a parliament from seven years to five .

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lucy. She was 3 years old and loved playing with her friends. One day, Lucy was so excited because a special gift was coming for her. She ran to the window to watch for the delivery person to arrive. 
Suddenly, there it was â a big, red box! Lucy could hardly contain her joy. She ran outside and smiled as the delivery person handed her the box.
As she hugged the box tightly, Lucy said, âThank you for my gift.â
The delivery person smiled. âYou're welcome. Now, I had better be going. Have a nice day!â
With the box in her hands, Lucy started to walk home. But then she had an idea â she would have a special kick with her friends. She asked them to join her at the park and they all said yes!
Once they were all gathered, they started to play. Lucy kicked the ball so far and everyone cheered. When the sun started to set, everyone said goodbye and went home.
As Lucy hugged the box to take it inside, she felt a little sleepy. She thanked her friends for coming, and she was so happy with her special gift. She felt so lucky and went to get some rest.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sophie. One day she set off to explore the woods near her home. As she walked, she kicked at the ash on the floor. She had never seen ash before!
As she continued to walk she heard a noise. It sounded like a little voice. She peered around a tree and saw an old lady. The lady was very small and wrinkly.
The old lady spoke to Sophie. "Why have you come to the woods?" she asked. Sophie told the old lady that she was exploring.
The old lady then told Sophie a story. "Once upon a time, there was a foolish knight who set off to find a dragon. He was sure he could catch it and make it his pet. But what he didn't know was that dragons can't be caught."
The old lady, who had once been the foolish knight, then smiled at Sophie. "Always remember to not be foolish like me," she said, "because you never know the consequences."
Sophie saw the wisdom in the old lady's words and thanked her, before heading back home.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little girl named Sara. She was always looking for something new and exciting to do. One day, while playing in her bedroom, she had a bright idea! She decided to create something special.
So she grabbed some paper, a pencil and some crayons, and got to work. Pretty soon, Sara had created a beautiful drawing of a freezer. She was so proud of what she had made that she held it up high and showed it to her mom.
"Mom, look! I created a freezer!"
Her mom smiled and said, "That's so wonderful, Sara! What should we put in it?"
Sara thought for a few moments, but then had another idea. She said, "Let's put ice cream in it!" Her mom smiled and said, "That sounds like a great idea!"
So they went to the store and bought some ice cream. As soon as they got home, they put it in the freezer that Sara had created. It was so much fun to have an ice cream treat anytime they wanted!
Sara had created something so special that her mom was very proud of her. Now every time Sara opened her freezer, she would remember her accomplishment with a smile.

One day, a little girl named Sue was very hungry. She knew it was time for lunch. Sue looked and looked, but she could not find her lunch. She started to feel sad.
Sue's big sister, Jane, saw her and wanted to help. Jane said, "Let's look together." They looked in the kitchen, but it was not there. They looked in the living room, but it was not there. Finally, they looked in the bedroom. There, under Sue's bed, Jane found a box. She opened the box and revealed Sue's lunch.
Sue was so happy to see her lunch. She thanked Jane for helping her. They both sat down and ate their lunch together. Sue felt calm and happy again. The two sisters enjoyed their time and promised to help each other always.

Once there was a little boy called James who was very excited for an adventure. He grabbed his special blue jacket, put it on and skipped away. As he skipped around the corner, he heard someone call for help. It was an old man who had lost his way.
James knew he had to help the old man, but he was also careful. He made sure to take a safe path so that he could help the old man and still stay safe. He skipped until he found the old man. Together they made their way back to the old manâs house and the old man thanked James for his help.
The moral of this story is to be kind and helpful, but also to be careful when we help others. We should always remember to stay safe when we help people.

Once upon a time, there was a compassionate girl named Lily. She loved to help others and make them happy. One day, she found a big piece of metal in her yard. She thought of a way to use it to spread joy.
Lily asked her dad to help her make the metal into a big, shiny slide. They worked hard together and soon, the slide was ready. Lily invited all her friends to come and play on the new slide.
Everyone had fun going up and down the slide. They laughed and smiled as they played. Lily was happy to see her friends enjoying the slide. She knew that her compassionate heart had helped spread happiness to everyone.

Once upon a time there was a mighty king. One day he decided to leave his castle and take a walk. He arrived at a well and decided to take a rest. Suddenly, a fish popped out of the well.
"What can I do for you?" the king asked.
"I need your help, mighty king," said the fish. "A wicked witch cast a spell on me, and the only way to break it is for you to take a sip of this magical water." 
The king agreed, and after taking a sip of the magical water in the well, the spell was broken. The fish thanked him and said its goodbyes, leaving the king feeling happy and proud that he had been able to help.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play games. They had many toys and cards and puzzles. But they always wanted to win. They did not like to share or take turns. They would fight and shout and cry when they lost.
One day, their mom had enough of their noisy fights. She said, "You two need to learn to value what you have. Some children have no toys or games at all. You should be thankful and kind to each other. If you don't, I will take away all your toys and games for a week."
Tom and Lily did not listen to their mom. They thought she was just angry and would not do it. They kept playing and fighting and shouting. They did not value their toys or games or each other.
The next day, when they woke up, they saw that their mom had kept her word. She had taken away all their toys and games and put them in a big box. She said, "You can have them back when you learn to value them and each other. Until then, you can only play with these books and crayons."
Tom and Lily were very sad and bored. They had nothing to play with. They missed their toys and games. They realized that their mom was right. They had been selfish and rude. They had not valued what they had. They had not valued each other.
They decided to say sorry to their mom and to each other. They hugged and said, "We are sorry, mom. We are sorry, twin. We love you. We will value what we have. We will value each other. We will share and take turns and be nice."
Their mom was happy to hear that. She smiled and said, "I am proud of you, Tom and Lily. You have learned a valuable lesson. You can have your toys and games back. But remember to value them and each other. And don't be so noisy!"
Tom and Lily were happy to have their toys and games back. They played with them and with each other. They shared and took turns and were nice. They were not noisy. They valued what they had. They valued each other. They had more fun than ever.

Once upon a time, there was a panda named Pandy. Pandy was very careful when he walked in the forest. He did not want to step on the little bugs or hurt the pretty flowers.
One day, Pandy saw a little girl crying. He asked her, "Why are you sad?" The little girl said, "I can't find my way home." Pandy wanted to help her, so he said, "I will mind you and take you home. Just hold my hand and be careful."
So, Pandy and the little girl walked through the forest. They were very careful not to step on bugs or hurt flowers. Soon, they found the little girl's home. Her mom and dad were so happy to see her! They thanked Pandy for minding their little girl and being so careful. Pandy smiled and went back to the forest, happy that he could help.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play together. But sometimes they did not behave well. They would fight over toys, make a mess, and not listen to their mom and dad.
One day, mom and dad had to go to a wedding. They told Anna and Ben to wear nice dresses and suits and to behave well at the party. Anna and Ben nodded, but they did not really want to go. They thought weddings were boring and they wanted to stay home and play.
At the party, Anna and Ben were troubled. They did not like the food, the music, or the people. They ran around, knocked over glasses, and made loud noises. Mom and dad were very angry and embarrassed. They told Anna and Ben to stop and to say sorry to the hosts. But Anna and Ben did not listen. They kept being naughty and rude.
Then, something bad happened. Anna tripped over a long dress and fell down. She hurt her knee and tore her dress. She started to cry. Ben saw what happened and ran to help her. He felt sorry for his sister and for being mean. He hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Anna. Are you okay?"
Anna looked at her brother and stopped crying. She said, "I'm sorry, too, Ben. I was not nice to you or to anyone. We should behave better and be kind." They both realized that they had made a mistake and that they had to change.
They went to mom and dad and apologized for their bad behavior. They also said sorry to the hosts and the guests. Mom and dad were glad that Anna and Ben learned their lesson. They hugged them and said, "We love you, but you have to behave well and respect others. That is the right thing to do."
Anna and Ben nodded and smiled. They felt better and happier. They decided to enjoy the party and to have fun with their family and friends. They also promised to behave well and to be nice to each other from then on.

The first church was markedly cruciform in shape and smaller than the present floor plan . This early structure had a choir without aisles and more truncated , and a nave with only a single aisle on its north and south sides ( Fig . 4 ) . The central tower rose above the crossing between the north and south transepts and may have held bells in its upper storey . The north wall of the choir is the earliest extant structure , dating to the years immediately after the church 's 1224 foundation ; the clerestory windows on top of it are from the later post-1270 reconstruction . This wall has blocked up windows extending to a low level above ground , indicating that it was an external wall and proving that the eastern limb then had no aisle ( Fig . 5 ) .

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Ruby. She was three years old, and she loved to explore. One day, Ruby was standing outside when she spotted something big in the distance. She couldn't quite make out what it was, but it was moving fast!
Ruby: "Mommy, what is that?"
Mommy: "That's a very large motorcycle, Ruby. It's rushing by us very quickly." 
Ruby smiled and watched with curiosity as the large motorcycle zoomed by. Suddenly, she felt an urge to hop on the bike and rush around like the driver! She jumped up and down with excitement. 
Mommy: "Oh Ruby, that's not a good idea. You're too young to drive a motorcycle!" 
Ruby pouted, but she knew her mother was right. With a heavy heart, Ruby said goodbye to the large motorcycle and went back inside the house. 
The days that followed were filled with adventures close to home, but Ruby never forgot the thrill of watching the large motorcycle rush by.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful lion. The lion lived in a big jungle. He liked to scare other animals. One day, he found a long string. The lion had an idea.
The lion tied the string to a tree. He hid behind the tree. When a little mouse walked by, the lion jumped out and said, "Boo!" The little mouse was very scared. "Please don't scare me," said the mouse. The lion laughed and said, "Okay, I won't scare you anymore."
After that, the lion and the mouse became friends. They played with the string together. They had lots of fun. The lion learned that it was better to be kind than to scare others. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a big desert, there lived a confused little rabbit. He liked to taste new things. One day, he saw a cactus. It was green and tall.
The rabbit thought, "I want to taste the cactus!" So he hopped close to the cactus. But when he took a bite, "Ouch!" he cried. The cactus hurt his mouth. The rabbit was sad.
A wise old owl saw the rabbit and said, "Little rabbit, not everything is good to taste." The rabbit learned not to bite things that can hurt him. And from that day, the rabbit only tasted good things like carrots and lettuce.

Once upon a time, there was a big red clock. The clock lived in a little boy's room. The little boy loved his clock so much. Every day, the boy would talk to the clock and say "please tell me the time."
One day, the clock stopped working. The boy was very sad. He asked his mom for help. His mom said, "please be nice to your sister, and I will help you fix the clock." The boy did not like to play with his sister, but he wanted his clock to work again.
The boy played with his sister, and they had a lot of fun. They laughed and played all day. Then, the mom fixed the red clock. The boy was very happy. He learned that being nice to others can make you happy too. And from that day on, the boy was always nice to his sister.

Wales have won 355 of their 690 Test matches for a 51. 45 % winning record . Their biggest Test defeat was 96 – 13 loss to South Africa in 1998 , and their largest victory a 98 – 0 defeat of Japan in 2004 . Their record for most tries in a match is 16 , scored against Portugal in 1994 – they also scored 102 points in this match , more than in any other Test . Wales ' record for consecutive Test wins is eleven , and for consecutive losses is ten .

Once upon a time, there was a farm. It was a calm and peaceful place.
On the farm, there was a big red barn. Inside the barn was an old cow.
The cow had big black spots on its back. Every day, the cow would clap its hooves and everyone around the farm would laugh. 
One day, an old farmer came to the farm. He sang a happy song and clapped his hands. All the animals were happy and clapped along with him. 
The farmer and the animals clapped and laughed for a long time. When all the clapping was done, the farm was even calmer and more peaceful. 
Everyone on the farm was very happy and they clapped more and more every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily went outside to play in her yard. She saw a tree with a big, round thing hanging on it. It was a pear!
Lily wanted to look at the pear more. She went closer to the tree to examine the pear. As she got closer, she saw a small, scared, and frightened bug on the ground. She thought the bug might need help.
Lily picked up the bug and put it on the pear. The bug was happy and not frightened anymore. It started to eat the pear. Lily knew that she had done a good thing. She went back inside to tell her mommy and daddy about her new friend, the bug. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear who loved to bake. He had a little bear friend who wanted to learn how to bake too. So, the big bear said, "I will teach you how to bake, little bear!"
One day, they went to the woods to find a special tree. The big bear told the little bear that this tree had a secret. The tree looked dead, but it was not. The big bear said, "This tree will help us bake something very yummy."
The big bear and the little bear took a piece of the tree and went back home. They used the piece of the tree in their baking. The little bear was so happy to learn from the big bear. They baked and baked, and then they had a big party with all their friends. The secret of the dead-looking tree made their baking the best ever, and everyone loved it.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a gifted girl named Lily. She had a special alarm clock. This alarm clock could talk!
Every morning, the alarm clock would say "Wake up, Lily!" Lily would repeat after the alarm, "Wake up, Lily!" They would laugh and start their day.
One day, Lily's friend, Sam, came to play. They played with toys, ate snacks, and had fun. Then, the alarm clock said, "Time to clean up!" Lily and Sam said together, "Time to clean up!" They put away their toys and smiled. They loved repeating the alarm clock's words.
Lily's mom saw how happy they were and said, "You two are so good at listening to the alarm clock!" Lily and Sam looked at each other and said, "Thank you!" The gifted alarm clock helped them have a great day, and they could not wait to play again.

One day, a little caterpillar named Tim was very upset. He saw his friends wear pretty clothes, but he had none. Tim wanted to wear something nice too. He crawled under a big leaf and started to cry.
A kind girl named Amy saw Tim the caterpillar crying. She asked, "Why are you upset, little caterpillar?" Tim said, "I want to wear pretty clothes like my friends, but I don't have any." Amy thought for a moment and smiled.
Amy picked some colorful flowers and made a tiny hat for Tim. She put it on his head and said, "Now you can wear this pretty hat!" Tim stopped crying and smiled. He was so happy to wear his new hat. Tim thanked Amy, and they played together all day. Tim the caterpillar was not upset anymore.

One day, a big boy named Tim found a telephone. He thought it was impressive. He showed it to his friend, Sue. Sue was very happy to see it. They played with the telephone, pretending to talk to each other.
But then, their friend, Sam, came and wanted to add his toy car to their playtime. Tim and Sue did not want to play with the car. They only wanted to play with the telephone. This made Sam sad and upset.
Sam walked away and found a big box. He put his toy car in the box and started to push it. Tim and Sue saw this and thought it was fun. They asked Sam if they could add their telephone to the box and play together. Sam agreed, and they all played happily with the box, the car, and the telephone.

When stars form in the present Milky Way galaxy they are composed of about 71 % hydrogen and 27 % helium , as measured by mass , with a small fraction of heavier elements . Typically the portion of heavy elements is measured in terms of the iron content of the stellar atmosphere , as iron is a common element and its absorption lines are relatively easy to measure . The portion of heavier elements may be an indicator of the likelihood that the star has a planetary system .

One day, a boy named Tim found a big, heavy box. He was very happy. He wanted to see what was inside the box. He opened the box and saw a computer. Tim was very excited. He wanted to play with the computer.
Tim took the computer out of the box. He put it on the table. He turned it on. The computer made a loud noise. Tim was scared. He thought something bad would happen. But he still wanted to play.
Tim played with the computer. He had fun. But then, the computer got very hot. It started to smoke. Tim was scared. He tried to turn it off, but it was too late. The computer broke and Tim was sad.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a shy cat named Tom. Tom liked to sit by the fireplace and watch the fire. He felt warm and happy there. But sometimes, he would hear strange sounds from the fireplace that scared him.
One day, Tom saw a little mouse named Jerry. Jerry was very fast, and he liked to run around the house. Tom wanted to play with Jerry, but he was too shy to ask. So, he watched Jerry from afar, hoping that one day they could be friends.
One day, Jerry got too close to the fireplace and his tail got stuck. Tom knew he had to help. He found a small thing to cut Jerry's tail free. Tom saved Jerry, and they became best friends. From that day on, they played together all the time, and Tom was not shy anymore.

Tom likes to help his mom in the kitchen. He likes to polish the spoons and forks with a napkin. He thinks it is important to make them shiny and clean. Mom says he is a good helper.
One day, Tom finds a big spoon in the drawer. It is very dirty and dull. Tom wants to polish it with his napkin. He rubs and rubs, but the spoon does not shine. He wonders what is wrong with it.
He shows the spoon to his mom. Mom smiles and says, "That is not a spoon, Tom. That is a ladle. We use it to scoop soup. It is made of wood, not metal. You cannot polish wood with a napkin. But you can wash it with soap and water."
Tom learns a new word: ladle. He also learns that different things need different ways to clean them. He is happy to help his mom wash the ladle. He still likes to polish the spoons and forks, but he also likes to learn new things. Mom says he is a smart helper.

When a player is shooting free throws , there are a certain number of players at the boundaries of the key , each occupying a slot traced at the boundaries of the key . In most cases , the free throw shooter is behind the free throw line , while three of his opponents are along the sides of the key , one side with two players , the other with one . Two of his opponents are situated nearest to the basket on both sides , while his two teammates are beside the two opponents closest to the basket , with the other player from the opposing team situated farthest from the basket . In the U.S. NCAA , there are as many as six players along the key , with the opposing team allowed to have as many as four players , with the same arrangement as in the NBA and FIBA but with another player facing his teammate farthest to the basket . ( See photographs to the right . )

One day, a mighty cat named Tom went to the market to sell napkins. He put the napkins on a big table and said, "Come and buy my soft napkins!"
A little girl named Sue came to the table and said, "I want to buy a napkin, please." Tom gave her a napkin and Sue was very happy. She said, "Thank you, mighty cat!"
Then, something unexpected happened. A strong wind came and blew all the napkins away. Tom was sad because he could not sell any more napkins. But Sue had an idea. She said, "Let's make a big kite with my napkin!"
Tom and Sue made a big kite with the napkin and played all day. They had so much fun, they forgot about selling napkins. And that day, Tom learned that sometimes, unexpected things can bring joy and new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play dress-up. She had a big box full of costumes. Lily liked to wear her costumes and pretend she was a princess, a superhero, or an animal.
One day, Lily had a fun idea. She wanted to have a costume party with her friends. She called her friends and told them to come over. Lily said they would play a game to see who had the best costume. They all wanted to win, so they tried very hard to find their best costume.
When the friends came to Lily's house, they saw that she had hung up a sign that said "Costume Party". Everyone put on their costumes and started to play. They danced, laughed, and had a great time. At the end of the party, Lily gave a prize to the person with the best costume. They all agreed it was a fun day and they loved playing dress-up together.

One day, a little boy named Tim was restless. He wanted to play outside but it was raining. So, he decided to play inside his house. He went to the kitchen and saw a big sink. Tim had an idea.
Tim called his friend, Sam, and said, "Come to my house. We will play with the sink and water." Sam came over and they started to play with the sink. They filled it with water and made a big mess. They were having so much fun.
But then, Tim's mom came into the kitchen. She saw the mess and was very mad. She said, "You boys need to clean this up right now!" Tim and Sam were sad. They cleaned the mess and Tim's mom locked the kitchen door. Now, they could not play with the sink again. They learned that they should not play with things that can make a big mess.

One day, a boy named Tim had a kite. He loved his kite so much. Tim wanted to fly the kite in the park. But it was a sleepy day. There was no wind to help the kite fly. Tim was sad.
Then, a big dog named Max came to Tim. Max saw the kite and wanted to help. So, Max ran very fast. Tim held the kite and let Max zip with it. The kite went up in the sky! Tim was so happy.
But, the kite got stuck in a tree! Tim and Max were sad. They did not know what to do. Then, a nice bird came and helped. The bird took the kite out of the tree. Tim and Max were happy again. They played with the kite all day.

Lily liked to draw with her crayons. She had many colors and papers. She made pictures of flowers, animals, and people. She put her pictures in a folder. The folder was blue and had a sticker of a star.
One day, Lily wanted to show her pictures to her friend Sam. She took her folder and went to his house. She knocked on the door and Sam opened it.
"Hi, Lily! What do you have?" Sam asked.
"I have my pictures. Do you want to see?" Lily said.
"Yes, please!" Sam said. He invited Lily inside.
Lily opened her folder and showed Sam her pictures. Sam liked them very much. He said they were pretty and colorful.
"Can I have one?" Sam asked.
"Sure, you can have one. Which one do you like?" Lily said.
Sam looked at the pictures and picked one. It was a picture of a butterfly. It had yellow and black wings and a red body.
"I like this one. It is a butterfly. It can fly and change. Sometimes it is a caterpillar, sometimes it is a butterfly." Sam said.
Lily smiled and gave him the picture. She was happy that Sam liked her picture.
"Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. Do you want to play with me?" Sam said.
"Yes, I do. What do you want to play?" Lily said.
Sam thought for a moment and then said, "Let's play pretend. We can be butterflies and change. We can fly and see the flowers."
Lily liked that idea. She and Sam put their folders away and went to the garden. They pretended to be butterflies and changed. They flew and saw the flowers. They had fun and laughed. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a man who wanted to sell his vehicle. The vehicle was old and tired. The man was sad because no one wanted to buy his vehicle.
One day, a boy came to look at the vehicle. The boy liked the vehicle very much. But the boy did not have enough money to buy it. The man and the boy were both sad.
Then, the boy had an idea. He asked the man if he could help him sell other things to make money. Together, they sold many things and the boy made enough money to buy the tired vehicle. The man and the boy were both happy.

One day, a cat and a dog were playing in the park. The cat, named Tom, was very flexible. He could jump and twist in many ways. The dog, named Sam, liked to run fast.
Tom and Sam saw a big, colorful menu on a tree. The menu had pictures of food. "Yummy!" said Sam. "Let's eat!" Tom agreed. They walked closer to the tree, but the menu moved away. They tried again, but the menu kept moving.
"Let's escape and catch the menu!" said Tom. They ran after the menu, laughing and having fun. Suddenly, the menu stopped moving. A friendly squirrel came out from behind the tree. "Surprise!" said the squirrel. "I was moving the menu to make you laugh!" Tom, Sam, and the squirrel all laughed and played together for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to play with her friends, Doggy and Bunny. One sunny day, they were playing in the yard when they saw a pan.
Kitty said, "Look, a pan! Let's play with it." Doggy and Bunny agreed, and they took turns kicking the pan. The pan made a loud sound every time they kicked it.
As they played, a bird flew down and asked, "Can I play too?" Kitty, Doggy, and Bunny said, "Yes! Let's all play together." So, they kicked the pan and had fun all day long.

Once upon a time, in a big town, there was a long road. On this road, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very eager to go to the park. He loved to play with his ball and his toy car.
One day, Tim asked his mom, "Mom, can we go to the park?" His mom said, "Yes, Tim. Let's go!" So, Tim and his mom walked on the road to the park. Tim was very happy and excited.
At the park, Tim played with his ball and his toy car. He had so much fun. When it was time to go home, Tim said, "Thank you, Mom, for taking me to the park!" They walked back on the road, and Tim couldn't wait for the next time they could go to the park again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy lived in an ordinary house with her mom, dad, and her dog, Spot. One day, Amy and her family went to the park to have a fun day.
At the park, Amy saw a big tree with lots of red cherries on it. She decided she wanted to pick some cherries to take home. So, Amy asked her dad to help her pick the cherries. Together, they picked the cherries and put them in a basket.
After they picked the cherries, Amy and her family had a picnic in the park. They ate sandwiches, apples, and some of the cherries they picked. Spot played with a ball and everyone had a great day. When it was time to go home, Amy decided she wanted to come back to the park again soon.

Bugsy the Bear was walking through the forest one day when he spotted something unusual. As he got closer, he saw an ancient frame stuck in a tree. He was so curious that he couldn't help but observe it. 
Bugsy noticed that something was inside the frame. He jumped up to see what it was, but the frame was too high for him. He tried to reach for it again, but he couldn't even get his paws on it. 
Bugsy was determined, so he tried one last time. He noticed that the frame was cracked and he thought he could be able to fit his claws in it and pull it off the tree. He carefully stuck his claws through the frame, and he was able to get it off.
When he opened it, he found a magical ruby inside. Bugsy was so excited, but then he noticed something else. There was a note inside the frame that said the magical ruby belonged to someone else. 
Bugsy was disappointed, but he knew he had to give the magical ruby back to the owner. He put it back inside the frame and hung it back up in the tree where he had found it. 
Bugsy felt happy that he had done the right thing and decided to enjoy the rest of his walk through the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a restless boy who liked to run and play all day. One day, while playing outside, Tim found a small magic rock. He picked it up with his hand and took it home.
That night, Tim had a dream. In the dream, the magic rock told Tim that it could make his restless legs run faster. Tim was very happy and excited. He wanted to be the fastest boy in his town.
The next day, Tim held the magic rock in his hand and ran as fast as he could. He was faster than all his friends and even the big kids. Tim was very happy and thanked the magic rock. From that day on, Tim and the magic rock were best friends, and they played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a funny little mouse named Mimi. Mimi lived in a house made of bricks. She loved to play and laugh all day long.
One day, Mimi found a big piece of cheese. She wanted to share it with her friends. So, she took a knife and started to cut the cheese into small pieces. Mimi was very happy because she knew her friends would love the tasty cheese.
Mimi invited her friends over, and they all enjoyed the cheese together. They laughed and played, and had a great time. At the end of the day, Mimi's friends thanked her for sharing her yummy cheese with them. Mimi felt very happy and proud.
The moral of the story is that sharing with others can bring happiness and joy to everyone.

One day, a boy named Tim found a big helmet in his room. It was clear and shiny. He put it on his head and went outside to play.
In the yard, Tim saw his friend, Sam. Sam wanted the helmet, too. They both yelled, "It's mine!" They were not happy and did not want to share.
Tim's mom came outside and saw them fighting. She said, "You both can use the helmet. Take turns, and then you can play together." Tim and Sam listened to her. They took turns wearing the helmet and played all day. They were happy again.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a colorful candle. The candle had many pretty colors, like red, blue, and yellow. It was a very special candle. It could talk and play with the kids in the house.
One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to play with the candle. He said, "Candle, let's play hide and seek!" The candle was happy to play with Tim. They played and had lots of fun.
But then, Tim's sister, Sue, wanted to play too. She said, "Candle, can I play with you and Tim?" The candle did not want to play with Sue. It refused to play with her. Tim was sad that his sister could not play with them. He told the candle, "Please, let Sue play with us. We can all have fun together." The candle thought about it and agreed. They all played together and had a great time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. Sally loved to eat spaghetti. One day, Sally's mom made her a big bowl of spaghetti for lunch.
Sally was very patient. She waited and waited for her mom to say, "Sally, you can eat now!" When her mom said that, Sally was so happy. She sat down at the table and looked at her bowl of spaghetti.
Then, Sally's friend Tommy came over to play. Tommy saw the spaghetti and said, "Yummy! Can I have some too?" Sally's mom smiled and said, "Of course, Tommy! I will make you some spaghetti too."
Sally and Tommy were so excited. They waited patiently for the spaghetti to be ready. When it was time to eat, Sally's mom helped them open their mouths wide to eat the spaghetti. They laughed and had so much fun eating their spaghetti together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very intelligent. He loved to learn and play with his toys. One day, Tim found a bottle of oil in the kitchen. He didn't know what it was for, but he thought it looked interesting.
Tim took the oil to his room and decided to stand his toy car on it. He thought the car would slide down the oil and go very fast. Tim said to his car, "Are you ready to go fast?" The toy car didn't say anything, but Tim knew it was ready.
Tim poured the oil on the floor and put his toy car at the top. The car slid down the oil and went very fast, just like he thought! Tim laughed and clapped his hands. He was so happy that his intelligent idea worked. Tim played with the oil and his toy car all day long.

Once there was a little boy named Tim. He liked to play with his toy rod. One day, he went to the park with his mom. Tim saw a big rock and wanted to lift it. His mom said, "Be careful, Tim."
When Tim tried to lift the rock, he found a small box under it. He opened the box and found a magic rod inside. The magic rod could make things move without touching them. Tim was very happy and started to play with the magic rod.
But then, Tim saw a rude dog that barked at him. He used the magic rod to make the dog stop barking. The dog was not rude anymore. It was friendly and played with Tim. They became best friends and had lots of fun together. Tim learned that sometimes, a little magic can turn something rude into a new friend.

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were knights and dragons. Lily had a stick that she called her sword. Max had a scarf that he tied around his neck like a tail.
"Roar!" Max said, running after Lily. "I am a big dragon and I will catch you!"
"No, you won't!" Lily said, waving her sword. "I am a brave knight and I will stop you!"
They chased each other around the trees and the swings. They had a lot of fun. Sometimes Lily would catch Max and tickle him. Sometimes Max would catch Lily and hug her.
One time, Max saw something shiny on the ground. He stopped and picked it up. It was a metal pin with a star on it. It sparkled in the sun.
"Wow!" Max said. "Look what I found! It is a rare star pin. Maybe it is magic!"
Lily came over and looked at it. She thought it was pretty.
"Can I see it?" she asked.
"OK, but be careful," Max said. He gave her the pin.
Lily held it in her hand. She felt happy. She liked stars.
"Thank you, Max," she said. "You are a nice dragon. Do you want to trade?"
"Trade?" Max asked.
"Yes, trade. You give me the pin and I give you something else. Like my sword. Do you want my sword?"
Max thought about it. He liked the pin, but he also liked the sword. It was a good stick.
"OK, let's trade," he said. He took the sword from Lily and gave her the pin.
They smiled at each other. They were happy with their trade.
"Let's play some more," Lily said.
"OK, but now I am the knight and you are the dragon," Max said.
"OK, but I am a friendly dragon," Lily said.
They ran off, laughing and playing. They had a rare and magic day.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jane and Andrew. Andrew wanted to complete a project, so he asked Jane for help.
"Please Jane, can you help me to complete the project?" said Andrew.
Jane replied, "Of course I can! What do you need?"
"I need some wine," said Andrew.
"I'm afraid I don't have any available," said Jane.
"No problem, I'll go and get some," said Andrew. 
He quickly ran to the store and bought some delicious wine. When he returned, he and Jane were able to complete their project. 
They worked together happily until the project was done. It was a great success! 
At the end of the day, Jane thanked Andrew for his help. She also gave him a gift of a bottle of wine to say thanks. 
"Thank you so much! I really appreciate your help," said Andrew. 
He and Jane shared a hug, and then went their separate ways, feeling proud of what they had accomplished.
The soldiers would be allowed safe passage in any direction carrying any personal and public property besides munitions of war .

One day, a boy named Tim went to the store with his mom. They needed to buy a new glove for Tim to play catch. Tim saw a harmless bug that was green and small. He liked the bug and wanted to take it home. But first, they had to pay for the glove.
After they paid for the glove, Tim looked for the bug. But the bug was gone! Tim was sad, but his mom said they had to go home. When they got home, Tim put on his new glove to play catch with his dad.
As Tim played catch, he felt something in his glove. He took off the glove and saw the harmless bug inside! The bug had come home with him in the glove. Tim was so happy and surprised. He played catch with his dad and the bug stayed on the glove, enjoying the game too.

Once upon a time, there was a green frog named Fred. Fred had a friend, a big green tree. The tree had many green leaves. Fred loved to play with the leaves.
One day, Fred saw a print on the ground. It was a big foot print. Fred did not like the print. He said, "I hate this print. It is not nice." Fred was sad because he did not know who made the print.
Fred asked his friend, the big green tree, "Do you know who made this print?" The tree shook its leaves and said, "I do not know." Fred and the tree looked around. They saw a big green dinosaur. The dinosaur said, "I made the print. I am sorry, Fred. I did not mean to make you sad." Fred, the tree, and the dinosaur became friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little red house. In the house, there was a big red bowl. Inside the bowl, there was a lot of red jelly. The red jelly was very yummy.
One day, a small boy named Tim saw the red jelly. He wanted to eat it. He tried to get the red jelly, but it was too high. Tim shouted, "Help, I want the red jelly!"
A kind cat heard Tim's shout. The cat jumped up and got the red jelly for Tim. Tim was very happy. He said, "Thank you, cat!" Tim and the cat shared the red jelly and had a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a little red car named Speedy. Speedy loved to go fast. He liked to race with his friends. They would all drive very quick.
One day, Speedy saw a perfect hill. He wanted to speed down the hill. His friends watched as he went up the hill. They were excited to see him go fast.
Speedy started to go down the hill. He went faster and faster. His friends cheered as he zoomed by. He felt so happy. Speedy won the race and had a great day with his friends.

Once upon a time, in an ordinary town, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim had a big map that he loved to look at. One day, Tim decided to go on an adventure to find a hidden treasure.
Tim took his map and started to walk. Soon, he met a girl named Sue. Sue wanted to find the treasure too. But Sue had a different map. They both wanted to go their own way. This made Tim and Sue feel sad.
Tim and Sue decided to work together. They looked at both maps and found a new way to the treasure. They walked and walked until they found a big tree. Under the tree, they found the hidden treasure. Tim and Sue were very happy. They learned that working together is the best way to solve a problem.

Once upon a time, there was a giant named Bob. Bob was very fast. He loved to run and play all day. One day, Bob met a little girl named Sally.
Sally said, "Hi, Bob! Do you want to play with me?" Bob was happy and said, "Yes, Sally! Let's play!"
But first, Sally wanted to dress up. She put on a pretty dress and a big hat. Bob wanted to dress up too. He found a big shirt and a funny hat. They both looked very nice.
They played all day long. They ran fast, jumped high, and laughed a lot. Sally and Bob became best friends. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was a curious girl who loved to play and have fun. One day, she went to a big park with her mommy and daddy. In the park, she saw something very exciting. It was a big, colorful bounce castle!
Lily was so happy and excited. She ran to the bounce castle and started to jump and bounce with her new friends. They laughed and had so much fun together. The bounce castle was like a magical place for Lily and her friends.
After a while, it was time for Lily to go home. She said goodbye to her new friends and left the bounce castle with her mommy and daddy. She was tired but very happy. That night, Lily dreamed of the curious bounce castle and all the fun she had. She couldn't wait to go back to the park and play again.

In 1837 , the British Government funded the installation of a magnetic observatory at Greenwich . The Association continued to press for the construction of similar observatories around the world , and in 1838 their suggestions were accepted by the Government and funds were provided . In 1839 the British Government and the Royal Society prepared four expeditions to build magnetic observation stations in Cape Town ; St. Helena ; Hobart , Tasmania and ( eventually ) Toronto . Teams of Royal Artillery officers were sent out to take the measurements . The team assigned to Canada originally planned to build their observatory on Saint Helen 's Island off Montreal , but the local rocks proved to have a high magnetic influence , and the decision was made to move to Toronto instead . The team arrived in 1839 , and set up camp at Fort York in a disused barracks while construction started on new buildings . The observatory was given 10 acres ( 4. 0 ha ) of land to the west of King 's College ; the Ontario Legislature now occupies the area on which the college was located .

Once upon a time, there was a big, ugly frog. The frog lived near a pond. Every day, the frog would hop around and play with his friends. He loved to watch the sunset by the pond.
One day, the frog met a bossy bird. The bird liked to order everyone around. The bird said, "Frog, you must hop over there!" The frog did not want to be told what to do, but he hopped over there anyway.
The frog and the bird watched the sunset together. The bird said, "This is a pretty sunset!" The frog agreed, "Yes, it is!" The bird stopped being bossy, and they became friends. From then on, they watched the sunset together every day.

Tom and Lily were playing by the river. They liked to throw stones and watch the water splash. Sometimes they saw fish or ducks or frogs. They also liked to cross the bridge that went over the river. It was a big bridge made of wood and metal. It had holes and cracks and rust. But Tom and Lily did not care. They thought it was fun and exciting.
One day, as they were crossing the bridge, they heard a loud roar. They stopped and looked around. They saw a big, ugly monster coming out of the water. It had green scales, yellow teeth, and red eyes. It was angry and hungry. It wanted to eat Tom and Lily.
"Run!" Tom shouted to Lily. They turned around and ran back to the other side of the bridge. The monster followed them, roaring and snapping. It was faster than them. It reached the bridge and started to break it with its claws and teeth.
Tom and Lily were scared. They did not know what to do. They saw a hole in the bridge. It was big enough for them to fit in. They decided to hide in the hole and hope the monster would not find them.
They crawled into the hole and stayed very quiet. They peeked out of the hole and saw the monster still breaking the bridge. It was making a lot of noise and dust. It did not see Tom and Lily. They hoped it would go away soon.
"Shh, don't make any sound," Tom whispered to Lily. "Maybe it will get bored and leave."
"I hope so," Lily whispered back. "I don't like the monster. It is very ugly and mean."
They hugged each other and waited for the monster to go away. They wished they had never crossed the bridge. They wished they were safe at home. They wished the monster would never come back.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. He had a friend named Sam. They liked to play and eat snacks together. One day, they found a big bag of celery in the kitchen. They thought it would be fun to eat it all.
Tim and Sam started eating the celery, but they did not share with their friend, Lily. That was rude. Lily was sad because she wanted to play and eat celery too. Tim and Sam saw Lily was sad and wanted to make her happy.
So, Tim and Sam said sorry to Lily and asked her to remain with them. They shared the celery with her. Now, they all ate celery together and played. They were all happy and promised to always share and be nice friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat cereal for breakfast. One day, he wanted to increase the fun, so he asked his mom if he could have more cereal in his bowl. His mom said yes, and Tim was very happy.
However, Tim was sometimes careless. When he poured the cereal into his bowl, it spilled all over the floor. Tim was sad, but his mom helped him clean up the mess. She told him to be more careful next time.
The next day, Tim tried again. He remembered to be careful and poured the cereal slowly. This time, there was no mess! Tim was proud of himself and enjoyed his breakfast. He learned that being careful is important, and he could still have fun with his cereal.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy who loved to bake. One sunny day, she decided to bake a big, yummy cake for her family. Amy felt very useful when she helped in the kitchen.
As Amy was baking, she felt the ground shake. It was an earthquake! Amy was scared, but she knew she had to save her cake. The cake was wobbling on the table, and Amy didn't want it to fall.
Amy quickly grabbed the cake and ran to a safe place. The earthquake stopped, and everyone was okay. Amy's family was so happy that she saved the cake. They all sat down and enjoyed the delicious cake together. In the end, Amy's baking was not only yummy but also very useful during the earthquake.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little girl named Lily. She loved to paint pretty pictures with bright colors. One sunny day, Lily went to the park to paint the flowers and the trees.
In the park, Lily met a small bird who was sad. The bird said, "I want to paint too, but my wings are too small to hold a brush." Lily did not want the bird to complain or be sad, so she had an idea.
Lily dipped her brush in the paint and let the bird pick the colors. Then, she painted a beautiful picture of the bird and the park. The bird was so happy and thanked Lily. They became good friends and painted together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a toy robot. The robot had a broken arm. Tim felt bad for his robot. He wanted to help the poor robot.
Tim went to his dad and said, "Dad, my robot has a broken arm. Can we replace it?" Dad smiled and said, "Yes, Tim. Let's fix your robot."
They went to the store and got a new arm for the robot. They put the new arm on the robot. The robot was happy. Tim was happy too. They played together all day.

One day, a boy named Tim went to play in the park. He saw a big box. The box had the word "equipment" on it. Tim did not know what that word meant. But he was excited to see what was inside the box.
Tim opened the box and found a lot of toys. He thought it was a gift for him. He played with the toys all day. He did not mention the box to anyone. He thought it was his secret. But he did something stupid. He left the box open.
The next day, Tim went back to the park. He saw that the box was empty. All the toys were gone. He was sad. But then he saw his friends playing with the toys. Tim's mom told him that the toys were for everyone in the park. Tim was happy because now he could play with his friends and the toys together. The unexpected thing was that the toys were for everyone, not just for Tim.

Anna liked to play with her toy cars. She had many cars of different colors and sizes. She liked to make them zoom and crash on the floor. Sometimes, she pretended to be a mechanic and fixed the cars with her tools.
One day, she was playing with her toy cars when she noticed something unusual. One of her cars, the red one, was missing. She looked under the sofa, behind the curtains, and in the toy box, but she could not find it. She felt sad and confused. Where did her car disappear?
She asked her mom, who was in the kitchen. "Mom, have you seen my red car? It disappeared!"
Her mom smiled and said, "Maybe it went for a ride. Why don't you look outside?"
Anna ran to the window and looked outside. She saw her dad, who was a real mechanic, working on a big red car in the driveway. He was wearing his blue overalls and his cap. He had a wrench in his hand and a smile on his face.
Anna gasped and shouted, "Dad, you found my car! You made it big and shiny!"
Her dad looked up and saw her. He laughed and said, "No, sweetie, this is not your car. This is a car I'm fixing for a friend. Your car is still in the house. I saw it on the table when I left."
Anna looked at the table and saw her red car. It was not missing after all. It was just hiding. She felt happy and relieved. She ran to the table and grabbed her car. She hugged it and said, "I'm sorry, car. I thought you disappeared. I'm glad you're here. Let's play some more!"
She took her car to the floor and made it zoom and crash with the other cars. She had fun playing with her toy cars. She liked to be a mechanic, just like her dad.

Once upon a time, there was a big red barn on a farm. In the barn, there were many animals. The animals were happy and loved to play together. The barn had cows, pigs, and chickens. The farm also included a big green field for the animals to run and play.
One day, a little boy named Tim came to the farm. Tim wanted to play with the animals in the barn. But every time he tried to play with them, they ran away. Tim felt frustrated because he just wanted to be friends with the animals.
Tim's mom saw that he was frustrated and had an idea. She gave Tim some food to feed the animals. Tim went back to the barn and gave the food to the cows, pigs, and chickens. The animals loved the food and started to play with Tim. Tim was so happy that he could finally play with the animals in the big red barn.

Once upon a time, there was a little peanut. The peanut was very small, but it was also great. It liked to play with its friends, the apple and the banana.
One day, the peanut, the apple, and the banana went to the park. They wanted to play on the swings and slide. They had a lot of fun playing together. The sun was shining and the sky was blue.
After playing, the peanut, the apple, and the banana were very tired. They sat down under a big tree to rest. They talked about their great day and how much fun they had. They all agreed that playing together was the best thing to do.

The soundtrack was nominated for the Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media at the 2013 Grammy Awards , the first video game soundtrack to be nominated for that category , though it did not win . Additionally , the game won the award for best music and was nominated for the best graphics award from IGN , and was selected as the best PlayStation Network game by GameSpot . At the Spike Video Game Awards , Journey won awards as the best PlayStation 3 game , the best indie game , and the game with the best music , and was additionally nominated for game of the year , best downloadable game , best graphics , and best song in a game for " I Was Born For This " . It received the 2013 Annie Award for video game animation . It won five awards at the 2013 British Academy of Film and Television Arts awards : Artistic Achievement , Audio Achievement , Game Design , Online Multiplayer and Original Music , and was nominated for Best Game , Game Innovation and Story . In March 2013 , it won six awards at the annual Game Developers Choice Awards : Best Audio , Best Game Design , Best Visual Arts , Best Downloadable Game , the Innovation Award , and Game of the Year .

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. They have a big calendar on the wall. The calendar has pictures of animals and numbers. Lily and Ben can count the numbers and name the animals.
One day, Lily and Ben have a fight. Lily wants to play with the calendar. She likes to look at the pictures and point at them. Ben wants to play with the calendar too. He likes to tear off the pages and make paper planes. Lily and Ben start to pull the calendar.
"Stop it, Ben!" Lily says. "You are ruining the calendar!"
"No, you stop it, Lily!" Ben says. "You are boring with the calendar!"
Lily and Ben pull harder and harder. The calendar rips in half. Lily and Ben both lose the calendar. They are sad and angry. They start to cry.
Mom hears the noise. She comes to see what is wrong. She sees the torn calendar and the crying twins. She is not happy.
"What happened here?" Mom asks. "Why did you break the calendar?"
Lily and Ben try to explain. They blame each other. Mom shakes her head.
"That was not nice, Lily and Ben," Mom says. "The calendar was a gift from Grandma. She wanted you to learn and have fun. You should not fight over it. You should share it."
Lily and Ben feel sorry. They say sorry to Mom and to each other. Mom hugs them and wipes their tears.
"It's okay, Lily and Ben," Mom says. "I know you love each other. And I love you too. But you have to be careful with your things. And you have to respect each other's choices. Sometimes you can play with the calendar together. And sometimes you can play with other toys. That is normal."
Lily and Ben nod. They understand. They smile and hug Mom. They decide to play with their blocks and dolls. They are happy again. They still miss the calendar. But they know they can make a new one with Mom. They can draw new pictures and write new numbers. They can make it even better. They are excited. They love Mom. And they love each other.

Tom and Lily were twins. They liked to play with their toys and make things. One day, they decided to make a display of their toys for their mom and dad. They used a big box, some paper, and some glue.
They put their toys on the paper and glued them to the box. They had cars, dolls, animals, and blocks. They made a road, a house, a farm, and a tower. They were very proud of their display. They wanted to show it to their mom and dad.
They called their mom and dad to come and see their display. Mom and dad came and looked at the box. They smiled and clapped. They said, "Wow, what a wonderful display! You are very creative and clever, Tom and Lily!"
Tom and Lily were happy. They hugged their mom and dad. They said, "Thank you, mom and dad! We love you!"
Mom and dad said, "We love you too, Tom and Lily! You are our special and unusual youth. You always make us happy!"
