Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to gather rocks in his big red bag. He would look for amazing rocks all day long. Tim's best friend was a fast car named Zoom. Zoom could go very fast and they would play together every day.
One sunny day, Tim and Zoom went to the park to gather more amazing rocks. They found big rocks, small rocks, and shiny rocks. They were having a lot of fun. Suddenly, they saw a big rock that was different from the others. It was very big and very shiny.
Tim and Zoom decided to take the big shiny rock home. But when they touched the rock, something unexpected happened. The rock started to talk! The rock was not a rock, but a magic rock. The magic rock told Tim and Zoom that it could make their wishes come true. Tim and Zoom were very happy and made lots of fun wishes together. And they all lived happily ever after.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a huge red apple on a tree. They wanted to eat it.
"Let's get the apple!" Tom said. "It looks yummy!"
They climbed the tree and reached for the apple. But they were not alone. A big squirrel was also on the tree. It saw the apple too.
"Go away, squirrel!" Lily said. "The apple is ours!"
The squirrel did not listen. It ran to the apple and bit it. It made a loud crunch.
"Hey, that's not fair!" Tom said. "You are mean!"
The squirrel did not care. It bit the apple again and again. It liked the taste. It was sweet and juicy.
Lily and Tom were sad and angry. They wanted to bite the apple too. But the squirrel was too fast and greedy. It ate the whole apple and left nothing for them.
"Bad squirrel!" Lily and Tom said. "You are a thief!"
The squirrel did not say sorry. It jumped to another tree and looked for more apples. It was happy and full.
Lily and Tom climbed down the tree. They felt hungry and disappointed. They looked for another fruit to eat. But they did not find any.
"Maybe we can find a banana or a grape," Tom said.
"Or a cookie or a cake," Lily said.
They walked away from the tree. They hoped to find something tasty and huge. But they did not forget the squirrel and the apple. They learned a lesson. They learned to share.

Sara and Tom are playing in the living room. They have many toys, but they like the rug best. The rug is rare. It has many colors and shapes. Sara and Tom pretend the rug is a map of a faraway land.
"Look, this is a mountain," Sara says, pointing to a red triangle. "And this is a river," she says, tracing a blue line.
"I see a castle," Tom says, finding a yellow square. "And a dragon," he says, spotting a green circle.
They make up stories about the mountain, the river, the castle and the dragon. They have fun.
Then they hear a voice from the kitchen. It is Mom. She calls them.
"Sara, Tom, time for lunch!"
Sara and Tom stop playing. They get up and run to the kitchen. They are hungry.
"Can we play with the rug later?" Sara asks.
"Of course, my loves," Mom says. "The rug is always here for you."
Sara and Tom smile. They love the rug. And they love Mom.

One day, a playful cat named Tom saw a big hole in the ground. He wanted to fill the hole with dirt. So, he started to dig with his paws. As he dug, he found a little toy car. Tom was very happy.
Tom showed the toy car to his friend, Sam the dog. Sam said, "Wow! That's a nice toy car. Let's play with it!" Tom replied, "Yes, let's play, but we should fill the hole first. I think something fun will happen when we do."
Tom and Sam worked together to fill the hole with dirt. They pushed and pushed until the hole was full. Then, they put the toy car on top of the filled hole. Suddenly, the toy car started to grow bigger and bigger! It turned into a real car that they could both ride in.
Tom and Sam were so excited. They jumped into the big car and went for a fun ride. They knew that filling the hole was a good idea. Now, they had a new car to play with and enjoy together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mommy, daddy, and her old cat named Mr. Whiskers. Lily loved to play with her toys and draw pictures with her crayons.
One day, Lily received a big box from her grandma. Inside the box, she found many colorful shapes. There were circles, squares, and triangles. Lily was so happy and excited to play with her new shapes.
Lily and Mr. Whiskers spent all day playing with the shapes. They made a big tower with the squares, a fun train with the circles, and a pretty house with the triangles. When it was time for bed, Lily gave Mr. Whiskers a hug and said, "Thank you, grandma, for the fun shapes!"

Tom is a restless boy. He likes to run and jump and play. He does not like to sit still and listen. One day, he goes to the farm with his mom and dad. He sees many animals there. He sees cows and pigs and chickens and horses.
He runs to the horses and wants to touch them. His mom says, "Be careful, Tom. Horses are big and strong. You have to be gentle and quiet with them." Tom nods, but he does not listen. He tries to pull the horse's tail and mane. The horse does not like that. It neighs and kicks and shakes its head.
Tom gets scared and runs away. He sees a goat with a big horn. He thinks the horn is funny and shiny. He wants to touch it. He runs to the goat and reaches for its horn. The goat does not like that. It bleats and butts and lowers its head.
Tom gets scared and runs away. He sees a duck with a big beak. He thinks the beak is cute and yellow. He wants to touch it. He runs to the duck and grabs its beak. The duck does not like that. It quacks and bites and flaps its wings.
Tom gets scared and runs away. He cries and looks for his mom and dad. He sees them by the fence. They are talking to a farmer. The farmer has a dog with him. The dog is brown and furry. It has a long tongue and a wagging tail. It sees Tom and runs to him. It licks his face and wags its tail. It offers him a ball to play with.
Tom stops crying and smiles. He likes the dog. He takes the ball and throws it. The dog runs after it and brings it back. They play together for a long time. Tom is happy and calm. He forgets about the horses and the goat and the duck. He listens to his mom and dad and the farmer. He learns about the farm and the animals. He says thank you and goodbye to the dog and the farmer. He goes home with his mom and dad. He is tired and sleepy. He has a good nap. He dreams of the dog and the ball.

One day, a little fish named Fin was very hungry. He wanted to find some food to eat. He swam around the big blue sea, looking for something yummy. As he swam, he saw a big building in the water. Fin was curious and decided to swim closer.
As he got near the building, he saw a little crab named Carl. Carl was also hungry. Fin said, "Hi, I'm Fin. I'm looking for food. Are you hungry too?" Carl said, "Yes, I am. Let's look for food together!" So, Fin and Carl swam around the building, searching for something to eat.
As they swam, they found a hidden door in the building. They went inside and saw a big room full of food! They couldn't believe their eyes. Fin and Carl ate and ate until they were not hungry anymore. They were so happy they found the secret food room. From that day on, Fin and Carl were best friends and always swam together in the big blue sea.

One day, a little cat named Mimi saw a long string on the floor. Mimi liked to play with strings, so she stared at it. She wanted to catch the string and have fun.
Mimi jumped on the string and pulled it with her paw. The string moved and Mimi chased it. She heard a voice say, "Hey, that's my string!" It was a small mouse named Timmy.
Mimi said, "I'm sorry, Timmy. I didn't know it was your string. Can we play with it together?" Timmy thought for a moment, then said, "Yes, we can share the string."
They played with the string all day. When they got hungry, they ate some food. Mimi tasted something sour and made a funny face. Timmy laughed and said, "That's a lemon, Mimi!" They both laughed and continued to play with the string, happy to be friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toys and listen to his mom's stories. One day, his mom gave him a lecture about not forgetting to put his toys away.
Later, Tim was playing with his toys when he heard a tiny voice say, "Hello!" He looked around and saw a little toy robot. The robot said, "Hi, I'm Robo! Can I play with you?" Tim was very surprised but happy to have a new friend. They played together all day.
At the end of the day, Tim remembered his mom's lecture and started to put his toys away. But, he forgot to put Robo away. The next morning, Tim found Robo cleaning his room. Robo said, "I didn't want you to forget me, so I helped clean up!" Tim was so happy and never forgot to put his toys away again.

Once upon a time, there was a big jar. The jar was in a store. It was the only jar available. A little boy named Tim saw the jar. He wanted to buy it.
Tim asked his mom, "Can I have this jar, please?" His mom said, "We will come back tomorrow. If it is still here, you can have it." Tim was sad but he knew he had to wait.
The next day, Tim and his mom went back to the store. The jar was still there! Tim was so happy. He bought the jar and took it home. He knew that waiting was worth it.

Once upon a time, there was a cheese. It was normal cheese, like what you might see in the store. The cheese spun around and around and around. It thought it was so much fun! Finally, it stopped and smiled. It loved spinning so much. 
The cheese wanted to share its joy, so it asked its friends to come join him. One by one, they all started spinning. They spun around and around until they were dizzy. Even the little ants that were watching joined in the spinning fun. 
The cheese laughed and clapped his hands. It loved to see everyone having so much fun. After a while, everyone slowed down and stopped spinning. They were all out of breath and worn out, but they had a great time. 
The Cheese knew it would always remember the fun they had spinning together.

Once upon a time, there was a thoughtful little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mom and dad at home. One sunny day, Lily wanted to do something nice for her parents. She thought of a surprise.
Lily decided to wash the dishes. She filled the sink with water and soap. Lily washed the cups, plates, and spoons. She was very careful not to break anything. She was happy to help.
When mom and dad came home, they saw the clean dishes. "Wow, Lily!" said mom. "Did you wash the dishes?" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, I wanted to surprise you!" Mom and dad were very proud of their thoughtful little girl. They all shared a big hug and enjoyed their clean home.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sally. She was walking through a meadow when she saw a hungry bee. The bee had gathered some pollen and wanted a lemon to sweeten it. Sally had a lemon in her pocket, but she felt bad for the bee. She didn't want to give it away.
The bee started to urge her to give it the lemon, but Sally wasn't sure. She wanted the lemon for herself. She was feeling sleepy, so she decided to take a nap and think about what she should do.
While Sally was sleeping, the bee got closer and closer. It kept urging her to give it the lemon. Suddenly, Sally woke up when the bee started to buzz in her ear. She quickly grabbed the lemon and threw it at the bee.
The bee flew away with the lemon, happy that it got what it wanted. Sally was glad that she had been able to help the bee, even though she was a bit sleepy.

Anna loved waffles. She ate them every morning with honey and butter. She liked to make them with her mom in the kitchen. They had a special machine that made the waffles round and crispy.
One day, Anna's mom said they had a new neighbor. His name was Ben and he was three years old, like Anna. He had just moved in with his dad next door. Anna's mom said they should go and say hello and introduce themselves.
Anna was shy. She did not know Ben. She wondered if he liked waffles too. She decided to bring him one of her waffles as a gift. She wrapped it in a napkin and put it in a basket.
She and her mom walked to Ben's house and knocked on the door. Ben's dad opened it and smiled. He said hello and invited them in. He said Ben was in his room, playing with his toys.
Anna followed her mom to Ben's room. She saw a boy with brown hair and blue eyes. He had a lot of cars and trucks on the floor. He looked up and saw Anna. He said, "Who are you?"
Anna felt nervous. She held out her basket and said, "I'm Anna. I live next door. I brought you a waffle. Do you like waffles?"
Ben's eyes lit up. He said, "I love waffles! Thank you, Anna. That's very nice of you. Do you want to play with me?"
Anna smiled. She said, "Yes, I do. Can I see your cars and trucks?"
Ben nodded. He said, "Sure. Come on, I'll show you. They are very cool."
Anna and Ben sat on the floor and played with the cars and trucks. They shared the waffle and talked about their favorite things. They became friends.
Anna's mom and Ben's dad watched them and smiled. They were happy that their children got along so well. They decided to make more waffles and have a picnic in the backyard.
The moral of the story is: Sharing and being kind can help you make new friends.

One day, a boy named Tom went to the park with his mom. They saw a big tent. Tom was very excited. He said, "Mom, look! A tent! Can we go see it?" Mom said, "Yes, but be careful, Tom."
Tom and his mom went to the tent. Inside, they saw a man making funny faces. Tom laughed and clapped his hands. The man said, "Hello, I am a funny man. Do you like my funny faces?" Tom said, "Yes, I like them a lot!"
After they left the tent, Tom and his mom went to play on the swings. Tom was very careful when he played. He had a fun day at the park with his mom and the funny man in the tent. They went home happy and tired.

" ... Thirteen Years Later " is the fifth episode of the third season of the American crime-thriller television series Millennium . It premiered on the Fox network on October 30 , 1998 . The episode was written by Michael R. Perry , and directed by Thomas J. Wright . " ... Thirteen Years Later " featured guest appearances by the members of the band Kiss , performing both as themselves and as minor characters .

One day, Tom and Sue plan to build a big tower with their toy blocks. They are very excited and ready to start. They put one block on top of another, making the tower taller and taller. They are happy to see their tower grow.
But then, something unexpected happens. A little bird flies through the window and lands on their tower. The tower wobbles and shakes. Tom and Sue watch as their tower starts to fall.
Just as the tower is about to fall, the little bird flies away. The tower stops wobbling and stands tall again. Tom and Sue are surprised and happy. They laugh and clap their hands. The little bird helped save their tower, and they keep playing together.

Once there was a big red bus. The bus loved to go fast. One day, a little boy named Tim saw the bus. He wanted to ride it. Tim asked his mom, "Can I ride the bus, please?"
His mom said, "Yes, you can ride the bus. But be careful."
Tim was so happy. He got on the bus and sat down. The bus started to move. Tim saw a ball on the floor. He thought it would be fun to kick it. So, he kicked the ball. The ball flew and hit the bus driver. The driver laughed and said, "That was a successful kick, little one!"
Tim felt proud and smiled. He knew that he had a fun day on the bus.

Rebbie later revealed that there was a lot of discussion at the time of the release of Centipede over whether she should use the Jackson surname professionally or not . To begin with Rebbie did not want to use her pre-marriage surname , but later reasoned that it was silly to deny her heritage . Jackson explained that she did , however , compromise with the use of her family name on the Centipede album cover - " Rebbie is large and Jackson is small " . She further stated that the success of siblings Michael and Janet had not been a hindrance to her , but served as an enhancement to her career . Rebbie added that she did not have to worry about " name recognition " .

One day, a fast car named Speedy went to a big house called a museum. In the museum, there were many things to see. Speedy liked the big animals and the old cars. He went around and saw many new things.
Speedy met a girl named Lily. Lily could not hear, so she was deaf. But she was very good at talking with her hands. Speedy and Lily became friends. They played and looked at the things in the museum together.
After playing, Speedy and Lily went outside. They had a race. Speedy was very fast, but Lily was fast too. They laughed and had fun. At the end of the day, they said goodbye. Speedy and Lily were happy they became friends at the museum.

Once upon a time, there was a woman named Jane. She had an incredible pet cat named Fluffy. They lived in a small house near a big tree.
One day, Jane heard a loud scream from outside. She ran out and saw a little boy named Tim. Tim was scared because a big dog was barking at him. Jane said, "Don't worry, Tim. I will help you."
Jane walked up to the big dog and said, "Shoo, dog! Go away!" The big dog stopped barking and went away. Tim was happy and said, "Thank you, Jane! You are incredible!" Jane and Fluffy smiled, happy to help their new friend.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous snake named Sam. Sam lived in a big sack near a tall tree. Sam was a good snake who liked to play and have fun.
One day, Sam met a little girl named Mia. Mia was not scared of Sam. She said, "Hi, snake! Want to play with me?" Sam was happy and nodded his head. They played together all day long.
At the end of the day, Sam went back to his big sack. Mia said, "Bye, Sam! Let's play again tomorrow!" Sam smiled and waved goodbye. From that day on, Sam and Mia became best friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a huge lion. The lion had a big, loud roar. One day, the lion was walking around when he saw a small, pretty angel.
The angel was lost and scared. The huge lion wanted to help her. So, he roared very loud to call all his friends in the forest. The birds, the rabbits, and the other animals came running.
The animals helped the angel find her way back home. The angel was happy and thanked the huge lion and his friends. From that day, the lion and the angel became best friends, and they played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a small, honest dog named Max. Max loved to play with his favorite toy, a soft triangle. Max would rub the triangle with his paws and carry it around in his mouth.
One sunny day, Max was playing with his triangle in the park. A little girl named Lily saw Max and wanted to play with him. Lily asked Max, "Can I play with your triangle, please?" Max wagged his tail and shared his triangle with Lily.
Together, Max and Lily played with the triangle. They would rub it and toss it in the air. They laughed and had lots of fun. Max and Lily became best friends, and they always played with the triangle in the park. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a big forest. In the forest, there lived an enormous bear. The bear was very friendly and liked to play with the other animals.
One day, the bear saw a little bird staring at him from a tree. The bear wanted to play, so he asked the bird to come down. The bird was scared of the enormous bear, but the bear promised not to hurt it. So, the little bird flew down and they started to play.
As they played, the bear and the bird found a big box in the forest. They opened the box, and out came a tiny mouse. The mouse looked at the enormous bear and the little bird, and started to laugh. The bear and the bird were confused. The mouse said, "I am a magic mouse! I will give you both one wish." The bear wished to be small, and the bird wished to be big. The magic mouse granted their wishes, and they all played happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lucy. She liked to play in the park. One day, she saw a shiny crystal on the ground. Lucy was glad to find it. She picked it up and put it in her pocket.
The next day, Lucy went back to the park. She took out the crystal and showed it to her friend, Tom. They both kneeled to look at it closely. Suddenly, the crystal started to glow. Lucy and Tom were surprised.
Then, a tiny fairy appeared from the glowing crystal. The fairy told Lucy and Tom that she was lost and needed help to find her way home. Lucy and Tom were happy to help the fairy. They followed the fairy's directions and found her home. The fairy was so thankful, and as a reward, she turned the crystal into a magic toy that could change into anything they wanted. Lucy and Tom were very glad and played with the magic toy every day.

One day, a waffle lived in a small house. The waffle was fearful because it did not want to rot. It tried to stay away from wet places and be safe. The waffle had a friend who was a cupcake. They played together every day.
One day, the waffle and cupcake went to the park. They played on the swings and the slide. They were very happy. But then, it started to rain. The waffle was scared because it did not want to get wet and rot.
The waffle and the cupcake tried to run home, but it was raining too much. The waffle got wet and started to feel bad. The cupcake tried to help, but it was too late. The waffle got too wet and began to rot. The waffle was not happy anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a graceful fish named Fin. Fin lived in a big pond with his fish friends. Fin loved to swim and play all day long.
One day, Fin found a shiny scale on the bottom of the pond. He picked it up and showed it to his friend, Guppy. "Look, Guppy! I found a pretty scale!" Fin said. Guppy looked at the scale and smiled. "Wow, Fin! That's really nice!"
Fin wanted to remember where he found the scale, so he made a little mark in the sand. Every day, Fin and Guppy would swim by the mark and remember the day they found the shiny scale. They loved to play with it and show it to all their friends in the pond. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once, in a little town, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a red cap that he loved very much. He wore it every day. One day, Tim went to the park to play with his friends.
At the park, Tim saw a big tree. He heard a voice coming from the tree. It was a bird! The bird said, "Hi, Tim! I like your red cap. It's incredible!" Tim was very surprised. He didn't know that birds could talk.
The bird asked, "Can I try your cap?" Tim said, "Yes, you can." The bird put the cap on its head. Then, something unexpected happened. The bird changed into a big, colorful bird with the cap on! The bird said, "Thank you, Tim! Your cap has magic!" Tim smiled and they played together at the park.

Once there lived two yellow chickens, a shy one and a brave one. The brave one was never scared to move around, jumping here and there. The shy one, on the other hand, stayed in the corner, scared to move.
One day, the brave chicken said to the shy one, "Let's move together to the other side of the yard. Come on. It'll be fun!" The shy chicken was unsure and scared but the brave chicken encouraged it to move. 
The shy chicken slowly moved and eventually, it started jumping and running with the brave chicken. They ran, flew and hopped all around the yard, pecking and playing, until the sun set in the horizon. By the end of the day, the shy chicken was no longer scared to move around.
This story illustrates the importance of facing our fears and not letting them affect us. If the brave chicken didn't encourage the shy one, it would have lived its entire day in the corner of the yard.

Timmy was a good boy who liked to work hard. He helped his mom and dad with chores, like cleaning his room, washing dishes, and feeding the dog. He also liked to work on his puzzles, his drawings, and his books. He was proud of his work and showed it to his mom and dad every day.
But Timmy had a problem. He was afraid of the dark. Every night, when he went to bed, he had bad dreams. He dreamed of scary things, like monsters, ghosts, and spiders. He called them nightmares. He woke up crying and ran to his mom and dad's room. They hugged him and told him it was okay, but he still felt scared.
One night, Timmy had a plan. He decided to work on his nightmares. He took his flashlight, his teddy bear, and his favorite book. He said to himself, "I am brave. I can face my nightmares. I can make them go away." He turned off the light and closed his eyes.
He dreamed of a big, hairy beast that roared and chased him. He was terrified, but he remembered his plan. He turned on his flashlight and shone it at the beast. He saw that it was not a beast, but a giant, fluffy bunny. He said to the bunny, "You are not scary. You are cute. Do you want to be my friend?" The bunny nodded and smiled. He hugged the bunny and felt happy.
He dreamed of a pale, spooky ghost that moaned and floated around him. He was nervous, but he remembered his plan. He held his teddy bear and said to the ghost, "You are not spooky. You are lonely. Do you want to play with me?" The ghost nodded and smiled. He played with the ghost and felt calm.
He dreamed of a huge, hairy spider that crawled and spun webs. He was disgusted, but he remembered his plan. He opened his book and said to the spider, "You are not hairy. You are clever. Do you want to read with me?" The spider nodded and smiled. He read with the spider and felt smart.
Timmy woke up feeling good. He had worked on his nightmares and made them go away. He had made new friends and learned new things. He was proud of his work and showed it to his mom and dad. They hugged him and told him they were proud of him too. He was not afraid of the dark anymore. He was happy.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a new thing in the park. It is a big square. It is red and yellow and blue. It has four sides and four corners.
"What is that?" Lily asks.
"I don't know. Let's go and see," Ben says.
They run to the big square. They touch it. It is hard and smooth. They climb on it. It is fun. They see a hole in the square. They look inside. They see something shiny.
"What is that?" Ben asks.
"I don't know. Let's go and see," Lily says.
They crawl inside the hole. They find a box. It is shiny and has a ribbon. They open the box. They see many small squares. They are brown and have letters on them.
"What are these?" Lily asks.
"I don't know. Let's try them," Ben says.
They take one small square each. They bite them. They are tasty. They are sweet and melt in their mouths.
"Mmm, these are good," Ben says.
"They are chocolate," Lily says. She knows the word from her mom.
They hear a voice from outside the hole.
"Hello, children. Do you like my gift?" the voice says.
They look outside. They see a man. He is smiling. He has a hat and a beard. He is holding a bag.
"Who are you?" Lily asks.
"I am Santa. I came to meet you and give you some chocolate. You have been good children this year," the man says.
"Wow, you are Santa. Thank you for the chocolate. It is very tasty," Ben says.
"You are welcome. Merry Christmas, Lily and Ben. I have to go now. I have more gifts to deliver. Be good and have fun," the man says.
He waves and walks away. Lily and Ben wave back. They are happy. They have met Santa and got some chocolate. They share the chocolate with their friends. They play with the big square. They have a wonderful day.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to school. She had a big bag with her. In the bag, there were many orange crayons. Lucy wanted to draw on the blackboard with her orange crayons. She was very excited.
Lucy went to the blackboard and said, "I want to draw with my orange crayons!" She started to unpack her big bag. But, when she opened the bag, there were no orange crayons! Instead, there were many orange balls. Lucy was surprised.
Her friend Tom saw Lucy and said, "Lucy, let's play with the orange balls!" They played with the orange balls and had a lot of fun. Lucy forgot about the orange crayons and was happy with her new orange balls.

One day, a kind fish named Fin wanted to swim with his friends. He loved to play in the water with them. But Fin had a problem. He needed an operation to fix his fin.
Fin was sad and told his friend, "I can't swim fast. I need help." His friend said, "Don't worry, Fin. We will find help for you."
They went to see a nice doctor fish. The doctor fish said, "I can do an operation to fix your fin, Fin." Fin was happy and said, "Thank you, doctor fish!"
After the operation, Fin could swim fast again. He was so happy to play with his friends in the water. They all had a fun time swimming and playing together.

Tina was feeling very guilty. She had done something wrong and she knew it. She wanted to tell her mom, but she was too scared.
Tina walked into her mom's room, tears streaming down her face. 
"What's wrong?" asked Tina's mom. 
"I did something bad," replied Tina. 
Her mom put her arms around Tina. 
"It's ok, let's talk about it," said her mom.
Tina took a deep breath and told her mom what she had done. Her mom listened carefully and then gave her a big hug. 
"It's alright, everybody makes mistakes," said her mom and gave her a sign. The sign was so special because it meant everything was going to be ok. 
Tina smiled and wiped away her tears. She knew she wasn't guilty anymore.

One day, a little bird named Tim was flying in the sky. Tim was a popular bird because he was very kind and liked to play with everyone. He was looking for a new friend to meet and have fun with.
As Tim was flying, he saw a big tree. In the tree, he saw a little squirrel named Sam. Tim flew down to the tree and said, "Hi, I am Tim. Do you want to be my friend and play with me?"
Sam the squirrel smiled and said, "Yes, I would love to be your friend, Tim!" So, Tim and Sam played together all day. They played hide and seek, and they raced around the tree. They had so much fun together.
At the end of the day, Tim and Sam were very happy. They knew they would be best friends forever. From that day on, they always played together under the big, blue sky.

Antimony was ranked first in a Risk List published by the British Geological Survey in the second half of 2011 . The list provides an indication of the relative risk to the supply of chemical elements or element groups required to maintain the current British economy and lifestyle .

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a friend named Sam. They liked to play and have fun together. One day, they found a dead bug in the park. Tim and Sam felt sad for the bug.
Tim said to Sam, "I hate to see a dead bug." Sam agreed and said, "Me too, Tim. Let's give the bug a nice place to rest." Tim and Sam dug a small hole in the dirt and put the bug inside. They covered the bug with dirt and said goodbye.
After that, Tim and Sam played in the park all day. They were happy to be friends and to help the bug. They knew that even when sad things happen, they could still have fun together.

One day, a little lion named Leo was playing in the big universe. He loved to roar very loud. He was a careless lion and did not know that his roars were too loud for his friends.
"Please don't roar so loud, Leo!" said his friend, the small bird. "It hurts our ears." But Leo did not listen. He just wanted to roar and have fun.
One day, something unexpected happened. When Leo roared, a big star in the sky heard him. The star came down to talk to Leo. "Your roars are so strong, they shake the whole universe!" said the star. Leo felt bad and promised to be more careful. From that day on, he roared softly and all his friends were happy.

One day, Tom and Sue went for a walk. They saw a shelter with many dogs. They wanted to choose a dog to take home.
"Look at that normal dog!" said Tom. "He is so cute!"
But Sue saw a big dog with three legs. "I want that one," said Sue.
Tom and Sue did not agree. They went home without a dog. They were sad.

Lily and Ben like to play with water. They have a big tub in the yard. They fill it with the hose. They splash and laugh. They have fun.
But one day, they play too much. They leave the hose on. The water runs and runs. The tub overflows. The water goes everywhere. It makes a flood.
The flood goes to the house. It goes to the flowers. It goes to the toys. It makes a mess. Lily and Ben are upset. They did not want to make a flood.
Mom and Dad see the flood. They are upset too. They turn off the hose. They tell Lily and Ben to stop playing. They tell them to help clean up. They are not happy.
Lily and Ben are sorry. They say sorry to Mom and Dad. They say sorry to the flowers and the toys. They help to dry and tidy. They learn to be careful with water. They do not want to make a flood again.

Once upon a time, in a quiet little house, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to imagine fun things. He liked to play with his toys and pretend they could talk. One day, he was playing with his toy cow. He said, "Hello, cow! What do you like to eat?"
The cow said, "I like to eat grass and make cream for you, Tim." Tim was so happy to hear the cow talk. He played with the cow all day long.
The next day, Tim went outside to play. He looked for his toy cow, but it was gone. He was sad. Then, something unexpected happened. A real cow was in his yard! The cow said, "Hello, Tim! I am your toy cow. I turned into a real cow because you used your imagination. Now, I can give you real cream!"
Tim was so excited to have a real cow. They became the best of friends and played together every day. And, of course, Tim always had cream for his snacks.

Once, in a small town, there was a church. It was a big church. People went there to pray. The church had a bell that rang loud. But, there was a deaf boy named Tom who could not hear the bell.
One day, Tom saw some kids playing. They were adding rocks to a pile. Tom wanted to play too. He went to add a rock. But the kids said, "No, you can't play. You can't hear the bell."
Tom was sad. He wanted to play with the kids. He wanted to hear the bell. He went to the church and prayed. He asked, "Please help me hear the bell."
The next day, Tom went to the church. He put his hand on the wall. He could feel the bell ring. He was happy. He went to the kids and said, "I can feel the bell. Can I play now?"
The kids said, "Yes, you can play." They all played together, adding rocks to the pile. Tom was happy. He could not hear the bell, but he could feel it.

Once upon a time, there was an adventurous little bug. He loved to play and explore. One day, the little bug found a plant. The plant was big and green. The little bug wanted to climb the plant and see what was on top.
As the little bug climbed the plant, he saw many things. He saw birds and butterflies. He saw the sky and clouds. The little bug was so happy. But then, something unexpected happened. The plant started to rot. The plant became brown and soft.
The little bug was scared. He did not want to fall. But the plant kept rotting. The little bug fell to the ground. He was hurt and sad. The little bug learned that he should not climb plants that are not strong and healthy.
Stela 43 is paired with Altar 35 . It is a plain monument at the base of the stairway of Temple IV .

Once there was a lovely little girl. She was only three years old, but already so smart. 
One day, she was walking in the park with her mom. They were admiring the trees and the flowers when suddenly, the little girl saw a bright sparkly sign. She asked her mom what it said, and her mom explained that it was a special sign that meant "no running". 
The little girl nodded and was so excited when she realized that she knew how to read the sign! She pointed and proudly said, "It says 'no running'!". 
A few days later, the little girl was at her ballet class. She learned to move her body in time to the music, and to make the most beautiful shapes with her arms and legs. After practicing for a while, the teacher taught her to sign with her hands.
The little girl never forgot the lovely movements of the sign language. She loved showing off to her friends, and soon, her mom noticed that she was becoming quite a pro at signing.
The little girl was so proud of herself. With her mom's help and love, she had already learned so much in such a short time.

A young boy named Mike and his dad were walking in the park one day. As they were walking, Mike noticed something in the grass. He asked his dad what it was and his dad said it was a game! 
Mike was very excited and asked to play. His dad agreed and told him he had to pull the hairy rope that was attached to the game. So Mike bent down, grabbed the rope, and pulled as hard as he could.
Suddenly, a loud noise filled the park. Mike and his dad looked around and saw a bunch of colorful balloons floating in the sky! Mike clapped and cheered, happy to have made them fly. His dad smiled and said it was a surprise and that the game was full of fun surprises.
Mike was so excited to experience all the fun surprises, and he couldn't wait to find out what else was in the game. He was sure he was in for an exciting adventure!

Stefan Matthew Wever ( born 22 April 1958 ) is a former professional baseball pitcher . He made his Major League Baseball debut , incidentally his only game , with the New York Yankees in 1982 , and had a 0 – 1 record a 27. 00 earned run average ( ERA ) , and two strikeouts in that game .

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She was playing in the park with her belt when suddenly a gust of wind came and covered it with leaves. The girl felt scared and started and started to cry. Just then, an old man calmly walked up to her. 
The man said, "Don't worry, child. Let me help you find it. We'll cover all the leaves and maybe we'll find your belt." 
The girl smiled and felt calm. Together they brushed away the leaves until they found the belt! The girl thanked the man, put on her belt and ran off to play.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy cat named Kitty. Kitty liked to play with a tie. One day, Kitty saw a dog named Spot. Spot had a dirty face.
Kitty said, "Spot, let me help you. I can wipe your face." Spot said, "No, I can do it myself." But Kitty wanted to help. She took the tie and tried to wipe Spot's face.
Spot got mad and said, "Stop, Kitty! I don't need your help." Kitty felt sad, but she listened to Spot. They learned that it is important to ask before helping others. From that day on, Kitty and Spot became good friends.

Once upon a time, in a big red truck, a nice man named Tom went to deliver a box. The box was for a little girl named Lily. Lily was very happy because inside the box was a toy for her to play with. Tom liked to see Lily happy, so he drove the big red truck very fast to her house.
One day, Tom had a big surprise for Lily. He told her that they were going on a fun trip called a safari. Lily was so excited to see all the animals. They got in the big red truck and drove far away to the safari. Lily saw big animals like elephants and small animals like monkeys. She was very happy.
On the safari, Tom and Lily saw a big red box. It looked just like the box Tom delivered to Lily before. They were very curious, so they opened the box. Inside the box was a big red balloon. The balloon started to grow and grow until it lifted the big red truck into the sky! Tom and Lily were scared at first, but then they saw all the animals from high up in the sky. They laughed and had a great time on their unexpected adventure.

Sara and Ben like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make roads and bridges with blocks and books. They have fun and share their cars.
One day, a new boy comes to play with them. His name is Max. He has a big red car that makes loud noises. He says it is the best car ever. He does not want to share his car with Sara and Ben. He says they can only watch him play.
Sara and Ben are sad and angry. They ask Max to share his car. They say they have many cars they can share with him. But Max says no. He says his car is too good for them. He is selfish.
Max drives his car fast and hard. He does not care about Sara and Ben's roads and bridges. He crashes into them and breaks them. He makes a big wreck. He laughs and says his car is the strongest.
Sara and Ben are very sad and angry. They do not want to play with Max anymore. They say he is mean and rude. They say he does not know how to play nice. They take their cars and go to another room. They leave Max alone with his big red car and his big wreck. He is not happy. He is lonely.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to be creative and make things with her hands. One day, she found a big box of colorful wraps. She was very happy and started to play with them.
Lily made a pretty dress for her doll. Her mom saw it and said, "Wow, you are so creative! Can you show me how to make a dress too?" Lily said, "Yes, I can!" and they made another dress together. They had lots of fun.
One day, Lily's little brother, Tom, took her wraps and started to make a mess. Lily said, "Stop, Tom! Those are my wraps!" Tom didn't listen and kept making a mess. Lily's mom heard them and came to help. She said, "Lily, you need to share your wraps with Tom. It's good to share with others." Lily thought about it and agreed to share with her brother. They both played with the wraps and made many fun things together. Lily learned that sharing can make playtime more fun for everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful, smelly crown. It sat in a castle owned by King Henry. He loved it immensely, and it was sure to bring him luck.
One sunny afternoon, the King noticed that his crown was missing! He was very confused and called out to all the castle staff.
Finally, he found one of his brave knights, Sir Owen, and asked him what had happened to the crown.
"Well," Sir Owen said, "it looks like a mouse snuck into the castle and stole the crown. He wanted a special hat for himself."
King Henry was very sad, and so he decided to replace his crown with a new one. He searched high and low throughout the kingdom, until he finally found a special crown for himself. It shone brightly and was full of sparkles.
When King Henry returned to the castle wearing his new crown, all his subjects cheered for him. He smiled, for he knew his crown would bring him luck once again.

Once upon a time, there was a nice elephant named Elly. Elly had a big trumpet on her face. She used it to make loud sounds. One day, Elly met a small mouse named Max.
Elly said to Max, "Hello, Max! Do you want to play with me?" Max was scared of Elly's big trumpet. He started to tremble. But Elly was very nice and did not want Max to be scared.
Elly said, "Don't be scared, Max. I will not make loud sounds with my trumpet." Max stopped trembling and smiled. He said, "Thank you, Elly. I want to play with you."
So, Elly and Max played together all day. They had lots of fun. Elly did not use her trumpet to make loud sounds, and Max did not tremble anymore. They became very good friends.

Once upon a time, in a dark forest, there lived a big bear. The bear had a lot of lumber. He liked to weigh the lumber every day. One day, while the bear was weighing his lumber, a little rabbit came to him.
"Hello, Mr. Bear!" said the rabbit. "Why do you weigh your lumber?"
The bear smiled and said, "I like to know how much lumber I have. It makes me happy."
The rabbit thought for a moment and then said, "I have an idea! Let's build a house with your lumber. It will be fun, and you will still know how much lumber you have."
The bear agreed, and they both built a beautiful house in the dark forest. They were very happy and became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a smart dog named Max. Max had a rubber ball that he loved to play with. He would run and jump to catch the ball. Max was very happy because he could own the best toy in the world.
One day, Max lost his rubber ball. He looked under the bed, behind the door, and in the yard. Max was very sad because he could not find his ball. He wanted to play with his ball again.
Max's friend, a little girl named Lily, saw that Max was sad. She wanted to help Max find his ball. They looked everywhere together. Finally, they found the ball under a big tree. Max was so happy to have his rubber ball back. He knew that he and Lily were smart and could find anything they lost. They played together all day, and Max knew he had the best friend in the world.

On September 6 , a tropical depression formed over the northwestern Caribbean Sea within a trough of low pressure extended southeastward from Delia , which was situated over southeast Texas at the time . The depression remained weak until it reached the Texas coastline on September 10 . Once onshore , it produced significant rainfall , causing significant damage that was attributed to Tropical Storm Delia . After turning northeast and tracking inland , the depression quickly increased in forward speed before dissipating over North Carolina on September 14 .

The ship was loaned to the Royal Hellenic Navy on 10 February and recommissioned by them on 25 March as Salamis . She was damaged while working up at Scapa Flow and was under repair at Hull from 28 April to 13 June . Salamis was assigned to escort duty at Gibraltar until October when she was transferred to the Aegean where she served with the 12th ( Greek ) Destroyer Flotilla for the rest of the war . The ship was used as a training ship after the war until she was returned to the Royal Navy at Malta on 9 October 1951 . Salamis arrived at Rosyth under tow on 15 April 1952 to be broken up by Metal Industries , Limited .

Lily and Ben were going to the zoo with their mom. They were very excited to see the animals. They got in the car and put on their seat belts. Mom said, "Always buckle up, it is safe and smart."
On the way, they saw a big sign that said "Zoo". It had pictures of a lion, a monkey, a giraffe and a penguin. Lily said, "I want to see the lion, he is the king of the jungle." Ben said, "I want to see the monkey, he is funny and can swing on the trees."
Mom said, "We can see both, and many more. But I recommend we start with the penguin, he is my favorite. He is very intelligent and can swim fast and slide on the ice."
They parked the car and walked to the entrance. They bought their tickets and got a map. Mom said, "Let's follow the map, it will show us where the animals are." They followed the map and found the penguin exhibit. They saw many penguins in a big pool. Some were swimming, some were diving, some were standing on the rocks. One penguin came close to the glass and looked at them. He tilted his head and blinked his eyes.
Lily and Ben smiled and waved at the penguin. They said, "Hello, penguin, you are so cute and smart." The penguin nodded and made a sound. He seemed to say hello back. Mom said, "He likes you, he is very friendly. Do you want to feed him some fish?" Lily and Ben said, "Yes, please!" They got some fish from a bucket and threw them into the pool. The penguin caught them and ate them. He thanked them with another sound.
Lily and Ben were very happy. They said, "We love the penguin, he is the best. Thank you, mom, for recommending him." Mom said, "You're welcome, my loves. I'm glad you enjoyed it. Now, let's go and see the other animals." They left the penguin exhibit and continued their adventure at the zoo.

The title of King of Ireland was re-created in 1542 by Henry VIII , then King of England , of the Tudor dynasty . English rule of law was reinforced and expanded in Ireland during the latter part of the 16th century , leading to the Tudor conquest of Ireland . A near complete conquest was achieved by the turn of the 17th century , following the Nine Years ' War and the Flight of the Earls .

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a big flame. The flame was very hot and bright. It was always burning and never stopped. The people in the village were sad because the flame made their houses very hot.
One day, a little girl named Lily decided to try to stop the flame. She thought the flame was selfish because it did not care about the people in the village. Lily went to the flame and asked, "Please stop, flame. You are making our houses too hot."
The flame did not want to stop. It said, "I like being big and bright. I don't want to stop." Lily was sad, but she did not give up. She went to the river and filled a bucket with water. She threw the water on the flame. The flame got smaller and smaller until it stopped.
The people in the village were very happy. Their houses were not hot anymore. They thanked Lily for being brave and helping them. The flame learned that it was not good to be selfish. From that day on, the flame only burned when the people needed it to keep warm.

Once upon a time, a little mouse named Mimi lived in a tiny house. Mimi loved cheese more than anything else. One day, she found out that there was a big, delicate cheese in the kitchen. Mimi was very happy and wanted to find it.
Mimi started to search for the cheese. She looked under the table, behind the door, and inside the cupboards. Mimi was very careful not to make any noise because she was scared of the big cat that lived in the house too.
Finally, Mimi found the delicate cheese on the table. She was so happy and wanted to take it back to her tiny house. But suddenly, the big cat jumped on the table and took the cheese away. Mimi was very sad and went back to her tiny house without any cheese. The big cat ate the delicate cheese and Mimi learned to be more careful next time.

Baker 's work received mixed reviews . His only two books not specifically gay themed ( though containing gay characters and a somewhat gay sensibility ) , Boy Wonder and Fuel-Injected Dreams , were better received by critics , and more popular with readers , though he was never a bestselling novelist . Baker himself estimated that his books sold approximately 25, 000 copies each . His following book , however , Tim and Pete , met with hostile reviews , primarily for its advocacy of political assassination and terror tactics in combating AIDS discrimination . Baker himself was ambivalent on the subject . " I think assassination does change things ... But I 'm not really calling for violence , " he said . " It 's a novel , not a position paper . "

Once upon a time, in a mild and warm place, there was a big red heart. The heart was very nice and loved to help others. Many people came to admire the heart because it was so kind.
One day, a mean and angry bird saw the heart. The bird did not like that everyone admired the heart. The bird wanted to be the one that everyone admired. So, the bird made a plan to take the heart away from the people.
The bird went to the heart and said, "I will take you away, and no one will admire you anymore!" The heart was sad, but it did not want to fight the bird. The bird took the heart away, and the people were very sad. They missed the heart and wished it would come back. But the heart was gone, and the people had to learn to live without it. The end.

A year after the freeway opened , traffic volumes along parallel roads like 44th , 56th and 68th streets dropped 40 – 50 % . At the same time , roads with interchanges along the freeway saw increased traffic . Wilson Avenue experienced a 120 % increase and sections of Byron Center Avenue jumped 100 % in traffic levels a month after M-6 opened . Property values in the townships surrounding the freeway increased 11. 3 – 12. 4 % by 2006 as a result of development attached to the freeway . Local officials credited the freeway for increased access to the area , driving housing starts as residents flocked to the communities for their schools and quality of life . In 2007 , the Metro Health Village , a commercial development centered around the Byron Center Avenue exit and the hospital opened . Described as being similar to a mall with the hospital as a tenant , the village features restaurants , shops , offices and a hotel . Metro Health relocated from Grand Rapids to the location in Wyoming in the face of opposition to planned expansions of their previous location . Since opening , even though the freeway was officially named for Paul Henry , the original South Beltline name is still in use .

Once upon a time, in an ordinary little town, there was a big red barn. Inside the barn, there lived a happy horse named Harry.
One day, Harry decided to go outside and play. Before he left the barn, he needed to tie his shoes. Harry tried very hard to tie them, but he just couldn't do it. He felt sad and didn't know what to do.
Just then, a friendly mouse named Molly saw Harry's problem. She came over and helped him tie his shoes. Harry was so happy and thanked Molly. Together, they went outside and played all day long. And from that day on, Harry and Molly became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, in a wild land far away, there lived a kangaroo. This kangaroo liked to jump and play all day. He had many friends who liked to play with him too.
One day, the kangaroo had to choose a game to play. He could pick the safe game or the fun, wild game. The safe game was easy, but the wild game was more fun. The kangaroo wanted to have fun, so he picked the wild game.
The kangaroo and his friends started to play the wild game. They jumped very high and very fast. But, they did not see the big hole in the ground. The kangaroo and his friends fell into the hole. They could not get out. The kangaroo was sad because he chose the wild game.

Lily liked to read books. She had many books in her room. She read about animals, cars, princesses and pirates. She learned new words from her books.
One day, Lily found a new book in her room. It was a big book with a shiny cover. It had a picture of a car on it. Lily opened the book and saw many words and numbers. She did not know what they meant. She saw a word that said "license". She remembered that her dad had a license. He showed it to her when he drove the car.
Lily wanted to have a license too. She thought it would be fun to drive a car. She took the book and ran to her dad. She said, "Dad, dad, look at this book! It has a license in it! Can I have a license too?"
Her dad looked at the book and smiled. He said, "Lily, this is not a book. This is a manual. It tells you how to fix a car. And you cannot have a license yet. You are too little to drive a car. You have to wait until you are older and learn how to drive safely."
Lily felt sad. She wanted to drive a car like her dad. She said, "But dad, the car on the cover is so attractive! It is red and shiny and fast! I want to drive it!"
Her dad hugged her and said, "I know, Lily, the car is attractive. But it is not mine. It is a picture of a car. And even if it was mine, you could not drive it. You have to read more books and learn more things before you can drive a car. Maybe when you are older, I will teach you how to drive. But for now, you can read your books and pretend to drive a car."
Lily nodded. She understood that she had to wait. She said, "Okay, dad, I will read more books and learn more things. And then you will teach me how to drive. Thank you, dad."
Her dad kissed her and said, "You are welcome, Lily. I love you. You are my smart and beautiful girl."
Lily smiled and said, "I love you too, dad. You are my strong and kind dad."
They went back to her room and read some books together. Lily still liked the car book, but she liked her dad more.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Tom. Tom was troubled because he had no friends to play with. He felt sad and alone.
One day, Tom went to the park. He saw a big sandbox. Tom decided to fill his bucket with sand and make a tall sand castle. He worked hard and was happy with his castle.
Soon, other kids came to see Tom's castle. They thought it was great! They asked Tom if they could help him build more castles. Tom said yes, and they all played together. Tom's troubled heart was filled with joy, and he made many new friends that day.

Once upon a time, there was a smelly dog named Spot. Spot liked to play outside and get dirty. One day, Spot saw a big ball in the yard.
Spot wanted to get the ball, so he ran very fast. But, oh no! Spot bumped into a tall man. The man had a big shoulder. Spot was not hurt, but he felt sad.
The tall man saw Spot was sad. He picked up the ball and threw it for Spot. Spot was happy again! They played together all day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was playing outside with his favorite toy, a red ball. He loved to throw it up in the air and catch it. One day, while playing, Tim saw a filthy puddle of mud. He thought it would be fun to drop his ball in the mud.
"Should I drop my ball in the puddle?" Tim asked his friend, Sue. Sue thought about the question and said, "I don't know, it might get dirty." But Tim didn't listen and dropped his ball in the puddle anyway. The ball became very filthy and dirty.
Tim tried to clean the ball, but it was too dirty. His mom saw the filthy ball and was upset. She told Tim that he couldn't play with the ball anymore because it was too dirty. Tim was sad and wished he had listened to Sue. Now, he couldn't play with his favorite toy anymore, and it was all because he dropped it in the filthy puddle.

Once upon a time, there was a group of friends. They wanted to go on an adventure and decided to visit the lake. It was a beautiful lake and they were so excited to explore.
When they got there, they were surprised to find that the lake was not beautiful at all. It was terrible! The water was murky and the shore was full of garbage.
One of the friends, Mira, looked around and said, "What a terrible place! How could anyone stand to stay here?"
Another friend, Josh, replied, "I think we should keep exploring - maybe we will find something better."
So the group kept exploring. Eventually, they stumbled upon a beautiful patch of beach. The water was crystal-clear and the sand was soft and white.
It was the most wonderful place they had ever seen. Everyone was so happy they had decided to visit. They knew they would always remember their adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a famous cat named Tom. He loved to play with a copper ball. One day, Tom met a dog named Max. Max said, "Hi Tom, can I play with your copper ball too?"
Tom said, "Yes, Max, let's split the time and play together!" They played and played all day long. They were very happy.
But then, something unexpected happened. The copper ball fell into a big hole! Tom and Max were sad. They tried to get the ball out of the hole, but it was too deep.
A little bird saw them and said, "Don't worry, I can help you!" The bird flew into the hole and brought the ball back to them. Tom and Max were so happy and thanked the bird.
From that day on, Tom, Max, and the little bird became best friends. They played together every day and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a big, round ball. The ball loved to play with his friend, a little girl named Sue. Sue was always careful when she played with the round ball. She did not want the ball to get hurt.
One sunny day, Sue and the round ball went to the park. They played and laughed all day. The round ball liked to roll around in the grass. Sue would insist that the ball be careful near the road. She did not want the ball to roll too far away.
As the sun went down, it was time for Sue and the round ball to go home. They said goodbye to the park and walked back home. Sue held the round ball tight in her arms, being careful not to drop it. They were both happy and tired after a fun day of play.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his marbles. He had big ones, small ones, and some that were very pretty. He played with them all day long.
One day, Tim found a yummy candy. He was very happy and wanted to eat it. But, he was also playing with his marbles at the same time. By mistake, he put a marble in his mouth instead of the candy. He started to chew the marble. It was very hard and not yummy at all. Tim was scared and did not know what to do.
His mom heard him cry and came running. She saw the marble and quickly took it out of his mouth. Tim was safe now, and he learned a big lesson. From that day on, Tim never played with his marbles while eating. He knew it was not safe to do both at the same time. And the yummy candy? His mom let him eat it after all, but only when he put his marbles away.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a wish. He wanted to ride his bike all by himself. But every time he tried, he would fall. Tim was sad.
One day, his friend Amy came over. "Why are you sad, Tim?" she asked. "I can't ride my bike," he said. "I always fall." Amy had an idea. "Let's try together!" she said.
Tim and Amy tried many times, but Tim still couldn't manage to ride his bike. Then, they saw a big hill. "Let's try going down the hill!" said Amy. Tim was scared, but he said, "Okay."
They went down the hill very fast. Tim was scared, but he didn't fall. At the bottom of the hill, Tim was happy. "I did it!" he said. "I rode my bike!" Tim's wish came true, and he and Amy rode their bikes together all day.

Once there was a policeman. He needed a pistol to protect the people in his village. He went to the market to buy one. He chose the most fragile one there was.
The policeman was very careful. He held the pistol gently so it wouldn't break. He brought it home and put it in his pocket. 
Happy that he now had a pistol to protect the people, he went out on his patrol. Suddenly, he heard a scream. He quickly pulled out his pistol and ran to help the screamer.
The policeman was able to help the person in need. He was glad he had the pistol to help. He knew it was fragile, but he knew it was necessary to save the day.

One day, a little girl named Sue was very excited. She wanted to write a poem. She thought about what to write. She thought about the sun, the moon, and the stars. She thought about the trees, the flowers, and the bees. She thought about her family and her friends.
Sue sat down and started to write her poem. She wrote about the sun shining bright. She wrote about the moon and stars at night. She wrote about the trees that yield fruit. She wrote about the flowers that make her smile. She wrote about her family and friends who love her.
When Sue finished her poem, she was very happy. She read it to her mom and dad. They loved it too. They were so proud of Sue. Sue felt good because she made her family happy with her poem. She knew that her poem was special and she wanted to write more.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Joe who loved to go fishing. One day he decided to take his boat out and he happily loaded it with all his fishing gear. Joe's boat had a little cabin and Joe went inside the cabin to get ready.
Suddenly, he heard a voice. 
"Hi Joe, what are you doing?"
Joe looked up and he was embarrassed to see his friend, Sally, standing there. Sally had decided to come with Joe without him knowing.
Joe smiled and said, "Hi Sally. I'm loading up my boat to go fishing. Would you like to come with me?"
Sally smiled and replied, "Sure, I'd love to!"
So Joe and Sally loaded the boat with their fishing gear, and off they went. They had a great day out on the lake and caught lots of fish. Joe and Sally were happy to be back in the cabin, tired from all their fishing.

Following the album 's release in Japan , it debuted at number nine on the Oricon Albums Chart . On the issue dated May 17 , 2010 , the album moved to a new peak of number seven and has since been certified platinum by the Recording Industry Association of Japan ( RIAJ ) for shipments of 250, 000 copies . In Australia , The Remix entered the ARIA Albums Chart at its peak position of number 12 on May 16 , 2010 , remaining on the chart for a total of five weeks . In the United Kingdom , the album debuted at number three on the official UK Albums Chart dated May 22 , 2010 , and has sold 166, 440 copies according to the Official Charts Company , being certified gold by the British Phonographic Industry ( BPI ) . Across Europe , the album debuted at seven on the European Top 100 Albums chart of Billboard . The Remix also reached the top of the charts in Greece , while attaining top-ten positions in Belgium ( Flanders and Wallonia ) , Czech Republic , Ireland , the Netherlands and New Zealand .

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a gentle cat. The cat liked to play with the kids and make them happy. Every day, the cat would run around the village, chasing butterflies and birds.
One day, the cat felt very tired. It let out a big yawn and decided to take a nap under a tree. As the cat slept, the kids in the village missed their friend and started looking for the cat.
Soon, they found the gentle cat sleeping under the tree. They all sat down quietly and waited for the cat to wake up. When the cat opened its eyes, it saw all the kids smiling at it. The cat let out another yawn and got up to play with its friends again. They all had a fun day together in the village.

Once upon a time, there was a shy alligator called Alex. He was very quiet and liked to stay away from other alligators. One day, Alex decided to pretend to be a different alligator. He changed the way he walked and made funny noises.
Suddenly, Alex heard a voice. It was Jill, a friendly alligator from his neighbourhood. She shouted: "Hi, Alex! What are you doing?" Alex was embarrassed and blushed. He told Jill that he was pretending to be another alligator.
Jill laughed and said: "Why don't we pretend together? We can both become different alligators, then explore the forest and have fun!". Alex was still a bit shy, so he thought about it for a few minutes. Eventually, he smiled and agreed.
Alex and Jill had a wonderful time pretending to be different alligators. They explored the forest and made funny noises with their friends. Alex was so happy that he was no longer shy around Jill. From that day on, they became the best of friends. The end.

Ben and Lily were playing outside with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and catch it. Sometimes they missed the ball and it rolled away. Then they had to run after it and bring it back.
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise in the sky. It was like a big drum. They looked up and saw dark clouds. They felt some drops of water on their faces. It was raining.
"Let's go inside!" Lily said. "It's going to storm!"
They picked up their ball and ran to the house. But Ben slipped on the wet grass and fell down. He hurt his knee and started to cry.
Lily stopped and ran back to him. She helped him get up and hugged him.
"It's okay, Ben. Don't cry. I'll get you a band-aid."
She pointed to the door. "Look, Mommy is coming. She'll make you feel better."
Mommy came out with an umbrella. She saw Ben's knee and said, "Oh, poor Ben. What happened?"
"He fell down," Lily said. "The grass was slippery. And there was thunder."
Mommy nodded. "Yes, there was thunder. It's very loud, isn't it? But it's not scary. It's just the sound of the clouds bumping into each other."
She took Ben and Lily inside. She cleaned Ben's knee and put a band-aid on it. She gave them both a glass of milk and a cookie.
"Thank you, Mommy," Ben said. "You're the best."
Lily smiled. She was glad Ben was okay. She was also a little embarrassed. She had been afraid of the thunder, too. But she didn't want to tell Mommy. She wanted to be brave like Ben.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a little bird named Billy. Billy loved to sing. Every day, he sang happy songs. All the animals in the village liked to hear Billy sing.
One day, a big, fearful cat named Tom came to the village. Tom liked to fight. He saw Billy singing and said, "Stop singing or I will fight you!" Billy was scared but he did not want to stop singing.
A wise old owl saw the problem and said to Tom, "Why do you want to fight? Let him sing. His songs make everyone happy." Tom thought about it and decided to listen to the owl. From that day on, Tom and Billy became friends. Billy kept singing and Tom never fought again.
The moral of the story is that we should not let our fears stop us from doing what we love, and that kindness can change someone's heart.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park with their toys. They liked to make sand castles and dig holes. They had a bucket, a shovel, and some cars.
"Look, Lily, I made a big castle!" Tom said, showing his sand creation.
"It's very nice, Tom. But I think you need a moat to protect it from enemies," Lily said, recommending a way to improve his castle.
"A moat? What's that?" Tom asked.
"It's a water ring around the castle. Like this," Lily said, digging a ditch around her own castle and filling it with water from the bucket.
"Oh, I see. That's cool. Can you help me make one?" Tom said.
"Sure, Tom. Here, take the shovel and dig here," Lily said, pointing to a spot near his castle.
They worked together to make a moat for Tom's castle. They were having fun and did not notice the dark clouds in the sky. Soon, it started to rain. The rain was fierce and heavy. It made the sand wet and sticky. It also made the water in the moats rise and overflow.
"Uh-oh, Lily, look! The water is coming out of the moats. It's a flood!" Tom said, worried.
"Oh no, Tom, you're right. The flood is ruining our castles. We have to save our toys!" Lily said, grabbing her cars and putting them in the bucket.
"Quick, Lily, let's go to the slide. It's high and dry there. We can wait for the rain to stop," Tom said, following her with his bucket.
They ran to the slide and climbed up. They put their buckets on the platform and looked at the park. The park was full of water and mud. Their castles were gone. They felt sad.
"I'm sorry, Tom. I didn't mean to make a flood," Lily said.
"It's okay, Lily. It's not your fault. The rain did it. Maybe we can make new castles when the sun comes out," Tom said.
"I hope so, Tom. I like playing with you. You're a good friend," Lily said.
"Me too, Lily. You're a good friend too. And you have good ideas. I like your moat recommendation," Tom said.
They smiled and hugged. They waited for the rain to stop and the flood to go away. They hoped to play in the park again soon.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Tom and Lucy. Tom and Lucy did lots of fun things together, like playing games and talking. But one day, they wanted to try something different.
"Let's do something new," said Tom.
"Like what?" asked Lucy.
"Let's make a plan," Tom said.
So Tom and Lucy began to discuss. They thought of lots of ideas but nothing felt right. Suddenly, Tom had an idea.
"Let's make a pen," he said.
"But how?" asked Lucy.
Tom grinned. He had a plan.
He searched the room and found some hard rocks, some string and some bits of wood. They worked together to shape the rocks and wood into a pen.
When the pen was complete, Tom and Lucy were so proud. They had done it! It had been hard, but together they had done it.
The next day, Tom and Lucy were back to playing games and talking. But now, when they wanted to plan something together, they knew they could do it, even if it was hard. They knew they could make anything they wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was very sad because she hurt her knee while playing. She wanted to feel better, but she didn't know how. Lucy's mom tried to help her by putting a bandage on her knee, but Lucy was still sad.
One day, a big, friendly dog named Max came to Lucy's house. Max was a very good dog who loved to play. Lucy's mom said, "Welcome, Max!" Lucy was scared at first, but Max wagged his tail and licked her hand. Lucy started to smile and feel a little better.
Max and Lucy played together every day. Max would bring Lucy a ball, and Lucy would throw it for him. One day, Lucy forgot about her hurt knee and started to run with Max. She was so happy that she didn't feel the pain anymore. Lucy's mom was surprised to see her running and smiling. The unexpected twist was that Max helped Lucy feel better, and she wasn't sad anymore. They became best friends and played together all the time.

One day, a little girl named Mia was in her room. She wanted to change her bed sheet. She thought it would be easy.
Mia asked her mom, "Can you help me change my sheet?" Her mom said, "Sure, let's do it together." They took off the old sheet and put on a new one. It was a pretty sheet with many colors.
Just as they finished, something unexpected happened. A little bird flew in through the window and landed on the bed. The bird said, "Thank you for my new home!" Mia and her mom were surprised but happy to have a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who loved to imagine. He would think about big cars, fast planes, and rich houses. He liked to play with his toy gear all day long.
One sunny day, he took his toy gear outside to play. While he was playing, he saw a big, rich house. He thought, "I want to see that house!" So he walked closer to the house, still playing with his gear.
As he got closer, he saw a big, mean dog. The dog saw the boy and his toy gear. The dog wanted the gear, so it ran fast to the boy. The boy was scared and tried to run away. But the dog was too fast and took the boy's toy gear. The boy was very sad and went home without his favorite toy.
