Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He lived in an old house with his mom and dad. In front of the house, there was a porch where Tim liked to play.
One sunny day, Tim wanted to make his toy car go faster. He asked his dad, "How can I increase the speed of my toy car?" His dad said, "Push it harder, Tim!" So, Tim pushed his toy car harder and it went faster on the porch.
Tim was very happy to see his toy car go fast. He played with it all day on the old porch. When the sun went down, Tim went inside the house with his toy car. He couldn't wait to play again tomorrow.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Milly. Milly loved to relax. Every night when it was dark, she would lie in her modern bed and close her eyes. The night would be quiet and she would have time to relax. When she relaxed, she would drift away to amazing places.
In these places she would have wonderful adventures! She would laugh, dance and play. She would explore the beautiful world around her. She would get up high to look down at the clouds and sometimes even visit the stars. It was always so much fun. 
When the sun would come up, Milly would feel very happy. She would jump out of bed and be ready for a new day. It was never boring with Milly around!

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big slide. It looks fun and attractive. They want to go on the slide.
"Can we go on the slide, please?" Lily asks her mom.
"Sure, but you need to wear the equipment first," her mom says. She gives them helmets and pads. They are for safety.
"Thank you, mom," Lily says. She puts on the equipment. Ben does the same.
They run to the slide. They take turns to slide down. They laugh and shout. They have a lot of fun.
"Can we go again, please?" Ben asks his dad.
"Okay, but only one more time," his dad says. He smiles and watches them.
Lily and Ben go on the slide again. They are happy. They love the slide and the equipment. They are good friends.

Once upon a time, in a regular house, lived a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toys and look for treasure. One day, while he was playing, he found a treasure map under his bed.
The map showed a big X in the backyard. Tim ran outside with his dog, Bob, to find the treasure. They dug and dug in the dirt where the X was. Finally, they found a big box. Tim said, "Wow, Bob! We found the treasure!"
Tim opened the box and found a big, red ball inside. He was so happy! He picked up the ball and threw it for Bob to catch. Bob ran after the ball, but when he tried to catch it, the ball slipped and slapped him on the face. Bob didn't mind. He picked up the ball and brought it back to Tim.
Tim and Bob played with the treasure ball all day long. They had so much fun together. In the end, they were both tired but happy. They went back inside the regular house and took a nap, dreaming of more adventures to come.

Once upon a time, there was a big stand with many toys. The toys were always together and happy. But one day, a mean girl came to the stand. She wanted to separate the toys and make them miserable.
The toys started to talk. A small doll said, "Please, don't let her separate us. We want to stay together." The other toys agreed, but they were scared. They did not know how to stop the mean girl.
The mean girl took the toys and put them in different rooms. The toys were very sad and miserable. They missed their friends from the stand. The mean girl did not care. She left the toys all alone, and they never saw each other again.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little dog named Max. Max loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Max found a big, red ball in his yard.
Max ran up to the ball and gave it a big kick. The ball went flying through the air and made a loop in the sky. Max was so happy and excited to see the ball make a loop.
Max kicked the ball again and again. Each time, the ball made a loop in the sky. Max played with the ball all day long. He was very tired, but he had so much fun.

Molly was a young girl who loved to help her mom. One morning, Molly and her mom were in the kitchen. Molly picked up the big pot and tried to place it on the stove.
"Be careful, Molly," said her mom.
But, Molly did not listen. Suddenly, the pot dropped to the floor and made a loud noise.
"Oh no!" Molly's mom cried. "Now we have a big mess on the floor."
Molly was scared but she knew she must help. They worked together to clean up the mess. In the end, they fixed the kitchen.
Molly was so glad they were okay. She learned a lesson that morning - to be more careful.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jenny. She had a blue towel. One day, Jenny went to the park with her towel. She found a muddy puddle and wanted to play in it. She put her towel in the puddle, and it got very dirty. She felt sad.
Suddenly, a fairy appeared and said, "Don't worry Jenny. I will give you a new towel and make your old towel clean again." Jenny smiled. The fairy gave Jenny a new, pink towel. Jenny said thank you and hugged the fairy. The fairy waved goodbye.
Jenny put her old towel in the sun and it became clean and fluffy again. Jenny smiled. She had a new pink towel and her old blue towel was clean. She was so happy!

Once upon a time, there was a playful dog named Buddy. Buddy loved to march around the yard and bark at the birds. One sunny day, Buddy found a big, shiny box under a tree. He thought it was a treasure!
Buddy ran to his friend, the cat named Whiskers. "Whiskers, I found a treasure!" Buddy said. Whiskers came to see the treasure. They both looked at the box and wondered what was inside.
Together, Buddy and Whiskers opened the box. Inside, they found fun toys and treats! They played with the toys and shared the treats. They were so happy they found the treasure. From that day on, Buddy and Whiskers loved to march around the yard, looking for more treasures to share.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim did not like to eat potatoes. He would say "I hate potatoes!" every time his mom tried to give him some. His mom was sad because potatoes are good for you.
One day, Tim was playing in the yard. He found a dirty potato in the ground. It was brown and covered in dirt. Tim thought it was a funny-looking potato. He decided to take it home and show his mom.
Tim showed the dirty potato to his mom and said, "Look what I found, Mom!" His mom smiled and said, "That's a potato from our garden!" Tim was surprised. He asked his mom if they could clean the potato and eat it for dinner. That night, Tim tried the potato and he liked it. He didn't hate potatoes anymore.

Once upon a time there was a little puppy who didn't have an owner. She was alone and very sad. Every day she would sit in the park and cry. 
One day, a boy came to visit the park. He noticed the puppy crying, so he stopped to pet her. The little puppy stopped crying and a big smile spread across her face.
"Do you want to be my puppy?" asks the boy. 
The puppy looked up, her tail wagging with excitement.
"Of course!" she said.
The boy and the puppy had lots of fun together. He taught her important things like how to sit, stay and fetch. They were the best of friends. 
The boy was very happy that he had found the perfect puppy and the puppy was extremely happy to have an owner who cared for her. They both realized how important it was to have someone who loves and cares for you.

Once upon a time, there was a big rhinoceros. He lived in a deep forest. He had many friends, like the birds, the monkeys, and the rabbits. They all played together and had fun.
One day, a mean man came to the deep forest. He wanted to take the rhinoceros away from his home. The rhinoceros did not want to go. He was very sad and scared. His friends saw this and wanted to help him.
The birds, monkeys, and rabbits made a plan to prevent the mean man from taking the rhinoceros. The birds flew in the sky and made loud noises. The monkeys threw nuts at the mean man. The rabbits dug holes in the ground to slow him down. The mean man was very scared and ran away.
The rhinoceros and his friends were very happy. They had stopped the mean man from taking the rhinoceros away. They all played together and had fun in the deep forest, safe and sound. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to the mall with her mom. Lily was so happy to see many things at the mall.
At the mall, Lily saw a big, upset dog. The dog looked very sad. Lily asked her mom, "Can I hug the dog, please?" Her mom said, "Yes, you can."
Lily went to the dog and gave it a big hug. The dog felt better and was not upset anymore. The dog wagged its tail and licked Lily's face. They became good friends and played together at the mall.

Once upon a time, there was a wealthy man named Tom. Tom had a big house and many toys. He also had a guitar that he loved to play every day.
One day, Tom made a plan. He wanted to share his guitar music with others. So, he went to the park where kids and their moms and dads were playing. Tom sat on a bench and started to play his guitar.
The kids and their moms and dads heard Tom's guitar music. They came to listen and dance. Everyone was happy and had fun. Tom was glad that his plan worked. From that day on, Tom played his guitar in the park for everyone to enjoy.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a tiny fairy. The fairy had impressive wings that sparkled in the sun. She loved to fly and play with her friends, the birds and the butterflies.
One day, the fairy was playing hide and seek with her friends. She hid behind a big tree and waited for her friends to find her. While she was hiding, she heard a voice. "Hello," said the voice. The fairy peeked out and saw a little girl. "Hi," said the fairy.
The little girl was very happy to meet the fairy. They played together all day. But then, the fairy did something silly. She flew too close to a flower and got her wings stuck. She felt embarrass. The little girl helped her get free. The fairy thanked the girl and they both laughed.
After that day, the fairy and the little girl became best friends. They played together every day and had lots of fun. And the fairy learned to be more careful with her impressive wings.

Ben and Sam are playing with toy guns in the park. They like to pretend they are cowboys and robbers. Ben has a red gun and Sam has a blue gun. They run and hide behind trees and rocks.
"Bang, bang, bang!" Ben shouts, pointing his gun at Sam. "I got you, robber! You are in big trouble!"
"No, you didn't!" Sam says, dodging behind a rock. "You missed me, cowboy! You are a bad shot!"
Sam pops out from the rock and shoots back at Ben. "Bang, bang, bang!" Sam yells, aiming his gun at Ben. "I got you, cowboy! You are in big pain!"
"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cries, holding his stomach. "You hit me, robber! You hit me in my stomach! It hurts a lot!"
Sam runs over to Ben and sees him lying on the ground. He feels sorry for him. He drops his gun and hugs him. "I'm sorry, Ben. I didn't mean to hurt you. It's just a game. Are you okay?"
Ben stops crying and hugs Sam back. He feels better. He smiles and says, "I'm okay, Sam. It's just a game. You are a good friend."
They get up and pick up their guns. They decide to play something else. They see a slide and a swing. They run to them and have fun. They forget about their rough game. They are happy.

One day, a peaceful cat named Tim and a dog named Sam were playing a game. They wanted to see who could jump the highest. "I will win!" said Sam. "No, I will win!" said Tim. They took turns jumping, but they could not tell who jumped higher.
Then, a big bird flew by and saw them playing. The bird said, "I can help you see who will win. I will watch from the sky." Tim and Sam liked this idea. They jumped again, and the bird watched from above. "Tim wins!" said the bird. Sam was sad but said, "Good job, Tim."
As they were talking, a bottle of shampoo fell from the sky. It hit the ground and made bubbles everywhere. Tim, Sam, and the bird started to play with the bubbles. They forgot about the jumping game and had lots of fun together. The bird said, "We all win when we play together and have fun."

Lily liked to read books. She had many books with pictures and words. She liked books about animals, and books about cars, and books about stars. But her favorite book was about an engine. The engine was red and shiny, and it could go very fast. The book showed how the engine worked, and what it did on the tracks.
One day, Lily saw a real engine at the station. It looked like the one in her book. She wanted to see it closer. She ran to the engine, but her mom said, "No, Lily, you can't go there. It's dangerous. The engine might start and go away. You have to stay with me." Lily was sad. She wanted to touch the engine, and hear it, and smell it. She thought her mom was mean.
Lily waited until her mom was busy. She saw a man with a hat and a whistle. He was the driver of the engine. He was talking to another man. Lily saw her chance. She sneaked to the engine, and climbed inside. She saw many buttons and levers. She remembered some of them from her book. She wanted to try them. She was very naughty.
She pushed a button, and the engine made a loud noise. She pulled a lever, and the engine moved. She was scared, but also excited. She felt like she was in her book. She didn't see the driver running to the engine, or the people shouting, or the other trains on the tracks. She only saw the engine going faster and faster.
The driver managed to get inside the engine. He saw Lily in the seat. He was angry, but also worried. He grabbed Lily, and put her on his lap. He tried to stop the engine, but it was too late. The engine crashed into another train. There was a big bang, and a lot of smoke. Lily and the driver were hurt. They had to go to the hospital. Lily was very sorry. She learned a hard lesson. She never played with engines again. She only read about them in her books.

Once upon a time, there was a brown bird who lived in a birdcage. The birdcage was in a big tree. The bird liked to sing and play all day.
One day, a little boy was walking by the tree. He heard the bird singing. The boy said, "Hello, bird! I like your song. Can I be your friend?" The bird said, "Yes, I want a friend too!"
Every day, the boy would pass by the tree and talk to the bird. They became very good friends. The bird was happy to have a friend, and the boy loved listening to the bird sing. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a reliable otter named Ollie. He lived in a river with his family. They all loved to play and swim together.
One day, Ollie's mom said, "Ollie, hurry and get some fish for dinner!" Ollie swam fast to catch fish. He saw his friend, the duck. "Hi, Ollie!" said the duck. "Hi, duck!" said Ollie. "I need to hurry and catch fish for my family."
While Ollie was catching fish, he found a big shiny stone. He thought, "This is not a fish, but it is so pretty!" Ollie took the shiny stone home to show his family. They all looked at the shiny stone and smiled. The shiny stone made everyone happy, and they forgot about the fish for dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a busy bird named Bob. Bob loved to fly high in the sky and sing songs. One sunny day, Bob saw a big tree with lots of branches. He decided to build his nest there.
Bob started to gather sticks, leaves, and grass. He was very busy. While he was working, he saw another bird named Bella. Bella was also building her nest on the same tree. They said "hello" to each other.
Bob said, "Bella, let's separate our nests a little. Then, we can both have space to live and play." Bella agreed and they both continued to build their nests. They became good friends and lived happily in their tree. They sang songs together and played in the sky all day long.

The first glowing reports of country rich with thousands of game animals came in 1806 when Meriwether Lewis and William Clark returned from their two-year expedition . Their journals described lands rich with thousands of buffalo , beaver , and river otter ; and also an abundant population of sea otters on the Pacific Northwest coast . In 1807 , explorer Manuel Lisa organized an expedition which would lead to the explosive growth of the fur trade in the upper Missouri River country . Lisa and his crew traveled up the Missouri and Yellowstone Rivers , trading manufactured items in return for furs from local Native American tribes , and established a fort at the confluence of the Yellowstone and a tributary , the Bighorn , in southern Montana . Although the business started small , it quickly grew into a thriving trade .

One day, a boy named Tom found a big, expensive helmet in his yard. He did not know where it came from. Tom thought it was very cool and wanted to play with it. He called his friend, Sue, to come over and see the helmet.
"Look, Sue! I found this big helmet!" Tom said. "Let's play hide and seek with it!" Sue agreed and they started to play. Tom put on the helmet and began to hide. Sue closed her eyes and counted to ten.
When Sue opened her eyes, she saw the helmet moving all by itself! She was very surprised. "Tom, is that you?" she asked. The helmet stopped moving and Tom came out from behind it. "Yes, it's me!" he said, laughing. "I was just hiding behind the helmet!"
Just then, a big wind came and blew the helmet away. Tom and Sue were sad to see it go, but they had fun playing together. They knew they would always remember the day they found the big, expensive helmet.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a big red ribbon. He wanted to tie it on his pet cat, Sam. Sam was a fast cat who liked to run and play. Tim thought the ribbon would make Sam look pretty.
As Tim tried to tie the ribbon on Sam, he saw a small flame in the kitchen. The flame was on the stove. Tim was scared, but he knew he had to help. He ran to the sink and filled a cup with water.
Tim threw the water on the flame, and it went away. He was happy that he saved the day. But then, Sam jumped up and the ribbon got caught on the stove. The ribbon was the flame all along! Tim learned that he should be more careful and not play with things he shouldn't.

Lily was a nosy girl. She liked to look at everything and ask many questions. One day, she saw her mom make juice in the kitchen. She wanted to try it too.
She waited until her mom went to the living room. Then she climbed on a chair and reached for the juice maker. She put some fruits inside and pushed the button. The juice maker made a loud noise and juice came out. Lily was happy.
But she did not see the juice spill on the floor. She tried to grab a cup and pour some juice. She slipped on the wet floor and fell down. The cup and the juice maker crashed on the floor too. Lily was sad and hurt.
Her mom heard the noise and ran to the kitchen. She saw the mess and Lily crying. She hugged Lily and said, "Are you okay, my sweetie? What were you doing?"
Lily said, "I wanted to make juice like you, mom. But I did not succeed. I made a big mess. I'm sorry, mom."
Her mom said, "It's okay, Lily. I know you were curious and wanted to try something new. But you should always ask me first before you use the kitchen things. They can be dangerous and you can get hurt. Next time, I will show you how to make juice safely, okay?"
Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I love you, mom."
Her mom said, "I love you too, Lily. Now let's clean up this mess and get you some juice."

Once upon a time, in a friendly town, there was a big rainbow. The rainbow had many colors. People in the town loved to see the rainbow.
One day, a little girl named Lucy went outside to play. She saw the rainbow and was very happy. Lucy wanted the rainbow to stay in the sky forever. She said, "Please, rainbow, don't go away."
Lucy had an idea. She went to her mom and dad. She said, "I want the rainbow to stay. What can we do?" Her mom and dad thought about it. They said, "We can ask the rainbow to stay."
So, Lucy and her parents went outside. They looked at the rainbow and said, "Rainbow, please stay with us. We love you." The rainbow heard them and was happy. It decided to stay in the friendly town. Everyone was happy and they played under the rainbow every day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a lot of mist. In this town, there was a girl named Lily. Lily was sad because her town was always misty and boring. She wanted to find a way to make her town fun and bright.
One day, Lily heard a story about a magic man who could make the mist go away. The magic man lived far away, but Lily knew she had to find him. She asked her mom and dad if she could go, and they said she could if she saved her money to pay for the trip.
Lily did many jobs to save money. She helped her mom and dad, and her neighbors too. After some time, she had enough money to pay for the trip. Lily was excited and went to find the magic man.
When she found the magic man, he was happy to help her. He gave Lily a magic stone and told her to take it back to her town. The magic stone would make the mist go away and make her town fun and bright.
Lily went back to her town and used the magic stone. The mist went away and her town became fun and bright, just like she wanted. Everyone was happy, and they all thanked Lily for her hard work. From that day on, the town was never boring again.

One day, a girl named Lily wanted to go on a trip. She wanted to see a big volcano. Lily was excited and she started to pack her bag. She put in her toys, clothes, and a big hat.
Lily's mom saw her packing and said, "Where are you going, Lily?" Lily said, "I want to see the volcano, Mom!" Her mom smiled and said, "That's a great idea, but we can't go today. We will go another day."
Lily was frustrated. She wanted to see the volcano now. She took her bag and went to her room. She sat on her bed and thought about the big volcano. Lily knew she had to wait, but she was still excited.
That night, Lily's mom read her a story about a volcano. Lily listened and imagined that she was there. She knew that one day, she would see the volcano for real.
When the day came to visit the volcano, Lily was so happy. She and her mom packed their bags and went on their trip. They saw the big volcano and had a great time. Lily was not frustrated anymore, and she knew that waiting was worth it.

One day, there was a modest painter who was doing some work in the house. He had all his tools out and was ready to start. Suddenly, he heard a loud sound and looked up to see that the wall had split! It was a big crack and he knew he had to fix it quickly.
The painter got to work, carefully smoothing the wall and covering the split. He worked hard until the wall was fixed just right. The painter was very proud of his hard work.
When the job was finished, the painter couldn't help but feel a little bit of pain in his heart. He wasn't sure why, but he slowly understood that the split in the wall reminded him of his own problems.
The painter was happy that he could help the house and make it look beautiful again. He packed up his tools and went on his way - feeling a bit more modest than before.

Once there was a youth who loved to sleep. Every night he would close his eyes, and drift away peacefully. But then one day, something terrible happened. His bedroom became incredibly boring! Nothing exciting ever happened.
The youth talked to his parents about it.
"It's so dull in here," he said. "I'm so bored!"
His parents thought for a moment. Then his father had an idea.
"Let's make it fun!" he suggested. So, they worked together to decorate the room. They painted the walls bright colors and hung fun decorations from the ceiling.
The youth was amazed! The room was now fun and exciting, and the youth loved it. He said goodnight to his parents and drifted off to sleep. He had the most wonderful dreams and was so happy he'd made his room more exciting.

Once upon a time, there was a mama and a daddy. They had a boy who was three years old. The little boy did something bad, so his parents decided to punish him. 
Mama said "No more TV. That's your punishment." The little boy was sad. He started to cry. 
But then Mama had another idea. She said "We're going to do something fun instead. We can go to the amazing billboard up the road." 
The little boy was so excited! He put on his shoes and ran to the car. 
Mama and Daddy drove to the amazing billboard. It was so big and beautiful and colorful. The little boy was amazed. 
They had a picnic beneath the billboard and laughed together. The little boy was happy again. 
Mama and Daddy knew that punishment was important, but spending time together was even more important.

The transitive reduction of a DAG G is the graph with the fewest edges that represents the same reachability relation as G. It is a subgraph of G , formed by discarding the edges u → v for which G also contains a longer path connecting the same two vertices . Like the transitive closure , the transitive reduction is uniquely defined for DAGs . In contrast , for a directed graph that is not acyclic , there can be more than one minimal subgraph with the same reachability relation .

The sun was shining brightly and it was a wild morning. Sally was in her backyard and wanted to see the animals in the wild. She was patient and waited for a long time. Suddenly, she saw a squirrel! She was so excited and ran to get a better look. But, the squirrel ran away and got too far for Sally to see.
Sally was sad, but she was patient and kept watching for animals. Soon, a rabbit hopped by. She slowly tiptoed closer and tried to get the rabbit's attention. But the rabbit didn't see her and hopped away.
Sally tried her best to be patient, but she was very sad. She decided to go back inside, but before she did, she looked up at the sky. She saw a beautiful rainbow shining in the sky. She smiled and said to herself "I don't need to see animals in the wild, this rainbow is enough!"

Once upon a time, there was a popular forest. Every day, lots of people served in the forest. They picked fruit, hunted for animals, and did many other things.
One day, some people decided that they wanted to serve in the forest a different way. They started cutting down all of the trees in the forest. Soon, the whole forest was nothing but barren land.
This made everyone very sad. It also caused a lot of damage to the animals who lived there. Without any trees, they didnât have any places to hide or get food.
This taught us an important lesson - we should always take good care of our forests! Serving in the forest should mean preserving it, not destroying it.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in their room. They had a big mattress that they put on the floor. They liked to jump on it and pretend it was a trampoline. Sometimes they made a fort with pillows and blankets and hid inside.
One day, their mom told them to be obedient and not make too much noise. She had to work on her laptop in the living room. She said she would come and check on them later. Ben and Lily said okay and gave her a hug.
But after a while, they got bored of being quiet. They wanted to have more fun. They decided to run around the room and chase each other. They ran faster and faster, laughing and shouting. They ran over the mattress and bumped into the dresser. They ran under the bed and knocked over the lamp. They ran into the closet and threw the clothes on the floor.
They did not hear their mom coming up the stairs. She opened the door and saw the mess. She was very angry. She said, "Ben and Lily, what are you doing? I told you to be obedient and not make too much noise. Look at this room. It is a disaster. You have to clean it up right now."
Ben and Lily felt sorry. They knew they had been naughty. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We were just playing. We did not mean to make a mess. We will clean it up. We love you, mom."
Their mom sighed. She said, "I love you too, Ben and Lily. But you have to listen to me when I tell you something. Playing is good, but you have to be careful and respectful. Now, help me pick up the things and put them back where they belong. Then you can play on the mattress again, but quietly."
Ben and Lily nodded. They helped their mom clean the room. They learned their lesson. They played on the mattress again, but quietly. They were obedient and happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Emily who was three years old. One day, Emily was playing in the garden when she found a dusty old box. She blew on the box to try and clean it up and when she opened it, she found an old counting frame inside.
âLook what I've found!â she said to her mom.

But there were some places that were too dirty to count. Emily's mom had to help her get rid of the dirt so she could count again. Emily was so excited to count more of the universe that she couldn't stop. And they both kept counting until the whole universe was counted.

One day, a jolly boy named Tim found a little boat. He wanted to sail it in the pond. Tim asked his mom if he could go to the pond. His mom said, "Yes, but promise to be back before dark."
Tim went to the pond with his boat. He put the boat in the water and watched it sail. A girl named Sue saw Tim and his boat. She said, "Wow, your boat is so nice! Can I sail it too?" Tim said, "Yes, you can!"
Tim and Sue had fun sailing the boat. They laughed and played all day. They kept their promise and went home before dark. Tim's mom was happy to see them. They all had a jolly time.

One day, a creative little girl named Lily went to the park. She saw a big leopard statue. She loved the statue so much, she wanted to play with it.
Lily said to the statue, "Leopard, let's play freeze!" The leopard didn't move because it was just a statue. But Lily pretended it was her friend.
Lily ran around the statue, laughing and having fun. She would shout, "Freeze, leopard!" and then stop moving. She played this game all day long until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, in a hidden place, there was a big tree. On the tree, there were many avocados. The tree was in a very quiet place, so no one could disturb it.
One day, a little boy named Tom was playing near the tree. He saw the avocados and wanted to eat them. But the avocados were too high for him to reach. Tom tried to climb the tree, but he couldn't. He felt sad.
Tom went to his friend, a tall giraffe named Gina. He asked her for help. Gina came and ate the avocados from the tree. She gave them to Tom. Now, Tom was happy. They both ate the avocados and played together. The quiet place was not disturbed anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a charming cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to stretch and play all day. One day, Kitty met a big dog named Max. Max liked to be the judge of all the games in the park.
One day, Max and Kitty had a race. Max ran fast, but Kitty stretched her legs and ran faster. Max was not happy. He wanted to be the winner. Max said, "Kitty, you can't win. I am the judge and I say I win!"
Kitty was sad, but she knew she was the real winner. She went to her friends and told them what happened. All her friends said, "Kitty, you are the best at stretching and running. We know you won!" Kitty felt better and knew that Max could not always be the judge.

One day, a girl named Lucy wanted to mail a letter to her friend, Tom. She put the letter in a big box and went to the mail place. On her way, she saw a radio on the ground. It was dirty and looked disgusting. She picked it up and tried to clean it.
Lucy turned the radio on and heard a voice. The voice said, "I am a magic radio. If you help me, I will give you a gift." Lucy was excited and asked, "What do you want me to do?" The radio said, "I need a new home. Can you find one for me?"
Lucy thought about where she could find a new home for the radio. She walked around and saw a boy named Jack. Jack was sad because he lost his radio. Lucy asked, "Is this your radio?" Jack said, "Yes, it is! Thank you for finding it!" Lucy was happy to help Jack and the radio.
In the end, the magic radio gave Lucy a gift for being so kind. Lucy and Jack became good friends and played together every day. And they never forgot the day they met because of the disgusting radio.

Once upon a time, there was a big, shiny diamond. It was incredible! The diamond lived in a cave with a little girl named Sue and her dog, Max. They loved to play with the diamond and watch it shine.
One day, a friendly monster came to the cave. He saw the shiny diamond and said, "Wow, that diamond is incredible! Can I play with it too?" Sue and Max were happy to share, so they all played together.
As they played, something unexpected happened. The diamond started to shine even more! It was so bright that it lit up the whole cave. The monster, Sue, and Max were amazed. They had so much fun playing with their new friend and the incredible, shiny diamond.

Sara and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to gather flowers and leaves and make pretend spells. They had a big pot and a wooden spoon. They put the flowers and leaves in the pot and stirred them with the spoon. They said funny words like "abracadabra" and "hocus pocus".
But Tom, the boy next door, did not like their game. He thought it was dull and silly. He wanted to play with his ball and his bike. He came over to the fence and shouted at Sara and Ben.
"Stop playing with that rubbish! You are not real witches or wizards. You are just babies. Come and play with me. I have a cool ball and a fast bike. They are much more fun than your stupid pot and spoon."
Sara and Ben felt sad and angry. They liked their game. They did not want to play with Tom's ball and bike. They thought they were boring and loud. They told Tom to go away and leave them alone.
But Tom did not listen. He climbed over the fence and ran to their pot. He kicked it over and spilled their flowers and leaves. He laughed and said, "There, I broke your spell. Now you have to play with me."
Sara and Ben cried. They were very upset. They had worked hard to gather their flowers and leaves. They had made a beautiful spell. They did not like Tom. He was mean and rude. They wished he would disappear.
Then, something strange happened. A cloud of smoke came out of the pot. It covered Tom and made him cough. He tried to run away, but he tripped and fell. He looked at himself and saw that he had turned into a frog. He croaked and hopped, but he could not change back.
Sara and Ben stopped crying. They looked at each other and smiled. They realized that their spell had worked after all. They had turned Tom into a frog. They felt happy and proud. They picked up their pot and spoon and went to find more flowers and leaves. They decided to make more spells and have more fun. They did not care about Tom's ball and bike. They left him in the garden, hopping and croaking. They hoped he would learn his lesson.

One day, a little girl named Amy went to the store with her mom. Amy saw lots of candy on the shelf. She asked her mom, "Can I have some candy, please?" Her mom said, "No, not today."
Amy was sad but she had an idea. She went to the candy shelf and took a candy when her mom was not looking. She felt a little embarrassed but she wanted the candy so much. 
When they got home, Amy's mom found the candy in her pocket. She was not happy. "Did you take this candy?" she asked. Amy nodded and said, "I'm sorry, Mom." Her mom said, "It's important to not take things without asking. Let's go back to the store and pay for the candy." Amy learned her lesson and promised to never repeat it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to climb. He climbed trees, rocks, and even his bed. One day, he saw a big hill. Tim wanted to climb the hill.
As Tim climbed, he met a girl named Sue. Sue had a toy car. Tim had a toy boat. They decided to trade. Tim gave Sue the boat and Sue gave Tim the car. They were both happy with their trade.
Tim and Sue climbed to the top of the hill together. The sun was shining and the sky was brilliant. They played with their new toys and had a great time. They became best friends and climbed the hill every day.

Once upon a time, a big red ball was on vacation. The ball was very attractive. It had a big smile and shiny eyes. The ball liked to give hugs to everyone it met.
One day, the big red ball met a small blue ball. The small blue ball said, "Hi! I like your smile. Can you give me a hug?" The big red ball smiled and gave the small blue ball a big hug.
Just then, something unexpected happened. The small blue ball grew bigger and turned into a big green ball! The big green ball said, "Thank you for the hug. Now I am big and happy too!" The big red ball and the big green ball became best friends and had a great vacation together.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tim and Ken. One day, they were walking in the park and Tim found a piece of paper on the ground. Ken said it was not interesting but Tim insisted on picking it up.
When Tim held it up, it was a surprise to both of them. The paper had a map of the park and some clues on it. Tim and Ken were so excited. They followed the clues and eventually found a hidden box with a toy inside.
Ken was so glad that Tim had picked up the paper. Without it, they wouldn't have found the treasure. He learned an important lesson: You can't always trust what others think. Always trust your gut and you might find a surprise.
Tim also learned an important lesson: sometimes, the most reliable thing is to not throw away something that looks ordinary. You never know where it might lead!

Once upon a time there were two groups of friends. The first group was big, and the second group was small.
One day, the small group was playing and having lots of fun. But suddenly, one of the members became sad. She started to cry.
The big group was a bit scared. They didn't know what to do.
Then the leader of the big group stepped forward. She found a way to make the small group smile again. She called out, "Let's share!"
The big group shared their toys, games and stories with the small group. The small group was very happy and so were the big group.
The big group was proud of their leader. They saw how she spread happiness by sharing.
The small group learned that when you share, it can make everyone feel calm and happy.
The end.

Lily and Max are friends. They like to play in the park. They run, slide, swing and laugh. They have fun.
One day, they see a bench in the park. It is big and red. It has a sign on it. The sign says: "Do not sit here. Wet paint."
Lily and Max want to sit on the bench. They think it looks nice. They forget the sign. They run to the bench and sit down.
"Ouch!" Lily says. "The bench is sticky. It hurts my legs."
"Me too!" Max says. "The bench is wet. It makes my pants dirty."
They look at each other. They see red paint on their clothes and skin. They are sad. They cry.
A lady comes to the bench. She sees Lily and Max. She is the painter. She is angry.
"Why did you sit on my bench?" she says. "Can't you read the sign? It says wet paint. You are not smart. You are silly."
Lily and Max are sorry. They say: "We are sorry, lady. We did not read the sign. We forget. We are not silly. We are smart. But we made a mistake."
The lady is not so angry. She sees that Lily and Max are young. She says: "It's okay. Everyone makes mistakes. But you have to be careful. Next time, read the signs. They are important. They help you stay safe and clean."
Lily and Max nod. They say: "Thank you, lady. We will read the signs. We will be careful. We will not forget."
The lady gives them a cloth. They wipe the paint off their clothes and skin. They say goodbye to the lady. They go to their moms. They tell them what happened. Their moms hug them. They say: "We love you. You are smart. But sometimes you forget. That's okay. Just try to remember."

Ben and Lily love to play in the park. They like to slide, swing and run. But their favorite thing is to climb. They climb on the rocks, the trees and the monkey bars.
One day, they see a big jet in the sky. It makes a loud noise and leaves a white trail behind. Ben and Lily are amazed. They want to see it closer.
"Let's climb on the hill!" Ben says. "Maybe we can touch the jet!"
"OK!" Lily agrees. They run to the hill and start to climb. They use their hands and feet and help each other. They are very brave and strong.
They reach the top of the hill and look at the sky. The jet is still there, but it is very far away. They cannot touch it, but they can wave at it.
"Hello, jet!" Ben shouts. "You are very fast and shiny!"
"Hello, jet!" Lily echoes. "You are very charming and cool!"
The jet seems to hear them. It winks at them with its lights and makes a funny sound. Ben and Lily laugh and clap. They are very happy.
They stay on the hill for a while and watch the jet fly away. Then they climb down and go back to the park. They have more fun with their friends. They tell them about the jet and the hill. They are very proud of their adventure. They are the best climbers in the world.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jane. Jane had a favourite toy. It was a car her mum had given to her. Jane loved to ride the car and make it zoom around the garden.
One day, she was playing outside when she saw something shiny in the grass. Jane went closer to look and saw a pair of scissors. She picked them up and thought they looked just like the scissors her mum used in the kitchen.
Suddenly, something disgusting flew by. Jane looked around and saw a big, ugly fly. Jane got scared and tried to chase it away. She waved the scissors in the air and shouted "Go away!".
The fly was zooming around so fast that it was almost impossible to catch it. Jane waved her arms around and tried to hit the fly with the scissors. But, every time she tried, the fly just flew faster.
In the end, the fly flew away and Jane put down the scissors. Her mum had taught her to never leave scissors lying around, so Jane picked them up and put them away in the kitchen.
And that is the story of how Jane tried to catch the disgusting fly with her scissors.

Once upon a time, there was a thoughtful boy named Will. He loved to help his mom in the house. One day, his mom asked him to fold the clothes.
Will went to the room and saw a big pile of clothes. He started to fold them one by one. As he was folding, he found a funny hat. He put it on his head and said, "Look, Mom! I'm a pirate!"
His mom laughed and said, "You are a very thoughtful pirate, Will. Thank you for helping me fold the clothes."
Will smiled and continued to fold the clothes with his funny hat on. He felt happy because he was helping his mom and being a pirate at the same time. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little red car who loved to go fast. Every day, the car would race down the street and all the other cars would say, "Wow, you are so fast!" The little red car was very proud of how fast it could go.
One day, the little red car heard a voice. The voice said, "Be careful, little red car. If you always go too fast, you may suffer." The little red car didn't listen to the voice and kept going fast, thinking nothing bad would happen.
But one day, the little red car went too fast and hit a big rock. The car suffered and broke down. The little red car remembered the voice and wished it had been more careful. From that day on, the little red car learned to be careful and not always go too fast.

One day, a big cat named Leo the Leopard was playing in the woods. He saw a mysterious box under a tree. Leo was very curious and wanted to know what was inside the box. He tried to open it, but it was closed very tight.
Leo went to his friend, Sam the Squirrel, for help. Sam said that they needed a special key to open the box. They both went to find the key. After a long time, they found the key under a big rock. They were very excited and happy.
Leo and Sam went back to the mysterious box. They used the key to open it. Inside the box, they found a beautiful part to play with. It was a fun game with lots of colors. They played with it all day and had a great time. The mysterious box had brought them a new and exciting game to enjoy together.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy dog named True. True liked to sleep all day and play all night. He had a best friend, a cat named Moon. They lived in a small house in a big green park.
One sunny day, True and Moon wanted to play. True wanted to play catch, but Moon wanted to play hide and seek. They could not agree on what to play. They both said "no" to each other's ideas. They started to disagree.
Then, a wise old owl saw them disagreeing. He told them to take turns playing each game. First, they played catch and had lots of fun. Then, they played hide and seek and laughed a lot. True and Moon learned that it is okay to disagree, as long as they find a way to play together. From that day on, they always took turns and were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a girl named Lucy. She loved to write with her soft crayons. One day, Lucy was writing on a big piece of paper when she saw a tiny bug. The bug was very quiet and did not make any noise. Lucy liked the silence and thought the bug was cute.
Lucy said to the bug, "Hello, little bug! Do you want to be my friend?" The bug nodded its head and started to walk on the paper. Lucy picked up her crayon and began to write around the bug. She wrote the word "friend" next to the bug.
The bug looked at the word and smiled. It then walked to the other side of the paper. Lucy wrote more words around the bug, like "happy" and "fun". The bug liked the words and danced on the paper. Lucy laughed and clapped her hands.
Lucy and the bug played together and wrote words on the paper all day. They had lots of fun and became best friends. When it was time for bed, Lucy put the bug in a soft little bed she made. They both went to sleep, happy to have found a new friend.

One day, a little boy named Tim was eager to go outside. He saw the wide world through his window. He wanted to play with his ball and run in the grass. Tim called his mom, "Mom, can we go out and play?"
His mom said, "Yes, Tim. Let's put on our shoes and go." Tim was happy and put on his shoes quickly. Mom and Tim went to the door. Mom said, "I will lock the door, so our house is safe."
Outside, Tim played with his ball. He kicked it far, and it went wide into the grass. Tim laughed and ran after it. Mom watched him play and smiled. They had a fun day playing outside.

Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there lived a little monkey named Momo. Momo had a long, curly tail that he loved to swing from tree to tree with. One day, Momo was playing with his friends, when his tail got stuck in a tree branch. "Oh no!" he cried.
A silly bird named Bree heard Momo's cry and flew down to help. "Don't worry, Momo," said Bree, "I will help you get your tail out!" Bree pulled and pulled, but Momo's tail was still stuck. Momo started to feel sad and said, "I want to quit trying. My tail will be stuck forever."
Bree didn't want Momo to quit, so she thought of a new plan. "I have an idea," she said, "Let's ask our big friend, Ellie the elephant, for help!" So, Bree and Momo went to find Ellie. When they found her, they told her about Momo's stuck tail.
Ellie the elephant was very strong. She used her long trunk to gently pull Momo's tail free from the tree branch. Momo was so happy that he could swing and play again. He thanked Bree and Ellie for their help, and they all played together for the rest of the day.
From that day on, Momo, Bree, and Ellie became the best of friends. They learned that no problem was too big when they worked together. And they all agreed that Momo's tail was not so silly after all.

Once there was a bunny named Benny. He was very small, but he had very big ideas. He wanted to explore the world, so one day he hopped off into the forest. 
As he hopped, he saw lots of things. He saw flowers, trees, and other animals. He saw a big, heavy diary lying by the side of the path. It was so heavy that he couldn't lift it, but he opened it and wrote down all the things he had seen. 
When he finished, he kept hopping. He saw more and more things, wrote them down in the diary, and hopped some more. He kept exploring and hopping, until he reached the far side of the forest. He closed the diary, tucked it beneath his arm, and hopped back home. 
When he arrived, he showed his diary to all his friends. He was so proud of all he had seen and written down. He had explored the world, and he knew he could go anywhere. Because his little hops had taken him everywhere he wanted to go.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly bean named Mark. He lived in a small garden with his bean friends. They all liked to play and have fun in the sun.
One day, Mark and his friends decided to play a game. They wanted to see who could jump the highest. Mark was very good at jumping. He jumped so high, he could touch the sky.
"Wow, Mark! You jump so high!" said his friend, Bean. "I want to jump like you!" Mark smiled and said, "You can do it, Bean! Just try your best!" So, Bean tried to jump as high as Mark. They all had a fun day playing together.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. At the park, there was a big machine that could supply candy. Tim was very excited to see the machine.
"Mom, can I have some candy from the machine?" Tim asked. His mom said yes and gave him a coin. Tim put the coin in the machine, and the machine supplied him with lots of candy. Tim was so happy.
After eating some candy, Tim felt dizzy. He sat down on the grass and said, "Mom, I feel dizzy from the candy." His mom told him to rest for a while. After resting, Tim felt better and played in the park with his mom. They had a fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a playful person named Tim. Tim liked to hang on the big tree in his yard. Every day, he would go out to play and have fun.
One sunny day, Tim met a new friend, Sam. Sam saw Tim hanging on the tree and said, "Hi! Can I play, too?" Tim smiled and said, "Yes! Come hang with me!"
So, Tim and Sam played together all day. They hung from the tree, laughed, and had lots of fun. They became the best of friends, and they played together every day after that. And they lived happily ever after.

One day, a little bird named Tim wanted to dive into the soft, green grass. He was in wonder at how fun it would be. So, Tim flew up high in the sky to get ready for his big dive.
As Tim was getting ready to dive, he saw his friend, the big yellow sun, smiling down at him. The sun made him feel warm and happy. Tim took a deep breath and then he started to dive down, down, down towards the soft, green grass.
Just before Tim touched the grass, he opened his wings and landed softly on the ground. He was so happy that he had done it! Tim looked around and saw his friends, the trees and flowers, clapping for him. They were proud of Tim for his big dive into the soft, green grass. And Tim was full of wonder and joy.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were lions and chase each other. They would roar and run and jump on the grass.
"Roar! I'm the king of the jungle!" Tim said.
"No, I'm the queen of the jungle!" Lily said.
They laughed and roared some more.
But then they saw a weird thing. It was big and round and shiny. It had wheels and a door and a window. It looked like a car, but not like any car they had seen before.
"What is that?" Tim asked.
"I don't know. Let's go and see." Lily said.
They walked towards the weird thing. They were curious and brave. They wanted to touch it and look inside.
But as they got closer, they heard a loud noise. It was not a roar. It was a beep. The weird thing was beeping and flashing. It scared Tim and Lily.
"Run!" Tim said.
They turned around and ran away. They ran back to their mom and dad, who were sitting on a bench. They hugged them and told them what they saw.
"It's okay, sweeties. It was just a spaceship. Someone was playing a prank. It's not real." Mom said.
"A spaceship? What is a spaceship?" Lily asked.
"It's a thing that goes to the sky and the stars. But it's very rare and weird. You don't have to worry about it." Dad said.
Tim and Lily felt better. They still liked to pretend they were lions, but they also liked to pretend they were astronauts. They would roar and beep and fly to the moon. They had fun and they had big hearts.

Once upon a time, there was a famous cat. The cat loved to play in the garden. One day, the cat saw a big vine. The vine was long and green. The cat wanted to climb the vine.
The cat tried to unlock the door to go outside. The cat pushed the door with its paw. The door opened, and the cat went outside. The cat was happy to be in the garden. It ran to the vine and started to climb.
The cat climbed up and up the vine. It saw many pretty things. The cat saw birds, flowers, and the sun. The cat played on the vine all day. When the cat was tired, it went back down the vine and went home. The cat was happy and sleepy after a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a baby who loved to play with his toys. He had a big, red ball and a soft, blue bear. The baby and the bear were best friends. They played together every day.
One day, the baby and the bear were playing in the kitchen. The baby saw a spicy pepper on the table. He thought it was a toy and picked it up. The baby said to the bear, "Look, I found a new toy!"
The bear knew the pepper was not a toy, but he didn't want the baby to feel sad. So, the bear said, "Let's show it to Mommy first." The baby and the bear went to Mommy, who was cooking dinner. She saw the spicy pepper and said, "Oh no, baby! That's not a toy. It's a spicy pepper for our food!"
The baby gave the pepper back to Mommy. She gave him a big hug and said, "Thank you for being so helpful!" The baby and the bear went back to playing with their toys, happy to have helped Mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a little chicken named Chicky. Chicky lived on a farm with many other animals. Chicky was very fragile and small, but she had a big heart.
One day, Chicky saw a big apple tree with yummy apples. Chicky wanted to get an apple but the tree was too tall. Chicky asked her friends for help. The big cow tried to reach the apples, but she could not yield any apples from the tree.
Then, Chicky had an idea. She asked all her friends to help. They all stood on each other and made a tall tower. Chicky climbed to the top and finally, they could yield the apples. Chicky and her friends were so happy to eat the yummy apples together.

Once upon a time, there was a crazy dog named Bob. Bob loved to play and jump all day. One day, Bob saw a yummy sandwich on a big rock.
Bob wanted to eat the sandwich. He tried to point at the sandwich to show his friend, the little bird. The little bird saw the sandwich too. They both wanted to eat it.
Bob and the little bird ran to the sandwich. They both tried to eat it at the same time. They pulled and pulled. The sandwich broke into two parts. Bob and the little bird fell down. They were sad because the sandwich was now all dirty and they could not eat it.

Once upon a time, there was a big giant. He lived in a wet forest. He was very tall and strong. He had a lot of friends in the forest. They liked to play with him. One day, the giant saw a little bird with a hurt wing. The bird could not fly.
The giant wanted to help the bird. He leaned down and picked up the bird. He took the bird to his home. The giant and his friends took care of the bird. They gave it food and a warm place to sleep. The bird started to feel better.
Soon, the bird's wing was all better. The bird could fly again. The giant and his friends were very happy. The bird thanked the giant for helping him. The giant learned that it is good to help others. The moral of the story is to always be kind and help your friends when they need it.

Once upon a time there was a bird who wanted to find a home. She looked high and low, but could not find a nice nest. She was feeling embarrassed and sad.
One bright, sunny day, she saw something that made her very happy. A thoughtful boy had build her a new nest for her to live in! The bird was so excited and thanked the boy for his kindness.
The bird and the boy became good friends. Each day he would come to check on the nest, and they would spend time playing together. Whenever other animals teased her, the bird felt safe knowing that the boy was there to look out for her.
The bird and the boy were soon best friends and they were always very happy together.

Once upon a time, there was a popular fish named Fin. Fin had a big smile and a shiny scale. All the little fish liked to play with Fin.
One day, Fin and his friends played in the sea. They swam and laughed all day. The sun went down, and it was time for the fish to go home. But, Fin's shiny scale was gone!
Fin was sad and worried. He looked and looked for his shiny scale. Then, something unexpected happened. A little crab walked up to Fin and gave him a big hug. The crab said, "I found your shiny scale!" Fin was so happy, he smiled a big smile. The little crab was a new friend, and they all played together.

Once upon a time, in a big world, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to climb. He would climb on chairs, tables, and even trees. One day, Tim saw a big, rough rock. He wanted to climb it.
Tim started to climb the rough rock. He used his hands and feet to climb higher and higher. As he climbed, he saw many things. He saw birds, bugs, and even a squirrel. Tim was very happy.
Finally, Tim reached the top of the rough rock. He looked around and saw the whole world. He felt like the king of the world. Tim waved to his mom and dad, who were watching him. They were proud of their brave little boy.

One day, a little girl named Sue was in her yard. She saw a small bird with an open beak. The bird looked very hungry. Sue wanted to help the bird.
Sue went to her mom and said, "Mom, please, can I have a prune for the bird?" Her mom gave her a prune. Sue took the prune to the bird. The bird was happy and ate the prune.
But then, a big cat came. The cat wanted to catch the bird. Sue was scared. The bird was scared too. The cat jumped to catch the bird, but something unexpected happened. The bird grew very big! The cat was scared now and ran away. The bird said, "Thank you, Sue" and flew away. Sue was happy she could help the bird.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a weird door in his room. He didn't know where it came from. He asked his mom, "Mom, what is this door for?" She said, "I don't know, Tim. You can imagine what's behind it."
Tim thought and thought. He imagined a big, fun playground behind the door. He opened the door and saw the playground! It was real! He played and played until he got tired.
Then, he imagined a big ice cream behind the door. He opened the door again, but there was no ice cream. Instead, he saw his dad with a big smile. "Surprise!" said his dad. "I brought you a new toy to play with!" Tim was happy and played with his new toy all day.

One warm day, Tim went to get a haircut. Tim did not like haircuts. They made him feel scared. He sat in the big chair and the nice lady put a cape on him. Tim's mom was there to tell him it would be okay.
The nice lady started to cut Tim's hair. He felt the scissors near his ear and got more scared. Tim's mom held his hand and told him a story about a brave boy who also got a haircut. Tim listened to the story and tried to be brave like the boy.
In the end, Tim's haircut was done. He looked in the mirror and saw his new haircut. Tim felt proud and happy. His mom told him he was very brave. They left the haircut place and went to get ice cream to celebrate.

One day, Rachel was in her bedroom playing with her toys. She noticed something strange near the bookshelf in the corner of the room. It was a box. She ran over and grabbed it. It was very light.
"Where did this come from?" Rachel asked.
Her mom came into the room and smiled at her. "It's a surprise for you," her mom said.
Rachel opened the box and realized it was filled with cheap books.
"Do you like them?" her mom asked.
"Yes!" Rachel said, excitedly.
The next day, Rachel's mom told her that they were going to the bookstore. Rachel was so excited she could barely contain her joy. When they arrived at the bookstore, Rachel ran towards the bookshelves. She was amazed at the abundance of books. She chose a few and eagerly put them in her box. 
Later that day, Rachel's mom placed the new books in the bookshelf in Rachel's room. Rachel had a big smile on her face. She finally realized that the box she found the day before wasn't a surprise but a foreshadowing of the great things to come!

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They shared their toys and snacks. They were honest with each other.
One day, a big dog came to the park. It barked and ran after the children. Ben and Lily were scared. They ran to the swings and climbed up. The dog could not reach them.
"Go away, dog!" Ben shouted. "You are not nice!"
The dog did not listen. It jumped and growled. It wanted to play, but it did not know how.
Lily started to cry. She missed her mom. She wanted to go home.
"Ben, I want my mom!" she sobbed.
Ben hugged Lily. He wanted his mom too. But he tried to be brave.
"Don't worry, Lily. I will provide for you. I will stay with you. We will be safe here. Mom will come soon." he said.
Lily nodded. She trusted Ben. He was her best friend. He was honest with her.
They held hands and waited. After a while, they saw their moms coming. They waved and shouted. The moms saw the dog and scared it away. They hugged their children and took them home.
Ben and Lily were happy. They had a big adventure. They learned to be brave and honest. They were still best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to go to the park with his mom. One day, he saw a big bench. Tim was confused. He did not remember seeing the bench before.
Tim sat on the bench and looked around. He saw a big tree and some pretty flowers. But he did not see his mom. Tim started to feel sad. He did not know where his mom was.
Tim waited on the bench for a long time. He started to cry. He wanted his mom to come back. But she did not come. Tim felt very sad and scared. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a fish named Bob. Bob loved to swim all day long. He was a very happy fish. One day, Bob went on a trip to a big museum. He was very excited.
When Bob got to the museum, he felt a little anxious. There were so many big things to see. He saw a big dinosaur, a tall rocket, and lots of colorful paintings. But Bob could not swim in the museum, so he was a little sad.
Bob's friend, a little girl named Sue, saw that he was sad. She had an idea! She took Bob to a big pond outside the museum. Bob was so happy to swim again. They played and laughed all day. And from that day on, Bob and Sue were the best of friends.

Sara loves to feed the ducks at the pond. She brings bread and corn and throws them in the water. The ducks swim and quack and eat the food. Sara likes to watch them and count them. She knows all their names.
One day, Sara sees a big duck with a red hat and a shiny medal. He looks different from the other ducks. He walks in front of them and makes loud noises. The other ducks follow him and make noises too. Sara thinks they are having a march.
Sara asks her mom who the big duck is. Her mom says he is a famous duck. He is the leader of the ducks. He helps them find food and water and keeps them safe. He is brave and smart and kind. He won the medal for saving a baby duck from a fox.
Sara thinks the famous duck is very cool. She wants to feed him some bread and corn. She calls his name and waves her hand. The famous duck sees her and swims to the shore. He takes the food from her and thanks her. He says she is a nice girl and a good friend. He gives her a feather as a gift.
Sara is very happy. She puts the feather in her hair and smiles. She says goodbye to the famous duck and the other ducks. She tells her mom she had a lot of fun. She says she wants to come back and feed the ducks again. Her mom says they can do that tomorrow. Sara hugs her mom and says she loves her.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. One day, they find a big box in the corner. They open the box and see many things inside. They see books, clothes, toys, and a frame.
"What is this?" Anna asks, holding the frame. It is brown and has a glass in the middle.
"It is a frame. You can put a picture inside," Ben says. He looks at the frame and sees a picture of a dog. The dog is black and white and has a big smile.
"Wow, look at the dog! He is so cute!" Anna says. She likes dogs very much. She wants to keep the frame and the picture.
"No, I want it! It is my frame!" Ben says. He likes dogs too. He grabs the frame from Anna.
"Hey, give it back! It is mine!" Anna says. She pulls the frame from Ben.
They start to fight over the frame. They tug and push and shout. The frame is hard and heavy. They are not careful.
Suddenly, the frame breaks. The glass shatters and the picture falls out. Anna and Ben stop fighting. They look at the broken frame and the picture. They feel sad and sorry.
They hear a voice from the door. It is their mom.
"What is going on here? What is this mess?" Mom asks. She sees the broken frame and the picture. She smells something smelly.
She picks up the picture and looks at it. She sees the dog. She knows the dog.
"This is your grandpa's dog. His name was Spot. He was very old and smelly. He died last year. Your grandpa gave me this frame and picture to remember him. He loved Spot very much," Mom says.
Anna and Ben feel more sad and sorry. They did not know the frame and the picture were so important. They did not mean to break them.
They look at Mom and say, "We are sorry, Mom. We did not know. We were fighting over the frame. We both liked the dog. We wanted to keep it."
Mom sighs and hugs them. She says, "I know you did not know. I know you liked the dog. But you should not fight over things. You should share and be nice to each other. You are twins. You are lucky to have each other."
Anna and Ben nod and hug Mom. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We love you. We love each other. We will share and be nice."
Mom smiles and says, "That's good. I love you too. Now, let's clean up this mess. And maybe we can find another frame and picture for you to keep. How about that?"
Anna and Ben smile and say, "Yes, Mom. Thank you, Mom."
They decide to help Mom clean up. They decide to be good twins. They decide to love the dog, even if he was old and smelly.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. He loved to listen to all kinds of music. Whenever music was played, he would dance with so much joy.
One day, his Mommy scolded him and said, "Jack, stop spoiling your music!" Jack was very sad, so he stopped moving and listened carefully. He asked, "What does spoil mean?"
Mommy lovingly explained, "Spoiling means destroying. Music should be enjoyed with respect. You can dance with joy but it should never be done in a fierce way, because it may hurt someone or damage something else."
Jack learned an important lesson that day. He understood that he should enjoy music with joy and respect, never spoiling it.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to look for bugs and flowers. They saw a lizard on a rock. It was green and brown and had a long tail.
"Wow, look at the lizard!" Lily said. "It is so cool. Can we touch it?"
Ben was scared of the lizard. He thought it might bite or scratch them. He shook his head.
"No, Lily, we can't touch it. It is not a toy. It is a wild animal. It might run away or hurt us."
But Lily did not listen to Ben. She wanted to see the lizard up close. She had an urge to touch it. She moved slowly towards the rock.
"Come on, Ben, don't be a baby. It is just a lizard. It is not a lion or a snake. It is cute and small. I want to pet it."
Ben tried to stop Lily. He grabbed her arm.
"Lily, stop! You are being silly. The lizard does not want to be petted. It wants to be left alone. You are scaring it. Come back here!"
But Lily pulled her arm away from Ben. She reached out her hand to the lizard. The lizard did not like Lily's hand. It felt threatened. It opened its mouth and showed its teeth. It hissed and jumped at Lily.
"Aaaah!" Lily screamed. She was surprised and scared. She fell back and dropped her hand. The lizard ran away and hid under a bush.
Ben ran to Lily. He hugged her and checked her hand. She had a small scratch on her finger. It was bleeding a little bit.
"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asked. "Did the lizard hurt you?"
Lily nodded. She was crying. She felt sorry and stupid.
"Yes, Ben, I am okay. But the lizard hurt me. It was angry at me. I should have listened to you. You were right. I was wrong. I was silly. I am sorry, Ben."
Ben smiled and kissed her cheek. He took her hand and wrapped it with a leaf.
"It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. You are not silly. You are curious. But you have to be careful. Some animals don't like to be touched. They need their space. Next time, we can look at the lizard from far away. Okay?"
Lily smiled and nodded. She hugged Ben and said thank you.
"Okay, Ben. Thank you for being my friend. You are very smart and brave. And tall. I like you."
They walked back to the house. They saw their mom and dad. They told them what happened. Their mom and dad were glad they were okay. They gave them a hug and a cookie. They said they were proud of them for being honest and kind. They said they loved them very much.

In 1966 , Reines took most of his neutrino research team with him when he left for the new University of California , Irvine ( UCI ) , becoming its first dean of physical sciences . At UCI , Reines extended the research interests of some of his graduate students into the development of medical radiation detectors , such as for measuring total radiation delivered to the whole human body in radiation therapy .

Once upon a time, there was a small gray bug. The bug liked to crawl on the ground. One day, the bug found a shiny knife in the grass. The knife was very big for the little bug.
The bug met a friendly bird. The bird said, "Hi, little bug! What are you doing with that big knife?" The bug said, "I found it in the grass. I want to take it home."
The bird helped the bug carry the knife. They were a good team. The bug crawled and the bird flew. They took the knife to the bug's home. The bug and the bird were happy and became best friends.

Tom and Lily were playing in the backyard. They liked to build things with the lumber that Dad had left there. The lumber was brown and hard and had nails in it. Tom and Lily had a hammer and some nails too.
They decided to make a house for their toys. They used the lumber to make walls and a roof. They worked hard and had fun. They put their toys inside the house and pretended they were a family.
"Look at our house!" Tom said. "It is so big and nice!"
"Yes, it is!" Lily said. "We are very good builders!"
They heard a loud noise. It was Dad. He was coming back from work. He saw the house that Tom and Lily had made. He was not happy. He shouted at them.
"Tom! Lily! What have you done? This lumber is for the shed! You can't use it for your games! You could hurt yourselves with the nails! Come here right now!"
Tom and Lily were scared. They ran out of the house and went to Dad. They said they were sorry. They did not know the lumber was for the shed. They just wanted to have fun.
Dad was angry, but he loved them. He hugged them and said they were not in trouble. But they had to help him take apart the house and put the lumber back. He also said they had to be careful with the nails and the hammer. He said he would find them some other things to play with.
Tom and Lily said okay. They helped Dad with the lumber. They were sad to see their house go, but they understood. They learned a lesson. They also had an idea. They asked Dad if he could make them a small house with some of the lumber. Dad smiled and said he would try. Tom and Lily were happy. They thanked Dad and gave him a kiss. They went inside to have some cookies. They still liked to build things, but they would ask first.
