"Let's go on the slide!" Tom says.
"OK, but be careful!" Jen says.
They run to the slide. Tom goes first. He twists his body as he slides down. He thinks it is fun. Jen goes after him. She twists her body too. But she twists too much. She falls off the slide. She hurts her arm. She cries.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Jen says.
Tom hears her cry. He runs to her. He sees her arm. It is red and swollen.
"I'm sorry, Jen!" Tom says. "Are you OK?"
"No, I'm not OK!" Jen says. "You made me twist too much! You are a bad brother!"
Tom feels sad. He did not mean to make Jen twist too much. He wants to help her. He sees a lemonade stand nearby. He has some coins in his pocket. He goes to the stand. He buys a cup of lemonade. He brings it to Jen.
"Here, Jen, drink this!" Tom says. "It will make you feel better!"
Jen takes the cup. She drinks the lemonade. But it is very sour. She makes a face. She spits it out.
"Yuck, yuck, yuck!" Jen says. "This is the worst lemonade ever! You are a bad brother!"
Tom feels worse. He did not know the lemonade was sour. He wanted to make Jen happy. He does not know what to do.
A lady sees them. She is a nurse. She works at the park. She comes to them. She sees Jen's arm. She has a bandage and some ice. She puts the bandage and the ice on Jen's arm. She smiles at them.
"Hello, children!" the lady says. "What happened?"
Tom tells her what happened. He says he is sorry. He says he loves Jen. Jen stops crying. She sees Tom's face. He looks sad. She feels sorry too. She says she loves Tom. She says she is sorry. She says he is a good brother.
The lady hugs them. She says they are good children. She says they should be careful on the slide. She says they should be kind to each other. She says they should share the lemonade. She gives them another cup of lemonade. It is sweet and cold. They drink it. They smile.
The end.
Moral value: Be careful on the slide. Be kind to your siblings. Share the lemonade.

The precursor to Tropical Storm Gilda was a large convective system partially due to a tropical wave . It gradually became better organized over the northwestern Caribbean Sea , and on October 15 , a tropical depression formed off the coast of Nicaragua . As it drifted to the northeast , it strengthened to a tropical storm , peaking at 70 mph ( 110 km / h ) winds . Before it hit the coast of Cuba , it weakened enough to cause only minor damage . By the time it struck the island , it had become very disorganized in nature .

Once, a big elephant with a long trunk lived in a forest. He had many friends. One day, he saw a small hole in a tree. He wanted to see what was inside the hole. He tried to put his trunk in the hole, but it did not fit. His trunk was too big for the small hole.
The elephant asked his friend, the bird, to help him. The bird could see inside the hole because she was small. She flew near the hole and looked inside. She saw a small, shiny stone. The bird picked up the stone with her beak and gave it to the elephant.
The elephant was happy to see the shiny stone. He thanked his friend, the bird. The bird was happy to help her friend. They played together in the forest, and the elephant kept the shiny stone with him always.

One sunny day, a little boat named Bobby wanted to sail. Bobby loved to feel the cool water as he moved. He liked to watch the fish swim under him. Bobby had a friend named Timmy, who was a tiny fish.
"Hi Timmy!" said Bobby. "Do you want to sail with me today?"
"Yes, Bobby! I love to swim with you," said Timmy. They started to sail and swim together. They saw many cool things in the water. They saw big fish and small fish. They saw pretty shells and plants.
As they sailed and swam, they met a new friend named Sally. Sally was a happy crab. She liked to play in the sand. Bobby and Timmy asked Sally to join them.
"Come sail and swim with us, Sally!" said Bobby and Timmy. Sally was excited and joined them. They all had a fun day together in the cool water.

Lily and Lola are twins. They look the same and like the same things. They have a big toy box with many toys. They like to play with their toys every day.
One day, Lily and Lola want to play with the same toy. It is a pink doll with a blue dress. They both reach for the doll and pull it. They start to fight.
"Give me the doll! It is mine!" Lily says.
"No, it is mine! I saw it first!" Lola says.
They pull harder and harder. The doll makes a loud rip sound. The doll's dress tears and the stuffing comes out. Lily and Lola stop and look at the doll. They feel sad.
They hear their mom coming. She smells something smelly. She sees the doll on the floor and the twins with tears in their eyes.
"What happened here?" Mom asks.
Lily and Lola look at each other. They do not want to tell mom that they fought. They do not want to get in trouble.
They remain quiet. They hug each other and say sorry. They pick up the doll and the stuffing. They ask mom to help them fix the doll.
Mom smiles and hugs them. She says, "I am glad you are sorry and you love each other. Fighting is not nice. Sharing is nice. Let's fix the doll together and then we can play with other toys."
Lily and Lola nod and smile. They are happy again. They love their mom and their twin. They do not like to fight. They like to share.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside in the sun. One day, he found a big chest in his yard. He was very happy and wanted to open it.
Tim tried to open the chest, but it was hard. He felt a little bitter because he could not open it. He stumbled and fell, but he did not give up. He tried again and again, and finally, the chest opened.
Inside the chest, Tim found many toys and games. He was very happy and shared them with his friends. The moral of the story is to never give up and always share with others.

" Hi , Infidelity " is the sixth episode of the third season of the American mystery television series Veronica Mars , and the fiftieth episode overall . Written by John Enbom and directed by Michael Fields , the episode premiered on The CW on November 17 , 2006 .

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was nervous because he wanted to make his mom a special lunch, but he did not know how to cook. He found a menu with yummy food on it and wanted to make something from it.
Tim tried to make a sandwich but he struggled. He asked his big sister, Sue, for help. "Sue, can you help me make a sandwich?" Sue said, "Sure, Tim. I will help you."
Together, they made a yummy sandwich for their mom. Mom was so happy and said, "Thank you, Tim and Sue! You worked together and made a great lunch!" Tim and Sue learned that when they work together, they can do anything.

Lily and Sam were playing in the park. They had a big hoop that they could roll on the grass. They took turns to push the hoop and run after it. They laughed and shouted as they chased the hoop.
"Look, Lily, I can make the hoop go very fast!" Sam said.
"Wow, Sam, you are good at this!" Lily said.
They played until they were very thirsty. They saw a water fountain near the swings. They ran to the fountain and took turns to drink some water. They drank with big gulps and made funny noises.
"Ah, this water is so good!" Lily said.
"Yes, it is!" Sam said.
They saw a lady with a dog walking by. The dog was brown and fluffy. It had a red collar and a blue leash. The lady smiled at Lily and Sam.
"Hello, children, do you like my dog?" the lady asked.
"Yes, we do!" Lily and Sam said.
"His name is Max. He is very gentle and friendly. Do you want to pet him?" the lady asked.
"Yes, please!" Lily and Sam said.
The lady let them pet Max. Max licked their faces and wagged his tail. He was very soft and warm. Lily and Sam giggled and hugged Max.
"Thank you, lady, Max is very nice!" Lily said.
"You're welcome, children, Max likes you too!" the lady said.
Lily and Sam said goodbye to the lady and Max. They went back to their hoop and played some more. They had a lot of fun in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia had a favorite color. She loved the color blue. She had a blue dress, a blue ball, and even a blue room. Mia also liked warm hugs from her mom and dad.
One day, Mia went to a store with her mom to order a blue cake for her birthday. Mia said, "Mom, can we order a big blue cake?" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, Mia. We can order a big blue cake just for you."
When they got home, Mia's dad gave her a warm hug. "I can't wait for my birthday," she said. "I will have a big blue cake!" Her dad laughed and said, "Yes, Mia, your cake will be very blue and very yummy."
On Mia's birthday, she got her big blue cake. It was so pretty and yummy. Mia's friends came to her party, and they all had a great time. They played with the blue ball and ate the blue cake. Mia felt very happy and loved.

One day, a boy named Tim found a big, wide potato in his yard. He was very happy and wanted to show it to his friend, Sue. Tim ran to Sue's house and knocked on her door. Sue came out and Tim said, "Look at my wide potato!"
Sue looked at the potato and then she pointed to a big hole in the ground. "I found this hole in my yard," she said. Tim and Sue were very curious about the hole and the wide potato. They decided to put the potato in the hole and see what would happen.
As soon as they put the potato in the hole, something unexpected happened. The wide potato started to grow and grow until it became a huge potato tree! Tim and Sue were very surprised and happy. They climbed the tree and found more wide potatoes. They picked them and shared them with everyone in their town. And that's how Tim and Sue became the best potato tree friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little comet who loved to fly fast. He was very competitive and always wanted to be the best. He liked to race with his friends, the stars, to see who could go the farthest in the sky.
One day, the comet felt very tired, but he did not want to stop. He thought that if he took a rest, he would lose the race. So, he kept flying and flying, even though he was very sleepy.
Soon, the comet learned that taking a rest is important. When he finally took a break, he felt much better and could fly faster. The moral of the story is that it is important to rest when you are tired, even if you want to win.

Once upon a time, a little girl called Mia wanted to fly. Everyday, she looked up into the sky and wished she could soar high above the clouds. 
One day, her wish came true! On her way to the park, Mia saw a sparkling fairy standing in the meadow. The fairy smiled at Mia and said, "I can allow you to fly, but there is something you must do first!" 
Mia was very excited and agreed to do whatever the fairy asked. The fairy said, âFirst, you must be brave and not be lazy. If you work hard, you can do anything! The key is to remember to breathe. That way, your heart will be filled with oxygen and you will be happy.â
Mia worked hard and never gave up. Soon enough, she could fly just like she'd always dreamed! She was so happy and thanked the fairy.
From this story, we learned that if we want to do something amazing, we must be brave, not be lazy and remember to breathe. Being brave and working hard will let us reach great heights!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was troubled because he had no one to talk to. One day, Tim went for a visit to his friend, the big tree.
"Hello, big tree," Tim said. "I am sad. Can we talk?"
The big tree did not talk back. Tim was very sad. He sat under the big tree and cried. A little bird flew by and saw Tim crying. The bird felt bad for Tim.
"Hello, Tim," said the little bird. "I can talk with you."
Tim was happy to have a friend to talk to. They talked and talked all day. But then, the sky got dark. The little bird had to fly away.
"Goodbye, Tim," said the little bird.
Tim was sad again. He had no one to talk to. The big tree still did not talk. Tim went home, feeling very lonely.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly lady named Nana. She lived in a small house with her cat, Whiskers. Nana liked to listen to the birds sing outside her window.
One sunny day, Nana's friend, Mr. Brown, came to visit. He brought a bottle of wine for them to share. "Nana, I have wine for us," said Mr. Brown. "Oh, thank you, Mr. Brown!" Nana replied with a smile.
Nana and Mr. Brown sat in the garden, listening to the birds sing. They drank the wine and talked about happy times. Whiskers the cat played in the grass nearby. It was a lovely day, and they all enjoyed the sun and each other's company.

Once there was a dad and his son, who was three. Dad wanted to fix a toy car and he needed a screw. He asked his son to help him find it.
But son wasn't feeling too helpful. He didn't think looking for a screw was any fun. He started to cry and insisted he didn't want to help.
Dad insisted again, and so son got up and looked for the screw. He looked everywhere, but he couldn't find it.
But Dad said he knew where it was. He followed him to a drawer, and when they opened it they saw something dead in the corner. It was the screw!
Dad was so pleased. He said to son, 'You found it! You found the screw!' And son felt happy and proud. 
The screw was safe and sound, and the dad and son worked hard together to fix the toy car. Everyone was happy when it was finished.
